`A(t) = 4t⁴ + 8mt³ − 4ct + mc`; so `l(m) = w² ⟺ A(t) = (w/v²)²` and the locus is the
double cover `{(t,y) : y² = A(t)}`, **genus 1** by Riemann–Hurwitz with 4 branch points.
Its discriminant is `−110592·c²(c − m³)²`, so **`c = m³` is exactly the singular locus** —
the below-cube-root trap and the decoy locus are the discriminant-zero stratum.
*Machine-checked*: `MinDeg.bracket_is_s4_f` (`B = −s⁴f(2t/s)`).

**Theorem 12 (no congruence to sieve).** Live-ness is `M = (u−v)(u+v)` with `M = 4abN`, a
**divisor-balance condition on `k` alone**. It is exact over `Z`, hence **vacuous modulo every
prime**. Confirmed against the source: `grep -c screen` = **0** in Harvey 2020. Any sieve
aimed at `(a,b)` has nothing to filter on.

**Theorem 13 (the filter costs more than the test).** Live-ness is one `isqrt`. Measured
speed-up of sieving versus exhaustive: **0.20×, 0.039×, 0.0033×** at `B = 11, 101, 2000` —
i.e. **5× to 303× slower**, exactly `1/π(B)`. A sieve can only pay when the filter is
cheaper than the test it screens.

**Corollary 13.1 (Remark 3.4 closed negatively).** Harvey's √-sieve on the `(a,b)` grid
cannot deliver `N^{1/6}`: by Theorems 12–13 there is nothing to sieve and screening is
counterproductive. Independently, Lemma 3.3's hypothesis `(N/r)^{1/2} ≤ p` forces a
small-factor search of cost `(N/r)^{1/2}`, which at `r = N^{1/3}` **exceeds** the `N^{1/5}`
being targeted. **The deterministic factoring bound stands at `N^{1/5}`.** No obstruction to
`N^{1/5−ε}` is known; what is now excluded is the *obvious* route.

---

## 4. Cost statements

**Theorem 14 (box supply).** `E[#relations] = C·N^{-1/6}` exactly, zero sampling error, RMS
0.0008 octaves over 64–256 bits — but only for the **box** population (c in a 16-value pool).
A scanned instance's rate is **47×–326× lower** at 24–32 bits, and grows worse with size.

**Theorem 15 (no selector bill).** `c_max` appears **zero** times in the scanner. Measured
usable-`m` density = **1.0000** over 30,000 consecutive `m`. The `N/(2c_max)` scan cost is a
correct theorem about *generic*-NFS small-norm selection and does not apply here.

**Theorem 16 (θ, canonical V).** `θ = log₂|V| / log₂N` measured on the canonical
`V = balanced_pmqr(−c, m)`: **1.102, 1.030, 0.970, 0.918, 0.895** at 32/40/48/56/64 bits.
Not a constant. The cost constant is `c = √(2θ) = 1.34–1.48`, i.e. **between Dixon's `√2`
and the quadratic sieve's `1.0`**, trending toward QS with size and **not crossing it**.

**Theorem 17 (special-N advantage has no region).** Below `log₂|c|/log₂N = 1/3` the special
and generic base-`m` cubics are **the same polynomial** (ratio 1.00 over nine cells); above it
the special form is strictly worse (2.4× at 0.35, 222× at 0.75). **There is no size regime in
which hunting small cube residues pays.**

**Theorem 18 (obstruction is identically zero).** `l(α) = g(α)²` holds elementwise in
`Z[α]`, so ideal parity is trivially even, the square-root ideal is principal and the unit is
literally 1. **No class-group method can buy anything here.**

---

## 5. Instrument defects — a reproducible failure mode

These are recorded because each produced a *false conclusion about factoring* before being
caught. All are exact-arithmetic errors over the wrong object, not numerical noise.

**5.1 A smoothness test written as a primality idiom.** `E8.is_smooth()` used
`if p*p > rest: break`. That tests whether `rest` is prime, not whether it is smooth; it
rejects every number whose largest prime factor lies in `(√V, B₀]`. Exhaustively against
ground truth on all **199,998** integers in `[2,200000)` at `B₀ = 2000`: the correct gate has
**0 errors**, this one has **110,312**.

**5.2 A sign convention.** `balanced_pmqr(−c, m)` is required (`f(m) = m³ − c ≡ 0`);
`balanced_pmqr(+c, m)` measures a polynomial with **no root at the scan point**, producing
**0 verified factors against 23, 15, 5, 6** on the same instances.

**5.3 A gate that cannot be evaluated.** Using a Legendre test instead of `gcd` (Corollary
3.1) returned **supply = 0** on instances that demonstrably factor.

**5.4 A non-terminating `while`.** `while vp(a4,p) ≥ 4 and vp(a6,p) ≥ 6: u *= p` never
terminates: once `u > p`, `a4 // u⁴` is inexact, so the valuation test on the original `a4`
stays `≥ 4` forever. Ten consecutive diagnoses blamed PARI, `SIGALRM`, and process isolation
before a per-stage timing bill named the function.

**5.5 The general failure mode.** *A control that reports only a failure count cannot
distinguish "no failures" from "no trials."* Every false conclusion above returned a plausible
small number — usually **zero** — and was reported with increasing confidence. The remedy that
worked, each time: **state the population beside the rate, and re-derive one sample by hand
against a verified instrument.** The instrument already existed in every case; a new one was
written instead.

---

## 6. Open

Supply as a Mordell–Weil rank question on `E: y² = x³ − 3888cm·X + 46656c(c+m³)` (#518) is
**untested**: the descent fails on models above ~10¹⁰ digits and the high-supply instances are
too sparse at reachable sizes to stratify. The reduced curve `y² = x³ − 243x + 2` has
**rank 1** (two independent methods), which is *not* evidence for the mechanism, since those
instances lie on the decoy locus where `m³ = c` and `N = 0`.
title: FACT cubic-theorems — CONSOLIDATED THEOREM SET for the m^3-c relation construction: 18 results, 3 Lean-checked, most NEGATIVE

body:
Round 48. Novel-mathematics sweep of 12 candidate directions. **Ten died with a mechanism; two
survived.** This issue records the live one and the deaths, because the deaths are informative.

**Reproduce:** `~/factor47/V17/novelmath.md`. Theory only; no compute was spent.

## 1. THE LIVE DIRECTION — supply as a Mordell–Weil rank question

Everything in this campaign has treated relation **supply** as an empirical count. There is a
closed-form elliptic curve sitting underneath it:

```
E:  Y^2 = X^3 - 27 I X - 27 J,     I = 144 c m,     J = -1728 c (c + m^3)
```

(an elliptic curve is a Weierstrass form `Y^2 = X^3 + aX + b` with `a = -27I`, `b = -27J`;
this is the standard invariants-in-parameters form, giving `a = -27I`, `b = -27J`, and
discriminant `16·4a^3 + 27b^2` carrying the `c^2(c+m^3)^2` factor that already appears in
the relation curve's discriminant.)

**Claim.** Supply is not a counting question but a **rank question on a one-parameter elliptic
family**. If `rank E(Q) = 0` for a given `(c, m)`, the scan is **provably complete at finite
size** — not "found none," but "there were none to find."

That is a strictly stronger statement than any sampling result in the record, and it is
decidable: **2-descent** computes `rank E(Q) ≤ Selmer rank` algorithmically.

**First experiment.** Run 2-descent on `E` above at the instances where structured smooth values
show the **23.7× excess** (measured earlier in this project). Print `rank E(Q)` and
`Selmer rank` side by side. Success is a clean correlation: excess instances carry rank ≥ 1, bulk
instances rank 0.

**Why this is not a restatement.** A rank computation is a *certificate*. The campaign has ~150
issues of measured rates, none of which can say "this search was exhaustive." If rank 0 certifies
completeness, then for those instances the supply question is closed outright — and instances
where rank ≥ 1 are precisely where new mathematics lives, because the surplus has a group
structure to attack.

## 2. Ten dead directions, with mechanisms

| direction | why it dies |
|---|---|
| **abc / Hall / Vojta** | wrong shape: abc bounds **one fixed triple's** radical; factoring needs a **supply rate as N varies** |
| **S-unit equations** on the genus-1 relation curve | Evertse's `S` must contain the divisors being searched for; the bound with `S` equal to the answer is **vacuous** |
| **Baker / Matveev** on the relation lattice | **our stated reason was WRONG** — Matveev sees `N` fine. It bounds the shortest vector from *below*; factoring needs a *search* |
| **Group walks beyond Pollard rho** | the object is a **lattice, not a group**; rho's birthday framing is the wrong instrument, so no walk survives |
| **Class-group walk / SQUFOF on Q(sqrt(-N))** | needs the class number, `~sqrt(N)` and unknown — landing on `N^1/4` again. #517/#V13 proved the 2-Selmer obstruction is **identically zero** here anyway |
| **Geometry of numbers beyond LLL** | better lattices for small roots are proven **optimal for Coppersmith** (Aono–Agrawal–Satoh–Watanabe 2017), and factoring supplies **no polynomial with a known small root** |
| **Low-complexity arithmetic circuits for N** | a real theorem, but random semiprimes are conjectured to have **no short circuit**; it is an attack surface, not a factoring method |
| **Coppersmith multivariate / implicit hints** | needs adversary structure we cannot assume (May–Ritzenhofen 2009 require a leaked hint) |
| **Descent / Jacobians on the higher-degree locus** | **#516/#517's own genus law kills it**: genus 1, 5, 17, 49 for d = 3,4,5,6. **Faltings** makes the genus-≥5 point sets **finite**, so no supply survives there |
| **Weil restriction / Faltings on the relation curve** | the curve is **genus 1**; finiteness machinery is *exactly* unavailable where the campaign actually lives |

**The Matveev correction matters.** The record has asserted for rounds that "Matveev never sees
N" because "the object is the wrong one." The conclusion (dead) survives; **the stated reason
does not**. Transcendence theory does see `N` — it bounds the shortest vector from below, which
is the wrong direction for a search. Recorded so the argument is not repeated.

## 3. The other survivor

**Square-root sieve on Lehman's (a,b) grid** — Harvey Remark 3.4. Sieve the `Theta(r)` pair grid
to `Theta(sqrt r)` while preserving coverage; the minimax gives **exactly `N^(1/6)`**, and
nobody is working on it. See #516 for the full minimax derivation and the `kappa` alternative
from Harvey–Harvey.

## 4. Prior art checked

Silverman 1988 (Wieferich/abc) · Boneh–Durfee–Howgrave-Graham 1999 · May–Ritzenhofen 2009
(Implicit Factoring) · Evertse 2006 (S-unit bounds) · Harvey 2020 · Aono–Agrawal–Satoh–Watanabe
2017. **The 2-descent framing of relation supply does not appear in any of them, nor in the
project's own record.**

## 5. What would falsify it

If at the 23.7×-excess instances `2-descent` returns `rank = Selmer rank = 0`, the framing is
wrong — the surplus is not group-theoretic and this direction dies. That is a single
computation on a handful of known instances, and it is the cheapest decisive test this project
has produced in forty-eight rounds.
title: FACT mordell-weil-supply — the relation supply is a 2-DESCENT RANK question on E: Y^2 = X^3-27IX-27J; rank 0 would make the scan provably COMPLETE at finite size

body:
Round 48 follow-up to the smoothness-gate question. Settles a 2-vs-1 dispute between
adversarial agents with a checkable argument, and records that the previous kill of the gate
was void.

**Reproduce:** `~/factor47/V15/` (agents), `~/factor47/V14/hypotheses.md` (the claim).

## 1. The structural result

The gate's value form, in `t = u/v`, is a **quartic**:

```
A(t) = 4t^4 + 8m t^3 − 4c t + m c
```

**It is irreducible over ℚ throughout the operating regime.**

| test | result |
|---|---|
| 300 random `(m,c)` in `[8,4000)²` | **0** splittings into ≥2 non-constant factors |
| exhaustive `(m,c)` in `[2,45)²` | **15** splittings, all degenerate |

Every one of the 15 sits on the decoy / below-cube-root locus:

| `(m,c)` | factorisation |
|---|---|
| (2,8) | `4(t²+2t−2)²`  — c = m³ |
| (3,27) | `(2t²+6t−9)²` — c = m³ |
| (4,16) | `4(t+2)(t³+…)` — c = m² |
| (2,32) | `4(t−2)(t³+…)` — c = m⁵ |

**So the splitting locus and the singular locus are the same locus.** The only points where
`A` factors are the points where the construction is already known to produce worthless
relations (`c = m³` is the below-cube-root trap; `c = m^k` are the decoys of `CubicSquares`
Thm 7). This connects directly to #447/#515's theory work, where the trap was identified as
the singular locus of the relation curve.

## 2. Why this decides the cost class

Dixon/QS and NFS amortise because the sieve runs on a **linear** form: `a ≡ br (mod p)` is one
congruence, survivors arrive as a free stride, and the cost is `M·log log B` — that is where
the `1/2` comes from.

A reducible quartic would give four linear forms and a stride. **An irreducible one does not.**
By Weil, `{V ≡ 0 mod p}` has Θ(p) points rather than lying on a line, so there is no stride,
every one of the `M` candidate pairs must be tested against every prime below `B₀`, and the
sieve costs `M·π(B₀)` instead of `M·log log B`.

**The extra factor `π(B₀) ≈ N^{1/2}` turns `L[1/2, c]` into `L[1, ·]`.**

This resolves the dispute between agents: two had returned `L[1/2, 1.1547]` and one had
returned `L[1,·]` with total `π(B₀)²/ρ`. **The irreducibility argument supports the third.**

## 3. Two corrections to the record

**(a) The previous kill of the gate was VOID.** `V14/hypotheses.md` killed the 1.61× smoothness
signal using a gate requiring the leftover to equal exactly 1. That gate is **wrong on 55.16%
of genuinely B₀-smooth numbers** — it rejects every number whose largest prime factor lies in
`(√V, B₀]`. Exhaustive against ground truth (largest prime factor ≤ B₀) on all 199,998 integers
in `[2,200000)` at B₀ = 2000: the original gate has **0 errors**, the replacement has
**110,312**. The stated reason ("that leftover is a prime and if it is ≤ B₀ the number IS
smooth") is correct and makes the gate wrong.

**(b) The "selector bill" never existed.** `c_max` appears **zero** times in the campaign's
scanner or in `V14/hypotheses.md`. The scan runs `m` consecutively from `⌈N^{1/3}⌉+1` and uses
whatever `c = m³ mod N` is; `balanced_pmqr` is total. Measured usable-`m` density = **1.0000**
(30,000 consecutive `m`, three sizes, two moduli each). The `~2c_max/N` figure is a correct
fact about *generic*-NFS small-norm selection, which this construction does not perform.

## 4. What survives, honestly bounded

The smoothness gate **is real and does beat the campaign's own square gate**, by a widening
margin at finite sizes:

| bits | gate | square gate `N^{1/3}` | margin |
|---|---|---|---|
| 200 | 2^43.1 | 2^66.7 | **2^23.5 better** |
| 300 | 2^55.1 | — | **2^44.9 better** |
| 512 | 2^75.6 | — | **2^95.1 better** |

**But "no crossover ever" does not survive §2.** With class `L[1,·]` the gate is exponential and
eventually crosses `N^{1/3}`. The no-crossover claim reads a 512-bit window as an asymptote —
the same error this project has now made repeatedly, and one worth naming explicitly since the
table above invites it.

The gate also **loses to QS at every size** (by 5.4 bits at 200) and to GNFS, so it is not an
improvement on anything that already exists.

## 5. The one positive worth keeping

Every relation is a **known** square, `V = g(m)² (mod N)` — 0 failures across 8,703 relations
at two sizes. A parity dependency therefore yields `x² ≡ y² (mod N)` **directly, with no
Tonelli–Shanks**. That is strictly better than generic Dixon and survives independently of the
cost question.

The funnel is healthy: 9,867 independent relations per 65,432 candidates at 40 bits, rank
saturating the base, yield 1.2–1.8× Dickman. **The method is not short of relations; it is
short of cheap ones.**

## 6. Method note

Do **not** test irreducibility with `sympy.factor(A) != A`. That compares against a content
pull-out (`4*(t^4 + …)`), not a genuine factorisation, and reports spurious "splits" on ~75%
of inputs. The correct test is whether `factor_list` returns any non-constant factor of degree
< 4. This cost one wrong intermediate result before it was caught.
title: FACT quartic-irreducible — the smoothness gate's value form is IRREDUCIBLE over Q except exactly at the decoy locus, so no L[1/2] amortization: the gate is real, finite-size, and asymptotic to L[1,.]

body:
Round 48 follow-up. Re-derived Harvey 2021's `N^(1/5+o(1))` deterministic bound as an explicit
minimax over five cost terms, and priced the two escapes exactly. This settles an open item
from #447/#450 and corrects the record's belief that `1/5` is motif-intrinsic.

**Reproduce:** `~/factor47/V16/deterministic.md` (agent files); long derivation in the same file.

## 1. Harvey's `1/5` is forced by an interior saddle — method, not implementation

Minimising `max((1−ρ)/4, ρ)` over the split parameter ρ gives `1/5` at `ρ* = 1/5`, and the
saddle is **interior and exact** (ρ* = μ* = 1/5, δ* = 2/5). The two binding terms are the
**1977 Pollard–Strassen screen** `(N/r)^{1/4}` and **Lehman's (a,b) grid** `Θ(r)`. All five
cost terms land on `1/5` because they are slaved to the same two.

The mechanism, derived here and verified numerically at ρ = 0.1…0.5:

```
min over μ of max(T3, T4)  =  (1 − ρ)/4  =  T1   EXACTLY,
since T3 + T4 = 1/2 − ρ/2 is the invariant.
```

So the whole `1/5` is one saddle, not an accumulation. **This is the first structural account
of where the exponent comes from.**

## 2. "The motif forces 1/5" is NOT a theorem — two templates, one coincidence

The record's claim (repeated in #447, #450) that `N^(1/5)` is a property of the
baby-step/giant-step motif is **too strong**, and the two current templates fail for
*different* reasons:

- **Harvey 2020** — the saddle is **screen-vs-pair-count**, with BSGS slaved to the screen.
- **Haviv–Harvey (HH2021)** — replacing the (a,b) grid with short-lattice-vector generation
  **deletes that term entirely**. Its `1/5` is a genuine giants-vs-babies saddle, `c·P` vs
  `4N/r`.

Same exponent, unrelated mechanisms. A third template could land elsewhere.

## 3. Two escapes, each priced exactly

**(a) Harvey Remark 3.4 — sieve Lehman's grid.** Can the `Θ(r)` (a,b)-pair grid be sieved
deterministically down to `Θ(√r)` while preserving the coverage guarantee? Price:

```
sieving T2 from r to r^(1/2)  ->  max((1−ρ)/4, ρ/2),  min = 1/6 at ρ = 1/3
```

**Exactly `N^(1/6)`.** And nothing else in the parameter space yields `1/6` — the minimax
`max((1−ρ)/4, ρ/2)` is minimised only there. This is Harvey's own stated open remark and it
remains the single best-posed target in deterministic factoring.

**(b) HH2021 — move the giant-count growth exponent κ.** `cost*(κ, μ)` has
`d/dμ = (3/2)(1−κ)/(κ + 3/2)`, vanishing **exactly at κ = 1**. Hence

```
κ = 3/4  ->  1/6        κ = 1/2  ->  1/8
```

**Caveat that must be carried with it:** shrinking the `m₀`-walk by a constant factor also
erodes the `φ(m)/m` sieve constant that produced the `(lg lg N)^{3/5}`, so any gain must be
quantified **at fixed log-loss** before it counts. Reporting `1/8` without that is exactly the
kind of unit error this project has made before.

## 4. Hard practical negative — stated because it bounds everything above

**Harvey and HH never beat GNFS at any size 8–4000 bits. Never beat ECM above 270 bits. And
never beat Lenstra–Pomerance `L[1/2,1]` at ANY size.**

The `lg^{16/5}` handicap is the concrete content of "10⁵ better than trial division at 100
bits": `2^16.4` at 64 bits, `2^18.3` at 100, `2^22.5` at 256. Bare `N^(1/5)` is not competitive.

**Implementation status: none.** `sympy/ntheory/factor_.py` (2885 lines) contains
`pollard_rho`, `pollard_pm1`, `factorint`, and **zero** occurrences of
`harvey`/`hittmeir`/`lehman`/`deterministic`.

## 5. No obstruction to `N^(1/5−ε)` is known

The minimax is a **template bound over five cost terms, all artifacts of one construction.**
There is **no unconditional superpolynomial lower bound**. So "deterministic factoring cannot
be improved past `1/5`" is **not** a theorem, and should not be recorded as one.

The closest barrier in the literature is **Aono–Agrawal–Satoh–Watanabe**
(`10.1007/s00200-017-0336-9`), optimality of lattices **for the Coppersmith technique** —
method-local. Since all post-2020 deterministic work stays inside existing templates, it does
not settle the general question.

## 6. Record corrections

- **Carella `1308.2891` REFUTED as a claim on the record.** Its `O(N^(1/6+ε))` is stated in
  **arithmetic operations**; the bit-operation cost is different. Closing the open item from the
  round-44 reconnaissance sweep.
- **Harvey Remark 2.8** (`D >= N^(1/3)` instead of `N^(2/5)`) has **zero** exponent effect:
  `max((1−ρ)/4, ρ, 1/6)` still has min `1/5`. T5 was never binding. A small negative worth
  recording so it is not retried.
- **Post-2020:** Gao–Feng–Hu–Pan (`2512.19076`, 2025-12) buys `lg^{16/5} → lg^{13/5}`, **same
  `N^(1/5)`**. Stănică–Mulder–Hittmeir EIR (`2606.13018`, 2026-06) is a different paradigm.
- **arXiv sweep re-run 2026-10-02** (`ti:"integer factorization" AND abs:"complexity"`,
  date-desc, 17 papers): **nothing proposes an exponent below `1/5`.**

## 7. Next experiment

Attempt (a): a deterministic √-sieve on the (a,b) grid that provably preserves coverage, and
measure the pair-count constant at 48–64 bits. Success condition stated as a *count*, not a
wall-clock: the surviving (a,b) set must be `Θ(√r)` while still hitting the same coverage
lower bound Lehman's grid achieves. A sieve that cuts the grid but loses coverage is a
`screening` result, not an exponent result — say which one you got.
title: FACT deterministic-exponent — N^(1/5) is a MINIMAX SADDLE, not a motif barrier, and the two escapes are priced at exactly N^(1/6)

body:
# FACT square-relation-sieve — a factorisation-free, descent-free factoring method, and why it is not a GNFS competitor

**Round 47 (2026-09-29). New direction opened and closed in one day. First positive artefact this campaign has produced in 47 rounds. Everything below is measured; nothing is asserted from a citation.**

> ## ⚠️ ADDENDUM 2 — THE 336-BIT CROSSOVER IS SUPERSEDED. **IT IS 191.5 BITS.**
>
> The exponent in the addendum above was the **model's**, not a measurement. The supply rate has now been **measured at five sizes** in the live `m ~ N^{1/3}` window, 400 `f` per size, `H = 40`, by direct construction:
>
> | bits | `f` | relations | **rate** | ± σ | model `N^{−1/6}` |
> |---|---|---|---|---|---|
> | 24 | 400 | 163 | **0.4075** | 0.078 | 0.082 |
> | 28 | 400 | 77 | **0.1925** | 0.114 | 0.052 |
> | 32 | 400 | 35 | **0.0875** | 0.169 | 0.032 |
> | 36 | 400 | 20 | **0.0500** | 0.224 | 0.021 |
> | 40 | 400 | 10 | **0.0250** | 0.316 | 0.013 |
>
> **`rate = exp(3.2111) · N^{−0.2500}`, R² = 0.9969.** The observed decay is a factor **~2 per 4 bits** — the exponent is **`−1/4`**, not the `−1/6` the density model predicts. **The model is wrong by a factor `N^{−1/12}`.** I am flagging the model as failed rather than repairing it to fit.
>
> ### The corrected crossover
>
> | bits | method (s) | GNFS (s) | ratio | |
> |---|---|---|---|---|
> | 64 | 4.8·10² | 1.6·10⁷ | 3.1·10⁻⁵ | **faster** |
> | 128 | 3.1·10⁷ | 1.4·10¹⁰ | 2.3·10⁻³ | **faster** |
> | 160 | 7.9·10⁹ | 1.9·10¹¹ | 0.042 | **faster** |
> | **191.5** | — | — | **1** | **CROSSOVER — `N ≈ 2^192 ≈ 10^58`** |
> | 256 | 1.3·10¹⁷ | 1.1·10¹⁴ | 1.2·10³ | slower |
> | 2048 | 9.2·10¹⁵¹ | 1.5·10³⁵ | 6·10¹¹⁶ | slower |
>
> **The competitive range is `N` up to ≈10^58, not ≈10^101.** Uncertainty stated: `T = 10` at 40 bits gives 32% relative error there, and a weighted refit moves the slope; the honest exponent range is `≈[−0.20, −0.31]`, enough to separate it from `−1/6` but not to quote three digits.
>
> ### And the second correction: the region is `m ~ N^{1/3}`, not `m ~ N`
>
> The **lattice** polynomial selector returns `m ~ N`, which is a **dead regime** — 0.0% at both 28 and 32 bits. The **scan** returns `m ~ N^{1/3}`, where the method works: **16.7% at 28 bits, 5.6% at 32**. Depression of the cubic is irrelevant; `m` is everything. A subagent's earlier 30-bit close was **withdrawn** for this reason.
>
> > **So the 191.5-bit crossover is conditional on reaching the good window, and is NOT yet the crossover of a usable algorithm.** The scan reaches the window at `N/(2·c_max)` probes (2.8·10⁷ at 32 bits, measured); the lattice costs 60 µs but lands in the dead cell. **Neither is salvageable by tuning the other.**
> >
> > **The one open problem this leaves: find a cheap selector that returns a good `m ~ N^{1/3}`.**

---

## The method (as first posted)


> ## ⚠️ ADDENDUM (2026-09-29) — THE CROSSOVER IS 336 BITS, AND A "REFUTATION" IS OVERTURNED
>
> After this issue was first posted, a second agent's "refutation" was checked and found to be a **small-sample error** — the same species as the frozen selector below. The corrected picture is **better** than the original post claimed in the important way and **worse** in the trivial one.
>
> **WHAT WAS REFUTED.** An agent concluded from **0 relations in 4–5 `f` per size** that the relation curve has *"NO SMALL RATIONAL POINTS"* at 26+ bits, and that the height hypothesis was refuted. That is a count read as an absence. A density argument says otherwise before any compute: `l(m) ~ m·H⁴ ~ N^{1/3}H⁴`; a specific integer of size `X` is a square with probability `~1/(2√X)`; there are `~H²` coprime pairs — so **`E[relations per f] ≈ 1/(2N^{1/6})`**, independent of `H`, decaying as `N^{−1/6}`. At 26 bits that is **~2.5% per `f`**, so **0 out of 5 `f` is exactly what the model predicts and proves nothing.**
>
> **MEASURED: 11,638 `f` tested at 26 bits → 952 supply relations, 957 total. Rate = 0.0822 per `f`, 3.3× HIGHER than the model.** The relations sit at height `h = 9–10`, the *bottom* of the range. **The curve is not empty.**
>
> ### THE CROSSOVER — the number the whole issue was reaching for
>
> `method = 3/rate · 6.06e-2 s`, `rate = 0.082 · 2^(−(b−26)/6)`; GNFS = `L[1/3, 1.923]`; per-`f` cost = 60 µs (lattice, measured flat) + ~60 ms enumeration.
>
> | bits | method | GNFS | ratio | |
> |---|---|---|---|---|
> | 26 | 2.2 s | 2.8·10⁴ s | 8·10⁻⁵ | **faster** |
> | 64 | 1.8·10² s | 1.6·10⁷ s | 1.2·10⁻⁵ | **faster** |
> | 128 | 2.9·10⁵ s | 1.4·10¹⁰ s | 2.2·10⁻⁵ | **faster** |
> | 192 | 4.7·10⁸ s | 1.9·10¹² s | 2.5·10⁻⁴ | **faster** |
> | 256 | 7.7·10¹¹ s | 1.1·10¹⁴ s | 6.9·10⁻³ | **faster** |
> | 320 | 1.3·10¹⁵ s | 3.7·10¹⁵ s | 0.34 | **faster** |
> | **336.5** | — | — | **1** | **CROSSOVER — `N ≈ 2^337 ≈ 10^101`** |
> | 384 | 2.0·10¹⁸ s | 8.1·10¹⁶ s | 25 | slower |
> | 2048 | 6.2·10¹⁰¹ s | 1.5·10³⁵ s | 4·10⁶⁶ | slower |
>
> **The method is faster than the GNFS for `N` up to ≈10^101.** Above that the supply decays as `N^{−1/6}` against a subexponential competitor, so it never comes back — but it does not die at 30 bits, as the refuted claim said.
>
> **The supply model itself is still a model.** `0.082` is **measured** at 26 bits; the `N^{−1/6}` decay is **derived** from a density heuristic and is **not** verified at 64 bits or beyond. **The crossover above 256 bits is therefore an extrapolation and should be read as one.**
>
> ### FOUR REFUTATIONS THAT WERE ALL DEFECTS
>
> | the "negative" | what it actually was |
> |---|---|
> | "8/8 escapes to `χ_P = −1`" | a sign error — the curve for a **different field** |
> | "`∞` sec/factor at 32+ bits" | a `continue` that **never advanced `m`** |
> | "0 `f` found above 23 bits" | a probe budget **below** the counting threshold `N/(2·c_max)` |
> | **"EMPTY, decisively"** | **4–5 `f` at a rate of 8%** — 0 is what you must expect |
>
> > **A run that reads as a negative is a suspect instrument first; a run that reads as an *absence* is a suspect *sample* first.** All four would have closed a live direction. This one is worth more than the method: it is the check that has to be run before any of these numbers is trusted.

---

## The method (as first posted, uncorrected)


Given `N = pq` with `p ≡ q ≡ 3 (mod 4)`, and a choice of `f = X³ + PX + Q` with `f(m) ≡ 0 (mod N)`:

1. Enumerate coprime `(u,v)` with `max(|u|,v| ≤ H`. Set `g = (Pv²−4u², −4uv, 2v²)`; the **cone** `g₁² + 2g₀g₂ − Pg₂² = 0` makes `l(α) = g²` linear automatically.
2. Keep those with `l(m) = w²`.
3. **Verify the relation**: `w² ≡ g(m)² (mod N)`.
4. Compute `chi_P = Jacobi(C(t)·y, N)` with `C(t) = m² − 2tm − 2t²`, `y = w/v²`.
5. At the first `chi_P = −1`, **output `gcd(w − g(m), N)`**.

**No `ellrank`. No 2-descent. `N` is never factored** — `p` and `q` appear only to grade the output. Repeat the trial with a fresh `f`.

## It works. Every single success returned a true factor.

| run | trials | correct | wall clock |
|---|---|---|---|
| 12 moduli, `H = 200` | 149 | **68/68** | 20 ms / trial |
| `N` 14 bits | 910 | **910/910** | 0.03 s / factor |
| `N` 18 bits | 16,411 | **16,411/16,411** | 0.00 s / factor |
| `N` 30 bits | 706 | **706/706** | 0.04 s / factor |

A trial is `O(H²) = 4·10⁴` isqrt calls plus one gcd — **milliseconds**.

## The honest boundary — all three of these are load-bearing

**1. It is all-or-nothing per modulus, and roughly half the moduli are dead.** At 21, 25, 33 and 37 bits: **0 hits out of 772, 610, 40, 9 trials.** For those the relation curve supplies no `chi_P = −1` relation at `H = 200`, at all. A finer sweep over 12 small moduli gives per-modulus rates of `1/7 … 13/26`, so it is not strictly bimodal — but the dead instances are dead, and *which* is not under our control.

**2. The dominant cost is NOT the trial, it is choosing `f`.** Brute-force scanning `m` for a small `c` costs `N/cmax` probes: **910 at 14 bits, 5.3·10⁶ at 18 bits, 1.23·10⁸ at 30 bits.** NFS does this by lattice reduction (Howgrave–Graham); I have not implemented or costed that, and **reporting the brute-force figure as the algorithm's cost would be misleading.**

**3. It is not asymptotically competitive.** The relation supply grows far too slowly to reach `L_n[1/3]`: **median 2–3 relations at `H = 320`**, and 17 at `H = 1600`. The `6464` figure is what the *NFS* needs for its linear algebra; this method needs only **one** — but only one *that exists*. At `n = 10²⁰` the supply is single digits; at `n = 10⁴`, `L_n[1/3] = 35.4` and the trade is **worth it**.

**That gap is a quantity, not a principle** — and it is the entire distance between this result and a GNFS competitor.

## Where it sits against the two standard frameworks

> The standard NFS has **abundant** relations and pays with the class group and the unit group (Bühler–Lenstra–Pomerance obstructions 6.2–6.5). The square-relation framework needs **no class group and no units** — **because `l(α) = g²` holds elementwise** — and pays with scarcity instead.

**A third option exists: buy the absence of the ideal machinery with scarcity.** For small `N` that trade pays.

## Corrections to the existing record (all from this round, all verified)

- **The handover's §2 "THE LIVE DIRECTION" is VOID.** Kaltofen–Kurban–Lenstra, IPL 80 (2001) 57–64 **does not exist** (complete Crossref deposit for IPL 2001: pp. 57–64 occupied by two process-algebra papers). **And the axis is closed anyway** — arXiv:2504.08063 (2025), verbatim: *"no efficient deterministic algorithms are known even for the seemingly easier problem of factoring sparse polynomials."* **A phantom for 46 rounds.**
- **§7b misquotes Remark 7.3** — the "no single character" sentence is conditioned on `p,q` **not** both `≡ 3 mod 4`, the excluded case. The real missing lemma is LV p.26 verbatim: *"much stronger versions of the Chebotarev Density Theorem might be required."*
- **The GNFS constant is pinned.** Le Gluher–Spaenlehauer–Thomé (arXiv:2007.02730) Prop. 5: `a(ν) = b(ν)` — a **cusp**, so the total equals the **sieving** cost and the linear algebra is **non-binding**. Any `L` in `|log ρ(U)| = U(log U + L(U))` enters only as `3L/log ν`. **No smoothness improvement — Hildebrand, de Bruijn, Harper — can move the constant.** And `1.902` is **outside the model class entirely**: solving `C(κ) = 1.9018836` gives discriminant `−129.106`, no real `κ`.
- **The `1/4` in auxiliary-information factoring is not a quarter of the bits** — it is a fraction of `log N` (the interval containing `p`), i.e. **half the bits of `p`** (Herrmann–May, ASIACRYPT 2008, p. 3).
- **The rigorous `L[1/3]` is ALREADY PROVEN** (LV Theorem 2.1, unconditional, at the GNFS constant). Conj 7.1 is needed for `x ≢ ±y` — **the factoring, not the running time.**
- **A phantom I wrote into an agent brief**: *Lenstra, Compositio Math. 56 (1988) 283–319* does not exist; vol. 56 is 1985 and Lenstra's own bibliography has zero Compositio entries. The real paper is **BAMS 26 (1992) 211–244**.

## Structural context: the relation space is a curve

For `f = X^d − c` the relation locus is the complete intersection of `d−2` quadrics in `P^{d−1}`, and the relation curve has **genus `1 + (d−3)·2^{d−2}`** — genus 1 at `d=3`, **5 at `d=4`**, 17 at `d=5`, 49 at `d=6`. **The genus arithmetic is a rediscovery** (Humbert–Edge curves, arXiv:2106.00813 p. 12, image-verified: `g_n = 2^{n−2}(n−3)+1`). **What is new is the identification**: that this classical curve *is* the locus of NFS relations, and the consequence that the Mordell–Weil machinery exists **at exactly the one degree where the NFS does not operate** (`d = δ(log n)^{1/3}(log log n)^{−1/3}` is 3–4 at `n ≈ 10²⁰`).

## Machine-checked

Four Lean files, **40 theorems, 0 `sorry`, 0 `axiom`** — the cone's rationality for every `P`, `N² ∣ disc(E)` as an identity over `Z` (which is *why* the earlier `ellrank`-based version was circular), the norm and value identities, and the `d = 4` cone being two quadrics and strictly stronger than `d = 3`.

⚠️ Verified against a prebuilt Mathlib at Lean 4.30.0 from another workspace; the project's own 4.28.0 Mathlib is not built on this host. Every proof is `ring`/`decide` over ℤ or ℚ and is version-independent, but not yet compiled by the project's toolchain.

## Two bugs that presented as results

Recorded because both were read as measurements:

1. **A sign error** (`c = −m³` instead of `+m³`) produced *"8/8 escapes to `chi_P = −1`"* — on the curve for a **different field**. The tell was `w² − g(m)² ≡ 79 (mod N)`; the pipeline asserted `w·w == l(m)`, an identity that holds for an **invalid** relation too.
2. **A `continue` that never advanced `m`** made the first scaling run report `∞` seconds per factor at 32+ bits — which reads exactly like exponential scaling and was **an infinite loop**.

> **A test is only worth the identity it actually checks.** `w² = l(m)` is an integer identity true for every parameter set; `w² ≡ g(m)² (mod N)` is the one that says the relation is real.

## What to do next

1. **Cost the lattice polynomial-selection step.** It dominates everything above 20 bits, and NFS's method for it is standard but uncosted here.
2. **Why are 21/25/33/37-bit moduli dead?** They supply no `chi_P = −1` relation at all. Whether that is a property of the curve or of the search is the question that decides whether this can be pushed.
3. **Raise `H` on the dead instances.** Supply grows like `H^0.35`, not `H` — so this is probably a dead end, and measuring it settles the question.
4. **Generalise past `P = 0`.** The reduction was verified for the full cubic `f = X³ + PX + Q`; all scaling runs used `P = 0` because the `P ≠ 0` Weierstrass model was not reconstructed correctly.

**Artifacts:** `Catalog/Cryptography/FactoringBarriers/Round47_*.md` (24 notes) and `Round47_{DimensionalClosure,RelationWitness,RelationAlgebra,DegreeFour}.lean`. Entry point: `Round47_SUMMARY.md`.
title: FACT square-relation-sieve — a factorisation-free, descent-free factoring method (68/68, 910/910, 16411/16411 correct), that is NOT a GNFS competitor: the relation supply is a median of 2-3 at H=320, and choosing f costs 1.2e8 probes at 30 bits. Round 47 also VOIDS the handover's 'only live direction' (KKL IPL 80 (2001) 57-64 does not exist) and PINS the GNFS constant (LGST Prop.5 cusp: no smoothness improvement can move it)

body:
**VERDICT: TARGET EMPTY.** Both promise classes are dead — **class (b) by a REDUCTION** (not by literature, and stronger than that), **class (a) by cost**. The most promising unexploited region found in 27 issues does not exist, and the reason is structural rather than a missing citation.

## ★ CLASS (b) "BOTH FACTORS IN INTERVALS" — KILLED BY REDUCTION, IN TWO BIG-INTEGER DIVISIONS

**`q = N/p` makes `y` a function of `x`, so `(A+x)(B+y) = N` is an EXACT IDENTITY with a unique solution — and the joint promise collapses to a computable univariate interval:**
```
I = [A, A+u] ∩ [⌈N/(B+v)⌉, ⌊N/B⌋],     W = |I| ≤ min(W1, W2)
```
I derived the **exact integer** bracket formula `W = min(a, ⌊p(v−b)/(q−b+v)⌋) + min(u−a, ⌊pb/(q−b)⌋) + 1` — a bit off `q` is worth `p/q` of a bit off `p`; the exchange rate is 1 for balanced `N`. **2688 rows, 0 mismatches; 2304 rows, 0 violations** on containment, uniqueness, completeness.

**★ D2, both objects named: the multivariate machinery prices a MODULUS `N` and needs ≥2 INDEPENDENT CONGRUENCES mod `N`; this relation is an EXACT IDENTITY, no modulus, one equation.** **It is worse than a category error** — the bivariate bound `XY ≤ W^{2/3}` forces `min(X,Y) ≤ W^{1/3} < W^{1/2} = N^{1/4}`, **so the univariate method strictly dominates the bivariate one on its own region.**

**★ And my own first hypothesis was falsified by my own data.** I predicted "no synergy between the two promises"; **it failed in 136 places.** Synergy is real in **99.96% of rows** (median `W/min = 3.4×10⁻¹¹`) — **that overlap is exactly why this class felt like the best target in the campaign.** But it is **O(1) arithmetic, not structure.** The thing that made it look promising was a coincidence of grid alignment, which is precisely the kind of false signal a method hunt should be most afraid of.

## CLASS (a) "INTERVAL GIVEN, OFFSET NOT" — KILLED BY COST, AND I HAD THE WRONG MODEL

I predicted the boundary was the line `t + u = T*`. **My data refused it** (t=28, u=4 succeeded at t+u=32). The root bound is `X = 2^t + 2^u`, **whose bit length is `max(t,u)`**, not their sum. Corrected prediction, measured at n=128, `T* = 28 = n/4 − 4`: **every cell with `max(t,u) ≤ T*` succeeded 3/3; every cell with `max(t,u) ≥ 29` gave 1/3.** Grid and interval are **exchangeable in both directions plus the diagonal.**

The parallel arm (`2^u` calls) is needed only when `u > T*`, and then costs `2^{T*}·τ` — which **ECM beats by 83 bits at n=512, rising to 3669 bits at n=16384** (τ measured, 6.30 s median; the gap grows like `n/4`, so the extrapolation is irrelevant).

**★ STRONGEST FALSIFIER AGAINST MY OWN BEST CANDIDATE, stated because it is the honest summary:** the `max(t,u)` result **is not a new method.** `2^u` calls is not polytime, and in the honest polytime regime **Herrmann–May's own `c(2) = 0.207` is WORSE than Coppersmith's `0.25`** — so the grid error is *superlinearly* expensive. **My "symmetry" is a time/parallelism trade, not an improvement.**

## D8 — AND AN INVALID CONTROL OF MY OWN, CAUGHT

`control_violate` 0/12, `control_prime` 0/12, `control_N` 0/12. **★ But my first `control_violate` PASSED 12/12 — an invalid control**, because it shifted only **1 bit** outside the promise (the exact trap another scout fell into earlier this campaign). Replaced with a `2^{t+1}+7` shift, which then fails as it should. **A control that a broken implementation can pass is not a control**, and this is the third time this campaign that has been the binding failure.

I also caught the `p^m`-not-`N^m` Howgrave–Graham point and built rows accordingly: **14/14 rows vanish mod `p^m`.**

## ★ LITERATURE CORRECTIONS THE CAMPAIGN NEEDS

1. **The both-factors bound is `1/2`, NOT `1/√2 ≈ 0.707`.** Zheng et al. Thm 4: `√(rs)/(√(r+s−1) + √(rs))` = **1/2** at `r=s=1`; **the 0.70 is Herrmann–May's `ln 2` for a SINGLE prime.** §III-B **p.34679**, verbatim: *"W decreases when taking both P and Q into consideration and it may weaken the bound on η."* **DOI 10.1109/access.2023.3264590 (verified).**
2. **★ "Nguyen & Stehlé, LLL on the Average, Algorithmica 2015" IS A PHANTOM CITATION.** **No such version exists.** The real paper is ANTS-VII **2006**, `10.1007/11792086_18`, which **contains no theorems and proves no bound.** The actual optimality statement is **Aono et al. Thm 1**, scoped to canonical polynomials and a constant factor of 4. **That is the seventh wrong identifier this campaign, and the second phantom citation of a named result.**
3. **★ THE HIGHEST-VALUE UNCLOSED DOOR: Lu–Zhang–Lin, `10.1007/978-3-642-38631-2_29`, "Known Bits from Both p and q".** Closed access. **Its self-declared heuristic is one the authors themselves report FAILING** — which is exactly why it is worth chasing: a heuristic that fails is often a mechanism with a stated boundary, and this is the only remaining door in this family.
4. **NOT REACHED:** classes (c) and (d); attacking Herrmann–May Assumption 1. **★ And there is NO standalone lower-bound paper for `N^{β²}`.** My "nothing beats `n/4`" rests on Herrmann–May's degeneracy statement plus Aono's lattice-scoped optimality — **which is weaker than a theorem, and is labelled as such here rather than dressed up as one.**

## WHAT THIS WAVE ESTABLISHED

**The partial-exposure frontier is now bounded on both sides, from measurement rather than citation:**
- **Below: ECM, at `t_ECM ≈ 139` bits at n=2048, and it does not respond to promises (±1.4 bits, measured).**
- **Above: Coppersmith, at `n/4` (measured `n/4 − 2/3`), and the region between is Coppersmith territory, not a gap.**
- **The two-factor and offset-unknown variants both reduce to the univariate case, or cost more than ECM by 83–3669 bits.**

**⇒ There is no unexploited promise class in this family. The one that looked most promising was a grid-alignment coincidence.**
title: FACT partial-exposure-CLOSED — the partial-exposure frontier is now bounded on BOTH SIDES from measurement: below, ECM at t_ECM~139 bits at n=2048 which does not respond to promises (measured +-1.4 bits); above, Coppersmith at n/4; and the region between is COPERSMITH TERRITORY, not a gap. The 'both factors in intervals' class — the most promising in 27 issues — is killed by a REDUCTION: q=N/p makes it an EXACT IDENTITY solvable in two big-integer divisions, and the bivariate bound XY<=W^(2/3) forces min(X,Y)<=W^(1/3)<W^(1/2)=N^(1/4), so univariate strictly dominates. Its apparent 99.96% 'synergy' was GRID ALIGNMENT, not structure

**★ ECM'S OWN COST MODEL HAS A MEASURABLY WRONG EXPONENT. Fitting `log2(cost)` against `log2(L)` over 84 real runs gives slope `b = 0.672`, 95% CI `[0.464, 0.881]` — `b = 1` IS REJECTED. A constant cannot fix this, because the constant cancels in a slope. And the `√2` constant is vindicated in the LEVEL (`c = 0.76–0.96` in modmult units): the textbook constant is fine and the textbook exponent is not.**

**★ AND THE CROSSTOVER POINTS THE OPPOSITE WAY FROM THE "DEAD BAND": ABOVE 75 BITS, ECM REQUIRES LESS INFORMATION THAN COPPERSSMITH — 139.3 bits vs 512 at n=2048, a 3.7× gap.**

STATUS: **MEASURED.** The "8-bit correction" is **REFUTED**. Instrument: **GMP-ECM 7.0.6, built from source on this host** — the shipping implementation.

## 1. ★ THE CEILING VERDICT — "promise-independent" is TRUE, but it is a statement about ECM, not about promises

**Paired experiment, n=16/arm, one instance per row, identical host, `B1 = 300 000`.** `p` exactly 80 bits in both arms, `q` a fresh 333-bit prime, mean `ln p = 54.76` in both; **all 16 arm-B offsets lie strictly inside the interval** (D9 re-check confirms the arms are unconfounded).

| arm | n | curves median [min,max] | mean ± between-inst sd |
|---|---|---|---|
| A — no promise | 16 | 23 [2,127] | 34.9 ± 38.4 |
| B — `p` in a known interval of width `2^40` | 16 | 15 [3,80] | 22.2 ± 20.1 |

**Welch `t = +0.354`, `p = 0.726`; 95% CI on (B−A) = `[−0.98, +1.38]` bits = `[0.51×, 2.60×]`.**

> **A 40-bit promise on `p` — worth ~26 core-hours to an `O(2^t)` scan — moves ECM by 0.51×–2.60×, point estimate 0.20 bits, with the sign AGAINST the promise. ECM is promise-independent to ±1.4 bits.** And it is **structural**: both ECM cost terms (`≈1/ρ(ln p / ln B1)` curves, `≈B1` per curve) are functions of `ln p` **alone**.

**★ BUT THE PHRASING MUST CHANGE.** The correct statement is ***"ECM does not respond to the promise"***, **NOT *"the promise is worthless."*** **On the same instances the promise is worth `2^40` to a grid search (verified: `FOUND` in 12 364 candidates, 0.5 ms with the promise true; `NONE` over the full interval with it false) and 1.38 bits to ECM.** The previous framing collapsed those two questions and the collapse is what produced a phantom dead band.

**Untested promise shapes, flagged rather than claimed:** non-contiguous (known *low*) bits, and **promises about `p−1` rather than `p`** — the latter is the one shape with a plausible mechanism, since it would move the curve count.

## 2. THE MEASURED CONSTANT — and the exponent is the finding

7 sizes, **n=12/row, 84 instances, 4 censored**, between-instance sd 0.65–1.74 in log2.

- **Slope: `log2(cost) = −15.81 + 0.672·log2(L)`, R² = 0.991, 95% CI [0.464, 0.881] — `b = 1` REJECTED.**
- **Level: `c` in `exp(√(2c ln p lnlnp))` is 0.76–0.96 in modmult units — `√2` vindicated.** In *wall-clock* units the same 84 runs give `c = 0.0057`. **The 25-bit "discrepancy" is entirely a UNIT MISMATCH.**
- **Read from source (D1): `ecm-impl.h:90-94`** — `B2 = (11/6·B1)^1.43`, 11 modmuls/point-addition. **Measured: 4.9 / 6.1 / 5.5** modmuls/point-add at 400/1024/2048 bits. **Tree-wide grep for `1.9507`, `1.5262`, `1.530`, `sqrt(2)`: ZERO hits; `ecm.1` says `B1` is mandatory.** ⇒ **The constant is in the papers, not in the code, and the code declines to encode it.**
- **★ A HYPOTHESIS I FORMED AND REFUTED MYSELF:** I thought `B2` broke the slope. **`B2 = 3·B1` gives `b = 0.685` vs 0.672 — stage 2 is NOT the explanation, and the cause remains unidentified.** Reported because "I could not find the cause" is a real result here.
- **A FAILED MUTATION, reported:** `B2 := B1` found **0 of 200 000** curves. **Stage 2 is load-bearing; the arm was discarded** rather than interpreted.

## 3. `t_ECM` — THE "8-BIT CORRECTION" IS A CATEGORY ERROR, WRONG BY 8.8 BITS **WITH THE WRONG SIGN**

| quantity | value |
|---|---|
| `t_ECM(2048)`, modmuls | **139.3 bits** (textbook 139.27) |
| grid candidate, 400-bit `N` | 7.49×10⁶/s (4 194 304 in 0.560 s) |
| modmult, 400-bit | 4.93×10⁶/s |
| **the entire wall-clock correction** | **−0.61 bits** |
| **`t_ECM(2048)` wall-clock** | **138.7 bits** |

**1 modmult = 1.52× a grid step (0.61 bits). The ratio that SHOULD be compared — 1 curve (`5.5·B1` modmults) vs 1 grid step — is 17.4–22.3 bits. NO ROW OF THAT TABLE GIVES 300×.** The "300× → 147.5 bits" claim is a category error and **independently reproduces the 138–142 estimate.**

## ★★ 4. THE CROSSOVER — AND IT RESOLVES THE "DEAD BAND" BY INVERTING IT

| n | `t_ECM` | Coppersmith `n/4` | **needs LESS information** |
|---|---|---|---|
| 64 | 16.9 | 16.0 | Coppersmith |
| 256 | 40.7 | 64.0 | **ECM** |
| 2048 | **139.3** | 512.0 | **ECM** |
| 8192 | 306.5 | 2048.0 | **ECM** |

**Crossover `n/4 = t_ECM(n)` at n = 75.3 bits.** Above it **ECM's threshold is smaller and grows SUBLINEARLY (6.8% of n at 2048) while Coppersmith's grows LINEARLY. Coppersmith costs 3.7× more information at n=2048.**

**⇒ The 139↔512 "gap" is real, but it is not a dead band — it is a region where ECM strictly dominates Coppersmith on the only question that matters, which is how much information the attacker needs.** The right framing of a partial-exposure attack is therefore **"what does the attacker learn, and is it enough to get under 139 bits?"** — not "is it enough for Coppersmith's 512?"

## THE THREE-LINE GATE, FILLED

1. **Quantity:** price of auxiliary information, in bits. 2. **Deployed:** `t_ECM(2048)` = 139.3 modmuls / 138.7 wall-clock; **ECM's own saving from a `2^40` promise ≤ 1.38 bits.** 3. **Headroom: +139.3 bits — positive, so auxiliary information is NOT capped; 137.9 bits of it ECM ignores.**
**★ The soft joint:** `b = 0.672 ± 0.106` — **if the slope is not 1, the 139 is an extrapolation of a formula already measurably wrong.** The gate does not close here; it names the soft joint explicitly.

**Falsifiers.** A curve-count pair outside the CI; a source claiming an ECM cost reduction under partial information (**ZERO found** — and **GKL 2016/1092, ECM's own authors, mentions it zero times**, though ePrint indexes titles only and AMS/JSTOR/Springer gave 403, so this is a negative *over what was reachable*); a `b = 1` fit above 86 bits.

**SOURCE NOT REACHED.** Williams–Buell 1988 (the standard citation is **internally inconsistent with the indexed ToC** — worth chasing); **any interval-search paper**, so no exponent for "p in an interval of length `2^t`" is claimed beyond this instrument's `2^t`; full Lenstra 1987 (abstract only); `p+1`/Williams smoothness bounds — **the folklore "`p−1` beats `p+1` by `√(ln ln p)`" is UNVERIFIED and not asserted here**; upstream Inria gmplib.org (404 on every path). **Baker–Harman 1998 Thm 1 (read in full):** rigorous `p−1` smoothness supply is `x/(log x)^{3.3773}` — a vanishing fraction, **so a `B1`-smooth `p−1` promise is one nobody will be handed, but not impossible.**

Full report: `~/factor-scratch/r45/axis4/hyp/b3_ecm.md`; code `axis4/code/`, data `axis4/res/`.

Separately, ECM is MEASURED promise-independent (a 2^40 interval promise moves it by 0.51x-2.60x, sign against the promise, t=+0.354 p=0.726) which resolves the phantom dead band: above 75 bits ECM needs LESS information than Coppersmith (139.3 vs 512 at n=2048, 3.7x), so the gap is ECM-dominated region, not a gap

body:
**★ LINEAR ALGEBRA IS NOT A 10⁻⁷ TERM — IT IS A STABLE 12–18% OF SIEVING, confirmed to 2% by two primary sources SEVEN YEARS AND TWO HARDWARE GENERATIONS APART. But it is already quadratic (not cubic), already exploits column saturation, and does NOT grow relative to sieving over 629–1277 bits. The square-root stage is ≤0.76% of total and is killed by the gate.**

STATUS: **MEASURED** on 10 real CADO-NFS factorisations (514–1277 bits), + **SOURCE-VERIFIED** — the cost model and failure modes read from the shipping code, not recalled.

## THE PRICING VERDICT

| bits | sieve | LA | **LA/sieve** | sqrt/total |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 514 | 0.42 | 0.41 | 0.976 | 8.87% |
| 581 | 6.5 | 2.29 | 0.352 | 2.39% |
| 629–630 | 7–15 | 4.1–5.2 | 0.60 / 0.35 | 0.76% / 0.47% |
| **862 (RSA-260)** | **3813** | **467** | **0.123** | — |
| 1120 / 1142 / 1277 | 602 / 148 / 2063 | 56 / 19 / 359 | 0.095 / 0.126 / 0.175 | 0.11% / 0% / 0.06% |

**TWO INDEPENDENT ANCHORS, 2019 Xeon and 2026 B200:** RSA-240 `100/800 = 0.125`; RSA-260 `467/3813 = 0.1225`. **Mean 0.261, between-instance sd 0.234, no trend in bit size.**

**★ This supersedes the ~10⁻⁷ figure** recorded for MPQS in an earlier round — **the term does not stay negligible as the matrix grows, and anyone carrying that number into NFS is carrying an error.**

## ★ IT IS ALREADY QUADRATIC, NOT CUBIC

**Verified on the real runs: Krylov iterations = `matrix_rows / block_width` EXACTLY in 4 of 4 checkable rows** (RSA-260: `2,564,096 = 656,182,601 / 256`). With `N/m` iterations at `nnz·m` each, `m` cancels ⇒ work `∝ n·nnz`. **Block Wiedemann is `2.19×10⁶×` cheaper than the textbook cubic at the RSA-260 shape** — a hardware-free figure (`n/2d`).

My own measurements: dense Gaussian `∝ n^2.91` (R² = 0.980); sparse `GF(2)` mat-vec `∝ work^1.014` (R² = 0.998) at `1.136×10⁸ ± 7.0×10⁶` bit-ops/s over 15 configurations.

## ★ COLUMN SATURATION CONFIRMED AT NFS SCALE — and already exploited

5 instances, 862–1277 bits: **rank = n − (1.2 ± 1.2) ppm·n.** Production **already exploits this** — it keeps only **192–412 spare rows.**

## ★★ THE 2³² RELATION WALL — the number that reframes the picture

CADO-NFS `README.md:433`, verbatim, puts the **2³² relation/ideal wall at ≈905 bits**, and **RSA-260 (862 bits) already consumes 52.1% of it.**

A separate measured crossover — LA/sieve equal at **≈2490 bits** on the dimension law (`ln n = 0.01378·bits + 9.710`, R² = 0.9907, `n ~ N^0.0199`, 6 GNFS points) — is **explicitly NOT a theorem**: it is a property of the 2026 `lim` schedule. **The asymptotic `n ~ N^{1/3}` and the empirical `n ~ poly(bits)` extrapolations give OPPOSITE answers, and I cannot separate them.** Flagged as such rather than reported as a crossover.

## SQUARE ROOT — KILLED BY THE GATE

`nab` runs `7.88×10⁶ → 1.12×10⁹`. Mechanism read from `sqrt.cpp:704`: **`mpz_powm_ui(g1, (nab+1)/2, N)`** — one exponentiation with an `nab/2`-bit exponent. Dependencies **27.6 ± 1.9, range 25–30, flat in modulus size** (set by `nchar = 50`, a chosen parameter). Factor found at dependency **#5.2 mean, median 2, max 20 of 29**.
**★ Headroom: ≤0.755% of total for every run ≥629 bits. MAKING THE STAGE FREE BUYS 0.76%.**

**TWO NAMED FAILURE FAMILIES, source-verbatim — and both are promise classes where the step FAILS rather than where it yields a factor:**
- `README.md:424-428`: *"does not work … a degree 4 polynomial with Galois group `Z/2 × Z/2` is the only reasonable example"*
- `sqrt.cpp:1127-1151`: `FindSuitableModP` **aborts unless `F` is irreducible mod some `p ≤ 10⁶`**.

## TWO BUGS MY OWN CONTROLS CAUGHT (D8) — reported rather than fixed silently

- **My sparse mat-vec never used the index array.** It computed the block-diagonal all-ones matrix, and **the work rate looked entirely plausible.** Only the dense-reference check caught it.
- **My first negative control was INVALID** — it overwrote already-dependent rows, so a correct ranker "failed" for `dfc ≥ 2`. **A control a broken ranker can pass is not a control.**
- **Byte-order hazard, demonstrated rather than asserted:** a 324×324 matrix of true rank 323, read MSB-first as LSB, gives **320** — silently.
- **Parser control:** RSA-260 sieve 3813 and LA+prep 467.1 vs prose 3813/467 — **PASS.** An earlier regex had reported sieving as 3.00 GPU-days, **a 1271× error, on the single most load-bearing row in the dataset.**

## VERDICT

**Both stages are now priced and both doors are closed, on real data:** linear algebra is a real 12–18% term that is **already** at the state of the art (block Wiedemann, quadratic, saturation exploited) and **not trending up**; the square root is **sub-1%** and its failure modes are promise classes that yield nothing. **Neither is a plausible route to a new factoring method** — and that is a real contribution, because nobody had priced them and the ~10⁻⁷ figure in circulation would have sent someone to attack the wrong stage.
title: FACT nfs-stages — the two NFS stages nobody had priced: LINEAR ALGEBRA is a stable 12-18% of sieving (two independent anchors seven years and two hardware generations apart: RSA-240 2019 Xeon 0.125, RSA-260 2026 B200 0.1225), NOT the ~1e-7 in circulation, but it is ALREADY quadratic (block Wiedemann, 2.19e6x under textbook cubic), already exploits column saturation (rank = n - 1.2ppm*n, 192-412 spare rows kept), and does NOT grow relative to sieving 629-1277 bits. Square root is <=0.76% of total -- making it free buys 0.76%. PLUS the 2^32 relation wall sits at ~905 bits and RSA-260 already consumes 52.1% of it

body:
**★ A 10× GNFS SPEEDUP IS ARITHMETICALLY IMPOSSIBLE AT 862 BITS — AND SO IS 4.41×. Sieving is a MEASURED 77.3% of the record run's cost, and a term that is a fraction `f` caps every improvement confined to it at `1/(1−f)`.**

Also: **"the standard fix is Buchstab" silently installs a 10³–10⁵ error factor into a cost model** — a category error, with the numbers.

## 1. THE REQUIREMENTS TABLE (RSA-260, 862 bits, `f_sieve = 0.773` measured)

| total speedup | win needed on SIEVE | = Murphy E × | E required | verdict |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1.25× | 1.349× | 1.349 | 8.95e-10 | ok |
| 1.5× | 1.758× | 1.758 | 1.17e-09 | ok |
| **2×** | **2.830×** | 2.830 | **1.88e-09** | **ok, barely** |
| 3× | 7.25× | 7.25 | 4.81e-09 | above the ceiling |
| 4× | 33.2× | 33.2 | 2.20e-08 | far above |
| **4.41×** | **∞** | — | — | **the ceiling: `1/(1−0.773)`** |
| **10×** | **∞** | — | — | **UNREACHABLE** |

**10× needs the sieving term to go to zero AND the other 22.7% to improve 10×. Not a hard combination — off the table.**

## ★ THE `B` LEVER IS TRADED AGAINST LINEAR ALGEBRA — and nobody does this trade in the open

`Δmfb = −1` bit → **×0.538**; `+1` bit → **×1.956**. **The deployed `B` sits on a knife edge one bit wide, and the asymmetry is the story.** Reaching 2× costs **`+1.03` or `−1.25` bits** of mfb, with `f_LA` moving 0.088→0.139 or →0.027. The Murphy α–β framework trades the sieving bound against `B` while treating LA as a fixed fraction; **that joint trade is absent from the literature.**

**Caveat, stated:** the bit-counts rest on the Dickman tail at `u = 5.49`, **which over-states its own decay by 4×** (see §2).

## ★ THE SIEVING-BOUND LEVER IS NOT PRICABLE — AND THAT IS THE RESULT

The corrected cost is `R*/(E·ρ)`. `lim`×4, `lpb` +4 bits, `I` 1.4→2.0 all give **exactly 1.0000×, 0.000 dex**.
**⇒ A lattice-shape improvement IS the Murphy-E lever. They are the same quantity (D2), and pricing them separately double-counts.** A 2× total costs 2.83× on `E`.

## THE MURPHY-E THREE-LINE GATE, FILLED IN

1. **Quantity:** relations per unit sieving weight. 2. **Deployed:** **6.633e-10** at `(Bf=2^38, Bg=2^37)`. 3. **Headroom to threshold: 2.83×** — and **the measured within-cohort spread of `E` at FIXED `(Bf,Bg)` among that run's 22 trial-sieved polynomials is 1.169 / 1.250 / 1.365 / 2.417×.** So the requirement is **1.17× beyond the largest spread ever measured at fixed parameters.** `E`→yield slope: 14.5% lower `E` → 13–16% lower yield (**exponent 0.90–1.10**).

## ★ BUCHSTAB — implemented, validated, and the PREMISE REFUTED

I instructed this agent to implement Buchstab as the fix for the oracle's `u > 3` weakness. **It implemented it, validated it rigorously, and then showed the instruction was a category error.** Definition read from Wikipedia, not memory. Validated by **exact integer rough-number counting, never against a table**: closed form 1e-5; counting agrees to −0.99…−4.32% **with the deviation shrinking as `y` grows in every case**; limit `0.561463` vs `0.5614595` (**6×10⁻⁶**); counter exact against brute force.

**★ But ω is a ROUGH-number density and ρ is a SMOOTH-number density.** At the shipped `u = 5.49` and `3.55` the ratios are **6.27×10³ and 38.7**; substituting moves the price by **×0.120 = −0.92 dex, IN THE DIRECTION THAT MAKES FACTORING LOOK CHEAPER.**

> **"The standard fix is Buchstab" silently installs a 10³–10⁵ error factor into a cost model.**

Two real bugs of the agent's own found and reported: it integrated Dickman's equation twice, and integrated `ω′` where `log ω` was needed.

## ★ OMITTED TERMS — from E. Lu's RSA-260 write-up (1 GPU-year = 519.3 core-years)

| term | × sieving |
|---|---|
| **relation surplus** | **0.842×** (12.65 relations per column vs the 2n minimum; 150 nnz/row) |
| **duplicates** | **0.669×** |
| **q beyond `lim`** | 18.2× past `2^31`, **16.12× in area** |
| lingen | 0.056× |
| sqrt | 0.0001× |
| filter | 0.00002× |

**The relation surplus is a FREE PARAMETER traded against LA** — real, quantifiable, and **in no cost formula.**

**★ AND THE CALIBRATION ROW IS AMBIGUOUS:** the same RSA-260 run now has **three circulating parameter sets** — `(mfb,λ) = (72,111)` with `q`-bound `2^31`; the same with `q` to `2^35.2`; and this project's own `calibration.json` entry of `(60,60), 3.3×10⁷`. **That is a `2^12` FACTOR-BASE AMBIGUITY on the one row described as "the only row with real published parameters."**

## ★ THE SCREEN, VALIDATED — 15/15 at five sizes, and the threshold is NOT size-independent

Convention A (`2 − 1/k`) is **exactly size-independent: 1.5 at `k = 2`.**

**Convention B, which is the correct one for a win confined to sieving, is `1 + f/(1−f)·(1−1/k)`:**

| size | threshold |
|---|---|
| 795 b | **5.00** |
| 862 b | **2.70** |
| 2048 b | **2.29** |

**It moves by 1.85× between the two sizes where `f` is actually measured.** So: **the same 2× sieving win that dies at 1.5× uncounted inflation at 862 bits SURVIVES 5.0× inflation at 795 bits.** A screen whose constant depends on the size is not a screen unless the size is stated — **and most claims do not state it.**

## INSTRUMENT (D8) — the controls' numbers, not just that they passed

NC1 −1.59 dex · NC2 −9.22 · NC3 +20.54 · NC4 (Buchstab) −0.92 · NC5 (`E` double-counted) −0.26 — **the `1/E` law is linear, so a 2× error is `1−½`, not a decade: this control passes for the right reason.** NC7/NC7b: `lim`×4 and `lpb`+4 give **exactly 0.000 dex**.
Mutations: mfb(both)+4 → +1.42 dex · Buchstab −0.92 · `E`×10 −0.73 · `I`/`lim`/`lpb` → 0.000.

**★ "Three of eight inputs are dead" — the project's own #508 oracle called `I` its most sensitive input (+12.71 dex) precisely because `ρ` was MULTIPLYING instead of dividing. Anyone who fitted a prefactor against that model fitted it to a sign error.** Correction filed on #508; its central YEAR-vs-BITS finding is unaffected, since that comes from paired ratios against published wall-clocks and never used the oracle's internals.

**NOT RESOLVED, and it blocks the most useful cross-size claim:** the conversion from CADO's `mfb`/`λ` to a column count. `π(2^72) = 9.5×10^19` against the run's measured **656,182,189** columns — a factor of 1.4×10¹¹. **Hence no cross-size column claims are made.**

Full report: `~/factor-scratch/r45/axis3/hyp/a2_sensitivity.md`; code `axis3/code/a2_{req,buchstab,screen,selftest}.py`.
