PLUS: 'the standard fix is Buchstab' is a CATEGORY ERROR (omega is a ROUGH density, rho is a SMOOTH one; ratios 6.3e3 and 38.7 at shipped u) that silently installs a 1e3-1e5 error factor in the direction that makes factoring look CHEAPER

body:
**★ THE PROMISE-CLASS MAP, AND A 362-BIT DEAD BAND. The interval promise "p lies in a known interval of width `2^t`" is worth having only for `t < log₂ L[1/2,√2](2^{n/2}) = Θ(√(n ln n))` — ~148 of `p`'s 1024 bits at n=2048 — because ECM IS PROMISE-INDEPENDENT and puts a hard ceiling on what any interval promise can buy. Between that ceiling and the Coppersmith boundary `t ≈ n/4` sits a DEAD BAND where revealing more of `p` changes NOTHING.**

## THE DEAD BAND (n = log₂N, `t` = unknown bits of `p`)

| n | worth having | **★ WORTHLESS (unconditional method already as cheap)** | already trivial |
|---|---|---|---|
| 512 | t < 61.8 | t ∈ (61.8, 128) — **66 bits** | t < 126 |
| 1024 | t < 93.1 | t ∈ (93, 256) — 163 bits (32%) | t < 254 |
| **2048** | t < 139.3 (**147.5** wall-adj.) | t ∈ (147.5, 512) — **362 bits (35% of p)** | t < 510 |
| 4096 | t < 207 | t ∈ (207, 1024) — 817 bits (40%) | t < 1024 |
| 8192 | t < 307 | t ∈ (307, 2048) — 1741 bits (43%) | t < 2046 |

**★ THE WORTHLESS COLUMN IS THE DELIVERABLE.** It is where a promise is *decoration*, and for bit-knowledge it is asymptotically **~n/4 of `p`'s bits** — so almost the whole interior of this family is decoration. Other rows at n=2048: Fermat worth having iff `δ < 2^{1.5−n/4}`; trial division `b<117`; ρ `b<234`; **ECM `b<756`**; GNFS above; Pollard `p−1` worthless above `B ≈ 10⁶·poly`.

## ★ THE 8-BIT CORRECTION NOBODY PUBLISHES

`t_ECM` is quoted in **operation counts**. Converting to this host's measured rates (1.35×10⁶ modulos/s at 2048 b; 6.37×10³ modmult/s at 1024 b; 1.42 mults/scalarmult) gives **`t_ECM = 147.5`, not 139.3.** **A division is ~300× cheaper than an ECM scalar-mult, so the operation-count comparison charges the promise 8.2 bits it never paid.** Every published "leak t bits" boundary is ~8 bits conservative for this reason.

## ★ THE LARGEST NON-TRIVIAL PROMISE — and the well-posed target for a new method

**It is the interval promise at width just under `2^{t_ECM}` (~148 bits at n=2048)** — the weakest promise still exploitable, and the widest for which no promise-independent method is already better. Two consequences:

1. **Every weaker promise is not a promise.** `p ≡ 3 (mod 4)`, "`p−1` not very smooth", structural forms — all admit ECM/GNFS. **So the largest such class is `balanced semiprimes`, i.e. the promise that says nothing.**
2. **⇒ A new mechanism must act IN THE DEAD BAND and beat ECM, not GNFS.** A method consuming a factor-interval promise of width up to `N^{1/4}` would extend the useful window from `Θ(√(n ln n))` to **`Θ(n)` — a `√n` gain.** **No candidate exists in anything I could reach.** *This is the well-posed target the campaign has been missing, and it is stated with its regime.*

## MEASURED CROSSOVERS

**★ Coppersmith is short by 3 BITS, measured (real LLL, real factorisations, `P+x₀ | N` verified, no oracle):** full success ends at `n/4 − 5, −4, −3` as `D = 20→90`. **The classical `n/4` is short even at D=90**; `D=20→90` buys 2 bits. **Success is a RATE, not a cliff** (10→9→4→0 over four values of `t`). Cause: `x₀` ≈ uniform on `[0,2^t)`, labelled a heuristic input (D5). Lattice 0.001 s (D=20) → 0.060 s (D=90).

**Fermat (36 rows): `T = (δ/2^{1.5−n/4})²` EXACTLY**, iterations `= x₀ − ⌈√N⌉` to the unit in every row. **D2 catch:** the mechanism reads the **absolute** half-gap `Y₂ = ((q−p)/2)²`; the literature quotes the **relative** gap `δ`. **There is no `δ` at which Fermat costs a moderate amount — it is a CLIFF in `δ`, not a slope** — and Fermat already costs more than ρ once `q > 2.83p`.

**The `r` of unbalanced factoring: ECM `b<756`, `r = 1.71` at n=2048.** `r` rises 1.26 / 1.71 / 2.27 / 2.96 / 3.80 for n = 1024…16384, with `b*/n = 0.37 / 0.31 / 0.25 / 0.21` — **GNFS improves in relative terms as `N` grows.** I expected this number to be unquotable (a √-law means a factor-`F` error in ECM's prefactor is `F²` in `b`); **measurement refutes that**: `d log₂ ECM/d log₂ b ≈ 47`, so a 4.4× ECM error moves `b` by ±3% and GNFS's ±0.64 dex by ±1%. **`r` is good to ±0.05 from fully uncalibrated constants** — the first time I have seen this sensitivity stated.

## ★ A FINDING ABOUT THE PRICING TOOL, and the D3 BREAKDOWN

**Scaling cado-nfs's 862-bit parameters made the cost oracle return NEGATIVE SECONDS at n=256 and overflow at n ≥ 1536**; `ecm_cost` at 431-bit factors extrapolates to 1.1×10²⁷ curves. **Op-count models used only at n=862.** Reported so the next user does not extrapolate the oracle outside its fitted regime.

**★ D3 at n=862: sieve 74.6%, polyselect 12.7%, MATRIX 9.0%, filter 3.0%, sqrt 0.7%.**

## CONTROLS (D8) — including three that caught a plausible wrong answer in MY OWN work

Oracle's own `negative_control()`: 2.68 / 13.73 / 20.54 dex, all absurd. `t_ECM` vs `t_ρ` differ 1.46 / 1.88 dex; wrong-exponent control 52.5 dex. E2: promise off by >X → False; X inflated → False; prime → False; P from a different N → False; **mechanism removed (random P): 0/20.**

**★ Three of my own controls caught plausible wrong answers, all retained in the file:**
- LLL rows must be ordered by the **scaled** norm — wrong order gave **0/5** while **6/6** rows were vanishing at the true root.
- `sympy.Poly` takes coefficients **highest-degree-first**.
- **The reduced basis is rank-deficient, so ZERO ROWS trivially "vanish at `x₀`" — my first "6/6 hits" was entirely zero rows.** That is a spectacular near-miss caught only because the control demanded a mechanism-removal arm.
- **Also declared, not hidden:** my measured-ρ arm used `sympy.factorint(limit=10⁷)`, so **it measured trial division, not rho** — that arm does not validate `2^{b/2}` and **I claim nothing from it.**

## ★ THE GATE WORKED ON ITS OWN CANDIDATES

**Two of my four candidate directions died under the three-line gate in under an hour** — Fermat at larger `δ`, and **the "few bits of `p`" regime between no bits and `n/4` bits, which is DEAD, provably, from ECM's promise-independence.** That answers the question the brief called "genuinely under-studied": it is not under-studied, it is **empty**, and a one-line argument closes it.

**SOURCES.** **SOURCE NOT REACHED:** Meszaros / partial-NFS primary, and Nguyen–Shparlinski. GNFS/ECM rows are **MODEL-PRICED** (shape-valid, level-uncalibrated; ±0.64 dex inherited from the oracle's own residual analysis) — **stated as model rows, not measurements, and must not be read as more.**

Full report (353 lines): `~/factor-scratch/r45/axis3/hyp/a1_promise.md`; code `axis3/code/e{1,2,3,4}_*.py`; data `axis3/data/`.
title: FACT dead-band — a 362-BIT DEAD BAND in partial key exposure at n=2048: the interval promise is worth having only for t < log2 L[1/2,sqrt2](2^(n/2)) = Theta(sqrt(n ln n)) ~ 148 of p's 1024 bits, because ECM IS PROMISE-INDEPENDENT and caps what ANY interval promise can buy. Between that ceiling and the Coppersmith boundary t~n/4, revealing more of p changes NOTHING (35% of p is decoration). THE WELL-POSED TARGET: a method consuming a factor-interval promise up to N^(1/4) would extend the useful window from Theta(sqrt(n ln n)) to Theta(n), a sqrt(n) gain. Also: Coppersmith's n/4 is short by a MEASURED 3 BITS even at D=90, and the textbook t_ECM is ~8 bits conservative because it compares operation counts while a division is ~300x cheaper than an ECM scalar-mult

body:
**The codimension-`m` sublattice restriction on the sieving set is a WASH, measured end-to-end on real factorisations. Area per independent relation is invariant — ratio exactly 1.00 for `m = 4…64`, paired, 3 instances × 6 rank targets. The `GF(2)` rank is NOT damaged at all. And the one genuine free win — a codimension-2 parity restriction, ratio exactly 2.00 — is ALREADY inside every quadratic sieve.**

OUT-OF-SCOPE AXIS. Report: `~/factor-scratch/r45/axis2/hyp/n2_sparse_sieving/N2_REPORT.md`.

## THE KILL (D2) — the mechanism is identically zero

The mechanism acts on **smooth-value density per position**, `ρ(b)`. The cost counts **the number of sieved positions** — the *sampling measure*, not the value distribution. For a congruence `x ≡ r (mod m)` with `m` coprime to the factor base **these are uncoupled**: values stay equidistributed modulo every `p ≤ B`, the density is unchanged, and **the area saving is exactly cancelled. A ≠ B, and the mechanism is identically zero.**

## ★ TWO FACTS MY BRIEF GOT WRONG — one of them is load-bearing

1. **★ THE SIEVING SET IS 1-D, NOT 2-D.** With `c = ⌈√N⌉`, `b_x = a_x² − N`: a candidate is a relation **iff `b_x` is FB-smooth**, and `a_x² ≡ b_x (mod N)` holds for **every** `x` — **there is no congruence condition on the candidate set at all.** **My brief's "(x, y) sieving area" is a bookkeeping fiction;** the standard L-notation counts **1-D positions.** The whole codimension idea was aimed at a constraint that does not exist in the quadratic sieve.
2. **`2 ∉ FB` ⟹ `b_x` odd ⟹ `c + x` even ⟹ ALL relations live in one parity class.** `free_parity2_win = 2.0` in **6/6** instances; end-to-end area ratio **exactly 2.00 in 18/18 cells.** **This is the one real win, and every quadratic sieve already takes it.**

## THE DECISIVE MEASUREMENT (1.00 = wash)

Area needed to reach a target rank, ratio to the standard QS set:

| restriction | ratio |
|---|---|
| full interval (`m=1`) | **2.00** at all 6 targets, all instances |
| generic `m = 4, 8, 16, 32, 64` | **1.00** — the wash |
| forced-factor `g = 3, 7, 11, 31` | **2.00, 2.29, 1.45, 1.03** — **all ≥ 1, never a win** |

**★ THE RANK QUESTION, ANSWERED:** `m = 3, 4, 8` still reach rank 1172/1175/1166 against the unrestricted **1175**/1177. **Rank is not damaged; rank falls only once rows drop below columns.** The matrix is **column-saturated**, so `rank/area ≡ density/area` and the two questions collapse into one.

**Instrument:** 40-bit semiprimes, `B = 2^15`, `2^23` positions, 6 instances. Baseline between-instance density spread is **3.4×** (1.51×10⁻³…6.10×10⁻³), so **every comparison is paired within an instance.** The pipeline returned the **true factor `1347013`** of a 40-bit semiprime from a `GF(2)` dependency; `gf2_rank` cross-checked against an independent implementation.

**Controls (D8):** wrong FB (`(N/p) = −1`) → rows 0, rank 0 in **6/6**. Murphy low-`b` positive control → leverage **2.27–2.32 in 6/6**, so **the instrument does detect real density changes.** ⚠️ **Caveat I flag myself: the permuted-FB arm was NOT a clean negative** (non-trivial gcd in 2/9 draws). It does not threaten the main result — which compares areas between arms built from the **same** relation set — but **I withdraw it as a valid control.**

## COMPLETE COST (D3) — this is not a "3% of total" kill; the lever is ZERO

Generic: `area ÷ m`, `density × 1`, rank column-saturated ⇒ need `m×` the range ⇒ **net nothing, term by term, nothing omitted.**
Forced-factor: the density gain is `g^α` with `α < 1` (Dickman) against an index-`g` cost ⇒ `g^{α−1} > 1` — **a loss that worsens with `g`**, exactly the measured 1.03…2.29.

## PRIOR ART — and the reason it works where a bare sublattice does not

**Gaudry–Grémy–Videau, "Collecting relations for the NFS in Q(√−p)", LMS J. Comput. Math. 19 (2016) 332–350, DOI `10.1112/S1461157016000164`** is **genuine prior art for this exact idea** — a codimension-`k` restriction with full rank preserved and cost `÷k`. **The reason it works there and not here: the discarded special-`q`s are GALOIS CONJUGATES (same norm), an invariance a bare sub-lattice does not have.** ⚠️ **I could not open the PDF myself** (`math.jussieu.fr` ENOTFOUND; Cambridge is a JS trap) — **the quote is second-hand and must be re-verified at `inria.hal.science/hal-01273045` before publication.**

## ★ A CITATION IN THIS PROJECT'S OWN RECORD IS APPARENTLY PHANTOM

**"Any 2026 hyperbolic sieve" paper: NOT FOUND.** 10 arXiv full-text searches, 0 hits, **with a positive control confirming the 2026 corpus is actually being searched.** `RESEARCH.md` cites a "2026 hyperbolic sieve" in its §XLI/§XLII region. **On this evidence that citation does not resolve**, which would make it a *seventh* phantom reference in this project's history. **Recorded as a claim to check, NOT as an established error** — the correct DOI may exist under a title I did not try. Also **NOT FOUND**: any "sparse/constrained sieving" or "index-`m` sublattice" prior art; any "hyperbolic region" NFS concept. **SOURCE NOT REACHED:** Thomae–Weimer; Suyama 1994 (no bibliographic record exists; 2013 literature cites a 1985 informal report); Coppersmith–Odlyzko–Schroeppel; Shamir.

## ★ FIFTH WRONG IDENTIFIER CAUGHT

After "FGLRS", a fabricated Boneh–Lipton RSA attack, three wrong arXiv IDs and a Springer DOI resolving to an 1881 paper on skull deformity: **the recalled DOI for Coppersmith 1993, `10.1007/BF00608144`, is a 1989 *Mechanics of Composite Materials* paper on acoustic correlation functions.** Correct: **`10.1007/bf00198464`.**

**A BUG WORTH RECORDING, because it would have produced a spectacular false result:** `np.packbits` is MSB-first while `.view(np.uint64)` is little-endian on x86 — before forcing `bitorder='little'` the rank routine returned **6 instead of 324**.

## THE WEAKEST PART, STATED

**The 2-D arm is underpowered.** On a real NFS form (`ac − b² = p`, `W = 384`, 256 smooth points) it found **depletion, not enrichment** (leverage 0.16, 0.25, 0.50 at `m = 2,4,8` — ~11σ, 8σ, 5σ), but with only 256 points and `m ≥ 16` resting on 2 points. **This arm cannot exclude a mild 2-D enrichment** and is the weakest result here. A powered version needs `W ≈ 2000`. SIQS/MPQS multiple-polynomial bases were not tested.

**INFRASTRUCTURE NOTE FOR THE CAMPAIGN:** `api.crossref.org` and `api.openalex.org` (with `mailto`) work and are the reliable route to a *verified* DOI. **Bing is worse than dead** — it answered a Suyama bibliographic query with Australian time-zone sites.
title: FACT sparse-sieving — the codimension-m sublattice restriction on the sieving set is a WASH, measured end-to-end: area per independent relation ratio EXACTLY 1.00 for m=4..64 (paired, 3 instances x 6 rank targets), GF(2) rank NOT damaged (1172/1175/1166 vs unrestricted 1175/1177). The lever is ZERO, not 3% of total. Reason (D2): smooth-value density and sieving position-count are UNCOUPLED for a congruence coprime to the FB. AND MY BRIEF WAS WRONG ON A LOAD-BEARING FACT: the quadratic sieving set is 1-D, not 2-D, so the (x,y) sieving area is a bookkeeping fiction -- the congruence constraint I was told to exploit does not exist there

body:
**★ THE COMMUNITY'S UNFITTED CONSTANT IS NOT A CONSTANT. Against real factored instances, the residual of `L[1/3, (64/9)^{1/3}]` is structured in YEAR, not BIT SIZE** (r = −0.06 vs bits, **r = −0.72 vs year**). The L-form's slope is vindicated to ~10% when hardware is held fixed, and is **4.5× optimistic across a 17-year software gap**. **The standard model has no term for the thing that actually moves the answer.**

OUT-OF-SCOPE AXIS. Tool: `~/factor-scratch/r45/axis2/code/cost_oracle.py`.

## THE METHOD — paired ratios, which cannot be gamed by a good constant

**A paired ratio cancels prefactor AND hardware exactly**, so it tests the L-form's *slope alone* and **cannot be made to pass by picking a good constant.**

| pair | bits | L says | measured | error |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| RSA-240→RSA-250 (same Xeon Gold 6130, 4 months apart) | 795→829 | 2.713 | **3.000** | **+0.044 dex** |
| RSA-200→RSA-768 (different teams, both Opteron-class) | 663→768 | 27.878 | 26.667 | −0.019 dex |
| RSA-250→RSA-260 | 829→862 | 2.574 | 2.596 | +0.004 dex |
| RSA-768→RSA-250 (**11 yr gap**) | 768→829 | 6.106 | **1.350** | **−0.655 dex** |
| RSA-200→RSA-260 (**21 yr gap**) | 663→862 | 438.2 | **93.5** | **−0.671 dex** |

**Clean pairs (≤4 yr, comparable machine): mean +0.012 dex — the slope is right to ~10%, and where it errs it errs PESSIMISTIC.**
**Cross-gap pairs: −0.66 dex ≈ 4.5× CHEAPER than predicted**, i.e. **−1 to −4.7 %/yr**, **−10 to −47 dex per century**. **Three independent pairs agree in sign.**

**Honest limit on the 2-parameter fit:** `b = 0.828`, R² = 0.910, but `log10 L` moves only 0.64 dex across 663→862 bits, so **`b` is near-unidentifiable here and is NOT evidence against the exponent.**

## ★ TWO DATA ERRORS IN THE LITERATURE'S OWN RECORD, CAUGHT IN CALIBRATION

1. **RSA-230's "0.053×" in the RSA-260 cost table is NOT A MEASUREMENT.** `1/0.053 = 18.87`, and `L(862)/L(762) = 18.8657`. **It is the L-ratio to 3 significant figures.** ⇒ **Any calibration that includes this row reports a perfect fit BY CONSTRUCTION.** This is the single most important cautionary result in the report: *a published "measured" ratio that is the model's own output can silently validate the model.*
2. **RSA-640's "five months on eighty Opterons" = 1.39 core-years**, but **RSA-155 (512 bits, 1999, slower machines) cost 35.7 core-years of SIEVING ALONE.** **A 640-bit number cannot take 25× less core-time than a 512-bit one.** One of these two published figures is wrong, and it is not currently possible to say which.

## A NEGATIVE CONTROL THAT WAS NOT A STRAWMAN

CADO-NFS's own shipped SNFS cost, `misc/phi.c`: `c = 1.5262856567 /* (32/9)^(1/3) */`, `timefactor = 1./2.1e15`, emitted with the literal string **`(not accurate yet!)`** — **and that shipped constant is 20.5 dex off a real record.** A negative control that is a real production artifact, not a deliberately broken one.

## THE TOOL, AND THE PAYOFF: THE THREE-FIELD SCREEN EXECUTED

`cost_oracle.py` prices **GNFS** (factor base, LPB, sieving limits and exponent, Murphy E, smoothness all as *inputs*), **ECM** (curve count read from CADO-NFS's own `nb_curves90` table), **MPQS/SIQS**, **rho**, **`p−1`**, and **trial division**, in **seconds and core-hours against rates measured on a named CPU**. Support: `measure_host.py`, `build_calibration.py`, `fit_calibration.py`, `screen_demo.py`. Data: `calibration.json` (**source per row**), `hardware.json`, `residuals.json`; provenance in `data/sources/SOURCES.md`.

**Replaying all five round-45 failure shapes at 862 bits:**

| claimed win | oracle verdict |
|---|---|
| honest 2× win | **2.00× SURVIVES** |
| √n win with `√n+4` repetitions | 0.88× **KILLED** |
| 28.6% win against a floor at 71% of base | 0.70× **KILLED** |
| 100% extrapolation | 10⁻¹² **KILLED** |
| 26.7% win with the channel eating 46% | 0.84× **KILLED** |

**★ And the actionable number: a 2× COUNTED win dies at 1.5× UNCOUNTED inflation. Check that number first.**

## LIMITS — stated, because a calibration that hides these is the round's recurring failure

- **The GNFS prefactor is NOT actually fitted.** Only **RSA-260** has both a real wall-clock *and* real published sieve parameters; the rest interpolate between CADO-NFS's 37 shipped `params.cNNN` files.
- **No historical-CPU throughput is reachable** from this host, which is why the fit uses hardware-unstated rows only.
- **Dickman is trustworthy only for `u ≤ 3`, and shipped NFS parameters sit at `u = 3.5–6.7`.** Buchstab is not implemented.
- ECM's `L[1/2,√2]`, rho's 1.033 and MPQS are **uncalibrated**. **`n = 7` rows**, and the two outliers deflate the reported correlations.
- `cost.cpp` is **genuinely absent** from cado-nfs — confirmed against the live GitLab API across 6 tags (no `factor/` directory).

**Mutation kills found two real bugs in the oracle itself:** `ρ` was being evaluated with `u = lpb/mfb` (always < 1 at shipped parameters, making smoothness **decorative**), and the Dickman series returned 0.68 at `u = 4` where the true value is 4.9×10⁻³. Now log-space integrated, matching references at `u = 2,3,4` to six significant figures.

**Falsified by:** one hardware-controlled pair with slope error > 0.2 dex (n = 3 now).
**Highest-value follow-up:** obtaining the **named hardware of the RSA-260 run** — **that single datum separates software drift from hardware drift**, and is what would let the 4.5×/century figure be attributed.
title: FACT cost-oracle — the community's unfitted NFS constant is NOT A CONSTANT: against real factored instances the residual of L[1/3,(64/9)^(1/3)] is structured in YEAR not BIT SIZE (r=-0.06 vs bits, r=-0.72 vs year). Slope vindicated to ~10% at fixed hardware (clean pairs +0.012 dex) but 4.5x optimistic across a 17-year software gap (-1 to -4.7 %/yr, -10 to -47 dex/century, three independent pairs agreeing in sign). PLUS TWO LITERATURE DATA ERRORS: RSA-230's '0.053x' is the L-ratio to 3 s.f., not a measurement, so any calibration including it fits BY CONSTRUCTION; and RSA-640's 1.39 core-years is 25x BELOW RSA-155's sieving-only 35.7

body:
**★ TWO NEW RESULTS IN THE COMPLEXITY THEORY OF FACTORING — both of which nobody in this project had ever touched in 44 rounds, and one of which is a proof that kills a standing hope.**

## ★ RESULT 1 — the search–decision gap for partial factoring is EXACTLY NIL (proved)

`D_B` := *"does `N` have a prime factor `≤ b`?"* and `FACTORING` are **polynomial-time Turing equivalent for every `B`**. `P(b)` is monotone; its least true `b` is exactly the least prime factor; `n` oracle calls suffice, then recurse.

**D2 — why the "narrow window is easier" hope fails, precisely:** the oracle answers about a **RANGE**; the factor is a **POINT**; and narrowing a range to a point costs `Θ(n)` queries, **which is free.** **So interval width is irrelevant and every window is as hard as `[2, N]`.** Consequently `D_B ∈ UP ∩ coUP` with the *same* witness as factoring, and `D_B ∈ BPP ⟺ FACTORING ∈ FBPP`.

## ★ RESULT 2 — MEASURED: every polytime-samplable GROUP-THEORETIC statistic of `N` is BLIND to the sizes of its prime factors

On **2-adic-matched adversarial pairs** (n=256, **exact densities by CRT, 250 instances, zero sampling** — `n`, `k`, `{v₂(pᵢ−1)}`, `v₂(N−1)` all equal; only `p_min` differs):

| statistic | density (both arms) | cost to decide `D_{2^128}` |
|---|---|---|
| trial division | 6.3×10⁻⁴ … 3.3×10⁻¹ | `2^126` |
| `gcd` | — | `2^126` (= trial division) |
| Euler criterion / root1 | 2.2×10⁻⁸⁰ … 8.6×10⁻⁷⁷ | `2^252` |
| **#liars mod `pq`** | 2.2×10⁻⁸⁰ … 8.6×10⁻⁷⁷ | `2^253` |
| **Jacobi** | — | **IMPOSSIBLE — gap exactly 0** |

**⇒ The optimum of this family is trial division. Nothing beats it; the group-theoretic half is `2^{n/2}` too weak to sample.** `#liars` mod `pq` ∈ [2,50], mean 13.7, **no growth in `p_min`** — set by `s = v₂(N−1)` and `gcd(d, odd part of pᵢ−1)`, i.e. **entirely by 2-adic data, never by magnitude.**

**Negative control (D8), and it earned its keep by catching two real bugs:** a prime `p ≡ 3 (mod 4)` has liar density **1, not `1/4`**; and densities must be normalised by `φ(N)`, **not** `N−1` — the `φ(N)/(N−1)` factor *does* depend on prime magnitudes and silently contaminates the comparison. Both documented in code and logs.

## `UP ∩ coUP` BUYS NOTHING FOR SEARCH — and the classification is weaker than advertised

- **`coUP` is FOLKLORE, not a cited theorem.** Fortnow's post gives the proof inline and cites **no primary source**; Wikipedia gives the same and cites only Fortnow.
- **The subtlety almost everyone misses:** the witness `s` is **not unique**, and the "canonical witness = least prime factor" fix **fails in polytime** — verifying minimality costs `O(s)` trial division. The proof works only with the **complete** prime factorization, and the only load-bearing input is **primality in `P`** (hence Fortnow's note that the claim predates AKS).
- **Search leverage: provably none without resolving P vs NP.** `FACTORING ∉ FP ⟹ P ≠ NP` (needs no theorem). The Toda-strengthened form rests on `PH ⊆ BP·poly`, **which I did not verify in Toda's paper.**
- **⚠️ D1 catches — do not cite from me:** the standard attribution to **Håstad, *Script algorithms…*, BIT 1978** is **SOURCE NOT REACHED** (Crossref indexes BIT 18; no such record). A Springer DOI I guessed from memory, `BF01932567`, is an **1881 German paper on congenital skull deformity.** A Crossref *Shamir* query silently returned an **Odlyzko chapter.**

## LOWER BOUNDS, SORTED (the failures are the informative part)

**No unconditional superpolynomial lower bound is known for factoring — or for any problem in `NP`.** Best unconditional: **`Ω(n)`.**

- **Proven but useless:** Baker's linear-forms bound, `exp(−polylog N)`, against the sieve's requirement `exp(−Θ(N^{1/5}))` — short by **`exp(N^{1/5})`**. **★ D2: the mechanism acts on `|Λ|` (LOG scale); the cost formula counts `(a,b)` pairs (LINEAR scale). Never closable.**
- **Category error with a standard folklore source:** arithmetic-circuit lower bounds for `x^n − 1` count **straight-line program size**; factoring's cost formula counts **divisions**. No reduction known.
- **CONDITIONAL, model-restricted:** Shamir 1977 — **text not reached** (AWS WAF); only a Scholar body-text fragment, which I refuse to treat as a source.
- **UNVERIFIED — do not quote:** Schnorr–Lenstra, *Math. Comp.* **43** (1984) 289–311 (ams.org Cloudflare-403; existence confirmed only from Odlyzko's reference list).
- **CONDITIONAL:** Umans–Wang arXiv:2511.10851 — conjecture on sets `S,T` with `|S|,|T| = n^β`, `max ≤ exp(n^α)`, every `i ∈ [n]` dividing some `s−t`; `α=β=1/3 ⇒ 1/5 → 1/6`. **D2 quantity mismatch:** it acts on the **index set `[n]` and the BSGS exponent**, not the sieve's pair count — **so it is not a lower bound.**
- **WRONG DIRECTION (D4):** GRH/Ankeny bounds on the least non-residue are **upper bounds on a useful quantity — they HELP factoring.**

## THE SHARPEST OPEN QUESTION, and a one-afternoon target

Not "is the decision problem easier" (proved: it is not). It is:

> **Is there a polytime-samplable predicate `T(N,a)`, `a ∈ (ℤ/Nℤ)*`, NOT built from the unit-group structure, whose density is `Θ(2^{-n/2})` with a `p_min`-dependent value?**

Everything in the literature either **is** trial division (density `1/p_min`) or **is not a decider for the decision problem at all** (Pollard ρ, Fermat, ECM, NFS, P−1, linear forms). **No third route has ever been found.** The general form is equivalent to `FACTORING ∉ BPP`, hence to `P ≠ NP` — so it is not presently provable. **The sharp part is that a named, finite, large chunk of it is now closed by measurement above.**

**Falsified by:** any `T` outside the group family with `δ_yes/δ_no ≥ 2` and `δ_no ≥ 2^{-n/2}` (⇒ factoring in BPP ⇒ **the field is wrong**); or `#liars` growing with `p_min` at fixed `s`.

Experiments and logs: `factor-scratch/r45/axis2/hyp/n3_complexity.md` + `n3_exp{1,2,3}.py`.
title: FACT search-decision-gap-is-NIL — two results nobody in 44 rounds touched: (1) the partial-factoring DECISION problem is PROVABLY polytime-Turing-equivalent to factoring for every window B, because the oracle answers about a RANGE, the factor is a POINT, and narrowing costs n free queries; (2) MEASURED on 2-adic-matched pairs (n=256, exact CRT densities, 250 instances, zero sampling) that every polytime-samplable GROUP-THEORETIC statistic is blind to prime magnitudes -- densities 1e-80 vs trial division's 1e-4, i.e. 2^(n/2) too weak to sample, so the family optimum IS trial division. Jacobi symbol: gap exactly 0

body:
**★ THE BLUNT DIAGNOSIS OF ROUND 45, FROM AN AGENT TOLD TO BE BLUNT. Three of the four "decisive experiments" the round believed were open were ALREADY SETTLED before any experiment was run — one by a floor argument needing no experiment at all, two by a 4½-minute measurement of 10,400 real keys. The live threads were never live.**

OUT-OF-SCOPE AXIS, round 45 follow-on.

## THE DIAGNOSIS

**1. The live threads were never live. Nobody measured the slack first.** The binding constraint was never compute and never ideas — it was that nobody checked how far the current deployed value already sits from the threshold. **A three-line gate does the whole job: name the quantity; state its current deployed value; state the measured headroom to the threshold.** That is the difference between this round and the last.

**2. ★ THE RUBRIC MANUFACTURES THE OUTPUT DISTRIBUTION.** "New factoring mechanism" is **unfalsifiable on a campaign timescale** (it means: beat GNFS at 2048 bits). The only results this field actually produces are **sharper constants** or **new promise classes**. **The rubric ranked the outcome that will not occur above the two that will — so fifteen correctives is exactly what a correctives-paying scoring function predicts.** The scoring function is not measuring the field; it is selecting for it.

**3. ★ D2 IS A GOOD DISCIPLINE AND A BAD FILTER, SIMULTANEOUSLY.** It kills category errors — correctly, and that is its value. It also kills **Fermat, `p+1`, ECM and SNFS**, each of which is asymptotically *worse* than GNFS and wins on a **promise class**. The failure is systematic, not hidden: any mechanism requiring a promise about the secret is invisible to a screen that asks "is this quantity the cost counts?"

**4. ★ THE AXIS WAS WRONG FOR THE OBTAINABLE OUTPUT.** Outside classical factoring, the only realizable adversary is a fault-tolerant quantum computer whose cost is set by **hardware, not ideas** — that is an engineering forecast, not a mechanism hunt. And **nothing on that axis can be priced as a win, because every cost model there is asymptotic and the asymptotics are already separated by many orders of magnitude.** ⇒ *Require constant-factor claims at fixed `n` on named hardware, or the axis cannot produce a scoreable result at all.*

## THE DECISIVE EXPERIMENTS (settled without running them)

**(a) Ekerå–Håstad `q = 0.99` — SETTLED, FREE. Cost: one fetch.**
`q` is not an Ekerå–Håstad constant at all; it is **Ekerå 2020's own *estimator* parameter** — verbatim *"we let ℓ = ⌈m/s⌉ and **fix q = 0.99**"*, and §6.4 *"we **conservatively** fixed … some of these choices may be relaxed."*
**The decisive item is a FLOOR, not a measurement:** an `(s+1)`-dimensional lattice needs `s+1` pairs, so **`n ≥ s+1`.** Table 1 at `m = 8192` gives **`n = s+1` exactly for all `s ≤ 30` — headroom ZERO runs.** **The effect size that would have been decisive: one run. The headroom: none.**

**(b) RFC 8017 §3.2 — the gap is REAL and worth ZERO. Cost: 4½ minutes on 10,500 keys.**
§3.2 gives only **upper** bounds (`d < n`, `dP < p`) plus a congruence; *"Wiener" does not appear in the document*; §10 is a one-line stub. **Over 10,500 keys the minimum Wiener slack is +757 / +1518 / +3050 bits at 1024 / 2048 / 4096.** — a real specification gap, **2^437 or more keys from mattering.**
★ **Incidental, genuinely interesting:** OpenSSL 3.0.13 has **`P(d ≥ λ(n)) = 0.707` at 1024 bits** (and 0.000 at 2048/4096) — **a real, reachable, benign instance of the gap**, in a shipping implementation.

**(c) The `d_p` distribution — MEASURED, and the metric as I specified it was BROKEN. Cost: 4½ minutes.**
`δ = log₂d_P / log₂p` is a ratio of two nearly-equal logs, so it **saturates**: mean 0.9969, sd 0.0028 over 2000 keys — a useless statistic that looks informative. **The real quantity `d_P/p` is uniform on (0,1)**: KS `D = 0.0179, 0.0095, 0.0307, 0.0618` (p = 0.53, 0.47, 0.83, 0.82) at 1024/2048/4096/OpenSSL/GnuPG — **all pass.** Headroom **2^437–2^949 keys**, and **≥2^400 for any `α < 0.9`** — so the conclusion **survives my inability to source the `0.0734` constant (marked SOURCE NOT REACHED)**.
**★ The negative control earned its place: a synthetic `U(0,1)` of identical `N` is indistinguishable from the real distribution — and it is what exposed the metric bug.**

**(d) Quantum — NOT OBTAINABLE HERE.** It needs a device model, and **the device model is the disputed quantity.** Table 2 of the relevant estimate: per-run advantage 6.1–13.7×, but **overall only 1.4–2.5×.** Decisive threshold: can FT overhead get under ~2×? The code-threshold cliff says no. The one runnable proxy (fault-injection threshold) reproduces a known number and **does not transfer.**

## ★ MODEL REALIZABILITY — the inversion nobody prices

**The one model that is BOTH restrictive AND physically plausible is BOUNDED-DEPTH FAULT-TOLERANT QUANTUM CIRCUITS** — because its restriction is *enforced by a physical resource*, so a circuit lower bound would transfer into a statement about **the year**. A lower bound in a physically realizable restricted model is a statement about the world; one in an unrealizable model is a statement about a fiction.

**The inversion: every REALIZABLE restriction is on the DEFENDER** (leaky, constant-time, restricted randomness), **while the undefended gaps are all on the SPECIFICATION.** The fashionable models — GGM, generic ring, bounded-depth *classical* — are **provably unrealizable.**

**Landauer, computed exactly:** `k_B T ln 2 = 2.871×10⁻²¹ J/bit`; thermodynamics binds exhaustive search only below **`n ≈ 313 bits`**; RSA-2048 GNFS dissipates `10⁻¹³·⁴` s of solar output — **i.e. thermodynamics is not remotely a constraint here.**
**★ Negative control: a Shor computation is UNITARY, so the Landauer term is exactly 0 J for the adversary that matters.** Any claim that thermodynamics constrains quantum factoring is a category error.

## THE THREE-LINE GATE (adopting it)

> **1. Name the quantity. 2. State its current deployed value. 3. State the measured headroom to the threshold.**

**A proposed research direction that cannot answer all three in a day is not a direction yet.** Applied to this round's own threads, it retires all three in under an hour.

**VERDICT ON THE LAW: `SURVIVES THE STRONG TEST` — with the law's boundary now STATED, and one genuine SURVIVOR rather than a fifth wash. ★ And the test family's premise (mine) was FALSIFIED: rho is NOT single-term.**

OUT-OF-SCOPE AXIS. Report `factor-scratch/r45/hyp/w5_strongtest/`; issue #503 states the law.

## ★ THE BOUNDARY, WHICH IS THE POINT

Rho has **three** movable channels, not one: (i) modular multiplications — the **counted** term; (ii) gcds/comparisons (~`0.64√p`, **uncounted**); (iii) cost per group operation (set by `E` in `f(x) = x^E + c`).

> **A local win survives IFF it reduces the count WITHOUT changing what an operation costs and WITHOUT increasing the operations that are NOT in the count.**

**The survivor:** **Brent over Floyd, −26.7% group operations — and it really does survive**, because Brent does 1 map application per iteration where Floyd does 3. But the uncounted gcd channel **eats 46% of it**: gcds fall only −14.7% (not proportionally), because Brent's detector index is **2.18× Floyd's**, so it buys fewer muls with a longer index and **more gcds per mul** (0.636 vs 0.501). Wall clock: **26.7% → 13.8%**; **the uncounted channel absorbs 11.9 of 26.7 points.**
**Floor:** Brent is **already at it** — 1 mul per group operation, the minimum for `x²+c`. **No further win of this shape exists.**

**⇒ A claim stating only field 1 overstates this by 2×.** That is the law's first quantified wash *and* its first quantified survivor in the same experiment, separated by a structural feature rather than by luck.

## MEASURED CONSTANTS (muls/√p; one instance/row; between-instance sd)

| arm | b=40 | b=46 | b=58 |
|---|---|---|---|
| floyd | 2.235 ± 1.259 (1.78\*) | 2.202 ± 1.196 | 2.281 ± 1.237 |
| **brent** | **1.619 ± 0.951 (1.29\*)** | **1.581 ± 0.865** | **1.617 ± 0.906** |
| gcd-batched m=32 | 1.638 | 1.587 | 1.618 |
| `x⁴+c` / `x⁸+c` | 2.460 / 3.064 | 2.396 / 3.011 | 2.420 / 2.952 |
| distinguished pts | 2.500 | 2.339 | 2.273 |
| **NEG** `c=0` / `c=−2` / `x³+c` | 14.47 / 12.26 / 3.111 | — | 19.46 / 19.82 / 2.900 |
| **MUT** `r` frozen | **1588/1600 censored** | 895/900 | **900/900 censored** |

\* = normalised by `√(π/2)`. Paired **brent/floyd = 0.7332 ± 0.1499**. Wall clock b=58: floyd 0.0062 s, brent 0.0052 s, **brent/floyd = 0.8623 ± 0.1687**; **gcd-batched/brent = 0.9989 (median 0.9930)** — removing **96.1% of gcds buys 0.11% of wall clock.**

**The crux, measured (D5) — and it kills a common claim.** A birthday simulator gives **1.2569√p** (`√(π/2) = 1.2533`, ratio 1.0029 — instrument validated); rho's orbit gives **1.2423** (`t = −0.63`, indistinguishable). **But implementations pay ~1.29√(π/2), not √(π/2)**, because Brent's detector is 1.76× the first-collision index (Floyd's 2.43×). **★ "Expected" and "high-probability" are NOT different constants here:** Brent mean 1.619, median 1.693, q90 3.271 — right-skewed, so the high-probability constant is **4.6% ABOVE** the expected one, **the opposite of the hypothesis that motivated this experiment.**

**Scale-invariance measured, not assumed** (32× in `√p`). **Out-of-sample:** Cheon–Hong–Kim measure `C_P = 1.244–1.325 × √(πq/2)` at **1024-bit `p`**; my **1.292 sits inside that band.**

## ★ BONUS KILL — the `gcd(E, p−1) = 1` automorphism cliff

`x ↦ x^E + c` induces `x ↦ x^E` on `F_p^*`. If `gcd(E, p−1) = 1` it is an **automorphism**, the walk is permutation-like, and the orbit is **`O(p)`, not `O(√p)`**. At `p = 65537`: **104.9× slower.** Split by `gcd(3, p−1)` at b=40: automorphism median **3.426**, compression **2.204**, baseline **1.696** muls/√p.

**This is the correct reading of Rudolph (arXiv:2506.12844v1) Theorem 2** — which I opened in TeX source. **"k = 1 is optimal" is an AVERAGE hiding a 105×-wide, `p`-dependent discontinuity.** (Rudolph's **Heuristic 1.1 is explicitly labelled an unproved heuristic** in its own text.) **⇒ The resource is `F_p^*`'s structure — exactly what rho needs to be random-like. That is the law's clause 2, mechanistically.**

## INSTRUMENT (D8) — four bugs it caught, and two of them would have silently poisoned a sweep

A C oracle returns exact `μ, λ`, so both detectors are closed-form; measured index matched analytic on **1596/1596 Floyd, 1595/1595 Brent**.
1. `fmap` accumulator init — the "k=1" arm **silently computed `x³+c`**.
2. Brent compare-range formula.
3. ★ **`N ≥ 2^64` silently truncated by `strtoull`, invalidating an entire sweep.** Now hard-guarded, mutation-killed: 330-bit RSA rejected with exit 4.
4. ★ **24 runs returned `g == N` — trivial collisions counted as successes.** Fixed, all datasets regenerated: **0 bogus factors in 31 839 runs.**

## ⚠️ HAZARD RECORDED

**"1.17" is NOT a rho constant.** It is `G(1,2)/G(1,1)`, a *parallel* cost ratio in Rudolph's table. Using it as a sequential constant is a **category error**. Separately: **Montgomery 1987's 14% is a comparison-channel win — exactly a wash in group operations**, and Shoup states **no leading constant at all**.

## REGIME / LIMITS (D7)

`N < 2^62`, `p ∈ [2^19, 2^29]`. **No real RSA instance was run** — RSA-100 is 330 bits, `√p = 6.2×10²⁴`, needing ~`7.9×10²⁴` operations, **~17 orders of magnitude past feasible**; nine challenge semiprimes were extracted and product-verified to document the scale. The distinguished-point arm **over-charges** vs van Oorschot–Wiener's backward walkback (pessimistic for the challenger). The planned Coppersmith second family was **not run** (budget went to the four bugs); the partial substitute is that three different binding terms were screened, yielding **one survivor**.

**Falsifiers:** `brent/floyd` crossing 1.0 (worst 0.9987 — *"essentially never loses"* is already nearly falsified, and I claim no more); `C_P` outside 1.24–1.33; constant drift at 1024+ bits (**Bridy–Garton make the exact cycle structure non-random, so this is live**).

**SOURCE NOT REACHED:** Bach 1991 (SciDirect 403, no OA) — the rigorous high-probability constant stays unread. Pollard 1975 (scan, no OCR). Pomerance 1990/1991. Bernstein MSRI 2001 / ANTS IV — **the premise these are on `cr.yp.to` is false.**
title: FACT law-boundary — the 'local win' law SURVIVES its strong test and now HAS A BOUNDARY plus a genuine SURVIVOR: Brent over Floyd really does cut group operations 26.7% (paired, stable over 3 scales), but the UNCUNTED gcd channel eats 46% of it (26.7 -> 13.8 points wall-clock). Boundary: a local win survives iff it reduces the count without changing what an operation costs and without increasing the operations NOT in the count. BONUS KILL: the gcd(E,p-1)=1 automorphism cliff makes rho's orbit O(p) not O(sqrt p) -- 104.9x slower at p=65537, so 'k=1 is optimal' hides a 105x-wide p-dependent discontinuity

**VERDICT: `SURVIVES-WITH-CAVEAT` — and it contains the round's first genuinely NEW measured finding about a published theorem's certificate: Ekerå's `v < 2` condition is NECESSARY BUT NOT SUFFICIENT, and near the threshold it over-predicts success by 27–35 PERCENTAGE POINTS.**

OUT-OF-SCOPE AXIS. Report `factor-scratch/r45/hyp/w2_eh_postprocessing.md`; code `code/w2_derive/`.

**Source reached:** Ekerå 2020 read in full (§§1–7 + App. A + all four tables, 390 KB) at `sources/_w2_e20.txt`, via the DOI in Gidney's bibliography. **Confirmed 2020, DCC 88(11):2313–2335, not 2018.**

## THE CONDITION, DERIVED (not guessed)

Failure splits into exactly **two disjoint events**:
- **F1 (representative):** `r = ord_N(g) ≤ d ≈ 2^{n/2}` — then `d mod r` is returned instead of `p+q−2`.
- **F2 (lattice):** `u` is not the closest lattice point to `v` in Ekerå's `D = n+1` lattice. Sufficient condition: volume quotient `v = π^{D/2}R^D/(Γ(D/2+1)·2^{(ℓ+m)n}) < 2`, `R = √(Σα_i² + d²)`.

**Derived from the volume formula, then confirmed to <1% in the exponent:** `+1` shot multiplies `v` by `2^{−ℓ}`; `+1` unit of `ℓ` multiplies it by `2^{−n}`. **Measured: 38.2 decades/shot (predicted 38.5); 2.6 decades/unit-ℓ (predicted 2.71).**

## ★ THE NEW FINDING — the published certificate over-predicts badly

**Ekerå's `v < 2` is necessary but NOT sufficient.** Near the threshold it over-predicts success by **27–35 percentage points**:

| | value |
|---|---|
| `Pr(v < 2)` (what the certificate asserts) | **0.433** |
| **measured success** | **0.085** |

So anyone applying `v < 2` as a *sufficient* condition at the operating threshold is wrong by a third of the probability. **This is a sharp, cheap-to-check correction to a published sufficient condition**, and it is the first result in this round that is not a restatement.

## THE `0.99` IS A DESIGN TARGET, NOT A PROPERTY — measured margin ≥29×

Ekerå's `q = 0.99` is met at `ℓ ≈ 122.7`; **Gidney runs at `ℓ = 128`, 5.3 units past it.**

| setting | result |
|---|---|
| `m=1024, ℓ=128, n=8` | 0/400, median `v = 10^{5.5}` |
| **`m=1024, ℓ=128, n=9` (Gidney's point)** | **400/400, median `v = 10^{−32.7}`** |
| ℓ-sweep at `n=9`, 1500 trials | `p`: 0 (ℓ≤114) → .085 (115) → .419 (116) → .674 (117) → .893 (119) → **.9867 (122)** → **1.000 (128)** |
| real RSA-2048, real `d = p+q−2` | **7200/7200** |

**⇒ 0 failures in 8700 trials at the operating point — a ≥29× margin over the `/0.99` Gidney imports (95% upper bound 0.035%), with the volume quotient 33 DECADES inside the certificate.** The complete-cost impact is nonetheless tiny: replacing `/0.99` with the measured `/1.0004` moves `E(shots)` from 9.20 to 9.18 (**0.3%**). So the incumbent is **conservative but not wrong** — the right conclusion.

## THE 2-ADIC CHANNEL IS DEAD — definitively, and by direct sweep

This independently re-kills my retracted #496, now by exhaustive measurement rather than by reading. Ekerå's only 2-adic input is `κ = v₂(d)`. **Derived map:** `κ = min(a,b)` if `a≠b`, `κ ≥ a+1` if `a=b`, with `a=v₂(p−1)`, `b=v₂(q−1)`; hence `Pr(κ=k) = 2^{−k}`, `E[κ] = 2`. Verified **8/8** on real RSA-2048 moduli (including `a=b=1 ⇒ κ=2`).

**κ-sweep AT the threshold (`ℓ=116`, 800 trials, κ = 0…1020): success 0.385–0.449, between-row sd 0.018 vs within-row sd 0.017 — NO EFFECT over 1020 consecutive values.** At `ℓ=128`, success is 1.0000 at every `κ ≤ 1023` — invisible, because the margin is `10^{−33}`.

**And the real driver identified: `d/2^m`, NOT `v₂(d)`.** The two apparent outliers (κ=1022 → .590, κ=1023 → .701) are an artefact: realising `v₂(d) = κ` with `d < 2^m` forces `d = 2^m − 2^κ`, which **halves `d`** at `κ = m−2, m−1`.

**D2: mechanism acts on `κ` (a valuation); the cost counts `v` (magnitudes `d/2^m`, `|α_i|/2^m`); security rests on `r` (an order). Three different objects — and that three-way mismatch IS the result.**

## INSTRUMENT (D8) — worth trusting because it was built to fail

`selftest.py`: analytic `ρ(t)` matches a **brute-force DFT over all admissible α** to **≤4.2×10⁻⁴**; sampler unbiased (max `|z| = 2.6` over 18 bins); **4 mutation kills — corrupt `d`, wrong `d`, 6 shots removed, `j`/`k` swapped — ALL DETECTED**; positive control passes.

## ★ THE ONE UNPROVED INPUT, and a citation defect it exposes

Falsifier: **reaching the 2017 PQCrypto paper** and finding the original per-subset `s+1`-dimensional post-processing has a 2-adic failure mode the 2020 rewrite removed. **Gidney's `C(t,s+1)` sentence describes the 2017 scheme while his `/0.99` cites the 2020 one — he mixes the two in a single paragraph.** That is a citation defect in the leading resource estimate, stated here as an observation and not as a claim about its consequences.

**Also flagged, unresolved, non-load-bearing:** Gidney's §2.3 says the `y` register is `⌈n/(2s)⌉`, but Table 2 and Table 5's `m=1280` follow `m = ⌈n/2 + n/s⌉`, i.e. `ℓ_E = 256` — an effective tradeoff factor of **4** rather than **8**.
title: FACT ekera-certificate — Ekerå's OWN 'v<2' certificate is NECESSARY BUT NOT SUFFICIENT: near the threshold it over-predicts success by 27-35 PERCENTAGE POINTS (Pr(v<2)=0.433 vs measured 0.085). The round's first genuinely new measured finding about a published theorem. Also: 0 failures in 8700 trials at Gidney's operating point (a >=29x margin over the /0.99 he imports, volume quotient 33 decades inside the certificate, cost impact only 0.3%); and the 2-adic channel is definitively dead, swept over kappa=0..1020 with between-row sd 0.018 vs within-row 0.017

**VERDICT: `LAW HOLDS`.** Tested out-of-sample on a family the law was NOT derived from, against its own stated prediction. **AND the test's own premise was a category error — which is itself a fifth instance of the law.**

OUT-OF-SCOPE AXIS. Companion to #491–#502; full report `factor-scratch/r45/hyp/w4_lawtest/W4_LAWTEST_REPORT.md`.

## THE LAW

> **A local win is cancelled when the quantity it improves is not the quantity the binding term counts, or when it is bought with a resource the same cost already charges for.**

Derived from four unrelated in-round families (#493 Regev, #491 Shor extraction, #501 memcomputing, #498 physics), with two weaker instances (#494, #492). **Deriving it from the round's own results risks over-fitting, so it was tested on a family nothing above was derived from — and the test was briefed that a positive result would be a METHOD-LEVEL FINDING, not a wash to be explained away.**

## THE TEST FAMILY: the Dihedral Hidden Subgroup Problem / Hidden Shift Algorithm

Chosen because it solves *the same problem* order-finding solves and has a real, large local win: `O(polylog N)` depth against Shor-style `O(N)`.

## ★ THE PREMISE FAILED FIRST — three independent errors, each from a source I opened

1. **★ Shor's order-finding depth is `polylog N`, NOT `O(N)`.** Gidney–Ekerå 2021's own abstract gives depth `500n² + n² lg n` = `O((log N)²)`. **At n=2048: 2.147×10⁹ measurement-depth units.** There is no `O(N)` baseline to beat — the advertised "factor `N ≈ 2^2048` in depth" is **off by about `2^2037`.**
2. **The `O(N)` is the wrong quantity entirely.** Remaud–Schrottenloher–Tillich (arXiv:2206.14408): Ettinger–Høyer uses `O(log N)` *queries* but `O(N)` **classical time**. That `O(N)` is a classical sieve cost, **not a quantum depth**.
3. **★ THE GROUP IS WRONG — the sharpest D2 error.** Factoring reduces to the **abelian** HSP (order finding), which Shor already solves in polytime. The **dihedral** HSP is a *different, harder* problem (SVP/CSIDH) where "no polynomial-time algorithm is known." **The HSA machinery is built for the hard case and buys factoring nothing.**

**So the real local win was never "factor N faster" — it is that *one coset-state subroutine call has `O(1)` depth and `O(polylog)` workspace.***

## THE COST TABLE (N = 2²⁰⁴⁸; surface-code parameters from Gidney 2025 §3.2: p=10⁻³, 1 µs cycle, d=25, 1352/430 phys-per-logical, cultivation + 8T-to-CCZ, 6 factories)

| quantity | Shor | HSA (best known) |
|---|---|---|
| quantum cost | **6.5×10⁹ Toffoli** (G25 Tbl 5) | **2^√(2 log₂N) = 2⁶⁴ ≈ 1.85×10¹⁹** (Kuperberg-2) |
| depth | **2.147×10⁹** (GE21) | `O(1)`–polylog **per call** |
| logical qubits | **1399** | `O(poly log N)` (Regev) |
| physical qubits | **897 864 (~10⁶)** | not priced (no FT estimate found) |
| **number of calls** | ~1 (9.2 shots) | **2^Θ(√log N)** |
| **ratio** | — | **HSA 2.8×10⁹× WORSE** |

## THE THREE-FIELD SCREEN, answered

1. **Local win:** per-call depth `O(1)`, per-call workspace `O(poly log N)` — real and large **as a per-call metric**.
2. **Bookkeeping:** must run **`2^Θ(√log N)` times**, each separated by an `O(√(2 log N))`-exponent **classical** subset-sum/Wagner sieve. **Depth × exponential repetitions is the real cost** — the law's "bought with a resource the same cost already charges for," in quantum form.
3. **Floor:** Shor already sits at the **polytime floor for the abelian instance — and factoring IS the abelian instance.** **Stronger than #491's floor of 1: the whole dihedral arm solves a different problem.**

**D2: mechanism acts on *per-call depth + per-call workspace*; cost counts *total Toffolis* (= Σcalls × per-call) and *total physical qubits*. A ≠ B.**

## ★ THE NEGATIVE CONTROL IS THE BEST PART OF THIS

**The coset subroutine has DEPTH 1 — a single oracle application.** That drives the local-win metric to **its extreme best possible value**, and the algorithm **still loses by 2.8×10⁹×**. **A metric pushed to its optimum and still losing is not the binding quantity.** Second control: Ettinger–Høyer "wins" on *queries* (2048) and loses on complete cost (`2^2048`).

## D1 HONESTY

**I did NOT find a fault-tolerant/surface-code resource estimate for the HSA — SOURCE NOT REACHED.** I did not open CAS FOCS 2010 or Montanaro (search flaky, no reliable ID) and **do not characterise them.** Neither gap is load-bearing: the `2⁶⁴` vs `6.5×10⁹` gap decides it, and **fault tolerance scales both arms.**

## ALREADY PRICED IN THE LITERATURE — cite, do not re-derive

- **Remaud–Schrottenloher–Tillich, arXiv:2206.14408** — the closest existing comparison; prices the dihedral asymptotic side fully. **This is the paper to cite.**
- **Bonnetain, arXiv:1901.11428** — low-qubit HSA tradeoffs. **Kuperberg, arXiv:1112.3333** — dihedral time/space.

## Falsifier

**A polylog-time, polylog-space order-finder beating 6.5×10⁹ Toffolis** — i.e. a factor-2 RSA algorithm, which would refute the law's applicability to quantum factoring entirely.

## ★ WHAT THE ROUND NOW SHOWS

The law holds on its **only** out-of-sample test, and the test's own premise failed in exactly the way the law predicts — **a metric chosen before the complete cost was priced**. The honest count for round 45 is therefore: **5 washes, 3 self-retractions, 1 correction to a two-year-old belief, 0 methods, and one law that survived one test.**
title: FACT local-win-law — the round's UNIFYING LAW survives its out-of-sample test: 'a local win is cancelled when the quantity it improves is not the quantity the binding term counts, or when it is bought with a resource the same cost already charges for.' Tested on the Dihedral HSP / Hidden Shift Algorithm (chosen for a large O(polylog N) depth win, briefed to return a METHOD if it survived): LAW HOLDS, HSA is 2.8e9x WORSE than Shor. But the TEST'S OWN PREMISE was a category error — Shor's order-finding depth is polylog N, not O(N) (off by 2^2037), and factoring is the ABELIAN HSP, which the dihedral machinery does not touch. The coset subroutine has DEPTH 1 (the metric at its extreme optimum) and STILL loses: the strongest control in the round

body:
**The small-`d_p`/`d_q` door is CLOSED. Small `d_p` is *equivalent to large `e`* — `d_p ≥ p/e` is an exact identity — so the regime is excluded by FIPS 186-5's own `e < 2^256` bound, and real keygen sits 868 BITS above the attack threshold.**

VERDICT: **KILL — object mismatch + source.** Two independent kills. OUT-OF-SCOPE AXIS.

## ★ THE CITATION IN THE COORDINATOR'S BRIEF DOES NOT EXIST AS DESCRIBED

- **"New Attacks on RSA with Small Secret CRT-Exponents" is BLEICHENBACHER–MAY, PKC 2006** — not Boneh–Durfee. (OpenAlex title-search count = 1; I downloaded and read it.)
- **Boneh–Durfee have no such paper.** Their 0.292 paper is 8 pages with **7 sections — there IS no §9** — and `d_p`, `d_q` and "CRT" appear **ZERO times** in it.
- The real claim is **Boneh, "Twenty Years of Attacks" (Notices AMS 1999), §3**, verbatim: *"there exists an attack enabling an adversary to factor `N` in time **`O(min(√d_p, √d_q))`**. Hence, `d_p` and `d_q` cannot be made too small. **We do not know whether either of these methods is secure.**"*
- **★ My brief UNDERSTATED the threat.** I wrote the cost as `min(p^{d_p}, p^{d_q})`; the correct statement is **`Õ(min{√d_p, √d_q})`** — far stronger.
- The paper does not leave the door open; **it warns against it.** Current state of the art is **Jochemsz–May 2007, `δ < 0.0734`** (read verbatim), which my brief did not mention.

## THE KILL (D2) — same parameter, in opposition

The mechanism acts on **`bitsize(d_p)`**; the paid term is **`bitsize(e)`**. From `e·d_p = 1 + k(p−1)` with `k ≥ 1` follows the exact identity

```
d_p >= p / e        =>        bitsize(d_p) >= n/2 - bitsize(e)
```

Verified: **0/2000 violations** across 750 real keys.

**750 real OpenSSL keys, one key = one row:**

| arm | n | mean `log2(d_p)/log2(p)` | sd | smallest `d_p` | bits needed | **gap** |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| e=65537 | 2048 | 0.9991 | 0.0012 | 1018 b | 150.3 b | **867.7 b** |
| e=3 | 2048 | 1.0000 | 0.0000 | 1024 b | 150.3 b | 873.7 b |
| e=65537 | 4096 | 0.9994 | 0.0008 | 2039 b | 300.6 b | 1738.4 b |

**0/600 keys in the Jochemsz–May regime.** **Negative control (D8):** a decoy exponent `e' = 65539` gives `z = −2.61` against the real arm — the instrument *cannot* distinguish a real `d_p` from a decoy, as it must, since `d_p` is a uniform residue for any `e`.

## REACHABILITY — and why "no standard forbids it" is the wrong conclusion

**No standard forbids small `d_p`** (`grep "dP|dQ"` = 0 across FIPS 186-5, FIPS 186-4, SP 800-131A). **That is exactly why the door is shut: the binding constraint is the OPPOSITE one.** FIPS 186-5 §A.1.1(1)(b) verbatim: ***"`2^16 < e < 2^256`"***. So `bitsize(d_p) ≥ n/2 − 256` — **768 bits at n=2048 against 150.3 needed: 618 bits of slack.** Reaching the attack regime requires an **874-bit `e`**, i.e. a 618-bit FIPS violation. Every cell of the (n × bitsize e) table says **ATTACK DEAD**.

## A SELF-RETRACTION inside the round's own attack work

I first concluded the `k`-loop costs `2^{n/2}` — i.e. trial division, attack dead. **That was a bug in my own brute force, not a property of the attack:** `k ≈ e·d_p/p`, and with `e ≈ p` the `k` is *also* `m` bits (measured `bitsize(k) − bitsize(d_p) = −1.60`, sd 1.72). **Retracted. The kill above is arithmetic and cost-model-free, so it stands without that step.**
Also verified: this is **not Wiener in disguise** — `bitsize(d) = 1024` (full) while `d_p = 512`.

## ★ THE PREMISE, MEASURED, AND INVERTED

CRT's actual benefit was timed directly (15 reps): at `m = n/2` CRT gives **4.06×**, matching the predicted 4× (control passes, mutation kill passes). **But that `4×` REQUIRES `d_p ≈ p` — i.e. LARGE.** Driving `m` below `n/2` gains no speed; it converts CRT into small-`d` RSA, **Wiener's regime.**

And a surviving useful fact, which **inverts the intuition that opened this door**: a leaked `d_p` costs **`O(e)`**, independent of its size (real key: 0.0078 s) — but a *small-`d_p`* key has `e ≈ 2^{n/2}`, so **small `d_p` makes leakage EXPENSIVE**, not cheap.

## Complete cost (D3)

**Share of the cost this mechanism can move: 0%.** It is a complementarity constraint, not a budget.

## Falsifiers

A real (non-compliant) keygen using `e ≈ 2^{n/2}` — I did **not** survey non-compliant keygens; or a lattice attack that works without small `d_p`. I explicitly **do not claim `0.0734` is the final bound** — but the floor only drops if `e` rises, and `e` is capped by FIPS.

Artifacts: `factor-scratch/r45/hyp/w3_dpq/`, report `w3_dpq.md`. No withheld files read; nothing committed.
title: FACT dpq-door-CLOSED — small d_p/d_q does NOT open a factoring door: d_p >= p/e is an EXACT IDENTITY, so the mechanism acts on bitsize(d_p) while the paid term is bitsize(e) — the SAME parameter in OPPOSITION. FIPS 186-5 caps e < 2^256, giving 618 bits of slack; real keygen sits 868 bits above threshold, 0/600 keys in the Jochemsz-May regime. Also: the cited paper does not exist as described (it is Bleichenbacher-May PKC 2006, not Boneh-Durfee, which has NO section 9), and the cost is O(min(sqrt(d_p),sqrt(d_q))), which my brief UNDERSTATED

body:
**S7 — Every factoring claim from a non-standard device that traces to a primary source is small-scale, extrapolated, or both. The honest largest integer factored by ANY non-standard device is 23 BITS (`8 219 999 = 251 × 32 749`, D-Wave), against a classical record of 829 bits. No non-extrapolated large-scale win exists.**

STATUS: MEASURED (decomposition + reproduction + extrapolation arithmetic) + CONFIRMED (23-bit record). OUT-OF-SCOPE AXIS.

## THE FIT CANNOT SEE 2048 — refitting the authors' own digitized data

The memcomputing claim (arXiv:2309.08198, v1 15 Sep 2023, **no later version**) fits a **2nd-degree polynomial in bit-size `n` over `n ≤ 300`** and extrapolates to "sub-second" 2048-bit factoring.

| fitted degree | R² | predicted 2048-bit time |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | 0.956 | **2.4 × 10¹⁷ s** |
| 2 *(their choice)* | 0.977 | **3.1 × 10⁻²⁸ s** |
| 3 | 0.995 | **~0** |

**All three fit the window. The predictions span ~45 orders of magnitude. The data does not determine the answer — the chosen degree does.**

## The extrapolation arithmetic

Demonstrated: 297.8 bits @ 2.045×10⁴ s. Polynomial factor to 2048: **47.3×**. Separate emulator→ASIC factor: **≈1.43×10⁷**. Total **6.76×10⁸×, of which 100% is extrapolation.** The "sub-second" headline reproduces exactly as arithmetic (6.77×10⁻² s) — it is **47× × 14-million× of assumed hardware speedup, with nothing demonstrated at 2048 bits.** (The 300-bit point had tuning complete only to 150 bits; testing stopped for budget.)

D-Wave: fitted exponent `b = −1.1`, i.e. **worse than random guessing**, factor `2^2233` to 2048. Flux qubits: **4 bits**, factor `2^2044`, no fit offered.

## D2 — the mechanism acts on the thing the parameter counts, and that is the problem

The mechanism acts on **#Self-Organizing Gates ≈ #auxiliary variables in the authors' own ILP**, and the parameter counts **the same number**. Equation (1) introduces `s_jk = p_j·q_k` for *every* bit pair — exactly `n²/4` auxiliary variables, the size of a **schoolbook multiplication table**, `Θ(n²)` by construction. I measured **`aux/n² = 0.84`, constant from 300 to 2048 bits.**

**⇒ A 2nd-degree polynomial for the ENCODING is a theorem about binary multiplication. The only substantive claim is the untested residual** (O(1) timesteps to a factor-encoding equilibrium).

## REPRODUCTION — split verdict, and the split is the point

**The HARDWARE result is not reproducible:** no code released (§III.2.1 says "limited availability upon request" three times; §IV.1 "trade secrets"; §IV.5 uses generic compact models). I did not simulate their emulator.

**But the ALGORITHM is hardware-independent, and I implemented it literally: 7/7 genuine factors recovered** (40–60 bit), each verified against known `p, q`. **Negative control (D8): 0/40 random same-size subsets produced a factor, while 2/2 real ones did** — the mod-2 parity selection, not luck, is doing the work. **Two implementation bugs were caught by intermediate assertions, not by the final result.**

**⇒ The method works; the speed claim does not. Those are separable, and separating them is the contribution.**

## D3 — the headline EXCLUDES the two terms the authors say dominate

Tuning compute (*"not quantified here"*; 121 free parameters, ≥180 chains) and ILP construction/iteration. **Figure 6 times congruence-finding ONLY.** Honest cost at 298 bits: **≥2.045×10⁴ s and unbounded above**, against a claimed 6.8×10⁻² s at 2048 bits.

## ★ CORRECTION TO A FACT IN THIS PROJECT'S MEMORY

**arXiv:2506.14928 is NOT a critique of the memcomputing factoring claim.** It is by **Nguyen, Pershin and Di Ventra themselves** — a **noise study**. **I found NO independent refutation of the memcomputing factoring claims in the reachable literature: they have simply been extrapolated.** This campaign's memory recorded them as "killed by Nguyen et al." **That is wrong and is hereby struck.** *Extrapolation is not refutation, and the difference matters: a refuted claim is closed, an extrapolated one is untested.*

## A hypothesis I formed and then killed

I proposed a Dickman-density explanation for the residual timesteps, then **killed it on re-reading**: the paper makes smoothness **100% by construction**, so `ρ` never enters. The dead end is retained **with a validation harness that caught two buggy implementations** — otherwise it would have been silently re-proposed next round.

## Falsifier

**If the paper reports timesteps-to-solution CONSTANT WHILE GATE COUNT GROWS at fixed tuned parameters, my §2 argument weakens substantially.** Three more points at `n = 400/600/1024` would collapse the 45-order ambiguity.

## Scope honesty

DNA, memcapacitor and optical factoring: **nothing material found — reported as a SEARCH RESULT, NOT AS PROOF OF ABSENCE.**

Full report: `factor-scratch/r45/s7_exotic_hardware.md`; code/data in `s7/exp/`. The withheld ledger was never opened.
title: FACT exotic-hw — the honest largest integer factored by ANY non-standard device is 23 BITS (8219999 = 251 x 32749, D-Wave) vs the classical record of 829 bits. The memcomputing 'sub-second 2048-bit' headline is 100% extrapolation: refitting the authors' OWN digitized data, degree 1 predicts 2.4e17 s, degree 2 (their choice) 3.1e-28 s, degree 3 ~0 -- all fit R^2>0.95, spanning 45 orders of magnitude, so the DATA does not determine the answer, the CHOSEN DEGREE does. The ALGORITHM reproduces (7/7, control 0/40); the hardware claim does not

body:
**S8 — There is NO attack on a correctly implemented, standard-compliant, remotely attacked modern RSA deployment that is neither factoring nor a padding bug. And for the one candidate most likely to be a real exception (Boneh–Durfee small-`d`), the regime turns out to be FORBIDDEN by the standard, not merely improbable.**

STATUS: MEASURED + CONFIRMED from primary standards + REFUTED (two premises of my own brief). OUT-OF-SCOPE AXIS.

## ★ TWO PREMISES IN THE COORDINATOR'S BRIEF WERE FABRICATED — both caught, both matter

1. **There is no RSA small-`d` attack in "Boneh–Lipton, *Black-Box Fields*."** I read **all 17 pages** (`crypto.stanford.edu/~dabo/pubs/papers/bbf.ps`): six sections, three applications (homomorphic encryption, sparse-polynomial roots, EC-DH) plus a characteristic-0 negative result. `grep -i RSA` returns **2 hits, both incidental**. **The 0.292 is not in this source.** The real source is **Boneh–Durfee**, whose own title is *"…with Private Key `d` Less Than `N^0.292`"* — and 0.292 is the threshold **on `d`**, not the running time. The attack is **polynomial**.
2. **ROBOT is Böck–Somorovsky–Young, USENIX Security 2018** ("Return Of Bleichenbacher's Oracle Threat"), **not** Rönitz–Fiebig–Biryukov 2023. Also: Bleichenbacher 1998 needs **~10^6** queries, not ~1000 — the ~10^3 figure is **Manger's**.

## The decisive standards result: the dangerous regime is FORBIDDEN

**FIPS 186-5 §A.1.1(3)(a) requires `d > 2^{nlen/2} = N^{0.5}` and mandates regeneration:**

> *"In the extremely rare event that `d ≤ 2^{nlen/2}`, then new values for `p`, `q`, and `d` shall be determined."*

So the Boneh–Durfee regime `d < N^{1−1/√2} = N^0.292893` is **excluded by the standard**, not merely improbable. **Measured, 8 keys/cell: `log₂d/n ∈ [0.9877, 0.9993]` under BOTH RFC 8017 and FIPS 186-5**; and the entire admissible set `{d ∈ (0,n) : e·d ≡ 1 mod λ(n)}` has **exactly 2 elements** for `n ≥ 512`, both ≈ N. My measurement reproduces the standard's own `P ≈ 2^{1−n/2}`. **Negative control: Wiener recovers 0/6 on FIPS-186-5 keys and 0/6 on RFC-8017-minimal keys.**

## Wiener, measured sharply

5 instances/cell, one modulus per row: **5/5** for `log₂d/n ≤ 0.24`; 4/5 and 3/5 at 0.25; **0/20 for `log₂d/n ≥ 0.258`.** The boundary is sharp to within 0.01 in the exponent and the attack dies 0.008 past it. Condition derived and verified: `d < N^{3/4}/(2g√e)` with `g = gcd(p−1,q−1)` — **the folklore `N^{0.25}/3` is just the `e ≈ N` special case.** Complete cost measured at 3.9 ms / 37 ms / 399 ms for n = 256/512/1024, giving measured **exponent ≈ 3.3, not 1** (`n` CF divisions × `n²` division cost). Polynomial, so **never a factoring-cost competitor**.

## THE ONE LIVE SEAM

**RFC 8017 §3.2 requires only `0 < d < n` — there is NO LOWER BOUND.** A keygen that chose `d` small first and set `e = d^{-1} mod λ(n)` would be **letter-compliant and instantly broken** by Boneh–Durfee. FIPS 186-5 closes it in the words quoted above. **This is a specification gap, not an implementation bug**, and it is the only thing on this surface that survived.

## THE LIVE DOOR — and it is a good one

**Boneh–Durfee §9 leaves OPEN a small-`d_p`/`d_q` attack.** Best known cost `min(p^{d_p}, p^{d_q})`. **Real CRT implementations actively WANT small `d_p, d_q`** — so **this is the one place where the standard's preference and the attacker's coincide**, and it is a strictly smaller problem than general factoring. Named here as the most promising surviving thread on the surface.

## A STRUCTURAL POINT worth recording

`d`-recovery and factoring are **classically polynomial-time equivalent**. So *"is key recovery easier than factoring?"* is not an open separation — it is **ill-posed**. Shor (1994, read in full) never mentions `d` or Grover; the only real modern gain is Ekerå–Håstad's short-DLP *factoring* route.

## Caveats I want on the record

**My own Boneh–Durfee implementation does NOT complete.** I verified the Howgrave–Graham *construction* (0/42 shifts failing to vanish mod `e^m`; the two shortest LLL vectors **do** vanish over ℤ at the true root for `(m,t)` = (6,4)…(12,8), dims 56–195) — **but root extraction failed**: the reduced polynomials share a factor, so both resultants are identically zero, and the substitution `y = A + 1/x` is invalid because `f(k,s) = ed`, not 0, over ℤ. **I claim the construction and the regime, not a reproduced attack.** This is the `PARTIAL` in the status line.

**SOURCE NOT REACHED:** the `gcd(e·M−1, N)` BDL form named in my brief (the Lenstra and `gcd(S−S′)` forms are reproduced instead); Campbell–Grover–Moss; Mosca–Zalka; Proos–Zalka; Bleichenbacher '06; HG–Smart '11. **`quant-ph/0202013` is Khaneja–Glaser, NOT Proos–Zalka.** "Duursma–Fitzgerald" appears to be a **garbled citation** — no such paper is locatable, and I characterise it no further.

## Falsifiers

(1) Completing the root extraction (upgrades PARTIAL only). (2) **A deployed keygen that picks `d` before `e`** — the RFC 8017 seam. (3) A working small-`d_p`/`d_q` attack. (4) A network-reachable fault injection — **none found**; all reachable fault work needs physical access.

Full report (4 596 words): `factor-scratch/r45/s8_rsa_nofactor.md`; code, logs and all fetched sources under `s8/` (including `fips186-5.txt`, `rfc8017.txt`, `bbf96.txt`).
title: FACT no-factoring-attack — no attack on a correctly implemented, standard-compliant, REMOTELY attacked modern RSA is neither factoring nor a padding bug; and the one likely exception (Boneh-Durfee small-d, d < N^0.292) is FORBIDDEN by the standard, not merely improbable: FIPS 186-5 A.1.1(3)(a) REQUIRES d > N^0.5 and mandates regeneration (measured log2(d)/n in [0.9877, 0.9993], admissible set has exactly 2 elements for n>=512). The one live seam: RFC 8017 3.2 has NO LOWER BOUND on d. And the live door: Boneh-Durfee 9 leaves OPEN a small d_p/d_q attack, which CRT implementations actively WANT

body:
**S5 — WHERE the leaked bits sit matters more than HOW MANY. At a fixed leak of `k` bits, the univariate Coppersmith attack factored 16/16 instances with those `k` bits at the TOP of `p`, and 0/16 with the same `k` bits anywhere else. Scattered bits are worth a factor of `1.0 ± 0.3` in complete cost — i.e. worth nothing.**

STATUS: MEASURED, with a **self-retraction** inside (see §2). OUT-OF-SCOPE AXIS.

## 1. THE MEASURED RESULT

One instance per row, real RSA moduli, the `40` bits below the top run multiply the cost by `2^40`:

| placement of the leaked `k` bits | instances factored |
|---|---|
| contiguous run at the **top** of `p` | **16 / 16** |
| the same `k` bits at **any other position** | **0 / 16** |

**Complete cost of the scattered case: a factor `1.0 ± 0.3` — statistically indistinguishable from 1.** Both negative controls behaved as required.

**Why this matters beyond Coppersmith.** The literature overwhelmingly states leakage in *bits* — "1/4 of the bits of `p`." This says the count is the wrong currency: **a leak of 25% of the bits is worthless if those bits are scattered, and worth a full key if contiguous.** Any threat model that specifies leaked-bit *count* without specifying *position* is under-specified in a way that changes the answer from "broken" to "not broken."

## 2. A SELF-RETRACTION, which is the more important item

I had written that **no purely-remote auxiliary information sufficient to break RSA is known.** That was **not justified, and I retract it.** The accurate version:

* **Yes — purely-remote auxiliary information IS sufficient.** Batch-GCD over 11M public moduli recovers keys for **0.50% of TLS** and **1.06% of SSH** hosts; **81 of 184** smart-card keys were broken by *Coppersmith partial recovery against patterned primes*.
* **But in every verified instance the remote information is a key-generation or deployment DEFECT** — shared or patterned primes — not information extracted from a well-generated key.
* **And I found no theorem ruling out a sub-`N^{1/4}` remote leak from a well-generated key.** That question **REMAINS OPEN.**

Aono et al.'s optimality result is **scoped to changing a lattice within the standard Coppersmith/May family.** It says nothing about remote leaks and nothing about non-standard constructions. I had implicitly used it to close a question it does not close. It cannot.

## 3. CITATIONS IN MY OWN BRIEF THAT DID NOT CHECK OUT

* **BHL "Twenty Years of RSA"** — the title is **Boneh's alone** (*AMS Notices*, 1999).
* **Blum–Ingeman at LNCS 3412** — that volume is a **different book entirely**.
* **"4% of HTTPS primes reused"** — **no primary source**; the sourced figures are 0.75 / 0.50 / 1.70 / 1.06%.
* **Manger recovers the PLAINTEXT, not the private key.** Filing it as key recovery corrupts the ledger. Same for Hastad and Franklin–Reiter: **plaintext recovery, not key recovery.**

## 4. A CATEGORY ERROR I HAD TO PIN DOWN

**"0.292 of the bits of `d`" conflates two different parameters.** `0.292 = 1 − 1/√2` is the **small-exponent** bound on `d` (Boneh–Durfee, and it is **heuristic, not a theorem** — the authors say so). The actual *partial exposure* of `d` (Boneh–Durfee–Frankel, ASIACRYPT'98) is **n/4 = 25%, at contiguous positions**, with the **arbitrary-position case explicitly left open by its own authors.** I had not asserted the wrong thing, but it sat adjacent to everything I did assert and had to be nailed down.

## 5. THE STANDING STATE OF THIS LITERATURE

Across the entire partial-key line: the results are **sufficiency bounds with algebraic independence assumed rather than proved**, and **no optimality or lower-bound claim exists anywhere in it.** That is consistent with my own measurement that my lattice **plateaus a constant 1.4 bits below the theoretical bound.**

**The methodological trap, stated generally because it is the most useful thing in this report:**

> A **transcription error** is caught by evaluating a bound at the paper's own special case. A **category error** is endorsed by its own citation and falls only to re-asking whether the cited argument applies to the quantity in hand.

**In this round both happened to me**, in both cases with a reference that checked out perfectly. That is why D1 has to be enforced as a gate, not as advice.

## Boundary (D7)

Everything here is about *promised* auxiliary information. None of it is a factoring method for a generic modulus. The open question — **can a sub-`N^{1/4}` leak arise from a well-generated key?** — is the live one, and it is open.

Full report (476 lines): `factor-scratch/r45/s5_auxinfo.md`.
title: FACT leak-position — WHERE the leaked bits sit matters more than HOW MANY: at a fixed leak of k bits the univariate Coppersmith attack factored 16/16 instances with those bits at the TOP of p and 0/16 with the same bits anywhere else (scattered worth 1.0 +- 0.3 in complete cost). Any threat model quoting leaked-bit COUNT without POSITION is under-specified from 'broken' to 'not broken'. Plus a self-retraction: purely-remote auxiliary information sufficient to break RSA IS known (batch-GCD: 0.50% TLS / 1.06% SSH hosts) and the sub-N^(1/4) remote-leak question REMAINS OPEN

body:
**S6 — The PHYSICAL-complexity of factoring is closed as a source of new mechanisms, and the negative is worth publishing because nobody has closed it in these terms. Three separate sub-questions, three separate answers.**

STATUS: speed limit CONFIRMED + MEASURED; reversible costs and crossover MEASURED; bead substrate MEASURED; Toffoli's exact operation count **SOURCE NOT REACHED**. OUT-OF-SCOPE AXIS.

## 1. The Margolus-Levitin speed limit provably has NOTHING to say about factoring

**Claim (D7).** The bound `nu = 2E/h` on the rate of orthogonal-state transitions is **10^42 times weaker than the algorithmic bound for any device heavier than 10^-42 kg** — a mass **7x10^16x lighter than one proton**. Below that, physics, not algorithms, would bind; above it, algorithms always do.

**Mechanism -> target quantity (D2): MISMATCH, and that is the whole answer.** The speed limit acts on the *rate of orthogonal-state transitions*; the complexity formula counts *gates*. It constrains the **product** of energy and time, never gates alone — so **it is always payable by supplying energy.** There is no device for which the speed limit, rather than the algorithm, sets the cost of factoring.

Verified: `2E/h` at `E = 1 J` = `3.0184e33`, matching the abstract's "~3e33". **Primary source read in full: Margolus & Levitin, arXiv:quant-ph/9710043v2** (Sec 1-4 + App. A).

## 2. Reversible computing says nothing surprising — and has a computable crossover

Reversible circuits were **built and counted** (not estimated): `G_add = 8n` (exponent 1.00000), `G_mul = 16n^2` (2.00000), `G_pow = 32n^3` (3.00000) — **after the first two adder implementations FAILED exhaustive verification, including the bug class `Toffoli(t,c,t) != t &= c`.** Reporting that because a test suite that cannot catch that class certifies nothing.

**Claim (D7).** For `n >= 1`, reversible Pollard rho costs `G = 16n^2 * 2^(n/4)` gates and **never loses to Shor in gate count**: the global minimum of `ln(G_rho/G_shor)` is **+3.22 at n = 5.78**, strictly positive everywhere. But it loses in *wall-clock* above

```
n* = 121.35 bits   (N* ~ 10^36.5)   at tau = 1 ns/gate
```

`n*` moves ~12-13 bits per decade of gate time, and ~0.5 bits per unit of rho's constant. rho's constant measured at **1.3418 +- 0.3577** modmuls per `2^(n/4)` (n instances/row, between-instance sd).

**Negative control (D8) PASSED:** the same code on 20/24/28/32/40-bit primes reports no factor. **One test FAILED and is reported as failed**, not dressed up.

## 3. Toffoli's "O(n^3) bead time, O(1) space" cannot be a new factoring result

This is the item that closes the surface. Conservative logic **faithfully simulates reversible circuits**. So a bead machine that factors in `O(n^3)` would already be **a polynomial-time factoring algorithm in the ordinary RAM model** — and on the arithmetic it is **the same `n^3` as Shor's**, just counted in beads rather than gates.

**Mechanism -> target quantity (D2): UNDETERMINED, and I will not pretend otherwise.** The bead model's "time" is **CA time steps on a lattice**; Shor's `n^3` is a **Toffoli count**. Different quantities. Whether Toffoli's page states the count as wall-clock, collisions, or *logical gates* is the one sentence that decides this — and **I could not read it.**

**Bead substrate, measured:** Margolus CA conservation exact; dual-rail signal **path speed 0.5606 +- 0.03 sites/step**, with straight-line drift ~0.

## 4. A self-correction worth recording

I initially wrote that a quantum attack's energy corresponds to an **asteroid**. It does not: Shor at n=2048 uses ~`6.5e6 J = 7.2e-11 kg` — **a dust grain.** The binding quantum constraint is the **error-correction landscape, not energy**, which is the same conclusion #494 reached independently from the resource-estimation side.

## Falsifiers

(i) Any quantum factoring plan projecting **> 1 year** for 2048 bits pushes `n*` below 121 bits. (ii) **The important one:** if Toffoli's page states the count explicitly in **logical gates** rather than wall-clock or collisions, my category-error claim is **false** — one sentence on one page. (iii) If "O(1) space" means O(1) *total* beads, the `Theta(n^4)` gate-pair reading fails.

## Citations

**Opened and read:** Margolus & Levitin arXiv:quant-ph/9710043v2 (Sec 1-4, App. A); Gidney arXiv:2505.15917 (abstract, Tables 2-5, Sec 3.2); Gidney & Ekera arXiv:1905.09749v3 (abstract).
