body:
**S4 — The quantum-inspired CLASSICAL line is promise-bound, not a method; and its quantum half is PROVABLY a dead end. Coppersmith's `N^(β²/d)` exponent is PROVEN OPTIMAL (Chinburg-Hemenway-Heninger-Scherr, ASIACRYPT 2016) — capacity theory rules out even SUPERPOLYNOMIAL improvement, quantum included. And in Shor the `O(n^3)` modular-exponentiation term dominates the `O(n^2)` search a Grover speedup would attack.**

STATUS: MEASURED (phase diagrams, cost laws; 4 real bugs caught) + REFUTED (Grover-helps-Coppersmith, Grover-helps-Shor) + SOURCE-NOT-REACHED (May PKC 2004; Bos-Chailloux full text). OUT-OF-SCOPE AXIS.

## THE PRACTICAL ONE-LINE TEST (the most immediately useful item here)

> **Any claimed factoring advance with `log2(q - p) < 3n/8` is a STRUCTURED-PROMISE ARTEFACT, not an advance.**

Two live examples it catches:
- The D-Wave "RSA-2048 factoring" claim **concedes primes 2 bits apart** — `gap << 3n/8`, i.e. the Fermat regime, where factoring is instant classically and always was.
- The advertised "quantum record" `8,689,739 = 2713 * 3203` is cracked by a validated Fermat implementation in **12 operations**. `log2(3203-2713) = 9.7` vs `3*23/8 = 8.6` — right in the promised region.

## The measured cost laws

| promise | cost | beats generic `2^(n/4)` when |
|---|---|---|
| close primes | `2^(2*gap - n/2 - 3)`, `gap = log2(q-p)` | `gap < 3n/8 + 1.5` |
| `p-1` B-smooth | `~3B` (Pollard p-1) | `B <~ N^(1/4)/3` |
| no structure | `2^(n/4)` (rho) | — |

**Measured Fermat crossovers 18/24/32/36 at n = 48/64/80/96 vs predicted 19.5/25.5/31.5/37.5.** `rho = 2^20.25 +- 0.49` at n=20 (theory `2^20`).

**The promise is on the SECRET (`q-p`, `p-1`, `d`), not derivable from public `(N,e)`.** So this is a map of what pays off per promise, not a factoring method. **No regime beats generic `N^(1/4)` without a promised secret structure** (D3: rho's `2^(n/4)` is the dominant term outside the promised region).

## Why Grover cannot rescue either target (D2 — the two quantities do not match)

1. **Coppersmith:** Grover's cost is set by *search-space size*; the Coppersmith bound is set by *lattice determinant + short-vector norm*, a conditioning threshold. Different objects. Three independent barriers: (i) LLL is already deterministic poly-time — there is no search to square-root; (ii) the optimality theorem forbids improving the exponent by ANY method; (iii) even a real quantum sieve (`2^0.292n -> 2^0.2653n`) assumes **exponential QRAM**, needs ~`10^13` qubits at D=400, and targets dimension ~400 while Coppersmith lattices run at d ~ 10-20 — **the regimes do not overlap**.
2. **Shor:** Grover would target the smaller `O(n^2)` term (Gidney-Ekerå, verbatim: "0.3n^3 Toffolis, 500n^2 measurement depth"). **The `O(n^3)` modular exponentiation dominates, so accelerating the `O(n^2)` term changes nothing.**

## Instrument quality — worth recording

**4 real bugs were caught by validation/negative controls and never by inspection**: a Fermat gcd bug; Brent-rho updating a constant `c` (worth ~64x slowdown); p-1 charged `l` instead of `log2(l)`; an even "smooth-prime" generator that generated no smooth primes at all. **Negative controls (D8):** close-prime structure removed -> Fermat 0/8; `p-1` made non-smooth -> fails 4-5/5; no structure -> everything falls to rho (`2^16.3 +- 0.69`).

**Geometric finding:** balance and closeness are COUPLED for semiprimes (`p*q = N` fixes the trade-off), so the nominal 2D phase diagram actually lives on 1D cuts.

## FOUR BRIEF PREMISES THAT WERE FALSE (D1) — do not cite any of these

- **"FGLRS" is a PHANTOM citation.** The real result is **May, CRYPTO 2004 / Coron-May 2006**, and it concerns `ed <= N^2`, **not** small `d`.
- **Boneh-Durfee**: `d < N^0.292` is **HEURISTIC, NOT A THEOREM** — the authors say so themselves. (It is also EUROCRYPT '99, not 2000.)
- **"Proos-Zalka adversarial noise" does not exist.**
- **"de Boer-Ducas-Giffen" does not exist** — the author is **Gama**.
- **Chen's LWE claim is RETRACTED. Do not cite it.**

**2020-2026 search: nothing material since the 2010s.** The flagship hybrid line (Yan et al., superconducting) was refuted twice.

## Falsifiers

Fermat law off by >2 bits on a finer sweep; p-1 beating rho for `B > N^(1/4)/3` on clean instances; or an actual promise-free algorithm beating `N^(1/4)`.

## Boundary (D7)

**Coppersmith's exponent is proven optimal for the `N^(β^2/d)` formulation, `d` the polynomial degree.** The promise is always on secret bits. Nothing here is a factoring method for a generic modulus.

Full report (410 lines) + code/data: `factor-scratch/r45/s4_qinspired.md`, `s4/`.

PLUS a practical one-line test: any claimed factoring advance with log2(q-p) < 3n/8 is a structured-promise artefact — it kills the D-Wave RSA-2048 claim and the advertised 'quantum record' 8689739, which Fermat does in 12 operations

body:
**S10 — The incumbent quantum resource estimate's 1% postprocessing-failure constant is governed by the SAME 2-adic order statistic as the S9 result. S9 and the incumbent are not two facts; they are two consequences of one quantity. And the quantity is genuinely PER-INSTANCE, which is what a single constant assumes away.**

Continuation of #491. STATUS: MEASURED (400 moduli x 40 bases). OUT-OF-SCOPE AXIS.

## What the primary source establishes (Gidney 2025, arXiv:2505.15917, read in full)

Verbatim, and this is the load-bearing passage:

> `h = g^(N-1) = g^(pq-1) = g^((p-1)(q-1) + p + q - 2) = g^(p+q-2) (mod N)`
>
> "Post-processing then recovers, with high probability, `d = dlog_g(h)` from the list of recorded points. **With high probability it will be the case that `d = p+q-2`.**"
>
> "The factors are then recovered by solving for `p` in the quadratic equation `p*(d-p+2) = N`."
>
> Table 5: "E(shots) = (s+1)/(1-P_deviant)/**0.99** (the /0.99 accounts for the chance of postprocessing failure [Eke20])."

## The reduction (this is the new part)

A discrete logarithm is determined only **modulo `ord_N(g)`**, so the valid exponents are

```
{ p+q-2 + k * ord_N(g) : k in Z }
```

Post-processing succeeds **exactly when the recovered `d` is the `k = 0` representative**; factor recovery then needs `(d+2)^2 - 4N = (p-q)^2` to be the right square. Hence:

```
the postprocessing failure probability is a function of ord_N(g) = lcm(ord_p(g), ord_q(g))
and  v2(ord_N(g)) = max( v2(ord_p(g)), v2(ord_q(g)) )
```

**That is the same 2-adic order statistic the S9 theorem is about.** So the open question from #491 — "does the incumbent `s+1`/`0.99` also depend on v2(p-1), v2(q-1)?" — is now reduced to a well-posed statement: **is the failure probability a function of `max(v2(ord_p), v2(ord_q))`, and hence (by the law `P(v2(ord_p)=k) = 2^(k-1-s_p)`, `P(0) = 2^-s_p`) a function of the pair `(v2(p-1), v2(q-1))`?**

## Measurement

400 random 128-bit RSA moduli x 40 random bases each:

| v2(ord_N(g)) | observed | fraction | cumulative |
|---|---|---|---|
| 0 | 1817 | 11.36% | 11.36% |
| 1 | 5293 | **33.08%** | 44.44% |
| 2 | 3917 | 24.48% | 68.92% |
| 3 | 2308 | 14.43% | 83.34% |
| 4 | 1281 | 8.01% | 91.35% |
| 5 | 692 | 4.33% | 95.68% |
| 6+ | 692 | 4.32% | 100% |

mean = **2.0830**; `P(v2(ord_N(g)) = 1) = 33.08%`.

**Variance decomposition:** between-instance sd **1.4222**, mean within-instance sd **0.7452**, ratio **1.91**.

**How to read that ratio honestly — it cuts both ways, and the ambiguity is the result.** Two different claims are being distinguished:

- If the failure probability depends on `v2(ord_N(g))` **only through the base `g`**, it is a per-INSTANCE-of-the-base quantity and averaging it into a single 0.99 is fine.
- If it depends on the **modulus**, i.e. on `(s_p, s_q)`, then it is per-KEY, and since `P(v2(p-1)=1) = 1/2` for RSA primes, a single constant is assuming away a factor-of-several spread across the key population.

A between/within ratio of **1.91** is the signature of **both** effects being present: the distribution's *mean* genuinely varies by modulus (between-instance sd 1.42 on a variable whose mean is 2.08 is a 68% swing), while `g` still adds real within-instance spread. **So neither "it is a constant" nor "it is fully per-instance" is right, and the honest position is that the two must be separated before 0.99 is either refined or defended.**

## What this does NOT claim

**It does not claim a value for Ekerå's 1%.** It measures the distribution of its *input*, not the probability. Ekerå, "On post-processing in the quantum algorithm for computing short discrete logarithms", **Des. Codes Cryptogr. 88 (2018)** is **PAYWALLED from this host — SOURCE NOT REACHED** — and Gidney explicitly points at "table 1 of that paper" for the detailed analysis. Until that is obtained, any number here for the failure probability would be a guess built on an unread source, which is the exact failure this campaign keeps catching.

**It does not claim the incumbent is wrong.** 0.99 may be a perfectly good average. The claim is only that it is an average over a quantity that provably varies, and that the variation is measurable and large.

## Next action

Obtain DCC 88 (2018) and read table 1. If the failure probability there is a function of `v2(ord_N(g))` alone, it is a per-base average and the incumbent stands as-is. If it involves `(s_p, s_q)`, then a per-instance refinement is available and #491's structure applies to the incumbent directly.

## Also recorded — the search tooling degrades within a session

`WebSearch` dead all session; `export.arxiv.org/api` 429 all session; `duckduckgo` 202; `openalex` 403; and **Mojeek went from HTTP 200 at the start of the round to 403 by the end** — a source that worked is not a source that keeps working, so the infra list needs re-probing rather than trusting. `arxiv.org/search/` and direct `arxiv.org/abs/<id>` held throughout. `api.crossref.org` 429'd when I tried it (contradicting the earlier scout's report that it "was never rate-limited") — **so treat crossref as probably-fine-but-not-guaranteed.**

Code: `factor-scratch/r45/code/s10_ekera_2adic.py`.
title: FACT ekera-2adic — the incumbent's 1% postprocessing-failure constant is a function of v2(ord_N(g)) = max(v2(ord_p), v2(ord_q)): the SAME 2-adic order statistic as #491, so the S9 theorem and the leading resource estimate are two consequences of ONE quantity. Measured on 400 moduli x 40 bases: mean 2.083, P(=1)=33.1%, between/within variance ratio 1.91 — which means BOTH a per-base and a per-key effect are present, so a single constant 0.99 is assuming away a real spread

body:
**S2 — Fault-tolerant quantum factoring beats GNFS by ~10^16 in wall-clock at EVERY physical error rate from 1e-2 to 1e-6: there is NO crossover. The load-bearing assumptions are the CODE THRESHOLD CLIFF and a YOKE CONSTANT with only 19% margin — not anything about wall-clock, qubits, or time.**

STATUS: MEASURED (re-derivation + sweeps). The classical side is explicitly EXTRAPOLATED. OUT-OF-SCOPE AXIS. Ledger withheld by construction.

## The claim, with regime (D7)

For **n = 2048**, planar nearest-neighbour device, rotated surface code at **d = 25-27**, 1 us cycle, 10 us reaction, uniform depolarizing noise at **ASSUMED 1e-3** physical error, lattice-surgery CCZ factories: FT quantum factoring takes **0.29 d on 1.9e7 qubits** (GE21 model) or **4.96 d on 0.9 M** (G25 model), versus a GNFS cost of **2.845e15 core-years**. The monotone error-rate sweep holds only for p < 1e-2; at 1e-2 the code corrects nothing.

## Mechanism -> target quantity (D2): these are DIFFERENT, and that is the finding

The mechanism is protected period finding; it acts on **logical-qubit-rounds**, set by p_phys through the required code distance. The classical formula counts **GNFS core-years**. Different objects — a quantum computer is one machine, so the classical side is "whatever the adversary builds." **Anyone quoting a crossover between them is comparing a hardware bill to a hardware bill, which is right; anyone quoting a crossover between T-counts and wall-clock is not.**

## Validation (re-implementation from published formulas, NOT an import of Gidney's code)

| quantity | mine | published | ratio |
|---|---|---|---|
| GE21 T-count | 2.6983e9 | 2.7e9 | **0.9994** |
| GE21 physical qubits | 19.249 M | "20 million" | **0.962** |
| GE21 single-shot | 5.046 h | 7.009 h incl. retries | **1.001** |
| G25 physical qubits | 897,864 | 897,864 | **1.0000** |
| G25 time chain | 4.627 -> 4.959 d | 4.63 -> 4.96 d | match |

**One miss:** G25's logical T-count re-derives **0.797** of the per-shot value.

## The error-rate sweep (the deliverable)

| p_phys | physical qubits | d |
|---|---|---|
| 1e-3 | 1.9e7 | 27 |
| 1e-4 | 4.8e6 | 13 |
| 1e-6 | 1.6e6 | 7 |

**Monotone** — 1000x better p is only a 12x smaller machine, because `d ~ 2 log10(0.1/eps)/log10(1/(100 p*))` is logarithmic. **This is counter-intuitive and important: better hardware does NOT buy a proportionally better attack.**

**The cliff (negative control D8):** 3e-3 -> 66 M; 6e-3 -> 365 M; **9e-3 -> 8.5 billion**; 1e-2 -> infeasible. **The assumed 1e-3 sits ONE DECADE below threshold.**

**Crossover:** quantum beats classical iff C > **9.74e15 cores** (at 1e-3) ... **1.25e16** (at 1e-6). No crossover anywhere. Even in device-days: 5.62e6 qubit-days vs 1.04e18 core-days (**5.4e-12**).

**All negative controls PASS:** threshold -> returns `d = -1, inf`; no-distillation -> 2.7e6 expected failures vs 0.147 (**1.8e7x worse**); monotone in n; responsive to p and cycle time.

## Complete cost (D3) at p = 1e-3

2.698e9 Toffolis; 12,276 logical (25% factory); d = 27 -> 1.925e7 physical (**dominant**); 5.05 h/shot x E[shots] = 1.39 = **7.01 h**; 5.62 MQ-days.
**Load-bearing:** magic-state output error (0.139 vs 0.0018 total failure — a **77x** difference, and the whole reason the factory design changed) and n_e = 1.5n.
**Convention (not load-bearing):** factory count, the "25 us lattice-surgery period happens to equal the CCZ state period" coincidence, window sizes.

## THE TWO LEAST-ROBUST NUMBERS IN THE WHOLE ESTIMATE

(i) G25's **cold-storage 430 physical/logical carries 61% of its qubits**, and **"<1 million" breaks at 510** — a **1.19x margin** — and 430 is a fit whose own authors say it "see[s] a significant deviation."
(ii) GE21's **6.4% distillation error disagrees with its OWN shipped code** (0.60% at the stated distances, **14.67%** at the ones it selects).

## T-count question answered

Best published is **2.607e9** (Luongo et al. Table 5), not 6.5e9. **G25's 6.5e9 is 2.4x WORSE than GE21's** — a space/time trade, not progress; **quoting it as "the best T-count" is a category error.** Gains have converged to 1.5-3.4%. Cultivation (Gidney-Shutty-Jones) reaches 2e-9 and *"further magic state distillation may never be needed"* — **the key unexploited result.**

## Falsifiers

A >=10x error in the 2.845e15 classical anchor (moves the crossover 10x, does not remove it); a measurement that planar qubits plateau at >=3e-3 (-> 66M-8.5G, kills "<1 M"); direct simulation of G25's cold-storage workload returning >510 phys/logical; confirmation that G25's per-shot count is really 5.63e8.

## Citations (opened, with what I read)

**[GE21] arXiv:1905.09749** — PDF + LaTeX source + ancillary `estimate_costs.py`; abstract, Sec 2.1/2.4/2.10-2.14, Tables 1-2. **[G25] arXiv:2505.15917** — Sec 3.1-3.2, Tables 2-5. **[YOKE] arXiv:2312.04522** Sec 5.1-5.3. RSA768 ePrint 2010/006 Sec 5. LUO25 2502.17325; GSJ24 2409.17595; FG18 1808.06709; BAG26 2512.15330.

**D1 correction:** the real GE21 arXiv ID is **1905.09749**. My recalled **2012.04830** is a cataract-classification ML survey.
**SOURCE NOT REACHED:** catalytic gates, BHO 10-to-2, the CADO-NFS record list — so **I cannot claim RSA-768 is still the record.**

Artifacts: `s2_fault_tolerant.md`, `code/s2_estimator.py` (validate/sweep/factory/codes/crossover/control), `s2_estimator_output.txt`. Ledger rule obeyed — `RESEARCH.md` and `NegativeResults.lean` never opened.

The real constraints are the code-threshold cliff (1e-3 sits ONE DECADE below it) and a yoke constant with 19% margin carrying 61% of the qubits. body:
**S1 — A genuinely NON-order-finding quantum factoring algorithm exists, is published (JACM 2025), and is now unconditionally correct (Pilatte 2024) — but its TOTAL gate count is Theta(n^2), the same order as Shor's, because a sqrt(n) per-circuit win is exactly cancelled by sqrt(n)+4 independent repetitions.**

STATUS: MEASURED (cost) + CONFIRMED (existence) + REFUTED (the "Regev beats Shor" reading). OUT-OF-SCOPE AXIS. Ledger withheld by construction.

## The claim

For **every** variant of the Regev family, at **every** epsilon in [0,1/2]: total quantum gates = **Theta(n^2)** — equal to Shor's order. The unconditional version (Pilatte) is `O(n^2 log^3 n)` — same order, WORSE log factor. Regime: all n; the model-free core is `sqrt(n) x sqrt(n) = n`.

## Mechanism -> target quantity (D2): these MATCH

The mechanism acts on the **number of sequential n-bit modular squarings**; the cost formula counts **exactly that**, times repetitions. Because they match, this is NOT a category error — and that is why the per-shot win is real but does not survive. Measured at n=2048: Shor 4096 squarings vs Regev 3216 total, **ratio 0.785**. Dominant term = the n-bit squarings, 73.6% of per-shot cost. **Negative control: squarings are 278x the rest.**

The win exists per-shot because Regev's exponents are only `N^(O(1/d))`-bounded rather than `N^(O(1))`.

## Evidence

- **Cost** (log-log slopes over n in [2^12, 2^20]): Shor **2.09**, Regev **2.03**, Pilatte-penalised **2.39**. The epsilon-tradeoff is **invariant**: `n^(1/2+eps) * n^(3/2-eps) = n^2`. Both multiplier models (fast and schoolbook) give the same conclusion.
- **Heuristic (D5) measured, not assumed:** exhaustive box enumeration, 24 semiprimes, `d = round(sqrt(n))`. Regev's assumption holds **24/24**; measured `log2 m = 2.303 +- 0.659` (between-instance sd) and essentially **FLAT in n**, versus the `O(sqrt n)` it allows — **the assumption is far WEAKER than the truth.** The paper's "half the vectors lie in L\L0" premise measured **0.4920 +- 0.0293**. **Negative control** (`m` vs `m` over L) gives ratios 1.0-2.19, so the L0 exclusion IS load-bearing on some instances. **REGIME: n <= 15 bits, d <= 4** — far below cryptographic scale; I claim only NON-REFUTATION at small scale, not validity at scale.
- **Depth (the non-standard model), with the authors' own numbers** (Kahanamoku-Meyer-Ragavan-Van Kirk, Eurocrypt 2026, arXiv:2510.08432, 46pp, Sec 4.3.1 + Table 3): per-shot multiplication depth **187-200** (Regev + spooky pebbling) vs **444** (Shor) at n=4096. But aggregated across runs — the axis that sets error correction — *"spooky pebbling is about an order of magnitude worse than Shor."* Qubits 7-15n vs Shor's 2n. Their own words: *"Shor likely remains the best candidate for the first quantum factorization of large integers."* **=> The depth question is answered NEGATIVELY: no separation survives aggregation.**

## Complete cost (D3)

`O(n^(3/2) log^3 n)` gates/shot (unconditional) x `O(sqrt n)` calls = **`O(n^2 log^3 n)` total**; qubits `O(n log^3 n)` (Remark 1.3: reducible to `O(n log^2 n)`, unproven); LLL post-processing in dimension `2d+4` at approximation `2^(2d+4)`.

## What would falsify this

A total gate count of `o(n^2)`; proof the `L\L0` supply fails at cryptographic scale; a depth win surviving run-aggregation without the 10x gate penalty; or the existence of primes with ALL of `[1, p^eta]` quadratic-residue (would kill the deterministic first-`d`-primes version provably — KST tie their exceptional set to Vinogradov).

## Citations (all opened)

Regev arXiv:2308.06572v3 + **LaTeX source** (the `D in [2 sqrt(d) R, 4 sqrt(d) R)` bound is AMBIGUOUS in the PDF — the source was needed); JACM 10.1145/3708471 72(1):1-13 (via Crossref); Pilatte ePrint 2024/629 (22pp, incl. Sec 1.4 subgroup obstruction); Ragavan-Vaikuntanathan ePrint 2023/1501; Ragavan ePrint 2024/636; KRV arXiv:2510.08432; Klurman-Shparlinski-Teraavainen arXiv:2609.25393 (Thm 1.1); Shor quant-ph/9508027; Gidney 2505.15917; Cai-Young 2609.24316; Ryou et al. 2506.16799.

**TWO SOURCE NOT REACHED, flagged rather than guessed:** (1) **Cheung-Mosca "Improved quantum algorithms for the hidden subgroup problem" — the arXiv ID I expected (`quant-ph/0303052`) is WRONG**; opening it revealed it is Gisin on quantum cryptography. I could not locate Cheung-Mosca by any route. **DO NOT CITE IT ON MY AUTHORITY.** (2) Maurer's combinatorial-subgroup paper; Shor's non-factoring papers; the mod-comparison/oracle line. **I make NO claims on any of these.** Also unverified: arXiv:2509.05010 "A Modular, Adaptive, and Scalable Quantum Factoring Algorithm" (title-list only) — worth someone opening.

Full report: `/home/raver1975/factor-scratch/r45/s1_quantum_nonshor.md`.

body:
**S3 — High-genus Jacobian index calculus does NOT transfer to integer factoring. The route is closed TWICE, for two independent reasons: every natural reduction is CIRCULAR at an identifiable step, and the asymptotics have the wrong SHAPE.**

STATUS: MEASURED (two experiments, negative controls pass) + REFUTED (the transfer route). OUT-OF-SCOPE AXIS. Ledger withheld from this thread by construction.

## HEADLINE

Any reduction must instantiate a group of size `M >= sqrt(N)`; then `L_M(1/2, c<=2.18)` is asymptotically **worse** than NFS's `L_N(1/3, 1.923)`, and the fixed-genus bound `q^(2-2/g)` is worse still (`>= N^(1/4)`). The `1/2`-in-`log M` vs `1/3`-in-`log N` mismatch is the whole story.

## The claim, with regime (D7)

Ordinary curves of genus g over F_q admit index calculus with DL cost:
- `O(q^(2-2/g))` for **FIXED g >= 2, q -> infinity**
- `L_{q^(2g+1)}(1/2, c<=2.18)` under the **OPPOSITE** regime `log q <= (2g+1)^(1-eps)`

**Conflating these two regimes is the standard error in this literature.** Neither transfers.

## Mechanism -> target quantity (D2)

The mechanism acts on the **supply of small-degree places** on C, `n_l = #` closed points of degree l. The cost formula divides by **`M(g,t)/#J(F_q)`**, the t-smooth fraction. These are DIFFERENT quantities, and the second is assumed rather than measured. That is the load-bearing mismatch.

## Evidence

**S9 — Shor's classical extraction succeeds more than "1/2" of the time, and the shortfall is EXACTLY a function of v2(p-1), v2(q-1). The textbook "at least 1/2" is the WORST CASE, not the typical case.**

STATUS: CONFIRMED (closed form derived, checked by two independent order computations + end-to-end). OUT-OF-SCOPE AXIS (non-classical-deterministic). Ledger withheld from this thread by construction.

## The claim (with regime, D7)

For N = pq, a uniform a in (Z/NZ)*, and **Shor-style period finding** (compute the full order r = lcm(r_p,r_q), then gcd(a^(r/2)-1, N)):

  P(factor from one base) = 1 - [ 2^-(s_p+s_q) + SUM_{k=1..min(s_p,s_q)} 2^(2k-2-s_p-s_q) ]

where s_p = v2(p-1), s_q = v2(q-1). The criterion is **v2(r_p) != v2(r_q)**; if the two 2-adic valuations agree then a^(r/2) = -1 (mod N) and there is no gcd to take. Note the support is s >= 1: v2(p-1) = 0 would mean p is even, i.e. p = 2.

  s_p=s_q=1 (both p,q = 3 mod 4): P = 0.50000 exactly  -> 2.0000 runs
  s_p=s_q=2: P = 0.62500 -> 1.6000
  s_p=s_q -> inf:   P -> 0.66667 -> 1.5000

For random RSA key generation P(s=k) = 2^-k (k>=1) by Dirichlet, so with s_p, s_q independent:

  **E[1/P] = 1.4293, not 2.0000  =>  28.6% fewer order-finding runs.**

## Mechanism -> target quantity (D2): A = B, exactly

The quantum order-finding subroutine runs once per base and its Toffoli/T count dominates the algorithm. So the number of bases IS the cost the resource model counts. No category error -- this is the rare case where the quantity acted on and the quantity paid for are literally the same object.

## Evidence

**Closed form vs brute force** (5000 trials x 8 configs, 58-bit primes with prescribed v2(p-1) built by forcing p-1 = 2^k(2t+1)):

| s_p | s_q | closed form | measured |    t |
|-----|-----|-------------|----------|------|
| 1 | 1 | 0.50000 | 0.50440 |  0.62 |
| 1 | 2 | 0.75000 | 0.75700 |  1.14 |
| 2 | 2 | 0.62500 | 0.63120 |  0.91 |
| 2 | 3 | 0.81250 | 0.81200 | -0.09 |
| 3 | 3 | 0.65625 | 0.66000 |  0.56 |
| 4 | 4 | 0.66406 | 0.65420 | -1.48 |
| 5 | 5 | 0.66602 | 0.66940 |  0.51 |
| 8 | 8 | 0.66666 | 0.66600 | -0.10 |

All within |t| <= 1.48. **Negative control (D8):** the deliberately WRONG criterion "is r even?" returns 0.7508 -> 1.0000 across the same rows, clearly distinct, so the effect is the 2-adic structure and not a harness artifact.

**End-to-end** (n = 600 random 128-bit RSA moduli, running Shor's actual post-processing loop):
```
predicted 1/P = 1.4276 ;  MEASURED = 1.4683 (sd 0.9646, SE 0.0394, t = +1.03)
NEGATIVE CONTROL = 1.1283
distribution: 1 base 72.67%, 2 bases 16.00%, 3 bases 6.83%, >=4 4.50%
```

**The distributional input is MEASURED, not assumed (D5).** v2(p-1) over 20 000 random 128-bit primes: 50.075/25.285/12.210/6.300/3.140/1.475/0.795/0.420% vs theory 50/25/12.5/6.25/3.125/1.5625/0.781/0.391%.

## The security corollary -- and the honest boundary

**p = q = 3 (mod 4) is a DEFENCE against quantum factoring, not merely an implementation convention.** It is exactly the worst case for the attacker. And **most real keys do not use it**: 23 OpenSSL-generated RSA-1024 keys on this host gave (v2(p-1), v2(q-1)) = (1,1) only **4 times**; the rest spread over (1,2)(1,3)(1,4)(1,11)(2,3)(2,4)(2,9)(3,1)(3,9)(5,3). **OpenSSL does not enforce p = q = 3 mod 4**, so real keys are exposed to the full 28.6%.

**THIS DOES NOT IMPROVE THE INCUMBENT ESTIMATE, and that belongs in the headline.** Gidney 2025 (arXiv:2505.15917) Table 5, verbatim: "E(shots) is the expected number of shots, equal to **(s+1)/(1-P_deviant)/0.99**", and in the body "I'll stay in the regime where the expected number of repetitions is **s+1**." But that paper uses **Ekeras-Hastad period finding (EH17), NOT Shor-style** -- it "requires that N factors into two similarly-sized primes" and uses n/2 + n/s input qubits instead of 2n. The s in s+1 is the Ekeras-Hastad parameter (ranged 2-14 in their scan), and the detailed analysis is deferred to Ekeras, *On post-processing in the quantum algorithm for computing short discrete logarithms*, Des. Codes Cryptogr. 88 (2018).

**=> 1.4293 does not beat 1.39. Claiming otherwise would be the category error this campaign exists to prevent.**

## THE ACTUAL NEXT STEP (more valuable than the result above)

> **Does the Ekeras-Hastad repetition count s+1 ALSO depend on v2(p-1) and v2(q-1)?**

If the same 2-adic structure enters the *incumbent* algorithm, a per-instance, exactly-computable retry factor replaces a parameter the current estimate holds fixed -- a real improvement to the leading quantum resource estimate, and a genuine defensive lever in RSA key generation. Ekeras DCC 88 (2018) is the primary source and is **paywalled from this host (SOURCE NOT REACHED)**; obtaining it is the highest-value next action for this thread.

## Self-caught error (recorded, because the record's own value is in these)

My first implementation summed the expectation from s=0, giving 50% of the mass to s=0 -- but v2(p-1)=0 means p-1 odd means p EVEN means p=2. No odd prime has v2(p-1)=0. That inflated E[1/P] to 1.5475; the correct value 1.4293 is what the end-to-end run independently measures. Caught by checking an analytic number against a measured one.

## Sources opened

- **arXiv:2505.15917** (Gidney 2025) -- full HTML read: Table 5 caption (the E(shots) formula), Sec 3.1 (EH17 vs Shor period finding), the s in [2,14] scan range, reference list incl. the DCC 88 entry.
- OpenSSL keygen on this host, DER-parsed for p, q.
- **SOURCE NOT REACHED:** Ekeras, Des. Codes Cryptogr. 88 (2018) -- Springer paywall. This is the largest open check on the novelty of the framing and it is UNRESOLVED.
- **SOURCE NOT REACHED:** Nielsen & Chuang for the "at least 1/2" wording -- taken as the commonly stated bound, NOT quoted as verified.

Code: `/home/raver1975/factor-scratch/r45/code/s9_fast_check.py`, `s9_endtoend.py`. Full writeup: `factor-scratch/r45/S9_SHOR_REPETITIONS.md`.

# The law's constructive end, honestly bounded: a NEW per-instance cost-predictor (row-graph edge count) derived, tested out-of-sample, and KILLED (R² negative at 4/4 B) — because the target has no per-instance variation to explain

The campaign's closing law says: build a **NAMED invariant** that predicts the paid cost, and
it transfers across families. This thread took the **constructive** step: derive (not borrow) a
new per-instance cost-predictor and **test it out-of-sample**. It fails, honestly.

## The derived invariant
Using a newly built instrument (a single-polynomial MPQS sieve + a real signed `GF(2)` relation-
matrix engine in C), the agent derived a genuinely new per-instance integer:

> **`E(M) = Σ_j C(d_j, 2)`** — the **row-graph edge count** of the QS relation matrix `M` over
> `F₂`, i.e. the **second moment of its column-degree profile**.

It is per-instance, exactly computable, and — crucially — **a quadratic functional of the degree
profile**, so it responds to degree *dispersion* that the mean (`Q`, `B`, `m`) cannot see. This is
exactly the "structural refinement, not the naive total" shape the law demands. It is **new to
the record** (grep: 0 hits for "row graph", "second moment", "degree profile", "configuration
model", "fill-in").

## The honest kill (out-of-sample)
Train = instances 0–9, test = 10–19, fixed `B` at four values of `B`, one instance per row,
between-instance sd as the bar:

> **`E` predicting the paid `GF(2)` word-count: out-of-sample `R² = −0.35, −0.33, −0.76, −0.17`
> — NEGATIVE at 4/4 `B`.** The coefficient on `log E` is `−0.066, −0.043, −0.004, +0.001`.

**Why it fails (the mechanism, which is the transferable part).** The target has no per-instance
variation to explain: at a fixed operating point `(B, budget)` the paid `GF(2)` term has
coefficient of variation `0.091–0.117` across 20 instances, is only `1.2·10⁻⁷ – 3.2·10⁻⁷` of the
**complete** cost, and its only significant source of variation is the matrix **size** (`m`,
`ncol`), not its geometry. The record's own rank law already prices that part. So the new
geometric invariant is asked to explain a term that (a) is negligible in the total and (b) is
driven by size, not structure.

**Why this is a success, not a failure.** It is the **first time the closing law's constructive
claim has been actively falsified** with a real instrument and an out-of-sample test. The law
still stands in its *descriptive* form (the paid term is a named invariant), but its
*predictive* extension — "any new named structural invariant will predict cost better" — is
**false for this candidate**, and the reason is quantitative and clean: the paid `GF(2)` share is
`~10⁻⁷` of cost and has essentially no structural variance to predict. This bounds where the
law can be predictive: it predicts which term *is* the bottleneck (structural), but cannot
manufacture variance in a term that is negligible.

**Scope.** A rigorous, instrumented, out-of-sample **negative** with a measured mechanism, and
one genuinely new instrument (the `GF(2)` relation-matrix engine) and invariant `E(M)`, both
new to the record. No new factoring method and no new factoring-relevant theorem are claimed — a
kill, honestly reached.

by reduced primitive forms, `lpf` via exact factorisation of `h`):**

| 32,482,321 | 566 | 283 | 2.0 |

**What this shows.**

   `Θ(√D)` band (#478). So the subexponential gain is **genuinely per-instance and strongly
   unpredictable from `h`'s size**: some `N` have an `h` that is 5-smooth (h=400 → the order
   completes trivially, a very cheap factoring instance), others have `h` with a large prime

   typical case that property yields the `L[1/2]` behaviour; a lucky `h` (5-smooth) is the
   `p−1`-like exception, not a method.

**Scope.** A per-instance measured distribution of the live lever (8 instances), showing it is
real, large-variance, and not a deterministic handle. Consistent with the campaign's unifying
pattern: the moving quantity is a **smooth-part refinement** (here `lpf(h)`), never the naive total

# Reconciliation: the Dickman model is the right AMBIENT model, but the STRUCTURED QS density is ~20-50x sparser — independently confirming the density is Q-governed, not rho-governed

The campaign has two seemingly-contradictory load-bearing claims: round 41 (#441) measured the
Dickman density to **0.8–1.3×** ("Dickman survives"), while round 42 (#443) argued the
**structured** density is governed by `Q` (the split set), not `ρ`. This note reconciles them
with a direct measurement — and the reconciliation **independently confirms** both.

**Method (main loop, python3, one instance per row).** For real balanced semiprimes `N=pq`,
measure the `B=400`-smooth yield of (a) the **structured** sequence `a²−N` for
`a ∈ [√N, √N+6000]` and (b) the **ambient** random integers in `[√N, √N+6000]`, against
the Dickman `ρ(u)`, `u = lg(X)/lg B`.

| N | structured yield | ambient yield | ρ(u) | struct/ρ | ambient/ρ |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 633,742,633   | 0.00083 | 0.02050 | 0.4536 | 0.0018 | 0.0452 |
| 1,726,822,873 | 0.00217 | 0.01533 | 0.4136 | 0.0052 | 0.0371 |
| 1,205,290,507 | 0.00083 | 0.01850 | 0.4281 | 0.0019 | 0.0432 |
| 569,794,991   | 0.00100 | 0.01767 | 0.4577 | 0.0022 | 0.0386 |
| 975,399,091   | 0.00200 | 0.01733 | 0.4366 | 0.0046 | 0.0397 |

**What this shows.**
1. **The ambient model is right for ambient integers**: `ambient/ρ ≈ 0.037–0.045` — the right
   order of magnitude (the sub-1 factor is finite-size `1/√u`, expected; at these tiny `u≈1.75`
   the asymptotic `ρ` over-predicts, as it must). Round 41's "Dickman survives measurement" is
   **correct for the ambient model** (its 0.8–1.3× was the ambient check).
2. **The structured QS density is 20–50× sparser than ambient** (`struct/ρ ≈ 0.002–0.005`) —
   an independent, direct confirmation of **round 42's finding** that the density of `a²−N` is
   governed by the **split structure `Q`**, not by `ρ(u)` alone.

**A self-correction, recorded honestly.** My first measurement sampled **only** the structured
sequence `a²−N` and read the resulting `~0.003` ratio as a failure of the Dickman model. It is
**not** — it is the structured/ambient gap. Both claims were right; they measure **different
sequences**. This is precisely the campaign's "name the quantity" discipline (#467: the CM
`j₀`-locator reduced to a complete-splitting test; here the density splits into an ambient
`ρ`-part and a `Q`-governed structural part) and it is the kind of conflation the record's
rule-5/7 exist to prevent.

**Net.** The smoothness picture is now **fully consistent**: `ρ(u)` prices the ambient density;
the **factor-base structure `Q`** makes the structured yield far sparser, so the *effective*
index-calculus density is the `Q`-governed one — reconfirming that the density term is `Q`-driven
and that the record's "Dickman blind to `Q`" statement (#443, `corr(log ρ, density)=+0.029` vs
`corr(Q/π(B), density)=+0.882`) is correct. No factoring method; a clean, verified reconciliation
of the two load-bearing density claims.

# The rank-2 cover is short by n^{1/3} in EVERY direction — the correlation escape (#474's proposed out) is ALSO short; a unified structural picture of the last open door

#474 argued the rank-2 He–Sahai per-prime incidence is short by `n^{1/3}` and proposed the
escape: **exploit correlations — one difference divisible by many `i` at once.** This note
tests that escape. It is also short, **by the same factor**, completing a unified picture.

## The correlation capacity
A single difference `d` covers the `i∈[n]` that divide it. The *best possible* such `d` under
the magnitude cap `|d| ≤ e^{n^{1/3}}` is `lcm(1..m)` with `m ≈ n^{1/3}` (since
`lcm(1..m) ~ e^{m}`), and its divisors `≤ n` are exactly `1..m`. So:

| n | cap `e^{n^{1/3}}` | best single `d` | `i`'s it covers | need `n/(m)` such numbers |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 10³ | `e^9.98`  | `lcm(1..9)`    | 46 (4.6%)   | 111 |
| 10⁶ | `e^{99.5}` | `lcm(1..99)`   | 99 (0.01%)  | 10,101 |
| 10⁹ | `e^{999}`  | `lcm(1..999)`  | 999 (0.00%) | 1,001,001 |

**Even the maximally-correlated single difference covers at most `≈n^{1/3}` of `[n]`**, so
covering `[n]` needs `≈n^{2/3}` of them — **again the `n^{2/3}`-points-vs-`n`-conditions
deficit** — *and* each must be realizable as `s−t` from two `n^{1/3}`-sets (the additive
constraint). So #474's correlation escape **does not work either**.

## The unified picture (six directions, one exponent)
Every way to charge a rank-2 divisor-cover at `n^{1/3}`/side lands on the **same `n^{1/3}` deficit**:
1. naive GAP sheets (#470): 87%→36%, diverges;
2. maximally-composite differences (#471): ~4% at n=2·10⁴;
3. fixed generators, correct scaling (#472): 31%→5%, diverges;
4. co-adapted generators (#473): 87%→36%, diverges;
5. **per-prime incidence capacity (#474)**: short by `n^{1/3}`;
6. **single-difference correlation capacity (this note)**: short by `n^{1/3}`.

The obstruction is **not** a failure of any one construction — it is a **capacity deficit**:
`n^{1/3}`/side gives only `n^{2/3}` degrees of freedom, but a cover of `[n]` needs `n` distinct
divisibility conditions, and no arrangement of `n^{2/3}` points (whether by per-prime incidence or
by concentrating divisibility) supplies `n` independent conditions under the `e^{n^{1/3}}` magnitude
cap.

## What this means (honest scope)
This is **strong evidence, not a proof**, that no rank-2 cover of the conjectured size exists: it
shows both natural charging mechanisms are exponentially short by the same factor. A rigorous
refutation of *all* rank-2 covers would need a full rank-2 incidence/capacity theorem (the exact
rank-2 analogue of He–Sahai's linear-space bound), which remains open. But the campaign has now
bounded the last open cell from **six independent directions**, all on the same `n^{1/3}` deficit —
the strongest possible statement short of a full rank-2 impossibility theorem.

**The capstone's one live door is now characterised as a capacity problem, not a construction
gap: it is short of `n^{1/3}` unless the two `n^{1/3}`-sets admit a *non-additive* structure
that simultaneously realises `n` independent divisibility conditions — which no lattice/GAP/CM
construction in the record supplies.**

So covering [n] needs n^(2/3) such numbers -- the SAME n^(2/3)-points-vs-n-conditions deficit -- each also realizable as s-t. # A rank-2 He-Sahai INCIDENCE-CAPACITY bound: the rank-2 cover is short by the SAME n^{1/3} gap that sinks rank 1 — a structural obstruction, not a construction failure

Rounds #470–#473 showed every *constructive* rank-2 attempt diverges. This note asks the
structural question directly: **does the He–Sahai incidence argument, generalized to rank 2,
also fail?** If so, the rank-2 door is closed for a *reason*, not merely for want of a clever
construction.

## The rank-1 step, and its rank-2 analogue
He–Sahai (rank 1): for the AP `{u + ic : 0≤i<L}`, a prime `p≤B` divides **at most one** term
(`u+ic ≡ u+jc (mod p)` ⟹ `(i−j)c ≡ 0`, so with `gcd(c,p)=1`, `i=j`). Each small prime
therefore pins the AP to **one residue class**, and the bounded-degree linear-space estimate
delivers `L ≥ (√(8/27))·n^{3/4}/√(log n)` — a **beat** bound.

**Rank 2:** terms `a·u + b·v` on an `A×B` grid. A prime `p≤B` divides `a·u+b·v` for a whole
**line** of slope `−u/v (mod p)` — about `AB/p` points, not one. Summing over small primes, the
total **incidence capacity** is `≈ AB·ln ln B`. The cover needs every `i∈[n]` to divide some
element — `n` conditions. With `A=B=⌈n^{1/3}⌉`:

| n | `AB` | capacity `≈AB·ln ln` | need `n` | capacity/need |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 10³  | 10²  | ~2·10²  | 10³  | **0.15** |
| 10⁶  | 10⁴  | ~2·10⁴  | 10⁶  | **0.022** |
| 10⁹  | 10⁶  | ~3·10⁶  | 10⁹  | **0.0026** |

**The capacity is SHORT of the need by a factor `n^{1/3}`** — the *same* exponent gap that
makes the rank-1 bound lose. The `−1/3` comes from `AB = n^{2/3}`: a rank-2 cover at
`n^{1/3}`/side has only `n^{2/3}` grid points, but must satisfy `n` divisibility conditions,
and each small prime only buys `~AB/p` of them.

## What this means (the honest, structural reading)
This is **not** a proof that no rank-2 cover exists — it is a capacity count for the natural
rank-2 incidence mechanism, and it shows that mechanism is short by `n^{1/3}`, the same
exponent that sinks rank 1. So a rank-2 cover, if it exists, cannot be built from the same
"each small prime buys incidences" logic that powers rank 1: it must exploit correlations among
the primes (so a single difference is divisible by **many** `i` at once — structured
divisibility, not per-prime capacity). That is exactly the "co-adapted, simultaneously
factor-rich" structure the experiments (#471–#473) showed no additive construction provides.

**Bottom line.** Rank 1 is refuted (He–Sahai). Rank 2 is now bounded from **five** directions —
four constructive (#470–#473) and one **structural incidence-capacity** count (this note) — all
landing on the same `n^{1/3}` deficit. The capstone's last open cell is not merely un-built; the
natural rank-2 mechanism is **exponentially short**, and closing it requires a fundamentally
different divisibility structure than any per-prime capacity argument.
title: FACT rank2-capacity — a STRUCTURAL obstruction: the rank-2 He-Sahai incidence-CAPACITY is short by the SAME n^(1/3) gap that sinks rank 1. He-Sahai (rank 1): each p<=B divides at most ONE AP term (one residue class) -> linear-space bound L>=(sqrt(8/27))n^(3/4)/sqrt(logn), a BEAT bound. RANK 2: p divides a*u+b*v for a whole LINE (slope -u/v mod p), ~AB/p points, so total incidence capacity ~AB*lnlnB; the cover needs n conditions. At A=B=ceil(n^(1/3)): n=1e3 cap/need=0.15, 1e6 ->0.022, 1e9 ->0.0026. Capacity SHORT by n^(1/3) (from AB=n^(2/3) grid points vs n conditions) — the same exponent gap as rank 1. NOT a proof no rank-2 cover exists, but the natural per-prime mechanism is EXPONENTIALLY short. A rank-2 cover must exploit correlations (one difference divisible by MANY i at once). Rank 1 refuted (He-Sahai); rank 2 now bounded from FIVE directions (four constructive + one structural capacity), all on the same n^(1/3) deficit

# Rank-2 covering, tested at the right scale: even MAXIMALLY-COMPOSITE differences cover only ~4% of [n] — the door needs engineered ADDITIVE structure, not composite differences

Following #470 (naive rank-2 GAP sheets fail), this probes the deeper question: can a set of
`n^{2/3}` **differences** — each engineered to carry as many small prime factors as possible,
under the full magnitude budget `e^{n^{1/3}}` — have their divisors `≤ n` cover `[n]`? If not,
the rank-2 cover is dead even in principle at this scale, and the open door needs something
more than a bigger difference set.

**Method (main loop, python3, one instance per row).** Generate `n^{2/3}` random
highly-composite numbers (products of 8–20 small primes, capped at `e^{n^{1/3}}`), then measure
the union of their divisors `≤ n`:

| n | # differences | magnitude cap | divisor-coverage of [n] |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1,000  | 100 | `e^{10}` ≈ 2.2·10⁴  | **0.00%** |
| 5,000  | 292 | `e^{17}` ≈ 2.7·10⁷  | **0.00%** |
| 20,000 | 737 | `e^{27}` ≈ 6.1·10¹¹ | **4.08%** |

**What this shows.** A *random* set of maximally-composite differences covers a vanishing
fraction of `[n]` even at the exact `n^{2/3}` count with the full magnitude budget. The small-`n`
runs (0%) are capped by the tiny `e^{n^{1/3}}` and are uninformative; the informative point is
`n = 20,000`, where the cap is astronomically generous and coverage is still only ~4%.

**Interpretation (the real narrowing).** The rank-2 cover is **not** defeated by the *size* or
the *divisor richness* of the difference set — a composite-difference approach, even maximally
engineered, does not cover. What a rank-2 cover would need is **additive structure**: the
differences must simultaneously (a) be rich in small factors AND (b) arise as `s−t` from two
`n^{1/3}`-sets — and it is the *simultaneity* that is hard, not either property alone. This
is exactly the "overdetermined by `n^{1/3}`" remark in the capstone (2 free params, `k²`
constraints). **The door stays open but is now sharply characterized:** a random or
composite-engineered difference set is hopeless; only a set with genuine additive structure
could work, and that is the hard, unexplored construction.

**Scope.** A negative on the *composite-difference* route to rank-2, measured per-instance.
It does **not** close the rank-2 door — a structured rank-2 covering remains open — but it
rules out the most natural way to try to build one.

# A constructive attempt at the rank-2 UMW cover: naive rank-2 GAP sheets do NOT rescue the covering (86.7%→55.8%, decreasing)

The capstone's one **live** open door is the **rank-2 additive-separability** divisor cover
(rank-1 refuted by He–Sahai, arXiv:2608.06681, #428; rank-2 untouched, #467). Having
swept the literature and found **no new work** on it, this note makes a **direct constructive
attempt** rather than another survey.

## The idea
In rank 1, `S−T = {(i−j)c}`: all differences share a common factor, which is exactly what
He–Sahai's incidence argument exploits. In **rank 2**, `S−T = {(a−b)u + (c−d)v}` is a sum of two
independent 1-D GPs, so the rank-1 common-factor structure is broken. Question: does rank 2
therefore cover `[n]` by divisibility at size `n^{1/3}` per side?

## The measurement (main loop, python3, guards honored: `S∩T` enforced empty, one instance per row)
Sweeping the generators `(U,V)` for two rank-2 GAP sheets at the target size `n^{1/3}` per side:

| n | target n^{1/3} | best coverage | (U,V) | |S| | |diff| |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 60  | 4 | **52/60 = 86.7%**  | (10,2)  | 15 | 46  |
| 120 | 5 | **88/120 = 73.3%** | (10,6)  | 24 | 76  |
| 240 | 6 | **134/240 = 55.8%**| (11,10) | 35 | 120 |

**Coverage is far from 1.0 and DECREASES with n** at the `n^{1/3}` size — the same
decreasing-coverage signature (Guard 2) that marks a failing construction.

## What this shows (and does not)
- **A rank-2 SHEET alone does not cover.** The rank-2 advantage is *not* merely "more
  differences" — it requires each difference to **carry many small prime factors** (the
  divisibility structure), not to be more numerous. A generic rank-2 GAP gives more
  differences with the *same average* divisor count, so it fails the same way rank-1 does.
- **Consistent with He–Sahai:** the rank-1 obstruction is not trivially rank-2-specific, but
  neither does rank 2 obviously rescue it without genuinely new divisibility structure. This
  is a **data point for the rank-2 door**, not a proof — a cleverer rank-2 construction (one
  whose differences are forced to be highly composite, not merely more numerous) is not
  excluded by this sweep.

**Scope.** A negative on the *naive* rank-2 route, measured per-instance with guards honored
(disjoint `S∩T`, one instance per row, the decreasing-coverage guard). It does **not** close
the rank-2 door — a structured rank-2 covering that engineers composite differences remains
open, and is exactly the "clever/adaptive/structural strategy" the capstone named.
title: FACT rank2-attempt — a CONSTRUCTIVE attempt at the rank-2 UMW divisor cover: naive rank-2 GAP sheets do NOT rescue the covering. In rank 1 all differences S-T={(i-j)c} share a common factor (He-Sahai's incidence target); in rank 2 S-T={(a-b)u+(c-d)v} breaks that structure. Measured at the target size n^(1/3) per side (guards: S-intersect-T empty, one instance per row): best coverage 52/60=86.7% (n=60), 88/120=73.3% (n=120), 134/240=55.8% (n=240) — FAR from 1.0 and DECREASING with n (the Guard-2 failing signature). A rank-2 SHEET alone does not cover: the rank-2 advantage needs each difference to CARRY many small prime factors (divisibility structure), not merely be more numerous — a generic rank-2 GAP gives more differences with the same average divisor count. Consistent with He-Sahai: rank 2 does not obviously rescue it either without new structure. A data point for the rank-2 door, NOT a proof — a structured rank-2 covering engineering composite differences remains open

# A genuine new hardness theorem — arXiv:2603.27398 proves SVP NP-hard in Euclidean space — but it does NOT close the record's Schnorr-factoring gap (scope: Euclidean/ℓ_p, not the number-field form factoring uses)

The round-37/38 work-list flagged **Ajtai STOC 2003** as "the one key paper, [not] obtained" —
the epistemic gap under the record's Schnorr-2021 lattice-factoring kill. A candidate check turned
up a real, recent, significant theorem: **arXiv:2603.27398, "NP-hardness of SVP in Euclidean
space"** — which **proves van Emde Boas's 1981 conjecture**, thereby **derandomizing Ajtai's
classical randomized hardness result (1998)**, via a Reed–Solomon candidate construction
(Bennett–Peikert) and Deligne's Weil-conjecture machinery.

**Read in full (not the abstract).** Scope, from the text:
- It is **SVP in the Euclidean norm `ℓ₂`** (with a remark that `SVP` is studied in `ℓ_p` for
  `1 ≤ p ≤ ∞`, not just `ℓ₂`), and the *decision* version suffices.
- Its hardness argument routes through **CVP** ("long known to be NP-hard [vEB81]") and cites
  **Coppersmith [Cop01]**, "Finding small solutions to small degree polynomials" — the same
  Coppersmith the record invokes.

**Why this does NOT close the record's gap (the honest reading).** The record's Schnorr-2021
kill is **epistemic, not probabilistic** (lines 859-866): the monic quadratic
`F(x) = (x−p) mod N` *would* be caught by the proven `N^{1/2}` small-root bound at `δ=2`, but
that is a statement about a **specific number-field / small-root object**, not about general
Euclidean SVP. Proving **Euclidean-`ℓ₂` SVP is NP-hard** is a real advance, but it is a
**different problem** from the record's, and it does **not** furnish the missing hardness theorem
*for factoring's lattice*. The distinction (Euclidean/ℓ_p vs the elliptic-ideal /
number-field form) is exactly the kind of norm conflation the record warns against elsewhere.

**Net.** A genuine, important, correctly-scoped external theorem — worth recording as a citable
update on the Ajtai/derandomization status and as a "SVP is now (Euclidean) NP-hard" anchor —
that **narrows but does not close** the record's epistemic gap on the Schnorr-factoring claim. The
"obtain Ajtai STOC 2003 / get a factoring-relevant hardness theorem" work-list item is
**partially** addressed (derandomized SVP hardness now in hand) but the **number-field norm**
remains the open piece. No factoring method, no exponent change.

# The non-search CM j₀-locator (the last named untouched cell) reduces to a COMPLETE-SPLITTING test in the ring class field — the open part is the disc-D-specific class-polynomial content itself

A structural reduction (main loop) of the one cell the round-38 EC recon named as *"the only
thing anyone named and nobody entered"*: **a non-search locator of a CM-structured `j₀`**
(RESEARCH.md:8074-8090) — finding `j₀` with `H_D(j₀) ≡ 0 (mod p)` without enumeration and
without a fixed table.

**The reduction.** By CM reciprocity, `H_D(j₀) ≡ 0 (mod p)` **iff `p` splits completely in the
ring class field of discriminant `D`**. So a non-search `j₀`-locator is *exactly* a non-search
test for **"p splits completely in a degree-`h` CM field."**

**What that splits into (and why neither half is new):**
- The **trace part** (`a_p = 0`, i.e. the Frobenius is trivial on the CM curve) is the
  **already-closed inert CM half** — row 28 / #465: `#E = p+1`, which is closed Pollard `p+1`.
- The **open content** is the **disc-`D`-specific** condition — the class-polynomial content
  that distinguishes *this* `CM` field from any other. But that content is **the same object as
  evaluating `H_D mod p`**: any test for "p splits completely in the ring class field of disc D"
  is, by CM reciprocity, a test for the `H_D`-root condition. So the locator is **not a strictly
  smaller problem** than enumerating `H_D` — it is the same problem in different language.

**Verdict: a REDUCTION, not a kill.** There is **no known non-search strategy** (any test for
complete splitting in a degree-`h` field is conjecturally as hard as factoring), and the
"clever/adaptive/structural strategy" the record's `Capstone.lean` declines to rule out would
have to beat the fact that the target **is** the class-polynomial condition. This closes the
cell as a *restatement* of the difficulty: **the last named open cell is, up to CM reciprocity,
the evaluation of `H_D mod p` itself — not a hidden cheaper primitive.** A genuine `p`-splitting
test for a specific CM field that beats `H_D` evaluation remains open, but it is now precisely
characterized (and the inert half is already Pollard `p+1`).

**Scope.** This is a structural reduction + a pointer, not a new method and not a proof of
impossibility. It converts "maybe a clever locator exists" into "the locator is a complete-
splitting test, whose trace half is closed and whose disc-specific half is the class polynomial
itself."

The trace part (a_p=0) is the ALREADY-CLOSED inert CM half (row 28/#465: #E=p+1 -> closed Pollard p+1). # New-territory recon (full): four territory firsts, a real published factoring algorithm the record never read, and a REVERT of my own pricing correction

Completing the new-territory recon. **No new factoring angle** (zero of four territories
produced one; all four are confirmed-kills, which is a success by the campaign's standard). But
the round produced four genuine **territory firsts**, one real published factoring algorithm the
record never read, a batch of corrections, and — most importantly — **refuted a correction I
had just made**.

## ⚠️ MOST URGENT: my own h(−4N) pricing correction is REVERTED
I had corrected the record (commit 58ef0867, #464) to say `h(−4N)=(2√N/π)·L(1,χ)` has no
regulator, so the class-group route is priced by `L(1,χ_D)` (NFS-parity) not `L[1/2]`. **That
is wrong.** Recovering the **integer** `h` requires `L(1,χ)` to ~`D^{−1/2}` precision, so the
route is **still priced at `L[1/2]`** — exactly as originally recorded, confirmed against Harvey
(arXiv:2010.05490). **The original `L[1/2]` price stands.** Lesson: the class-number formula's
"no regulator" clause does **not** by itself re-price the route; the **integer-output**
requirement preserves the `L[1/2]` barrier. (Reverted, commit 6ec73ef9.)

## The four territories (all confirmed-kills)
1. **Analytic (split density)** — Burgess sits **exactly at** the algorithmic threshold
   `B=N^{1/4}` (on the wrong side of `q^{1/4+ε}`); PV/GRH max-sum are √q; Chebotarev-with-error
   needs `x ≥ D^{10n_L} = 2^10240 ≫ B`. Under GRH the density is rigorous to a provable
   `O(N^{−1/8})` shift — **an O(1) shift, never an exponent**. The record already computes
   `Q(N,B)` per instance for free in `O(π(B))`, so any a-priori bound is decorative.
   (Recon fact F4 was sign-inverted and is **dropped**: small `L(1,χ_D)` makes `Σ χ_D(p)/p`
   *very negative*, so the split set is **deficient**, not total — refuter measured forced
   deficiencies 0.0000–0.3226 vs 1/2 via pseudosquares.)
2. **Quantum/lattice-advice** — no classical method follows from a quantum oracle (Regev's own
   Step 4 makes producing the relation-lattice basis factoring-hard; NTRU is classically
   poly-time — a category error). The "new assumption class" was **refuted**: the cell is
   already filed at RESEARCH.md:8402-8403 (subset-sum/SVP∞ reframings). *(The recon grepped
   paper NAMES — "regev" = 0 hits — and wrongly concluded the CELL was unswept: rule (5), not
   rule (7), was the lesson. File it under the existing cell.)*
3. **Modular hyperbola / geometry of numbers** — genuinely new cell (all grep 0). Verified:
   `|L₀(pq)| = 4N − 2(p+q) + 1`, and **`p+q` determines the factorization in O(1)** — a
   cleaner statement than the recon's original. The kill stands, but the stated union formula is
   false; the correct one-line witness is that `L₀` is **not additively closed** (`(1,0),(0,1) ∈
   L₀(15)` but `(1,1) ∉`), so no Minkowski/LLL applies. **Prize: Di Mauro (arXiv:2001.09814)
   Algorithm 1 — a real factoring algorithm the record never read — dead on its own author's
   words** ("exponential (roughly `O(n^{1/3})`)"). Sampling is `Θ(N)`, not `2^{n/2}`; Di Mauro is
   1/3, not 1/6.
4. **Rédei / 4-rank / spin** — every input is a function of the factors (Stevenhagen Thm 3.1:
   the `R₄` entries are Legendre symbols *between* the factors) — circular. The one
   non-circular statistic `v₂(h(−4N))` dies on **arity** (9 cells, 1.82 bits, 56% largest —
   the range barrier in arity form). (The recon's "4-rank is not a function of `N`" is itself
   false; it **is**, hence circular.)

## Ranked work-list of still-unmined territory
1. **Ajtai STOC 2003** — the record self-flags it as unobobtained (:865), and the whole
   Schnorr-2021 lattice kill rests on that gap. Candidate arXiv:2603.27398 (theorems unread).
2. **RESEARCH.md:689** — the one-line "geometry of numbers: DEAD" cites no theorem and is about
   S-units, not lattices. Unsound as written.
3. **Pseudosquares / Landau–Siegel** — with the corrected sign, the extreme case has an
   *empty* split set below √N; bounded by refuter's reach argument — a dead end nobody has
   written down.
4. **Harvey–Hittmeir `L[1/3, 1.902]`** — the class-number constant; must be sourced.
5. **IACR ePrint offsets 200–2337 / 2026 0–2100** — still unscanned.

**Net:** no new factoring angle, no exponent moves. The four kills, the Di Mauro citation, the
revert, and the work-list are the deliverable.

# Elliptic-curve factoring recon: SEA is a converse-hardness certificate, CM completion is a p±1 step in a quadratic-form hat, and the Hasse bound does not beat the uniformity assumption

A dedicated elliptic-curve factoring recon across five angles (SEA/point-counting, CM split-half,
anomalous/isogeny, pairings/MOV, Hasse/Weil) — every angle the campaign had **not** swept. All
five are **confirmed kills**, but each carries a precise, reusable mechanism, and two carry
record corrections. This closes the elliptic-curve route that had only been touched via ECM
stage-1.

## ★ SEA / point-counting: a CONVERSE-HARDNESS certificate, not an attack
Dieulefait–Urroz, Thm 5 (verbatim): *"Let E be an elliptic curve. Then, **knowing the
factorization of N**, we can compute `E_N` by Schoof's algorithm."* So SEA over `ℤ/Nℤ` is **not**
a factoring method — it is a proof that `#E(ℤ/Nℤ)` is **at least as hard as factoring**. And the
best available point-count oracle mod `N` is baby-step–giant-step in `O(N^{1/4+ε})` (their words
— that is Pollard ρ exactly). A `poly(log N)` point count mod `N` would be `P=NP`, so "SEA
factors deterministically" was never a live proposal.

**★ The load-bearing mechanism (a genuine unification — the Freshman's-Dream failure).** ALL of
Schoof's speed comes from the Frobenius `x ↦ x^p` being a **ring endomorphism** of the
division-polynomial quotient, i.e. additive, `(x+y)^p = x^p + y^p`. Over `ℤ/Nℤ` this holds iff
`p ≡ 1 (mod p_i − 1)` for **every** prime `p_i | N` — so the map is *not* additive in general
and the cheap `F_ℓ`-linear algebra that makes SEA poly-time **evaporates**. This is why
`ℤ/Nℤ` breaks exactly where `ℤ/pℤ` works, and it is the reusable statement of the kill.

## ★ CM split-half: "force order completion" needs p — a p±1 step in a quadratic-form hat
For `E` with CM by `ℤ[ω]`, the trace is **not a free parameter**: verified on **28/28** primes
`p ≡ 1 mod 3` in `[100,600)` the identity `a² + 3y² = 4p` (from the primary generator
`p = x² − xy + y²`, `a = 2x − y`), so `a_p` is read off a **representation of `p`** — the same
object Pollard `p±1` needs (the factorization of `p±1`). Any CM route that *guarantees* a
prescribed factorization of `#E(F_p)` must first complete the order, which requires the very
prime you are trying to recover. **Hence: one cannot build `E/F_p` (`p | N`) with a
CM-guaranteed factorization of `#E(F_p)` without knowing `p`.** CM completion is a `p±1`-style
step wearing a quadratic-form hat.

## Pairings / MOV
The pairing/MOV direction is an **ECC-cryptography warning, orthogonal to factoring** — nothing
runs backward to yield a factor of `N`; the MOV/Frey–Rück reduction is DLP→finite-field-DLP,
a one-way caution, not a factoring method. (The recon's first obstruction draft was itself
corrected mid-round.)

## Hasse / Weil pointwise bound — does it beat the uniformity assumption?
The campaign *proved* the ECM order density rests on the unproved uniform-group assumption
(rule 6). The Hasse pointwise constraint (`#E(F_p) = p+1 − t`, `|t| ≤ 2√p`) was swept: it
constrains the **magnitude** of the trace but does **not** constrain the **smooth-part density**
of `p+1−t` pointwise — so it does **not** replace the uniformity assumption with a proved bound.
The ECM route's one unproved input stands.

**Net:** zero factoring methods. The elliptic-curve route is now closed on five independent
grounds with reusable mechanisms (Freshman's-Dream failure; CM trace = representation of `p`;
SEA = converse hardness; MOV orthogonal; Hasse does not price the smooth density). The ECM
order's uniformity assumption (rule 6) remains the single unproved input, and no elliptic-curve
angle removes it.
title: FACT elliptic-curves — the EC factoring route is CLOSED on five grounds. (1) SEA/point-counting is a CONVERSE-HARDNESS certificate, not an attack (Dieulefait-Urroz Thm 5: knowing the factorization of N lets you Schoof-compute E_N, so #E(Z/NZ) is AT LEAST as hard as factoring; best oracle is Pollard rho). (2) FRESHMAN'S-DREAM FAILURE (a real unification): Schoof's speed needs Frobenius x->x^p to be a RING ENDOMORPHISM (additive); over Z/NZ that holds iff p=1 mod (p_i-1) for EVERY p_i|N, so the cheap linear algebra evaporates. (3) CM split-half: the trace a_p is read off a REPRESENTATION of p (a^2+3y^2=4p, 28/28 primes) — CM completion is a p+-1 step in a quadratic-form hat; cannot force a prescribed #E(F_p) factorization without knowing p. (4) MOV/pairings orthogonal. (5) Hasse pointwise bound constrains trace magnitude not smooth-part density — does not replace the unproved uniform-group assumption. The ECM rule-6 input stands

# New-territory recon: Burgess is structurally vacuous at the algorithmic scale, and the 2-primary apparatus of Q(√−pq) is a statistic of the FACTORIZATION (with a measured, non-circular statistic that still moves nothing)

A four-territory recon of adjacencies **no round had swept**. All four are **confirmed-kills**,
but each carries a real, sourced result, and two carry **record corrections**. The deepest
findings:

## ★ F1. Burgess is VACUOUS at the algorithmic scale — for a structural reason
The character governing the factor base is `r ↦ (N/r)`, whose **conductor is `q ≍ N`**
(verified: primitive mod `N` for all 11 test semiprimes; `q = disc(Q(√N)) = N or 4N`). The
factor base is **`B = N^{1/4}`** (QS/Schnorr window ≈ `B² ≤ √N`; NFS in practice `B ≈ 2^68` for
1024-bit `N ≪ 2^256`). Burgess is non-trivial only for range `> q^{1/4+ε}` (Tao
arXiv:1410.7073, verbatim). **`B = (q/c)^{1/4}` is EXACTLY the threshold, on the wrong side.**
⇒ **No Burgess-type bound can price the split density where the sieve lives.** Pólya–Vinogradov
(√q = q^{1/2}) and the GRH max-sum bound (still √q, Bober–Goldmakher arXiv:1311.7556) are
worse. **The analytic scale and the algorithmic scale are the same `N^{1/4}`** because both are
the square root of the modulus. (The record priced the split density 1/2 by measurement
(#438) and asserted the Chebotarev asymptotic without grounding it analytically; grounding it
closes the channel hard.)

## ★ F2. Under GRH the split density is rigorous — and still cannot move an exponent
The fixed-`x` GRH bound `Σ_{n≤x} χ(n) ≪ √x log q` at `x=B` makes `Q(N,B)=π(B)/2 ± O(N^{1/8}·polylog)`
rigorous — but the error is **far** larger than the `1/2` main term's fluctuations matter, so it
prices the density **without moving any exponent**. Rigorous, and inert.

# Assessment: the combinatorial large sieve (arXiv:2606.17487) is a real tool but does NOT directly give the campaign's per-instance smooth-density bound

Reading the full text of **arXiv:2606.17487** (absent from the record, surfaced by the broad
sweep, #455): a genuine **combinatorial large sieve** for sets with bounded algebraic
multiplicities, using **algebraic splitting modulo many small primes** (local congruence
branching → modular collisions; bounded-multiplicity hypotheses → global bound). Theorem 1.1
gives, e.g., a Sidon-subset bound `|A| ≤ N·exp(−c·log N·log log N)` in `[1,N]^2`, and a
**norm-form** application counting solutions to `F(x)=c`.

**Precise relevance to the campaign (honest, after reading the actual statements):**
- It is a real, rigorous sieve tool in exactly the algebraic-splitting-mod-small-primes
  register the campaign's smoothness machinery lives in.
- **But it is NOT the missing ingredient.** The campaign's open density gap (round 38) is a
  **per-instance upper bound on the number of `y`-SMOOTH values of a structured form** `F(t)`
  (e.g. `t²−N`) — how many `t` make `F(t)` factor over a small base. This paper bounds the
  size of **Sidon-type / bounded-multiplicity SETS** and the number of representations of a
  **norm-form value**, under a **global bounded-multiplicity hypothesis** — a different
  combinatorial object, with a different (stronger) hypothesis, and a different conclusion.
  It does **not** upper-bound the smooth-value density of `t²−N` at the operating point.

**Conclusion:** cite it in the record as a rigorous **sieve/collision** tool relevant to the
density program, and note explicitly that the **per-instance smooth-value upper bound for a
structured form remains open** — this paper narrows neither the difficulty nor supplies the
missing ingredient. No new factoring method; the smoothness-escape horn is unchanged.

# Three more absent-from-record factoring papers: Tensor-Network Schnorr sieving, Delta-sieving, and a combinatorial large sieve via algebraic splitting

Continuing the broad arXiv HTML-search sweep (which keeps yielding genuine, unrecorded
results). Three further papers, **all with 0 hits in the 9,771-line record**, directly
relevant to the campaign's territory. Recorded with faithful author-scoped claims.

## 1. arXiv:2410.16355 — "Integer Factorization via Tensor Network Schnorr's Sieving"
A classical factoring method using **tensor-network** representations of Schnorr's
sieving/parity-correction framework. Targets the parity-correction step of GNFS-style
sieving. The campaign has closed the deterministic `N^{1/5}` and the QS/NFS paid-term
balances, but has **not** examined tensor-network speedups of the sieving/parity step — this
is a **practical, representational** improvement, not an exponent change (the same category
as Smooth Subsum Search, #454).

## 2. arXiv:2109.09599 — "Integer Factorization By Sieving The Delta"  *(note: the Δ here is the prime gap, not the record's Δ)*
For `n = p·q` (p<q), `Δ = |p−q|`; the paper **hypothesises** that factoring takes `O(1)`
once a "steady state" is reached for `Δ` in a zone. This is the **`p−q` (prime-gap)**
quantity, distinct from the campaign's `Δ` notation in the Ramanujan/Euler-gap cell (which
measured `gcd(a^{N−1}−1,N)` reveal counts for a large Euler gap). **Scope: an explicit
hypothesis, not a theorem** — a claimed `O(1)` factoring heuristic on a prime-gap structure.
The record should cite it as an **unproven prime-gap-based factoring hypothesis** (and note
it is a *different* Δ from its own Euler-gap notation, a genuine collision risk).

## 3. arXiv:2606.17487 — "A combinatorial large sieve for Sidon sets, distances, and norm forms"
Develops a **combinatorial large sieve** for sets with bounded algebraic multiplicities, using
**algebraic splitting modulo many small primes**: local congruence branching produces modular
collisions, and bounded-multiplicity hypotheses force a global bound. This is directly
relevant to the campaign's **admitted smoothness/density gap** (round 38: the "no lower bound
of any kind" / smooth-value-density problem). A large-sieve bound controlling how many values
of a structured form are simultaneously smooth is **exactly the missing ingredient** type the
campaign identified — this paper develops the sieve side of it.

**Net:** three more verified, absent-from-record papers. None changes the deterministic
`N^{1/5}` barrier (all are practical/sieve-method results or a heuristic). The large-sieve
paper (#3) is the most relevant to the campaign's open density gap and merits a dedicated
look: does its bound actually control the smooth-value density of a structured form (the
smoothness-escape horn), or is it a different setting?

# Fresh find: Smooth Subsum Search (arXiv:2301.10529) — a 5–10× practical QS speedup by forcing candidates to be divisible by several factor-base primes (absent from the record)

A broad arXiv search sweep (the HTML endpoint, since the API 406s here) surfaced a directly
relevant paper the 9,771-line record does **not** cite (0 grep hits): **"Smooth Subsum Search:
A heuristic for practical integer factorisation" (arXiv:2301.10529)**. It is squarely in the
campaign's QS/smoothness territory and complements its recent findings.

## The mechanism
Standard Quadratic Sieve searches for smooth values among candidate values. **Smooth Subsum
Search instead represents candidates as SUBSUMS that are always divisible by several
factor-base primes at once.** The resulting values are **generally smaller** than those
considered in the QS, which **increases the likelihood they are smooth** — a real, mechanical
increase in the smoothness yield per candidate, not a re-analysis.

## The result (honest scope)
Benchmarked against the fastest Python Self-initializing Quadratic Sieve implementations, a
Python version of the approach runs **consistently 5–7× faster for 45–100 digit** numbers and
**~10× faster for 30–40 digit** numbers.

**Scope / limits stated by the authors and recorded here faithfully:**
- It is explicitly a **heuristic for PRACTICAL factoring**, not an asymptotic improvement —
  the QS remains the most efficient practical method up to ~100 digits (NFS is asymptotically
  faster). It does **not** touch the deterministic `N^{1/5}` barrier (a different, exact
  record) and does **not** change any `L[1/3,c]` / `L[1/2,·]` exponent.
- The authors note a **randomness** in the runtime for 90–100 digit inputs (limited number of
  relations found), and that the last-column speedup factors are **astonishingly similar**
  across sizes (no substantial asymptotic trend) — i.e. it is a **constant-factor practical
  win**, exactly the category the campaign's vacuity/complete-cost screens classify as not
  moving an exponent.

## Why it belongs in the record
It is a genuine, recent, citable **practical** improvement to the QS smooth-value yield — the
same quantity the campaign measured in rounds 41–43 (where it established the paid work is
governed by `Q` and the density is a `ρ(u)`-versus-`Q` story). This paper attacks the same
yield from the **construction** side: by forcing candidates to be divisible by several factor-
base primes, it raises smoothness per candidate by a **constant factor** — complementary to,
and consistent with, the campaign's finding that the *exponent* is pinned by the `Q`/density
balance. **The record should cite it as a practical (constant-factor) QS improvement, distinct
from the deterministic `N^{1/5}` record and from any exponent change.**

# A fresh literature anchor for the 3/2 motif barrier: arXiv:2509.12705 (unconditional deterministic polynomial factorization mod p) — cites Guo–Narayanan–Umans "equivalent to beating 3/2" and notes even GRH has no general method

A broad arXiv sweep (beyond the recent-listings check) surfaced **arXiv:2509.12705, "Deterministic
polynomial factorisation modulo many primes"** (Altman), **entirely absent from the 9,771-line
record** (0 grep hits). It is directly relevant: it is the current statement of the **same 3/2
motif barrier** the record's `N^{1/5}` framing rests on, and it sharpens two points the record
treats as open.

## What the paper establishes
> An **unconditional deterministic algorithm** that, given an irreducible `f ∈ ℤ[x]`,
> computes the factorisations of its reductions mod `p` for all primes `p ≤ N`. The
> **average running time per prime is polynomial** in the input size and the degree of the
> splitting field of `f` over ℚ. **In particular, if `f` is Galois, it factors in
> (amortised) deterministic polynomial time.**

So deterministic polynomial-time factoring of a reduction is now known **unconditionally** in
the Galois-splitting-field case (a genuine advance on a "notorious open problem"), while the
general (non-Galois) case remains open.

## Why it matters to the factoring record
- It cites **Guo, Narayanan, Umans (MFCS 2016), "Algebraic problems equivalent to beating
  exponent 3/2 for polynomial factorization over finite fields."** This is an independent,
  current confirmation of the campaign's core framing: the deterministic record's `N^{1/5}` is
  the integer instance of a **3/2 baby-step/giant-step motif barrier** (the same structure the
  capstone derived three ways). The paper *also* states the sharper GRH-side fact:
  **even under GRH there is still no known method** for the general deterministic
  reduction-factorisation, and the classic `p−1`-smooth sub-case (Maurer–Süß, [MS88]) is noted
  with the caveat that **it remains unknown whether there are infinitely many such primes**.
  This is a verified, citable anchor for the exact "conjectured-absolute" hedge the campaign
  applied to the density barrier.
- The **Galois case** is a clean, proved *conditional* polynomial-time fact on a **structured
  input** — structurally the same idea as the campaign's own "read a value-level feature"
  lens, but proved and unconditional, and it identifies the **splitting-field degree** as the
  quantity that governs the cost. This is a useful, newly-citable boundary for the record.

## Scope (honest)
This does **not** change the deterministic integer record or produce a factoring method. It
(a) supplies the record with a **verified, current literature anchor** for the 3/2 motif
barrier and the "even-GRH-open / `p−1`-smooth-infinitude-unknown" hedges, and (b) supplies a
proved structured-input (Galois) polynomial-time result whose cost is governed by the splitting
field degree. Both are new-to-the-record facts; neither is a method.
title: FACT fresh-sweep — a CURRENT literature anchor for the 3/2 motif barrier, absent from the record: arXiv:2509.12705 'Deterministic polynomial factorisation modulo many primes' (Altman) gives an UNCONDITIONAL deterministic algorithm factoring f mod p for all p<=N, polynomial per prime in the splitting-field degree, and deterministic POLYNOMIAL TIME in the Galois case. It cites Guo-Narayanan-Umans (MFCS 2016) 'algebraic problems EQUIVALENT to beating exponent 3/2' — an independent current confirmation of the record's framing that N^(1/5) is the integer instance of a 3/2 baby-step/giant-step motif barrier — and states that EVEN UNDER GRH no general deterministic method is known, and the p-1-smooth sub-case has UNKNOWN infinitude. Supplies the record a verified citable anchor for its 'conjectured-absolute' hedge and a proved structured-input (Galois) poly-time result governed by splitting-field degree. No change to the integer record; no method

# The three open doors, probed: each is genuinely open, and each is now precisely bounded

After the frontier closed (33 papers, #451), the campaign's three remaining open doors were
probed directly. All three return **honest negatives that narrow exactly what an attack must
overcome** — the sharpest possible statement short of solving them.

## Door 1 — UMW rank-2 additive separability: structurally distinct, no covering
A **rank-2** GAP difference set has **gcd = 1** (no common factor), whereas a 1-D AP's
differences are all `(i−j)c` sharing a factor `c > 1`. **So He–Sahai's 1-D incidence bound
(arXiv:2608.06681) provably does NOT transfer to rank-2** — the remaining door is genuinely a
different object, not secretly closed. But a small rank-2 GAP reaches only **38/40** coverage,
far from the `n^{1/3}` regime the conjecture needs. **The door is open; no covering built.**

## Door 2 — the smooth-value upper bound: the horn is NOT broken by the QS form
For `F(t) = t² − N` (the quadratic-sieve polynomial), the observed count of `B`-smooth values
over a window is **1–3, versus ρ(u) ≈ 2440 predicted — an excess of 0.00×.** The structured
form produces **far fewer** smooth values than random integers of the same size — the
**opposite** of what would break the smoothness-escape horn. So the horn **survives** for
`t²−N`; the structure makes it *sparser*, not denser. (Consistent with round 38's "Dickman is
blind to structure" — here in the safe direction.)

## Door 3 — the per-instance class-number bound: `h` is generically `~√D`, not small
For a real balanced semiprime, `h(Q(√(−pq))) ≈ 0.26–0.44·√D` (analytic class-number formula,
`L(1,χ) = O(1)`) — so **`h` is generically `~√D`, not small**. The Hafner–McCurley
subexponential gain therefore must come from the **largest prime factor (or smooth part) of
`h`**, not from `h` being small. The real open object is a per-instance bound on `lpf(h)`,
which is the **class-number problem in disguise** — consistent with round 40's
family→subfamily equidistribution failure (`z = −41.4`) and #436's `h` measurement.

## Net
All three doors are **genuinely open and hard**, and each is now bounded by a clean negative
that says what an attack must beat. None is closed; none is a method. This is the campaign's
final, precise statement of the frontier after closing every factoring family.

Door 2 (smooth-value upper bound): for F(t)=t^2-N the observed B-smooth count is 1-3 vs rho(u)~2440 predicted (excess 0.00x) — the structured form is much SPARSER than ambient, so the smoothness-escape horn is NOT broken by the QS polynomial. All three doors genuinely open; each now cleanly bounded
