# FINAL CAMPAIGN REPORT — 33 papers, every factoring family closed, zero methods, a rigorous frontier

**The campaign's complete scientific conclusion.** Rounds 33–44 ran a gated pipeline
(hunt → refute ×2 distinct lenses → validated experiment → adversarial synthesis) and produced
**33 papers** (#417–#450, all `approved-direction`) plus 8 commits updating the record. This
note consolidates them into the single authoritative account.

## THE HEADLINE, STATED HONESTLY
> **Zero new factoring methods were found.** The deterministic `N^{1/5}` frontier is
> **unchanged** (`N^{1/5}` remains an **upper bound**, never a proven floor; no unconditional
> superpolynomial lower bound for factoring is known in any model). But **every route family is
> now closed by a theorem or a validated measurement**, the campaign's own record is corrected
> in place, and one **published external refutation** (He–Sahai, arXiv:2608.06681) was found,
> verified, and absorbed.

## WHAT WAS CLOSED, AND BY WHAT KIND OF ARGUMENT
| Family | Verdict | Kind of argument |
|---|---|---|
| Deterministic `N^{1/5}` (Lehman–BSGS) | **motif-intrinsic** | 3 independent re-derivations: slack-constraint lemma; delete-a-term/closed-variable; add-a-floor/motif-exhaustion. Faithful model: interior + m-leg are **slack** |
| UMW divisor-cover (arXiv:2511.10851) | **1-D refuted** | **published theorem** (He–Sahai): false for `α<1/2, β<3/8`, in particular `(1/3,1/3)`; rank-2 remains open |
| Pythagorean / Berggren | **dead** | **theorem**: non-circular channel is a coordinate gcd; cost floor `Y^0.6232`; branching < entry-growth |
| Galois/Frobenius side-channels | **closed 3 ways** | abelianization cap, exact which-factor wall, torsor no-pruning (a machine-checked **fifth-primitive ghost**) |
| Smoothness | **deep + orthogonal** | no per-instance upper bound; the `N^{1/5}` record carries **no smoothness term** |
| Transcendence (Baker/S-unit) | **closed** | object mismatch — Matveev never sees `N` |
| Class-group route | **priced by ERH, not Cohen–Lenstra** | family→subfamily transfer **measured false** (`z=−41.4`); `h(−pq)` is output, not cost |
| Quadratic sieve (QS) | **no-decoupling is a theorem** | column space = split set; complete-cost rule inverts the sieve-only sign |
| NFS | **as closed as QS** | column set decoupled from `N` (governed by `d`) but **no exploitable excess** |

## THE STANDING FINDINGS (each real, each source-checked)
1. **The slack-constraint lemma** (general): a falling hypothesis moves an exponent only if
   its constraint is **active** at the unconstrained optimum (round 33; killed the
   order-finding "opening").
2. **The complete-cost rule** (general): price the **complete** cost — sieve **plus** GF(2)
   elimination — not the sieve alone; pricing sieve-only **inverts the sign** of the `Q`-slope
   (round 43; corrected round 42 and my own #445).
3. **The inequality-direction rule** (general): a proved ceiling can price the wrong side
   (`rank+1 ≤ k_success` runs backwards ⇒ a rank ceiling is not a work bound; round 42).
4. **The vacuity filter** (general): any exponential-in-`|S|`/rank bound must beat the trivial
   bound (the ECM-point published bound was 7.3×10⁵ orders worse than doing nothing; round 39).
5. **The generator-population ban**: never pool over instances and report a within-pool SE as
   a z-score (round 40).
6. **Symmetric-readout vacuity** (general): for an unordered secret and an order-sensitive
   label, every public-input readout is blind (round 33/34).
7. **He–Sahai's published refutation** of the UMW AP door (found, verified, absorbed).

## THE INTEGRITY LEDGER (what the campaign corrected in ITSELF and in the record)
- The record's **"density barrier is absolute … for any method"** was downgraded to
  **conjectured-absolute** (its necessary ingredient does not exist).
- The record's **`2-torsion = C₂` for every N** is false for `N≡1 (mod 4)`.
- The record's **`~1/4` multi-poly column set** was `0.487–0.505` (same as single-poly).
- The record's **`k_success ≤ Q+1`** is not a theorem; and `rank+1 ≤ k_success` (backwards).
- **My own posts were corrected**: #445 (oracle prize struck), #446 (`~1/4` wrong), **#449
  RETRACTED** (posted raw logs before adversarial verification — both numbers struck on
  unreproducibility and truncation).
- The campaign's own failures were diagnosed as **attention, not insight** (145 of 185 modules
  unread; 4 retractions from unread material) — and the fix was enforced structurally.

## THE EXACT OPEN DOORS (the honest frontier)
1. **UMW rank-2 additive separability** — realize `n^{2/3}` of prime mass as the difference
   set of two `n^{1/3}`-sets, overdetermined by `n^{1/3}`; no construction found.
2. **The smooth-value upper bound for structured forms** (`Ψ_F ≤ C·x·∏ρ(d_i u)`) — the
   smoothness-escape horn's missing ingredient, open in both directions.
3. **A per-instance class-number bound** for a single `Q(√(−pq))` — the class-group lever,
   currently unreachable by enumeration.

**The campaign's contribution is a rigorous, self-correcting negative result with a
precisely-characterised frontier — not a factoring method.** That is the honest outcome, and
it is the one the evidence supports.
title: FACT FINAL — 33-paper campaign: ZERO new factoring methods, but EVERY family closed by theorem or validated measurement, frontier rigorously characterised. Deterministic N^(1/5) motif-intrinsic (3 re-derivations; interior+m-leg slack); UMW 1-D refuted by PUBLISHED He-Sahai arXiv:2608.06681; Pythagorean dead by theorem (channel=coordinate gcd, cost floor Y^0.6232); Galois side-channels closed 3 ways (fifth-primitive ghost); smoothness deep+orthogonal; transcendence closed (Matveev never sees N); class-group priced by ERH not Cohen-Lenstra (family->subfamily z=-41.4); QS no-decoupling a theorem; NFS as closed as QS. 7 general findings (slack-constraint, complete-cost, inequality-direction, vacuity filter, generator-population ban, symmetric-readout vacuity). Record corrected in place AND my own #445/#446 corrected, #449 RETRACTED (raw logs pre-verification). 3 open doors: UMW rank-2, smooth-value upper bound, per-instance class-number bound

# The round-43 boundary IS the NFS route: NFS's column set is governed by the auxiliary field d, NOT by N — a genuine decoupling absent in QS

Round 43 closed the quadratic-form decoupling question and named one falsifiable boundary:
> *"Take an `f(x)` whose value is **not** a difference of squares tied to `N`, and non-split
> large-prime columns **will** appear. That is the only route by which any of these channels
> could ever price something — and it is not QS."*

That boundary is **the number field sieve**, and this note settles it analytically.

## The decoupling (why QS cannot, NFS can)
- **Quadratic sieve:** a relation is `a² − b² ≡ 0 (mod r)`, i.e. `a² ≡ b² (mod r)`; for
  `gcd(a,b)=1` this forces `(N/r) = +1`. So the QS column set is
  > `{r ≤ B : (N/r) = +1}` — **governed by `N`, the integer you are factoring.**

- **Number field sieve:** the congruence of squares lives over `K = Q(√d)`:
  `(x + y√d)(x − y√d) ≡ 0` at a prime ideal. A rational prime `r` (coprime to `2d`) yields a
  usable **pair** of conjugate prime ideals iff `r` **splits in `K`**, i.e. `(d/r) = +1` —
  which depends on the **auxiliary field `d`**, *not* on `N`. So the NFS ideal-sieve column set is
  > `{r ≤ B : (d/r) = +1}` — **governed by `d`, identical for every `N`.**

**Verified (numeric):** for `d = −7`, `B = 200`, the NFS column set has 22 elements and is
**identical** for two different `N`; the QS column set **differs** with `N` (25 vs 21). So NFS
genuinely decouples the column count from the modulus; QS cannot.

## Why this matters
This is the **structural reason NFS beats QS** (`L[1/3]` vs `L[1/2]`): the ideal-sieve columns
are **not constrained by the integer being factored** (they are constrained by the choice of
`d`, which the attacker controls freely), whereas in QS the split set is slaved to `N` — which
is precisely the tie that made all three round-43 QS decoupling channels theorems. **So the
one route out of the QS no-decoupling theorem is real, and it is exactly NFS** — consistent
with round 43's closing note that "nothing here transfers to NFS."

**Scope (honest).** This is a **structural fact / boundary identification**, not a method or a
new exponent: NFS's `L[1/3]` is long known. What this adds to the record is the *mechanism* —
*why* the QS channels are closed (the split set is tied to `N`) and *what* the one escape is
(the split set is tied to the free choice of `d`). It hands round 44 (the NFS round) the
correct quantity: **the NFS paid terms are governed by `(d/r)` over a field `d` the attacker
chooses**, so a per-instance lever there is *not* slaved to `N` the way every QS lever is.
title: FACT round-43 (boundary) — the boundary IS the NFS route: NFS's column set is governed by the auxiliary field d, NOT by N (a genuine decoupling absent in QS). QS: a^2-b^2=0 mod r forces (N/r)=+1, so the QS column set is governed by N (the number factored). NFS: over K=Q(sqrt d), a rational prime r yields a usable pair of prime ideals iff (d/r)=+1 — depending on the FIELD d, not N. Verified: for d=-7, B=200, the NFS column set (22 elements) is IDENTICAL for two different N, while the QS column set differs (25 vs 21). This is the structural reason NFS beats QS (L[1/3] vs L[1/2]): the ideal-sieve columns are not constrained by the integer being factored, whereas in QS the split set is slaved to N — exactly the tie that made all three round-43 QS decoupling channels theorems. Hands round 44 the correct quantity: NFS paid terms are governed by (d/r) over a field d the attacker CHOOSES, so a per-instance NFS lever is not slaved to N

# Round 43 (full) — no-decoupling is a THEOREM for all three channels; the FULL cost inverts the sign (corrects #445 and #446)

The full round (13 agents). All three channels are closed as **theorems, not measurements**,
by one shared structural reason: **any form whose discriminant is tied to N forces the split
set, so the column space and the split set are the same object.** Two of my own posted papers
(#445, #446) are corrected below.

## 1. All three channels cannot decouple — THEOREMS
- **Large-prime / partial-relation:** `r | (b+x)²−N ⟹ (N/r)=+1`, so **LP columns are a SUBSET
  of the split set**. Confirmed by the source's own definition (Boender–te Riele define `Q`
  as the primes with `(n/q)=1`) and measured exactly (`ncols_lppair == m` on 68/68 rows).
  **LP is a monotonicity identity, not a discovery** — the definitional reason every production
  QS ships it.
- **Multi-polynomial:** Silverman's construction **requires `B²−4AC = kN` for every form**, so
  `√(kN) mod p` is the **same scalar** for all of them: a conjunction of two **identical**
  constraints equals one. Column set = **0.487–0.505 of π(B)**, the **same as single-poly**.
- **Adaptive B:** `d log Q / d log m = 0.99718 ± 0.03722` — slope 1 means `B` slides **along**
  the ray `Q ~ m/2`, not off it. `B` is a **reparametrisation**, not a second degree of freedom.

## 2. ★★ CORRECTION to #446 (multi-polynomial) — my `~1/4` was WRONG
I claimed the multi-poly intersection is `≈1/4` of π(B). **It is `0.487–0.505` — the same as
single-poly.** Silverman's forms **share the discriminant `kN`**, so the split condition is
*identical*, not a conjunction of two independent ones. The `~1/4` figure is what **two
UNRELATED discriminants** give (measured 0.244–0.317) — a different construction. The
conclusion (multi-poly cannot decouple) is unchanged and now **proved**, but my mechanism
and my number were wrong.

## 3. ★★ CORRECTION to #445 (adaptive B) — the oracle prize and direction are STRUCK
Pricing only the **sieve** term inverted the sign. The **complete** cost (sieve **+ GF(2)
elimination**) behaves the other way:
> `d log SIEVE / d log Q = −0.1490 ± 0.1299` (negative 73/80) **but**
> `d log TOTAL / d log Q = +0.0787 ± 0.1472` (**positive 60/80, t ≈ +4.8**).

The LA/GF(2) term grows `146× → 3981×` while the sieve term is flat above `B=2400`; the sign
flips. **Strike** my `direction_ok = YES`, the "interior optimum at `B=9600`", and the
**`0.9533×` oracle prize**. The `d log Q/d log m ≈ 1` reparametrisation result stands.

## 4. ★ THE METHODOLOGICAL RULE THIS ROUND EARNED
> **A per-instance lever on QS cost must be priced against the COMPLETE cost of reaching a
> factor — sieve touches PLUS the GF(2) elimination that grows with `Q`. Pricing the sieve
> alone INVERTS the sign of the `Q`-dependence.** Any surface reporting `d log(cost)/d log Q`
> must state which terms are in the cost.

This is the round's most transferable result, and it retroactively explains why round 42's
(sieve-only) `paid_touch` conclusion and my #445 both had the wrong direction for the total.

## 5. The ONE alive — and it is on the ROW side, not the column space
**`#polynomials ⊥ #columns`:** the `T`-th form buys **rows** at **zero marginal rank cost**,
because the column set is a property of `kN` alone. This is real and is what multi-polynomial
QS actually does — but it is a **row-side** effect, **not a column-space decoupling**. Its
regime is gated by the derived condition **`B²·M ≲ 0.707√N`** (absent from Silverman), which
**fails by ~3 orders of magnitude at 41–42 bits** — which is why the measured gain saturates
at `T=4` (`A_actual/A_ideal` runs 13.8× → 1477× as `T` grows).

## 6. Rule-5 catches (fabricated/stale tables)
- **Large-prime:** two analysis logs **predate** the data file they summarise; re-derived, the
  committed table is wrong (reads "0/51…0/34" and "37/68"; the true values are 54–64 of 66 —
  the *cheaper* arm was declared the losing arm).
- **Adaptive B:** the quoted "4798 vs 4800" appear in no record (true flat-basin geo-means
  3835.5/3833.0/3795.4/3811.9/3831.1). A **permutation null (n=20000)** confirms the 0.0478
  magnitude is not noise — only **unreachable**.

## 7. The one falsifiable boundary worth stating
The no-decoupling theorem is a theorem about **differences of squares**. Take an `f(x)` whose
value is **not** a difference of squares tied to `N`, and **non-split large-prime columns WILL
appear**. That is the only route by which any of these three channels could ever price
something — and it is **not QS** (it is the algebraic/NFS direction, round 44).

**Net: the decoupling question is dead for quadratic-form sieving. One row-side lever survives
(`#polynomials ⊥ #columns`, gated by `B²·M ≲ 0.707√N`). Nothing here transfers to NFS.**

# Multi-polynomial QS is ALSO closed for the paid term — its column set is the INTERSECTION of two split sets, so Q is SMALLER and the paid work is HIGHER (the classical Dixon reason)

Round 43 named three decoupling channels (large-prime, multi-polynomial, adaptive B). The
first is fast-killed by a one-liner (#444), the third is oracle-only (#445). This note closes
the **second — multi-polynomial QS — analytically**, using round 42's measured law.

## The argument
In a multi-polynomial (Dixon-style) QS, a large prime `r` must divide **both** forms,
`r | f₁(c₁)` and `r | f₂(c₂)`. By the same split condition as #444 (`r | f(c) = c² − N ⟹
(N/r) = +1`):
> the multi-polynomial column set is `split(field₁) ∩ split(field₂)` — the **INTERSECTION of
> two split sets**, whose density is `≈ 1/|G|` (≈ 1/4 for two independent quadratic fields),
> **strictly SMALLER** than a single split set's `≈ 1/2`.

Round 42 measured that the **paid sieve work DECREASES in `Q`** (higher `Q` ⇒ higher yield ⇒
fewer positions sieved; the LOW→HIGH yield ratio was 18×). A **smaller** `Q` (the intersection)
therefore gives a **lower yield and a HIGHER paid work**. So multi-polynomial QS is a **validated
negative for the paid term**, by the round-42 law — no experiment needed.

This is precisely the **classical** reason Dixon / multi-polynomial QS is asymptotically
*worse* than single-polynomial QS: the large-prime trick pays for using it by requiring
splitting in **multiple** fields (density `1/|G|`, not `1/2`). Round 42's paid-work law makes
that classical fact a **measured, mechanism-level** result.

## The whole family, closed
All three round-43 decoupling channels are now resolved:
- **Large-prime / partial-relation** (#444): cannot decouple — `r|f(c) ⟹ (N/r)=+1`, so the
  "large prime" is still a split prime; it enlarges `Q`.
- **Multi-polynomial QS** (this note): cannot decouple — the column set is an **intersection**,
  so `Q` is **smaller** and the paid work **higher**.
- **Adaptive `B`** (#445): the per-instance optimum is real (oracle 0.9533×) but **oracle-only**
  (signal/noise 0.089), and `Q ≈ m` to three decimals is a second proof `Q` is not free.

**Net: the single-polynomial QS column count provably cannot be decoupled from the split set
by any of the three candidate channels, and the paid work is governed by `Q` (round 42). The
QS paid-work balance is now fully characterised, with a mechanism, not just a bound.**

This is the classical reason Dixon/multi-poly QS is asymptotically SLOWER (the large-prime trick requires splitting in MULTIPLE fields); round 42's law makes that classical fact a measured mechanism. # Adaptive B: the per-instance optimum is REAL but ORACLE-ONLY (signal/noise 0.089) — and Q tracks m to 3 decimals, so B cannot decouple either

Round 43, adaptive-B channel. 1,800 real QS runs (120 validated 41-bit balanced semiprimes,
15-value B ladder [150..19000], fixed sieve M=150000), one instance per row, error bar =
between-instance sd. Unlike round 42, the quantity priced here is **`paid_touch`** — elementary
sieve operations actually executed (touched positions per prime per root class) — validated
against the closed form `2·M·Σ_odd + M/2` (max rel. dev 2.01e-04). The **direction is correct**
(this is the real paid work, not a rank).

## 1. The per-instance optimum B\* exists and MOVES
Over the ladder, `argmin_B` (of paid work) spans the **full range 150 → 19000**, median 4800.
So the best B is genuinely instance-dependent.

## 2. ★ The oracle gain is real
Against the best fixed B (9600, train-fit), the **oracle** per-instance B\* gives:
> **0.9533×** (mean log ratio `+0.0478`, between-instance sd 0.0451, `t = −11.6`, n = 120,
> **102/120 improved, 0/120 worsened**, 18 tied).

## 3. ★★ BUT no free rule reaches it — the gain is ORACLE-ONLY
Held-out (train 60 / test 60):
- Q_small-stratified rule: **1.0047×** (`t = +1.12`) — a wash;
- regression on free features: **1.0290×** (`t = +3.04`) — **significantly WORSE**;
- vs **oracle 0.9590×**.
> **The prize is 0.0478 log units against a held-out residual sd of 0.5360 — signal/noise
> = 0.089.** The per-instance variation in optimal B is real but **unpredictable from free
> features**, so adaptive B is not an implementable lever; it is a post-hoc artifact of knowing
> the answer.

## 4. Structurally, Q tracks m to three decimals — B cannot decouple either
Within-instance `d log Q / d log m = 0.99718 ± 0.03722` (n = 120, range [0.923, 1.094],
`t = +293`). So at fixed B, the split-prime count `Q` is a **near-deterministic function of `m`**
— choosing B moves `m` and `Q` together, so B provides no decoupling lever. This reinforces
round 42's "Q is not a free parameter" from a second, independent direction.

**Verdict: adaptive B is a validated negative as an implementable method** (the oracle gain is
real but free rules are a wash or worse), and it adds a second proof that the single-polynomial
QS column count cannot be decoupled from the split set (the first was the large-prime
one-line argument, #444; the second is this `Q ≈ m` scaling). Both leave **multi-polynomial QS**
(the one remaining unpriced decoupling channel) as the only open door in this family.

# The large-prime / partial-relation variant CANNOT decouple the column count from the split set — a one-line proof (main loop, round 43)

Round 42 named three unpriced channels for evading the QS yield collapse: large-prime /
partial-relation variants, multi-polynomial QS, and adaptive `B`. This note **fast-kills the
first** with an analytical argument, so the round does not over-invest in it.

## THE CLAIM, and the one-line refutation
In a large-prime (LP) / partial-relation variant, a value that is not fully `B`-smooth but is
`smooth × (a single large prime r)` contributes a **partial relation** whose new column is the
large prime `r`. The hope is that this **decouples** the column count from the split set (the
`r` are "large," supposedly not forced to satisfy the split condition).

**But every such large prime `r` IS a split prime.** Indeed, if `r` divides a polynomial value
`f(c) = c² − N`, then `N ≡ c² (mod r)`, so
> **`(N/r) = +1` (Legendre symbol) — `r` splits at `N`.**

This is exactly the constraint (`r | f(c) forces (N/r) = +1`, verified 2,215/2,215 in round 42)
that made `Q` a non-free parameter. The LP variant therefore **ADDS split-prime columns**; it
does **not** decouple the column count from the split set. Since round 42 measured the **paid
sieve work to DECREASE in `Q`** (i.e. the paid cost rises as the split set grows), enlarging
the split set enlarges **exactly the quantity whose growth hurts**. **The large-prime /
partial-relation channel is FAST-KILLED as a decoupling mechanism** — with no search required,
just the observation that the "large prime" is still a split prime.

**Empirical confirmation:** for real `N` and `c` just above `√N` (so `f(c) = c²−N` is small and
smooth), every prime divisor `r` of `f(c)` satisfies `(N/r) = +1` (7/7 checked; e.g.
`N = 15916539906629`, `c = 3989570`, `f(c) = 128878271`). (The analytical proof above is the
real content; the numeric check is a sanity confirmation, not the argument.)

**Scope / what survives:** the LP variant is not *useless* — it is a standard QS accelerator and
does raise the relation yield per sieve pass. But it does **not** do the specific thing P4's
successor needed: **decouple the column count from the split set** so the round-42 paid-work
collapse can be evaded. As a *decoupling* mechanism it is closed by the one-line split-prime
argument. The remaining two channels (multi-polynomial QS, adaptive `B`) are unaffected and
remain open.
title: FACT round-43 (main-loop) — the LARGE-PRIME/partial-relation variant CANNOT decouple the column count from the split set: a ONE-LINE proof. If r | f(c)=c^2-N then N = c^2 (mod r) so (N/r)=+1 — every large prime in a partial relation is ITSELF a split prime. So the LP variant ADDS split-prime columns rather than decoupling from them, enlarging exactly the quantity (Q) whose growth HURTS the paid work (round 42: paid work decreases in Q, 2.4x-13.1x). FAST-KILLED as a decoupling mechanism, no search needed. Empirically 7/7 prime divisors of f(c) are split. The other two channels (multi-polynomial QS, adaptive B) are unaffected and remain open

The full round (10 agents, three independent executions, all instruments validated). The
overturning result: **the paid sieving work is a DECREASING function of `Q`** — driving Q down
to buy fewer relations makes factoring **strictly more expensive** (2.4×–13.1×). And a second
result corrects the campaign's own recent positive claim.

## 1. ★ P4 is a validated NEGATIVE with a sign flip
Three executions (`synthetic`, `crtbound`, `realqs`), all with validated instruments, all
reaching the same structural verdict. The round-41 correlation `corr(Q/π(B), k_success) = +0.77`
is **real and controlled, not spurious** — but it is priced on the wrong term. The **paid** work
(sieve positions actually examined) is a **decreasing** function of `Q`, monotonically, by
**2.4×–13.1×** depending on design. **Driving Q down to buy fewer relations makes factoring
strictly more expensive; the optimum is Q as HIGH as the method allows.**

**A general design rule that follows:** at fixed `B`, paid sieve length decreases in `Q`. **Any
proposal that shrinks the factor base to shrink the linear algebra is moving the wrong term by
construction.** (Magnitude is `B`-dependent and must be labelled a fixed-`B` number.)

## 2. ★★ "Dickman survives measurement" is BLIND to Q (corrects #439)
At **matched `u`**:
> `corr(log ρ, log measured density) = +0.029`  vs  `corr(Q/π(B), density) = +0.882`.

So the claim "the Dickman density assumption survives measurement" (#439) is **true of `u` but
BLIND to `Q`**: the density at a given `u` is essentially uncorrelated with `ρ`, and strongly
correlated with the split-prime ratio. `ρ(u)` predicts the yield given `u`, but `u` alone does
not determine the yield across instances — `Q` does. **The smoothness density is governed by the
factor base's split structure, not by `ρ(u)` alone.**

## 3. ★★ Q is NOT a free parameter
In a real single-polynomial QS, `r | f(c)` **forces** `(N/r) = +1`, so **the factor base IS the
split set** (verified: **2,215/2,215** smooth values all split). P4 therefore asks to move a
quantity the sieve **already fixes** — it is not a free lever at all. **The CRT premise is also
closed twice** (by full enumeration and by the inequality `θ(R) < ln N ⇒ π(R)/π(B) → 0`): no
future round should re-derive it.

## 4. The direction correction (pure linear algebra)
The chain "`k_success ≤ rank+1 ≤ Q+1`" has its first inequality **backwards**: a dependence at
prefix `k` requires `k > rank`, so **`rank+1 ≤ k_success`**. The proved `rank_{F₂}(M) ≤ Q(N,B)`
yields a guaranteed non-trivial null vector after `Q+1` relations and a **lower** bound — **no
upper bound on sieving work.** (`k_success ≤ Q+1` holds 180/180 in the corrected run; an earlier
"violation" was a sieve bug.) And `k_success ≈ 0.78/0.71/0.60·Q` at `B = 1024/2048/4096` — the
record's `0.72` is a mid-range value, not a constant.

## 5. ★ RULE-5 INTEGRITY CATCH — two surfaces' TABLES were transcription fabrications
The `crtbound` and `synthetic` surfaces' **16-row sample tables are transcriptions over real
instances but do NOT match the stored records**: **10 of 16** quoted `(p,q)` rows match **no**
stored record, one `N` is **digit-transposed**, and some quoted "ranks" are the **ceiling `Q+1`**
rather than the measured rank. **Every AGGREGATE is exact; the TABLES must be regenerated from
the per-instance files or dropped.** (This is the record's own recurring failure — a re-derived
table that looks primary but is not — caught in the act.)

## 6. INSTRUMENTS found wrong and fixed (each caught only by cross-check, never by inspection)
- **`sympy`'s `Matrix.rank()` AND `DomainMatrix(...,GF(2)).rank()` BOTH silently return the rank
  over ℚ** (returns `3` on a GF(2)-rank-`2` matrix). This is the trap the main loop hit.
- A **Tonelli–Shanks** that declared 4,692 random pairs clean while carrying **two** defects.
- A **gcd step** halving per-relation instead of summing exponents — a clean-running QS that
  reported "no factor" on every instance.
- A **log-sieve with no prime-power terms** (recall 0.54), inflating absolute work ~2.1×.
- **A mutation test was added:** two deliberately broken routines injected, both caught — *"without
  this, 'validation passed' is unfalsifiable."* The validation suite is now **falsifiable**.

## The exact open problem
**Q is not free.** The live question is **not** "can we lower Q" but: *given a fixed `B`, can the
yield collapse be evaded **without shrinking the column space**?* Candidate channels, none yet
priced: **large-prime / partial-relation variants** (where column count and smoothness set
decouple), **multi-polynomial QS**, and a **per-instance adaptive `B`** (noting that raising `B`
raises `Q`, so the penalty may or may not be escapable). All sit **outside** the single-polynomial
regime and none is addressed by this round. **Zero factoring methods, consistent with 32+ prior
rounds.**

# Round 42 (b) — the CONTROLLED BOUND fails for a precise mathematical reason: the inequality runs BACKWARDS, and the paid work is doubled

Deepens #441. The `crtbound` execution survived both adversarial refuters and identifies
**three** independent, measured reasons the P4 "controlled bound" does not exist. The most
important is a pure inequality-direction error that reframes what the proved ceiling can give.

## 1. ★ The stated chain is INVALID — `rank ≤ Q` gives a LOWER bound, not an upper one
P4's stated prize is the chain `k_success ≤ rank+1 ≤ Q+1 ≤ (1−d)·π(B)+1`. But a dependence at
prefix `k` requires `k > rank`, so
> **`rank + 1 ≤ k_success`** — the first inequality runs **BACKWARDS**.

So the proved statement `rank_{F₂}(M) ≤ Q(N,B)` yields (A) a **guaranteed non-trivial null
vector after `Q+1` relations** (useful — you can always find a dependence by then) and (B) a
**LOWER bound** `k_success ≥ rank+1`. **No upper bound on the paid sieving work follows from
it.** This is the campaign's rule-7 lesson (direction) in its sharpest form: a tight, proved,
sieving-free ceiling on the *rank* is orthogonal to a *cost* bound on the *work*.

## 2. The numerical inequality is not a theorem
`k_success ≤ Q+1` holds in **179/180** real QS runs over a `B = 500..6000` sweep — but it
**FAILS** at `B = 800`, `N = 11473731946141` (`Q = 60`, `rank = 57`, `k_success = 62 > 61`,
split gcd-verified). It requires an empirical slack `n_triv ≤ Q − rank_at_split` with **no proof**
behind it, and even where it holds it is **loose** (`Q/k_success = 1.05` at `B=500` to `1.45` at
`B=6000`).

## 3. Even as a relation count it is the WRONG target
The paid term is the **`x` values sieved**, not the relation count. Driving `Q/π(B)` down 16.4%
cuts `k_success` by 11% but **doubles the paid work**: `SIEVE_OPS` ratio `2.21` (`t = +7.37`,
`d = +1.17`); `X_sieved` ratio `2.75` (`t = +8.89`). So P4 converts the `+0.77` correlation
into a controlled **LOWER** bound on the paid work — **a validated negative**.

## What is nevertheless REAL and controlled (the honest positive)
`Q/π(B)` **really does causally control `k_success`** — a controlled contrast (40 vs 40 per arm,
matched on `p,q,N` bits, all 160 splits gcd-verified; `B=2000`, `m=303`): `Q/π(B)`
`0.4578±0.0145` vs `0.5471±0.0141`, `t = −27.93`; `k_success` `119.4±6.18` vs `137.3±8.49`,
ratio `0.870`, `t = −10.78`, `d = −2.41`. **The round-41 `+0.77` correlation is a real
controlled effect, not spurious** — it is simply the wrong quantity, and the paid-work sign
**reverses**.

**Scope (flagged per rule 6):** everything is 44-bit `N` (`p,q ∈ [3·2^20, 2^22)`) at
`B = 2000..6000`; these are **per-instance statements at fixed `B`**, and **no exponent is
claimed to move** (and cannot, for a fixed-`B` per-instance result).

**Net:** P4 is closed as a validated negative, now for a **mathematical** reason (the inequality
direction) as well as an empirical one (the paid work doubles). The proved `rank ≤ Q` ceiling
remains a real, sieving-free, per-instance statement — it just prices the rank, not the work.

# Round 42 — P4 EXECUTED: a validated NEGATIVE with a measured mechanism, and a SIGN FLIP that CORRECTS #440

Round 42 executed the campaign's P4 lever (round 41's named positive direction) with a
**validated** linear-algebra instrument and a 1,400-instance validated pool. Result:
**P4 is a tautology, and the paid term moves the OPPOSITE way.** This corrects #440.

## Instrument validation (the gate; 11/11 PASS, reported before any number was believed)
`f2rank_r42valid.py`: `T1 rank ≤ min(nrows,ncols)` 300/300; **`T1b` replays the EXACT
discarded main-loop bug** (`rank ≤ ncols` on 1,960 dense 5–11-column matrices, 0 violations);
plus known-rank matrices, permutation invariance, and a mod-2 reference cross-check. The
campaign's earlier bugs (the 200–800-rank blowup, the rational-vs-GF(2) sympy default) are now
permanent regression tests.

## 1. The correlation is REAL and controlled (reproduces round 41)
`k_success` drops in the low-Q arm: **44.74 ± 6.99 (LOW) vs 65.09 ± 5.45 (HIGH)**, ratio
1.455, `t = +13.39` on the between-instance sd. The dose-response over the whole `Q/m` range is
strictly increasing (bin means 44.0, 52.1, 53.0, 54.9, 56.8, 62.2), Spearman `(Q/m, k_success) =
+0.734`, Pearson `+0.767` — **reproducing round 41's `+0.77` (`+0.766` here)**. Cohen's `d = +3.25`.
The control is tight (identical bit-length multiset, fixed `B` and `m`, matched Dickman `u`,
ratio 1.001).

## 2. ★★ BUT IT IS A TAUTOLOGY — the effect carries no information
> **`k_success / Q` is INDEPENDENT of `Q`:** `corr(Q/m, k/Q) = +0.012`, `t = −1.19` (n.s.).
> So `k_success = Q × (a constant)`, **forced by the rank ceiling, not discovered.**

The synthetic arm (uniform GF(2) rows on the ON-columns) makes it exact: `k/Q = 1.0124 ± 0.0287`;
on real instances `k/Q = 1.007`, `t = −0.89`. So the relation is the statement *"a `Q`-dimensional
space needs `Q` rows"* — **not a bound, not an exploitable lever.**

## 3. ★★★ THE PAID TERM MOVES THE OPPOSITE WAY (the sign flip, and the real result)
> **Low-`Q` instances are ≈7.1× MORE expensive to sieve, not less.**

Driving `Q` down does **not** save sieving work. It forces a higher Dickman `u` (fewer split
primes ⇒ each relation is harder to harvest), so the paid sieving cost per relation rises faster
than the relation count falls. **This is a validated negative with a measured mechanism.**

## 4. What DOES survive (the proved ceiling — but it prices the wrong direction)
The **proved** ceiling `rank_{F₂}(M) ≤ Q(N,B)+1` **binds**: `0/68` violations,
`rank/(Q+1) = 0.950` on average (min 0.784, max 0.976), computable in `O(π(B) log B)` with no
sieving. But it bounds the **rank**, not the **paid sieving work** — so for a *cost* bound it
prices the wrong direction. (That is the campaign's recurring lesson, now demonstrated
empirically: a true, tight, sieving-free statement that is orthogonal to the term you pay.)

## 5. SELECTION, not CRT — and the honest reason is measured
CRT control of `(N/r)` for a set `S` needs a modulus `prod(S) < √N` (since `p,q` must be primes
in prescribed progressions), allowing only ≈6 controllable primes at `p ~ 2^20` (7 at `2^21`).
So `Q` cannot be CRT-driven low at cryptographic sizes — it can only be **selected** for.

**Verdict: P4 is a validated negative.** The campaign's one named positive lever is closed —
not for lack of a signal (the signal is real and strong) but because the signal is a **tautology**
and the paid cost moves the **wrong way**. Correction to #440 (which reported the low/high ratio
as a positive controlled relation; it is a tautological one, and the paid term inverts).

# P4 executed: the sieving work to first dependence is a DETERMINISTIC function of the split-prime count, and Q/π(B) is the control (validated instrument)

Main-loop execution of the campaign's P4 lever (open after #439), with a **validated**
linear-algebra instrument.

## Instrument validation — the gate, and two bugs it caught
The first P4 attempt (rank 200–800 with 5–11 columns) was **discarded**. Re-execution caught
two more bugs via validation, before believing any number:
1. **Column-extraction bug** — `mat[0].bit_length()` mis-sized the matrix (`identity(8)` gave
   rank 1). Fixed by passing `ncols` explicitly.
2. **Mis-specified cross-check** — `sympy.rank()/det()` default to the **rationals**; a GF(2)
   matrix with determinant `−2` is full-rank over ℚ but determinant `0 mod 2` (rank-deficient
   over GF(2)). The correct cross-check reduces mod 2.

**Final validation — all pass:** `identity(8)=8`; `6 identical rows=1`; `rank ≤ min(rows,cols)`
on 80 random; **sympy GF(2) (mod-2) cross-check on 60 random matrices, 0 mismatches.**

## P4 result (controlled; one row per instance; between-instance sd as the bar)
Fixed `B=50`; `N=pq` chosen by prime selection to drive `Q(N,B)=1+#{r≤B:(N/r)=+1}` LOW vs a
matched HIGH group; `k_success = rank+1` of the QR relation matrix over `a²−N` (`a ≤ 4000`);
`m` = number of split primes.

| group | Q/π(B) (mean ± sd) | k_success (mean ± sd) |
|---|---|---|
| LOW-Q  | 0.392 ± 0.024 | 6.5 ± 0.5 |
| HIGH-Q | 0.708 ± 0.071 | 11.1 ± 1.0 |

> **`k_success(LOW)/k_success(HIGH) = 0.584`; the `Q` ratio is `0.553`.**

**P4 holds, and stronger than a correlation.** `k_success = m+1` exactly (the relation matrix
reaches full column rank `m`, so `rank = m`, `k_success = rank+1`), and `m` is the count of
primes `≤B` that **split at `N`** — i.e. `m ≈ Q`. So the sieving work to first dependence is a
**deterministic function of the split-prime count**, not a statistical object. Choosing `N` to
drive `Q` low drops `k_success` in near-exact proportion. This converts round 41's `+0.77`
correlation into a **controlled, per-instance relation** — the campaign's first executed positive
lever.

## ★ The honest limit: the bound is proved, its economic value is not
The **proved** ceiling is `rank ≤ Q`; the measurement shows `rank` saturates at `m ≈ Q`, so
per instance `k_success = m+1 ≤ Q+1`. **But the cost to FIND an `N` with low `Q`** (you must
search/select primes until `Q` is small) **may exceed the sieve saving.** That search-vs-sieve
trade is not settled here. **Whether driving `Q` low is net-cheap is the open question**; the
per-instance bound is established, its value is not. (Consistent with round 41's warning: do NOT
extrapolate to NFS — for NFS the ceiling is governed by `r`'s splitting in the defining field, and
none of this transfers to the `L[1/3]` balance.)

Paper: main loop, #440. Companion: #438 (the QR ceiling), #439 (P4 named as the lever).

Validation caught TWO bugs before any number was believed: a column-extraction bug (identity(8)->rank 1) and a mis-specified sympy cross-check (rank()/det() default to RATIONALS; a GF(2) matrix with det -2 is full-rank over Q but rank-deficient over GF(2) — must reduce mod 2). # Round 41 (full) — the QR rank ceiling is PROVED and refutes the record by 1.96×; the Dickman density assumption SURVIVES measurement; and a new per-instance lever (P4) is found

Follow-up/refinement to #438. The full round (13 agents) additionally delivered a
**reassuring positive**: the smoothness-density assumption the whole index-calculus
pricing rests on **survives direct measurement**, and the harvest surface was killed on a
**mis-scaled null**, not on the phenomenon.

## 1. THE PROVED PART (refinement of #438) — report the PROVED factor as 1.96×
The QR ceiling is unchanged: `rank_{F₂}(M) ≤ Q(N,B) := 1 + #{r ≤ B : (N/r) = +1}` — elementary,
per-instance, sieving-free, `O(π(B) log B)`. The synthesis re-derived it from scratch (924
(r,N) pairs, brute-force solvability of `a² ≡ N (mod r)`, **0 violations**) and gives the
conservative figure:
> **`Q/π(B) = 0.5113 ± 0.0286`** (between-instance sd) ⇒ refutes RESEARCH.md:6904 by **1.96×**.

(**Precision vs #438:** this issue reports the *measured* `0.5113` and the *proved* factor
`1.96×`; #438's `0.5157 / 1.94` is the same result at a coarser rounding — the substantive
claim, the per-instance sieving-free ceiling, is unchanged. **The proved factor is `1.96×`;
the "2.7× total" sometimes quoted mixes in a `k_success ≈ 0.72·Q` factor that is MEASURED, not
bounded** — `rank ≤ Q` only forces `k_success ≥ rank+1`, an inequality in the wrong direction
for an upper bound. Report `1.96×`.)

**Conjectural residue (P4 — the new lever).** Across a real 35-instance quadratic-sieve campaign
(27-instance grid `m = 127..753` + 8 larger), the per-instance cost predictor
> **`corr(Q/π(B), k_success/m) = +0.77` at fixed `B` (n = 12), +0.46 at `B = 3000`**, surviving
de-confounding from `B` on fresh seeds.

This is the first **per-instance, upper-bound-flavoured** statement in the thread. The clean
`k_success` is `0.3801 ± 0.0796` (grid, between-instance sd; clustered `0.0743`), and
`k_success` **never reached `m` in 35/35 runs** — so the balance's `E = √B = π(B)` is a **~3×
over-count** of the paid term, and the surplus over the trivial minimum is `~1.22 ± 1.25`
(max 4): there is **no exploitable surplus** (this kills "rank saturation = a computable win").

## 2. ★ THE DICKMAN DENSITY ASSUMPTION SURVIVES (the round's reassuring positive)
Directly auditing the smoothness density that the whole `L[1/3,c]` balance rests on, on a real
QS run:
> **`ρ(u)` predicts the per-magnitude `B`-smooth yield of the QS polynomial within a factor
> `~0.8–1.3` across instances (between-instance spread ~25%).**

So the density assumption — the one the record prices heuristically and round 38 called an
unproved input — **matches measurement** at the operating point. It is still not a *theorem*,
but it is now a *measured* one.

## 3. The harvest surface: killed on a MIS-SCALED NULL, not on the phenomenon
Two attempts at a smoothness-density signal died on the **null**, with a clean rule-7 diagnosis:
the null `ρ(2u)` was evaluated at integers of size `~(b+M)² ≈ N`, but the values actually sieved
(`f(t) = t² − N` for `t ∈ [b, b+M)`) only reach `~2bM ≈ 0.08 N`. The mis-scaling factor is
`log(2M/b)/log B` — itself monotone in `B` — so the "u-slope" was **manufactured by the null**.
Proof it was arithmetic: `ρ(u_F)/ρ(2u)`, computed from `(b,M,B)` alone with **no sieve**,
reproduced the excess to 7–14% at every `B`. A magnitude-matched **proven** ambient control
(random integers of the same size, no conjecture) gave excess `0.990–1.022` — indistinguishable
from 1 (slope `−0.196 ± 0.057`). **So the density itself is fine (see §2); only the test was
mis-set.** A separate "Legendre/Buchstab mechanism" kill was a **straw man** (used
`∏_{p≤B}(1−1/p)`, B-ROUGH density, missing the measured quantity by 20–123×); flipped to the
correct sign (`P[p|f(t)] = 2/p` for a residue prime, not `1/p`), the same data fits with slope
`+1.87` (t = 5.69, R² = 0.70), replicated at `+1.98` on fresh instances.

## 4. Confirmations, retractions, and a text correction
- **The record's `2.176×` finite-`X` Dickman inflation is RIGHT** (re-derived: `Ψ(2×10⁷, 66) =
  207198` by exact DP). The round-41 claim of `10.54×` is **retracted** — `exactpsi.py` silently
  ignored its `y` argument when given a prime list.
- **Text correction confirmed:** the record's `u`-formula at RESEARCH.md:186 is an **algebraic
  error** (reproduced: residual `0.402` vs `4.676`, an 11.6× gap).
- Two more round-40-style errors caught: a "T-scaling" claim confounded by changed B-composition
  (1.56× at matched `B`), and a generator emitting 57/58/59-bit `N` when asked for 60 (pooling
  across sizes) — the generator-population error, in new costume.

## 5. The exact open problem
**Execute P4 properly:** fix `B`, CRT-choose `N ≡ 1 (mod 8·(small primes))` to drive `Q/π(B)`
low, and show the sieving work to success actually drops. That converts the `+0.77`
correlation into a **controlled per-instance upper bound** — the ingredient several closed
surfaces in this record are missing. **Do not extrapolate to NFS:** for single-polynomial QS the
ceiling is `(N/r) = +1`; for NFS it is governed by the splitting of `r` in the defining number
field, and **none** of the `1.96×` transfers to the `L[1/3]` balance.

**Net:** a proved, per-instance, sieving-free correction to a paid term (the QR ceiling, `1.96×`);
the Dickman density assumption surviving direct measurement; a new per-instance lever (P4); and
three honest retractions/corrections. No exponent moves, no method — but this is the round that
turned "the record assumes `≈π(B)` relations and a heuristic density" into "the relation count
is a proved ceiling and the density is a measured input."

# Round 41 — RANK SATURATION: the record's "≈π(B) relations" is provably wrong by ~2× (a Legendre-symbol ceiling, no sieving)

**The second hypothesis of the whole campaign to survive both adversarial refuters** ("attacked
on five fronts, survived all five"; the theorem independently reproduced). It prices a **paid**
term (`E`, the input to the `B²+E²` balance — not an output like the struck class number `h(−pq)`).

## THE PROVED PART (elementary, per instance, no sieving)
> For an odd semiprime `N = pq` and a factor base `B < p`, a prime `r ≤ B` can divide a value
> `a² − N` **only if** `(N/r) = +1` (Legendre symbol). Hence the relation matrix satisfies
>
> **`rank_{F₂}(M) ≤ Q(N,B) := 1 + #{r ≤ B : (N/r) = +1} ≈ 0.5157·π(B)`**,
>
> computable in `O(π(B) log B)` **with no sieving at all**.

**Consequence — a record correction.** The record prices the `B² + E²` balance assuming `≈ π(B)`
independent relations (RESEARCH.md:6904). This is **provably wrong by a factor ≈ 1.94**: the
achievable rank is bounded by `Q(N,B) ≈ 0.5157·π(B)`, a **ceiling, not an estimate**, and it holds
per instance with no probabilistic input. (Half the factor-base primes are inert at `N` and simply
cannot contribute a relation — the Legendre-symbol `(N/r)` selects exactly the split ones.)

**Verification (exhaustive, independent of any harvesting code):** 2303 **nonresidue** primes
(`(N/r) = −1`) — **0** admit any `a` with `a² ≡ N (mod r)`; 2352 **residue** primes — **0** lack
one. The bound is tight empirically and per instance.

## THE MEASURED PART (one row per instance, between-instance sd — never a within-pool SE)
`rank / Q = 0.9874 ± 0.0108` (n = 8 instances, m = 1 …): the Legendre ceiling is essentially
attained, so `Q(N,B)` is not merely an upper bound but a **good model of the true rank**.

## A MECHANISM CORRECTION WITHIN THE ROUND
The mining initially attributed the rank deficit to "factor-base activation concentrated in the
small primes, so the tail is never used" (2.78 hits/relation in the smallest decile vs 0.112 in
the largest). That is a **red herring** — a small-prime divisibility artifact. The **real**
mechanism is the **Legendre-symbol selection**: only the ≈ half of `π(B)` that split at `N` can
ever produce a relation, regardless of size.

## What it prices
`E` (the relation count at which the first dependence splits `N`) is an **input** to the sieving
work (cost `≈ E/ρ(u)`), not an output. It is the same term `TradeoffBarrier.lean` and
RESEARCH.md §6 price at `E = √B` (= `π(B)` after the normalisation), and §8.5 names as the
`L[1/2]` barrier's content. So correcting `π(B) → 0.5157·π(B)` **moves a real, paid term in the
deterministic index-calculus / `L[1/2]` balance**, in the right direction (fewer relations needed
than the record assumes ⇒ the balance shifts). This is the campaign's first *proved, per-instance,
paid-term* correction to an index-calculus constant.

## Scope (honest)
This does **not** yield a factoring method or a new exponent: it corrects the **relation-count
constant** in the `B²+E²` balance from `π(B)` to `≈ 0.5157·π(B)`, a factor ~2. Whether that
factor translates into an exponent change depends on where `E` sits in the overall
`L[1/3,c]` / `L[1/2,c]` balance (the `B²+E²` is an `L`-quantity; a constant factor inside it is
an `O(1)` exponent shift, i.e. it does **not** change `1/3` or `1/2`). Its value is a **proved,
per-instance, correctly-quantified paid term** — the kind of input the record has been assuming.
The other round-41 surfaces (harvest cost, factor base) were **killed** — the factor-base one
because "the null is evaluated at the wrong argument scale, and the entire headline is arithmetic,
not measure" (a sharp refuter catch, the instrument itself validated).
title: FACT round-41 — RANK SATURATION: the record's '~pi(B) independent relations' is PROVABLY wrong by ~2x. For odd N=pq, B<p: a prime r<=B divides a^2-N ONLY if (N/r)=+1 (Legendre), so rank_F2(M) <= 1+#{r<=B:(N/r)=+1} ~ 0.5157*pi(B) — a CEILING, computable in O(pi(B) log B) with NO sieving, per instance. Verified exhaustively: 2303 nonresidue primes -> 0 admit a solution; 2352 residue -> 0 lack one. Tight per instance: rank/Q = 0.9874 +- 0.0108 (between-instance sd). Corrects RESEARCH.md:6904. Prices a PAID term (E, the B^2+E^2 balance input, not an output like h(-pq)). Mechanism is Legendre selection, not small-prime concentration (that was a red herring). # Round 40 — Cohen-Lenstra: the record has NO such pricing (my premise was wrong), h is OUTPUT not cost, and the family→subfamily bridge is MEASURED FALSE (z=−41.4)

Round 40 attacked the "cheapest work-list item" (Cohen-Lenstra measurement). It is a **kill** —
but the kill corrects a premise **I introduced**, and it produced a real, decisive measured result
and six record corrections. Zero factoring methods in, zero out; a kill is success.

## ⚠️ CORRECTION 1 — the premise was MINE and it was FALSE
`grep -i "cohen.lenstra\|cohen.martinet"` over `Catalog/Cryptography/FactoringBarriers/`
(RESEARCH.md, all `.lean`, NegativeResults.lean) returns **ZERO hits**. The record's 18 "Lenstra"
hits are Lenstra–Pomerance, Bühler–Lenstra–Pomerance, ECM, Kleinjung–Bos–Lenstra,
Bernstein–Lenstra; its 3 "Cohen" hits are Cohen–Oesterlé. **The record does NOT price the
class-group route by Cohen–Lenstra** — it prices it by **ERH-conditionality**
(RESEARCH.md:9852–9857). The work-list item (and my round-40 framing) targeted a **citation that
does not exist in this record**, introduced by a prior round's scratch header. Recorded here so
the next round does not chase it again.

## ⚠️ CORRECTION 2 — Cohen-Lenstra's odd part is a CONJECTURE, not a theorem
Smith, *Recent Progress around Cohen-Lenstra Heuristics* (arXiv:2606.06024): the odd part
remains "still almost entirely unproven"; the 2-primary part is Gerth's conjecture
(Fouvry–Klüners) and higher `2^j` (Smith). CL-1984 could not be opened; the statement was taken
verbatim from Smith arXiv:1710.01350 §2 and Delaunay–Jouhet arXiv:1303.7337, which label it
**Conjecture 1**.

## ★ THE DECISIVE KILL — `h(−pq)` is the OUTPUT of Hafner–McCurley, not an input
Hafner–McCurley's own abstract (opened verbatim): *"expected running time of `L(d)^{√2+o(1)}`
… Thus, of course, also **includes the computation of** the class number `h(−d)`."* **`h` does
not appear in the cost.** So **no amount of class-number measurement converts the pricing from
conjectural to measured** — the quantity measured is a *byproduct*, not a term the algorithm
pays. (The earlier "first alive" relation-pool reading was refuted as **non-binding**: supply
16–38× surplus over demand, so it cannot set a price either.)

## ★★ THE REAL MEASURED RESULT — the family→subfamily bridge is FALSE (z = −41.4)
Cohen–Lenstra/Cohen-Martinet equidistribution is over the **family** of imaginary quadratic
fields. Measured transfer to the factoring subfamily `D = −4pq` (semiprime discriminants vs the
whole family, `n = 44,099 / 107,660`):
> **z = −41.4**; the ratio falls **−12%**, and the gap **widens** with `|D|` (−2.0 → −32.9 across
> 7 slices).

So the family-equidistribution **does not transfer** to the discriminants factoring actually
uses. This is a clean, decisive rule-6 result: the pricing the route would need is not just
unproved, it is **measurably false**.

## Further record corrections (six)
- **Genus theory, 0 violations in 20,000 cases** — but RESEARCH.md ~2620's "the 2-torsion is
  EXACTLY `C₂` … for **every** such `N`" is **false for `N≡1 (mod 4)`** (`D=−4pq` has three
  prime discriminants, 2-rank 2, `|Cl[2]|=4`, 50.2% of the family). The record's *conclusion*
  survives; its *universal* does not.
- **CF period of `√(pq)`**: median exponent **0.4329** (680 points, 112 bits, `R²=0.976`) —
  extends the record's 4-point note; the record's `Θ(√N)` is the **upper tail** (`0.5` is the
  p95=0.514), not the median.
- **Finite-`X` Dickman inflation factor `2.176×`** at `X=2e7, B=66` (exact enumeration) —
  reusable by any future finite-size pricing.
- The record's "p divides a convergent in 1/12" is **not reproduced** (measured 57.5%);
  retracted as an unscoped citation.
- A **record correction on the round's own ℓ-part normalisation** (true `P(ℓ∣h) = 1−∏(1−ℓ^{−k})`;
  the earlier `1/(ℓ(ℓ−1)²)` was mis-normalised).

## ★ A NEW SCREENING RULE (banned pattern)
**Generator-population error:** a per-instance quantity measured by **pooling over instances**,
with a within-pool SE reported as a z-score. The z=22–182 significances were against a null that
**ignored the dominant variance component** (sd(log F) ≈ 0.71 between instances). **Every future
measurement must be one instance per row, with the between-instance sd as the error bar.**

## The exact open problem (and a recommendation)
A per-instance class-number bound would need (i) a theorem transferring class-group statistics to
the **almost-prime** discriminant family `D=−4pq` (Smith: results reach only the 16-rank,
Koymans–Milovic 2019 — *"beyond that … all is darkness"*); (ii) a family-limit → single-`N`
bridge, which CL by construction never supplies; and (iii) an identification of which term in
`L[1/2,√2]` the class number is *supposed* to price — since `h` is on the **output** side.
**Recommendation: strike the Cohen–Lenstra work-list item permanently.** Two named replacements,
both terms the algorithm actually pays: **rank saturation** (how many relations before the `F₂`
matrix is full rank) and **harvest cost** (sieving operations per relation).

CL's odd part is a CONJECTURE (Smith: 'almost entirely unproven'), not a theorem. DECISIVE: h(-pq) is the OUTPUT of Hafner-McCurley ('also includes the computation of h'), not a cost term — so no measurement converts the pricing from conjectural to measured. REAL RESULT: the family->subfamily bridge is MEASURED FALSE (z=-41.4, ratio -12%, gap WIDENING with |D|) — CL equidistribution does not transfer to the factoring discriminants D=-4pq. Six record corrections (2-torsion C2 universal false for N=1 mod 4; CF period median exponent 0.4329 not 0.5; finite-X Dickman inflation 2.176x; 1/12 convergent claim not reproduced). # Cohen-Lenstra measurement: h(Q(√(−pq))) is ~0.26·√N and ALWAYS EVEN — confirming the which-factor wall and correcting the "small h" misconception

Round 40 (the cheapest work-list item: pure enumeration). Direct computation of the class number
`h(Q(√(−pq)))` via reduced primitive binary quadratic forms, for **200 balanced semiprimes**
`p,q ∈ [500, 6000]`, fundamental discriminant `−pq` (if `N≡3 mod 4`) or `−4pq`:

> **mean h = 752.3, median = 650, max = 2786.  mean ratio h/√N = 0.2609.  Parity: 100% EVEN (200/200).**

## Fact 1 — h is even for EVERY semiprime (confirms the machine-checked which-factor wall)
By genus theory the 2-rank of `Cl(Q(√(−pq)))` is `ω(D)−1 = 1` (D has two odd prime factors),
so `2 | h` always. Measured: **200/200 even.** This **empirically confirms** the
machine-checked claim (`NegativeResults.lean` row 21 / the round-33 harvest) that the imaginary
`Cl(Q(√(−pq)))` has its 2-torsion **forced to `C₂`** — so the class number of the *factoring field
itself* is **structurally blind to which factor is which.** A factor-labeling reader of `h` gains
exactly zero bits from its parity, because the parity carries no which-factor content.

## Fact 2 — h ≈ 0.26·√N, NOT subpolynomial (corrects a real misconception)
Consistent with the analytic class number formula `h ≈ √D/π·L(1,χ)`: `√N/π ≈ 0.318√N`, and the
measured `0.26√N` ⇒ `L(1,χ) ≈ 0.8` on average, exactly the expected size. **So the
Hafner–McCurley subexponential factoring does NOT come from the class number `h` being small**
(it is `~√N`); it comes from the class **GROUP structure** — the smooth part / largest prime
factor of `h`, which is `exp(O(√(lg N·lg lg N)))`. Anyone who prices the class-group route by
"enumerate the `h` reduced forms" is pricing a `Θ(√N)` term, not the subexponential one. The
record's Hafner–McCurley `L[1/2,√2]` is a *group-structure* bound, and this measurement makes
the distinction concrete.

## What remains conjectural (unchanged, and this round does not touch it)
Cohen–Lenstra is a statement about the **family** of imaginary quadratic fields (a probability law
weighted by the Cohen–Martinet constant). The **per-instance** behaviour of the single field
`Q(√(−pq))` for a given `N` is **not** thereby bounded, and no measurement of finitely many `N`
changes that. This is a finite, reproducible statistic that (a) confirms the which-factor wall
empirically and (b) corrects the "small `h`" misconception — but it prices **no per-instance
cost**. The genuine open problem is a **per-instance (worst-case) class-number bound**, which
would need the missing ingredient: an unconditional **upper** bound on the relevant part of
`h(Q(√(−pq)))` for a single, adversarially-chosen `pq` — the same structural gap that closed the
smoothness horn (round 38) and the transcendence surface (round 39).

**Note on a premise (corrected by the round-40 mining):** "Cohen-Lenstra is a theorem" is
**false** as stated in the relevant sources — the distribution claim is labelled a *conjecture*.
This measurement is independent of that distinction: it is a direct, finite computation, not an
invocation of any distribution theorem.
title: FACT round-40 (main-loop) — Cohen-Lenstra MEASUREMENT: h(Q(sqrt(-pq))) ~ 0.26*sqrt(N) and ALWAYS EVEN (200/200). EVEN 100% = genus theory (2-rank=omega(D)-1=1), so the class number of the FACTORING FIELD is structurally blind to which-factor — empirically confirms the machine-checked forced-C2 which-factor wall. h ~ 0.26*sqrt(N) NOT subpoly (analytic formula, L(1,chi)~0.8) — so Hafner-McCurley subexp does NOT come from h being small but from the class GROUP structure (smooth part of h); pricing the class-group route by 'enumerate h forms' is a Theta(sqrt N) term, not subexp. Finite reproducible stat: prices no PER-INSTANCE cost. Open: worst-case class-number bound for a single Q(sqrt(-pq)) — same missing upper-bound ingredient that closed smoothness+transcendence. Premise corrected: 'Cohen-Lenstra is a theorem' is FALSE (a conjecture); this is a direct computation

# Round 39 — Transcendence theory is CLOSED for factoring, by OBJECT MISMATCH (Matveev never sees N) — plus a reusable vacuity filter

Round 39 swept the last un-attacked surface (Baker / S-unit / Subspace / Darmon–Granville —
the "only classical route from existence to largeness"). I independently confirmed this surface
is **virgin**: the record has **zero** hits for Baker, S-unit, Subspace, transcendence, Frey,
Mihailescu, or Catalan. The verdict: **no transcendence theorem prices any term a factoring
algorithm pays** — but the reason is new and sharp, and the round produced a reusable filter.

## The kill: OBJECT MISMATCH, not direction
Baker/Matveev, Evertse, Beukers–Schlickewei and the Subspace theorem bound solutions to a
**fixed** exponential equation in a **fixed** finitely generated group, with parameters
`(t, D, max|bᵢ|, h(γᵢ))` or `(m, s=|S|)`. The term factoring pays is
`Ψ_F(x, x^{1/u}) = #{t ≤ x : F(t)=t²−N is B-smooth}` — a count over the values of a **moving**
polynomial, with `N`, `x` and `B = x^{1/u}` **all varying**. **Matveev never sees N.** No
sharpening of a constant bridges that: it is a **category error, not a distance.**

## The deep reason (the round's real content)
> **Every theorem here excludes, by hypothesis, exactly what factoring hands it. Divisors of N
> are a MONOID in the free abelian group `⟨p₁,…,p_ω⟩` — maximally multiplicatively DEPENDENT;
> Baker controls FREE SUBGROUPS.**

The one direction-correct shape (an upper bound on a count) needs `S` specified, and
`S = {∞}∪{q ≤ B}` **grows with the input** — which is exactly where its power lives and where
it dies. Rule 6 bites literally: the smoothness form **vanishes by construction**
(`p−1` B-smooth ⟺ `Σ e_q log q − log(p−1) = 0`, measured 0.0 at 200 dps, with a discriminating
negative control at `|L| = 21.44`), and the S-unit normalisation requires `1/N ∈ Γ_S`, i.e.
`primes(N) ⊆ S`, i.e. **N already factored** — circular. Darmon–Granville's degeneracy is
`c = 0`. The smoothness-escape horn is in any case trivially satisfied (`f(0)` is already
`N^{1/2}`-smooth in `O(1)`); the real object is **rank acquisition**, which is linear algebra,
not transcendence.

## ★ A reusable VACUITY FILTER (adopt as a standing pre-flight check)
> Base-45 per rank: `45^{π(B)+1} > 2^{1024}` as soon as `π(B) ≥ 187` (first at `B = 1109`). At
> the ECM point `|S| = 443,438`, the best published bound is `10^{733,097}` against
> `Ψ ≈ 10^{228}` — **~7.3×10⁵ orders of magnitude worse than doing nothing.** Non-vacuity
> would require base `< 1.0016`.

**Adopt this for ANY exponential-in-`|S|` or exponential-in-rank bound:** a theorem whose
numeric output exceeds the trivial bound is not a result. (This is round 38's "direction"
lesson generalised: a real, explicit, published theorem can still be vacuous at the operating
point.)

## A real (but unpriced) theorem, and a self-retraction
- **HKKPW (arXiv:2211.14399, Hirata–Kohno–Kawashima–Poels–Washio) Thm 1.1** — a genuine, fully
  explicit, uniform improvement on Evertse for every `(m,s)`, base 45 vs 49. A real theorem —
  it prices the solutions of a **fixed** S-unit equation, which nobody pays.
- **★ SELF-RETRACTION.** This round asserted "`Baker` is a *small*-solution theorem; the
  work-list's 'solution is large' is backwards." That is **struck**. `|Λ| > cB^{−K}` with a
  Diophantine `|Λ| < δ` gives **`B > (δ/c)^{−1/K}`** — a *lower* bound on coefficient size,
  the signature of a **large**-solution theorem (raw bound `n < 6.6×10^{28}`, reduced by
  Baker–Davenport to the published `n ≤ 42`). **The work-list's phrasing was correct; the
  retraction is ours.**

## Rigor notes that must NOT be absorbed into the record
- The **Dickman parameter for smooth values of `t²−N` is `u = (½ log N + 2 log x)/log B`, NOT
  `log x/log B`** — a definitional error that manufactures a fake gap or a fake excess. Four
  "measured" Dickman figures in one submission were wrong by 1–3 orders (true `log₁₀Ψ`:
  9.72 / 21.76 / 26.65 / 34.68).
- The ECM working point "`p ≈ 2⁵¹²`, `B = 6.4793e6`" is internally inconsistent (`6.47e6` is the
  ~35-bit value; at 512 bits `B ≈ 2⁵⁶³`) — the conclusion is invariant and a fortiori stronger.
- `log₁₀ 45^s = 733,097` (not 733,062); the vacuity threshold is `s ≥ 187` (not 190).
- "`50.54%` of bases succeed" is ill-posed (`r` even ⟹ `m` non-integer); corrected: `a^r = 1`
  for 100% of units, tautologically.

## The open problem (precise)
> **Is there any quantity in a factoring running time that is a solution count for a FIXED form
> in a finitely generated group, uniform in the input?** Everything found this round says no.
> Størmer/Pell (§5d), Baker–Heegner–Stark, Stewart/Batte–Luca, and the S-unit family are now
> **four dead branches** of the same obstruction and should be listed as such.

**Net:** no method, no exponent move, no new finite computation. One retraction of our own
direction claim, one reusable vacuity filter, one modest real theorem (HKKPW) that prices
nothing factoring pays, and a definitive closure of the transcendence surface.
title: FACT round-39 — TRANSCENDENCE CLOSED for factoring by OBJECT MISMATCH (Matveev never sees N): Baker/Evertse/Subspace bound a FIXED form in a FIXED group; factoring pays Psi_F over a MOVING polynomial with N,x,B varying — a category error. DEEP REASON: divisors of N are a MONOID in the free abelian group (multiplicatively DEPENDENT); Baker controls FREE SUBGROUPS. Rule 6: the smoothness form vanishes by construction (0.0 at 200dps); S-unit normalisation needs primes(N) subset S = N already FACTORED (circular). REUSABLE VACUITY FILTER: 45^(pi(B)+1)>2^1024 at pi(B)>=187; ECM-point bound 10^733097 vs Psi~10^228 = 7.3e5 orders worse than nothing — adopt for any exp-in-|S| bound. SELF-RETRACTION: 'Baker is small-solution' struck (B>(delta/c)^(-1/K) is a LARGE-solution bound). Dickman param for t^2-N is u=(1/2 logN+2 logx)/logB. Open: is ANY factoring term a fixed-form solution count uniform in the input?

# ERRATA to #432/#433 (round 38) — the identity is exact, but the PRICE was conditional; and the record's "absolute density barrier" must be downgraded

Round 38's own adversarial refuters, on the full text, materially corrected the two papers I posted
hours ago. Recording the corrections here and on the originals.

## ⚠️ #432 (ECM exact price) — the identity stands, the PRICING is CONDITIONAL
**Theorem 1 is exact and verified** (`Σ_{m≤X} gcd(m,k)/m = Σ_{d|k}(φ(d)/d)·H_{⌊X/d⌋}`; I
re-ran it independently to relerr 0…1e-16). That part stands.

**But the conclusion `curves = 1/R_H(B,X) ≳ X/(1.0828·ln B)` is CONDITIONAL on group orders
being UNIFORM in the Hasse window** — which is the standard ECM assumption, *not a theorem*
(rule 6). Averaging over a uniform distribution of orders is the very model the round was
mandated to strip out. Therefore:

> **#432 does NOT close the "no lower bound of any kind" gap.** It supplies an **exact,
> assumption-free identity** for the order-completion probability *given* a distribution over
> group orders, plus a proved two-sided band **conditional on that distribution**. It prices
> no unconditional ECM quantity. The "first PROVED pricing of an ECM term" claim in #432 is
> **withdrawn**; the honest claim is "an exact identity that isolates precisely the unproved
> step (the order distribution)."

This is, ironically, a *cleaner and more useful* result than the over-claim: the identity
**localises** the ECM heuristic to a single input.

## ⚠️ #433 (Dickman bounds + uncredited lemmas) — real sources, wrong direction
- The **Weingartner (2606.07785) and Gorodetsky (2211.08973) bounds are real and should be
  credited** (with ranges), turning RESEARCH.md:6693's unnamed "PROVEN" into named theorems.
- But they **price a constant (ρ(u)), not the density of smooth values of a STRUCTURED
  sequence** (rule 7): the record charges ρ to the smooth values of `t²−N` (QS) / the NFS
  linear form, and the ρ→Ψ_F passage is precisely the unproved step. So they do **not** price
  a real algorithm term.
- `L_lower_sieve` is a union bound (axiom-free) but bounds **supply from below** — the wrong
  sign: it makes factoring *easier* and is vacuous for `u > e`. "First lower bound" is
  **withdrawn**; it is an axiom-free finite shadow of classical Ramaswami, not new mathematics.
- **Do not enter the `(log(1/α))^{1+…}` sandwich** — it appears in none of the five sources
  opened; the real statement is `Ψ = xρ(u)(1+O_ε(log(u+1)/log y))`.
- **Decoys struck** (independently confirmed): `Algebra/SmoothWindows/` is signal processing;
  `SingmasterSmoothness/Hierarchy` is Pascal's triangle; `SchubertSmoothPatterns` is
  permutation pattern avoidance. None bear on smoothness of integers.
- **Hygiene, mandatory:** three hand-rolled Dickman solvers destabilised past `u≈3`, and one
  report's "measured grid" was its own formula × 0.885–0.964. **No Dickman number enters this
  campaign without cross-validation against a certified source.** A bound in Mine (2410.09558)
  also had a **dropped radical** (`γ_f = ½ + t + √(t+t²)`), currently verified by one refuter
  only (rule 5: needs a second before it enters the record).

## ★ THE ONE SUBSTANTIVE EDIT TO THE RECORD
The round's most important output is a **downgrade** of the record's rhetoric. RESEARCH.md:6685
claims the density barrier is **"absolute … for any method, in any sampling or inspection
model."** That is a theorem-shaped claim whose necessary ingredient **does not exist** (see the
open lemma). It must be **downgraded to CONJECTURED-absolute**. Likewise RESEARCH.md:6693's
"closed by a theorem, not a conjecture" over-claims (the Dixon case smuggles an equidistribution
assumption). The honest statement of the gap:

> **The exact open lemma.** For `F = t²−N` (QS) and the NFS linear form, prove an
> unconditional **upper** bound `Ψ_F(x, x^{1/u}) ≤ C·x·ρ(d₁u)···ρ(d_ku)`, or even `≤ x^{1−δ}`,

# Two external/internal finds from the smoothness gap: explicit Dickman bounds (arXiv:2606.07785) and a battery of uncredited proved smoothness lemmas

Companion to #432 (the ECM exact price). Round 38 also surfaced two things absent from the
9,771-line record.

## (1) arXiv:2606.07785 — explicit bounds for Dickman's function (new, verified at source)
**"Explicit bounds for Dickman's function"** establishes numerically explicit upper and lower
bounds for `ρ(u)` — the natural density of integers whose largest prime factor is `≤ n^{1/u}`
— with **relative error `< 0.005/u²` for all `u ≥ 5`**, allowing approximate evaluation of
`ρ(u)` without solving the delay differential equation. (I opened the abstract and confirmed
title + statement.)

**Why it matters here.** The Dickman function is the currency of the smoothness half of this
campaign: ECM stage-1 firing, `p−1`, the NFS relation-collection, and Harvey's smoothness sieve
are all *priced* in units of `ρ(u)`. Until now the record could only treat `ρ(u)` as a formal
function (or approximate it by solving the DDE). A paper giving `ρ(u)` to a **proved 0.5%/u²
relative error** means: **every smoothness-dependent constant in the record can be pinned to a
rigorous interval, not a heuristic** — the first concrete tool for turning the campaign's
admitted "no lower bound / unproved Dickman model" gap into *bounded* statements. It does not
change any exponent; it makes a family of constants rigorous.

## (2) A battery of PROVED, entirely UNcredited smoothness lemmas in the Catalog
Grepping all 16 relevant basenames against `RESEARCH.md` returns **zero hits** for every one:
`SmoothNumberLowerBound`, `ScaleSmoothnessDispersion`, `SmoothnessDispersionDecay`,
`SubexpStratumDickmanTail`, `SingmasterSmoothness`, `SingmasterSmoothHierarchy`,
`SchubertSmoothPatterns`, `ECMStage1SmoothPart`, `Algebra/SmoothWindows`, …

The flagship is **`SmoothNumberLowerBound.lean`**, theorem **`L_lower_sieve`**:
> `x − Σ_{y<p≤x, p prime} x/p ≤ L x y`,  where `L x y = #{n ≤ x : P⁺(n) ≤ y} = Ψ(x,y)`.

This is a **pure union bound** — **no random model, no distributional assumption** (rule-6
clean), giving a rigorous *lower* bound on the count of `y`-smooth numbers. Its companion
`L_lower_under_U` and the strict deficiency `L_two_mul_lt` (Bertrand-type) are also proved.
The agent re-proved `L_lower_sieve` from scratch in Lean (against the locally built Mathlib) as
a third independent check, since the pinned toolchain is unavailable on this box.

**Why it matters.** This is the campaign's own admitted gap — "no lower bound of any kind" —
and here is a machine-checked, assumption-free lower bound on the single counting function the
whole smoothness side of factoring rests on. It prices the ECM/p⁻¹/NFS smooth-count term from
one direction (the #432 identity prices it from the other, and the Dickman bounds pin the
density). Together these three form a coherent, first partial answer to the gap.

**Scope (honest).** None of this beats `N^{1/5}`, changes the deterministic frontier, or
produces a factoring method. All three are **pricing/rigour results** — the campaign's genuine
contribution to the "everything is heuristic" problem that the record itself flags. The
honest note the round-38 miner recorded: the Dickman-density *direction* (ρ as a LOWER bound
on density) is the wrong side to price a relation-COLLECTION cost, which needs an UPPER bound
on the smooth count; but the #432 identity and the union bound supply the useful directions.

# The ECM stage-1 firing rate has an EXACT, assumption-free price — killing the record's random-model baseline

Round 38 (proof-side smoothness gap). The record prices the ECM stage-1 expected number of
curves with the RANDOM model `1 − exp(−1.44·B1/p)`, and admits (RESEARCH.md 321/7538/7674)
that it has **"no lower bound of any kind."** This surface yields an **exact identity** and a
**proved two-sided price** instead. **This is new (nothing in the record aggregates over the
group order) and it CORRECTS the ECM baseline** — replacing an unproved random-model constant
with an assumption-free prime-product constant. It is the first PROVED pricing of an ECM term
the record uses heuristically, closing one branch of the "no lower bound" gap.

Notation: `k(B) = lcm(1..B)` = the record's own `stage1Scalar` (`ECMStage1OrderCompletion`).
For a curve over a prime field of size `X`, Hasse puts the group order `m ∈ I = [A, A+W]`,
`A = X − ceil(2√X)`, `W = 2ceil(√X)+1`. Define the average stage-1 firing rate
`R_H(B,X) := (1/W)·Σ_{m∈I} gcd(m,k(B))/m` — the exact per-curve order-completion probability
averaged over uniform group orders in the Hasse window. This is the record's own `gcd(m,k)/m`,
aggregated.

## Theorem 1 (EXACT IDENTITY, assumption-free, elementary)
> `Σ_{m≤X} gcd(m,k)/m = Σ_{d | k, d≤X} (φ(d)/d)·H_{⌊X/d⌋}`,  `H_n = Σ_{j≤n} 1/j`.

**Proof.** `gcd(m,k) = Σ_{d | gcd(m,k)} φ(d) = Σ_{d | k, d | m} φ(d)`; interchange the two
finite sums; `Σ_{m≤X, d|m} 1/m = (1/d)·Σ_{j≤X/d} 1/j`. Restricting `m` to the Hasse window `I`
gives the same statement with `Σ_{j : dj ∈ I} 1/(dj)` in place of `H/d`. No assumption enters.

**Verification (main loop, independent of the mining agent).** Direct gcd-sum vs the
φ-weighted divisor sum agree to relative error `0 … 1.2e-14` on `(B,X) = (10,10³), (20,5·10³),
(7,30²), (5,10²)`, … (I re-derived and re-ran this myself; the mining agent's harness also
agrees to `6e-15…1.2e-14`.)

## The proved price
`curves = 1/R_H(B,X)`, and from the identity,
> `curves ≳ A / Π_{p≤B}(1 + 1/p) ≍ X / (1.0828·ln B)`

in the regime where the tail term `Ψ_pow(B, A+W)/W` is small compared with
`Π_{p≤B}(1+1/p)` — which held in all 8 computed cases (`Ψ_pow/W = 1.0` against
`Π = 2.74…8.69`, within a factor 3–8). The record prices the SAME term with the unproved
constant `1.44` from the random model; the exact identity replaces it with an assumption-free
Euler-product constant. The two coincide to within the tail factor in the computed regime, so
**this is a rigorous justification of the record's baseline, not a refutation of its value** —
the random constant 1.44 happens to be close, but it is now a theorem rather than a heuristic.

## Scope (honest)
- This does **not** beat NFS and is not a method — it is a **pricing/barrier result**. Its
  value is that it puts a *proved* number under a term the record (and the state of the art)
  assume, which is exactly what the round's rule-6 mandate demanded.
- The `Ψ_pow/W` regime condition is stated explicitly and was checked in all computed cases; it
  is a hypothesis of the *asymptotic form*, not of Theorem 1 (which is exact and unconditional).
- The full firing-rate analysis across the Hasse window, and the `p−1` analogue, are the
  companion results; the broader round-38 surfaces (the uncredited
  `SmoothNumberLowerBound.lean` `L_lower_sieve`, the Dickman/de Bruijn direction) are reported
  in the round synthesis.

**This is the first machine-checked, assumption-free ECM pricing in the campaign — a real,
new, rigorously-verified result, and a correction of provenance (random model → theorem).**
title: FACT round-38 — the ECM stage-1 firing rate has an EXACT, assumption-free price, killing the random-model baseline: Theorem 1 (exact, elementary, no assumption) sum_{m<=X} gcd(m,k)/m = sum_{d|k,d<=X} (phi(d)/d) H_{X//d}, k=lcm(1..B)=stage1Scalar, proved via gcd(m,k)=sum_{d|gcd}phi(d) and interchanging finite sums. Verified to relerr 0..1.2e-14 by the main loop independently. Proved price curves ~ A/Prod_{p<=B}(1+1/p) ~ X/(1.0828 ln B), replacing the record's UNPROVED random-model constant 1.44 with an assumption-free Euler-product constant. NEW (nothing in the record aggregates over the group order) and it CORRECTS the ECM baseline's provenance: random heuristic -> theorem (the value is close, so it justifies rather than refutes the baseline). First PROVED pricing of an ECM term the record uses heuristically — closes one branch of the admitted 'no lower bound of any kind' gap. Does NOT beat NFS (pricing/barrier, not a method)

# ERRATA to #428/#429/#430 (wide-recon refutation round) — three corrections, incl. a claim re-instated after retraction

The wide-recon round's own adversarial refuters caught real problems in three of this campaign's
papers. Correcting them here, in the same breath they are wrong.

## ⚠️ #430 — TWO RETRACTATIONS (the serious one)
**(i) "1/6 is an INFIMUM, not a minimum" is RETRACTED.** The `additive_sep` agent's headline —
that the campaign's own condition `2β+α ≥ 1+(1−α)n^(−α)` proves `1/6` unreachable — **reinstates
a claim that round 36 had already retracted** (#427: the second-order boost *decays to zero*,
and the argument needs the **unproved** input `n−θ(n) = o(n^{2/3}ln n)`). Presenting it as a
clean exclusion is the campaign's own known failure mode (a retraction re-filed as a discovery).
**The campaign has NOT established that `1/6` is unreachable.** The only rigorous `1/6`/`1/3`
exclusion is **He–Sahai's published theorem (#428)**, which is 1-dimensional — see below.
**(ii) "per-element Dickman capacity = ρ(3) EXACTLY" is RETRACTED.** The covered set is a
**strict subset** of the n^{1/3}-smooth set (measured 0.671× at n=10⁶), so `ρ(3)` is an
upper-bound proxy, not an exact per-element capacity.

## ⚠️ #429 — the Pythagorean re-mined paper needs three corrections
- **The "centrality-locus lemma" is essentially the DEFINITION of a scalar matrix**
  (`W` scalar mod p ⟺ off-diagonals `b,c` and `a−d` vanish mod p) — correct, but tautological,
  not a new theorem. The *consequence* (the non-circular group channel is a coordinate gcd)
  still stands and is the useful part.
- **The word-search cost floor `Y^0.6232` assumed brute force is optimal** — it is not.
  **Meet-in-the-middle halves the search exponent to `Y^0.3116`**, so the "3^L enumeration"
  step is an upper bound on a *suboptimal* search. The robust, assumption-free part is the
  **divisibility floor** `L ≥ log_{3+2√2} Y`; the enumeration exponent is search-dependent.
- **The CF-period branch re-runs `NegativeResults.lean` rows 3 and 21 verbatim** (not new).

The **sound** new Pythagorean facts that survive: `det(word) = ±1` for every word (0 bits,
absent from the ledger); and **`max|W| = (3+2√2)^L / 2` EXACTLY** (ratio 1.000000 at L=2..14),
certifying `jointSpectralRadius(Berggren) = ρ(M₂)` — the two unipotent branches buy nothing.
Sell this as "the first bound free of distributional assumptions," NOT as "better than the fit"
(it is looser in expected cost, and it supersedes the fitted `3^d(p)≈p^1.00` only in rigour).

## ✓ #428 is SOUND — but its scope must be stated sharply
He–Sahai (arXiv:2608.06681) **survived both refuters** (each opened the full text; Thm 1.1 /
Cor 1.2 verbatim; the record-absence confirmed). It unconditionally refutes the
**one-dimensional arithmetic-progression** UMW cover at `(1/3,1/3)`. **Critically — the
campaign's live open content is RANK-2 additive separability** (#426/#427 §4), and He–Sahai's
**Remark 4.2** states the AP version implies the Strong version with **no converse**; the
at-most-one-intersection step (which is genuinely 1-D, since `(u+ic)−(u+jc)=(i−j)c`) **fails
for rank-2 GAPs**. So: **one dimension is now provably insufficient; two remains open.** The
standing door is *narrowed*, not closed.

## Net
Deterministic `1/5` frontier unchanged; **no factoring method**. The wide-recon's genuine
external find is real and published (#428), and it retires the **1-D AP** sub-door. The
Pythagorean route is dead (some of #429's framing overstated). The campaign's honest remaining
open content is **rank-2 additive separability** and the proof-side smoothness/sieve work-list.
