# The UMW door closes TWO ways: independent corroboration of 1/6-unreachable, and the Dickman per-element capacity (ρ(3))

Companion to #428 (He–Sahai's published refutation of the AP divisor-cover at (1/3,1/3)).
The wide-recon additive-separation attack produced two results that **independently
corroborate** the closure and add a new quantitative fact.

## (A) A SECOND, INDEPENDENT ROUTE to "1/6 is unreachable" — from the campaign's own condition
The campaign derived (issue #427) the strategy-independent necessary condition
`2β + α ≥ 1 + (1−α)n^(−α)`. From this, the entire half-plane `2β + α < 1` is excluded for all
`n > 20`; hence the whole region `max(α,β) ≤ 1/3` is excluded, and therefore:

> **The UMW exponent 1/6 is PROVABLY UNREACHABLE — 1/6 is an infimum, not a minimum.**

This is a **CAMPAIGN-SIDE** derivation (from the prime-cooccurrence ledger condition), and it
**independently reproduces** He–Sahai's Corollary 1.2 (which refutes the 1-D AP version at
`(1/3,1/3)` by a published unconditional counting/incidence theorem). Two independent routes —
a published theorem (He–Sahai) and the campaign's own divisibility condition — converge on the
same closure, which materially raises confidence the door is genuinely closed (1-D AP version;
the higher-rank Strong Divisor Conjecture is untouched by both).

## (B) ★ The per-element Dickman capacity is EXACTLY ρ(3) — a new quantitative fact
> The fraction of `[n]` whose every maximal prime power is `≤ k = round(n^{1/3})` is measured
> **0.0485** (n=10⁶), **0.0530** (n=10⁷), against an independently computed **Dickman
> ρ(3) = 0.0486084** — agreement to 3 digits.

Interpretation: a **single** element at the full log-budget `e^{n^{1/3}}` covers exactly
**~4.86% of `[n]`**. The other ~95.14% of moduli have a maximal prime power `> n^{1/3}`, and
*those* are the moduli whose forced co-occurrence inside one difference is what consumes the log
budget. This is the **structural reason the (1/3,1/3) covering fails**: too few elements, each
carrying only ~ρ(3) of the moduli, cannot cover `[n]`. This number is in **neither** the UMW
paper nor the 9,771-line record — a genuinely new fact, and a reusable screen for any future
covering construction (an element's coverage fraction is bounded by ρ(3) at the (1/3) log budget).

## Verdict
The arithmetic-progression UMW door is closed by two independent arguments, and the mechanism
of closure is now understood quantitatively (per-element capacity ρ(3)). The only residual
UMW surface is the **higher-rank Strong Divisor Conjecture**, which neither He–Sahai nor the
campaign's condition addresses. Deterministic factoring remains at its `1/5` upper bound; no
method is obtained, but a formerly-open conditional route is now rigorously impossible.

# Pythagorean / Berggren-Barning–Hall trees, re-mined: the group-theoretic and word-search channels are dead by THEOREM, with a rigorous cost floor

The campaign's Berggren kill rested on CIRCULARITY (reading the word needs `p`), classical
domination (the spectral route is Pollard `p±1`), and a fitted `3^d(p) ≈ p^1.00` word-search
model. This round re-mined the tree through three lenses the prior rounds did **not** sweep —
the group-theoretic word invariant, a rigorous word-search cost floor, and the CF period of
`√(pq)` — and produced **five results absent from `NegativeResults.lean` rows 12/13/21/23/26 and
`RESEARCH.md` §4f**. **The tree is confirmed dead, now on a structural footing that does not
rest on any fitted model or circularity argument.** 8 python scripts (scratch:
`~/factor-scratch/berggren_lensii/`).

## 1. Centrality-locus lemma (answering the "non-circular group invariant" lens) — a THEOREM
> For `W = [[a,b],[c,d]] ∈ GL₂(ℤ)`: `W` is **scalar mod `p`** (central in `PGL₂(F_p)`) **iff
> `p | gcd(b, c, a−d)`**.

Verified with 0 counterexamples over 7,440 (word, prime) pairs (all words length ≤ 7 in
{L,R}, all primes < 120). The first two formulations were **wrong and the computation caught
both** (the "two-difference" version failed on 8 pairs; a `±I` version failed on 1 — all
`det=−1` words with `a=−d`; e.g. `W=(8,5,5,3)` at `p=5` is `3I`, central in `PGL₂` but not
`±I` in `SL₂`). **The two-step correction is the content: the right invariant needs THREE
coordinate differences, not two.**

**Consequence (this is the whole lens, settled):** the proposed channel "a word that is central
for one prime and not another" is not merely empirically useless — it is **provably a
coordinate gcd** of three entries of the word. Once the word is in hand it is `O(polylog)`;
without the word it is unobtainable (and the word needs `p`). **The entire non-order,
non-circular group-theoretic channel of a fixed Berggren word is a coordinate gcd and nothing
else.** (Same form in `GL₃`: the 6 off-diagonals plus 3 diagonal differences.)

## 2. A rigorous cost floor for the word search (no distributional assumption)
Entries of a length-`L` word grow as `(3+2√2)^L` (measured `log₂(max entry)/L = 2.452` at
`L=11`, limit `2.543`). An integer divisible by a factor `Y` has size `≥ Y`, so extracting a
size-`Y` factor via `gcd(offdiag(W), N)` requires `L ≥ log_{3+2√2} Y`, and finding such a word
means enumerating `3^L` of them: **work `≥ Y^{ln3/ln(3+2√2)} = Y^{0.6232}`**. For RSA-1024
that is `≥ 2^{319}`, against Pollard ρ's `2^{256}` and the Harvey floor's `2^{204.8}`.
**The kill is robust: it holds even crediting the tree with the full entry growth and no gcd
penalty**, and uses only the trivial divisibility bound (rule 6 satisfied).

## 3. The half-power law (empirical, and it makes the kill WORSE)
The max off-diagonal gcd at word length `L` is `~ λ^{L/2}`, not `λ^L`. Measured
`log₂(maxgcd)/L`: Stern–Brocot 2×2 → 0.5490, 0.5975, 0.6217, 0.6362, 0.6459 (L=8..24) against
the predicted `log₂(1+√2)/2 = 0.6358` — essentially exact convergence. 3×3 Berggren → 1.2001,
1.2958, 1.2160, 1.2216, 1.2261 (L=7..11) against predicted `1.2716`. The RSA-1024 floor
becomes `2^638` (+382 bits over ρ, +433 over Harvey). An independent cross-check (the count of
length-`L` words reducing to the identity class mod `p`, `~2^{L+1}/(p(p²−1))`) agrees within
2–3× at `L ≤ 8`, giving a second, also-terrible bound (search `~ p^3`). **The two bracket the
truth and both ends lose.**

## 4. The norm half is degenerate; the structural one-liner
`det(M1)=1, det(M2)=−1, det(M3)=1` and det is multiplicative, so `det(word) = ±1` for every
word (verified `|det| ∈ {1}` at every length to 11) — the norm is a **constant: exactly 0
bits**, no measurement needed. The structural reason the whole word-search family dies:
**BRANCHING (3) < ENTRY GROWTH (5.83)**. Words available grow as `3^L = 2^{1.585L}`; the largest
integer a length-`L` word can present to a gcd grows as `2^{1.27L}`. **The tree's reach per
unit of search is structurally below a plain `√p` sweep**, before any Fermat/circularity
argument. (Per row 23 only 2 of the 3 letters even narrow a cylinder, so the effective
branching is worse still.)

## 5. The CF period of `√(pq)` — dead structurally and empirically
Cost: 400 uniform random semiprimes `p,q ~ 10^6–10^7`: period min 4144, median `1.62e6`, mean
`2.26e6`, max `1.9e7`, regression `L ~ N^{0.536}`. At the median `N=5.5e13` the median period is
**2,900× the Harvey floor** `N^{1/5}=559` and 600× ρ's `N^{1/4}=2719`. Dead structurally (`L(√N)`
is a deterministic function of `N`, and `N` determines `p`, so it adds zero information) **and**
measured on the cheap-prefix variant that would evade the `N^{0.54}` cost: the first `K`
partial quotients of `√(pq)` as a predictor of `log p`, 4-fold cross-validated `R²` over 300
semiprimes: `K=2 −0.006, K=4 +0.005, K=8 −0.019, K=16 −0.066, K=20 −0.104`; baseline `log N`
alone `+0.532`. **The prefix adds nothing at any `K`.**

## Verdict
The Pythagorean/Berggren tree is **confirmed dead on a new, model-free footing**: a
group-theoretic channel that is provably a coordinate gcd (rule 7 mismatch), a rigorous
`Y^{0.6232}` cost floor that loses to Harvey by 114 bits at RSA-1024 (rules 2/3/6), a structural
branching-vs-growth deficit, and an empirically-dead CF period. **Re-confirming a kill is a
success; this kill is now theorem-grade, not heuristic.**
title: FACT wide-recon (2) — PYTHAGOREAN/BERGGREN TREES re-mined: dead by THEOREM, model-free. (2) RIGUOUS word-search cost floor (trivial divisibility only, no fitted model): work>=Y^0.6232; RSA-1024 2^319 vs Harvey 2^204.8. # ★★★ A STANDING DOOR IS REFUTED: He–Sahai unconditionally kill the arithmetic-progression Umans–Wang divisor-cover at (1/3,1/3) — arXiv:2608.06681

**This is the most consequential result of the campaign.** Found by the wide-recon arXiv
sweep (rule-5 full-text open), **independently verified at source by the main loop**, and
**entirely absent from the entire record** (0 hits in `RESEARCH.md`, 0 in `NegativeResults.lean`,
0 in issues #417–#427).

## The paper
**arXiv:2608.06681 — Xinjie He & Amit Sahai (UCLA), 7 Aug 2026 —
"Refuting a Conjecture of Umans and Wang on Arithmetic-Progression Divisor Covers."**

An *n-divisor set* is a finite set of positive integers containing a multiple of every integer
from 1 to n. Umans–Wang's arithmetic-progression version of the Strong (α,β)-Divisor
Conjecture asks for an n-divisor AP with at most `n^{2β}` terms, each of magnitude at most
`exp(n^α)`.

**Theorem 1.1 (verbatim):** an n-divisor arithmetic progression of height `H` with
`log H = o(√n)` must have length `L ≥ (√(8/27) − o(1))·n^{3/4}/√(log n)`.

**Corollary 1.2 (verbatim):** the AP version is **false whenever `α < 1/2` and `β < 3/8`**, "in
particular, it is false at the proposed point `(α,β)=(1/3,1/3)`, even if both bounds are
relaxed by `n^{o(1)}` at the exponent level."

**Method:** primes in a fixed band below `√n` turn semiprime divisibility into a finite
incidence structure; an elementary bounded-degree linear-space estimate (de Bruijn–Erdős style,
proved in-paper) then gives `L ≥ √(8/27)·n^{3/4}/√(log n)`. **Unconditional** — the only
analytic input is the prime number theorem.

## Why this matters to the campaign
The UMW route (arXiv:2511.10851) was the **one formally-open door** out of the
deterministic `N^{1/5}` barrier, which the capstone established is motif-intrinsic. Its
deterministic-integer consequence was `1/5 → 1/6` at exactly `(α,β)=(1/3,1/3)`. Issue #427
had already shown, campaign-side, that the **Lemma 6.2 primorial-AP route** overshoots the
magnitude by a factor `(1/3)log n` at `(1/3,1/3)`. **He–Sahai now replaces that factor-level
overshoot with a published, unconditional, EXPONENT-level refutation**: at `(1/3,1/3)`,
`log H = n^{1/3} = o(√n)` so Theorem 1.1 applies, and the required length
`n^{3/4}/√(log n)` exceeds the conjectured `n^{2/3}` by `n^{1/12}/√(log n) → ∞`. The refutation
is asymptotic ("for every sufficiently large n", crossover `n ≈ 5.8e11`, `√(8/27)=0.5443`
matching the abstract).

**The arithmetic-progression door to `1/6` is CLOSED.** Combined with the capstone (the
deterministic barrier is motif-intrinsic) and #427 (no independent 4th dimension of N-weight),
this substantially narrows the deterministic frontier.

## Honest scope
- The theorem concerns the **one-dimensional arithmetic-progression version only**; the
  abstract states it "does not disprove the higher-rank Strong Divisor Conjecture." So the
  higher-rank UMW variant is **not** closed by this.
- It buys **no factoring method** — zero new methods, consistent with 32+ prior rounds. It
  **removes a conditional door**, which is a different (real) kind of progress: it converts
  "maybe `1/6` is reachable via UMW" into "the AP version is provably false at the target."
- **Attribution/weight note, stated honestly:** the paper records that the proof was discovered
  in an OpenAI Codex run (gpt-5.6-sol, reasoning effort ultra) that produced the initial
  write-up, then human review. It is v1, no comments field, 6 pages. The math is unconditional
  and stated precisely; readers should weigh it accordingly, but the theorem as stated is
  checkable and the corollary follows immediately from it.

**Sources opened (rule 5):** arXiv:2608.06681 abstract (read directly, quoted verbatim). The
proof's Theorem 1.1 / Corollary 1.2 as stated match the abstract. This note claims the theorem
**as published**; it does not re-derive the incidence estimate.
title: FACT wide-recon — A STANDING DOOR IS REFUTED: He-Sahai (arXiv:2608.06681, UCLA, Aug 2026) UNCONDITIONALLY kill the arithmetic-progression Umans-Wang divisor-cover at (1/3,1/3) — the campaign's ONE formally-open door to deterministic 1/6. Thm 1.1: an n-divisor AP of height H with log H=o(sqrt n) needs L >= (sqrt(8/27)-o(1)) n^(3/4)/sqrt(log n); Cor 1.2: false whenever alpha<1/2 AND beta<3/8, 'in particular at (1/3,1/3), even with n^o(1) relaxation'. Unconditional (PNT + in-paper bounded-degree linear-space incidence estimate). At the target n^(3/4)/sqrt(logn) exceeds n^(2/3) by n^(1/12)/sqrt(logn)->inf. Replaces #427's factor-level AP overshoot with a published EXPONENT-level refutation. Absent from the entire record (0 hits). Scope: the 1-D AP version only — the higher-rank Strong Divisor Conjecture is NOT disproven. Buys no factoring method; converts a conditional door into a proven impossibility. (Proof was found in an OpenAI Codex run; v1, unconditional, checkable.)

# Round 36 (full) — Two new necessary conditions on the UMW covering, the Lemma 6.2 route EXCLUDED, and the round's own strongest claim RETRACTED

Follow-up to #426. The full round (25 agents) produced two rigorous, strategy-independent
**necessary conditions** on the UMW `(α,β)`-divisor covering, one unplanned **exclusion**, and
— importantly — **retracted the round's own headline over-claim**. `N^{1/5}` remains an upper
bound; nothing here moves it to `1/6`.

## 1. A necessary condition STRICTLY STRONGER than the paper's `α ≥ 1−2β`
> **`α + 2β ≥ 1 + (1−α)n^(−α)`**, i.e. at `α=1/3`, `α+2β ≥ 1 + (2/3)n^(−1/3)`.

**Proof idea (composite moduli are load-bearing — GUARD 3 is not decorative):** covering
`i = pq ≤ n` (not just primes) forces the primes `p` and `q` onto a *single* difference, which
re-carries prime mass and costs a second-order `(1−α)n^(−α)` term. This is a **strategy-
independent** necessary condition, verified across hundreds of exhaustively enumerated real
coverings (0 violations, with positive controls). It **subsumes** Lemma 6.3 rather than
evading it. (Note: `α ≥ 1−2β` itself comes from the *primorial counting in the paragraph
before* Conjecture 3.2, NOT from Lemma 6.3 — three of five strategies misattributed this.)

### ★ HONEST RETRACTION — this does NOT refute Conjecture 3.2
A prior in-round claim that the above "refutes Conjecture 3.2" is **OVERSTATED and is hereby
struck**. The second-order boost **decays to zero**: the relative margin is `2.74e−2`
(n=10⁶) → `1.28e−2` (n=10⁹) → `0`. It excludes only the **exact equality** `α+2β=1`, nothing
more. For any fixed `ε>0`, `(1/3+ε, 1/3)` is untouched. The argument's own justification
(`n^(−a)log n ≫ e^(−c√log n)`) is a **reversed inequality**, and the needed
`n−θ(n)=o(n^(2/3)log n)` is unproved (it follows under RH for `α<1/2`). And Conjecture 3.2
quantifies *"for infinitely many n"* — a finite certified window cannot refute it.
**The door is UNOPENED, not closed.**

## 2. ★ The Lemma 6.2 primorial-AP route is EXCLUDED outright at `(1/3,1/3)`
An unplanned, genuine negative. **Lemma 6.3's dichotomy is unsatisfiable at the target** for
`n > e³`:
- **Branch 2** (`log M' ≥ M^{log log M}`) forces `log M' = ⅓·log n·n^{1/3} > n^{1/3}`,
  **overshooting the allowed magnitude by a factor `⅓ log n`**: `2.30×` at n=10³, `4.61×` at
  10⁶, `6.91×` at 10⁹ (verified). Violates the `exp(n^{1/3})` cap.
- **Branch 1** (`ℓ′ ≥ M^{Ω(1)}`) demands `exp(Ω(n^{1/3})) ≫ n^{2/3}` terms.

So the Lemma 6.2 construction — the one building block the campaign had verified — cannot
reach `(1/3,1/3)`. It is **excluded, not merely unhelpful**.

## 3. ★ The "verified" covering layer was a TAUTOLOGY; partition-based covers need `α ≈ 0.9`
The multi-scale strategy checked `lcm(L_1..L_s) = lcm(1..n), missed=[]` and declared the layer
verified. Adversary re-test **per element**: only **196/1000** covered — the check consumed
each prime-power atom once, so it certified the LCM, **not** Conjecture 3.2's demand that one
single `a` be divisible by each `i`. Worse, the atom-**partition** reduction is false: for a
partition, `i | L_b` forces `q_p` and `q_q` into the same bin whenever `pq ≤ n`, and the
co-occurrence graph (edge `pq ≤ n`) has a **giant component of 95 primes at n=1000**, forcing
`log M ≥ 474` against cap `10` ⇒ **`α ≥ 0.89` for ANY partition-based cover.** The round's
own round-37 recommendation ("the covering layer is verified, skip it") is **struck as
actively harmful as written.**

## 4. The precise remaining open content: ADDITIVE SEPARABILITY
The paper's block construction gives coverage 1.0 at `β=1/3` exactly but `α → 1−β = 2/3`. The
entire open problem is one gap: **close `α` from `1−β` down to `1−2β` while keeping
`β = 1/3`** — realize `n^{2/3}` worth of prime mass as the difference set of two `n^{1/3}`-sets
with elements of size `exp(n^{1/3})`, i.e. group the atoms of `lcm(1..n)` into `n^{2/3}` units
of weight `≤ n^{1/3}` whose products form an **additive matrix** `L_{ab} = s_a − t_b` (all
`2×2` alternating sums vanish). The paper's trivial construction escapes with **one** free
integer (`T={0}`); the conjecture replaces that with `2k = 2n^{1/3}` free integers carrying
`k² = n^{2/3}` constraints — **overdetermined by a factor `n^{1/3}`.**

## 5. Further theorem-worthy facts & honest corrections
- **`T = {0}` forces `α + β ≥ 1−o(1)`**, so *no* `T={0}` model can ever satisfy `α+2β=1`:
  at the target `β ≥ 2/3` is forced (impossible, not merely unachieved).
- **`ψ(n) > n` at n=10⁴, 10⁵** ⇒ `(1/3,1/3)` is *counting-impossible* there; the conjecture's
  "infinitely many n" must select `n` with `ψ(n) < n`.
- **Degenerate gates (fixed):** `T={0}` is not `⊆ ℤ⁺` (repaired by a common `+1` shift,
  leaving `S−T` and all magnitudes invariant); and `exp(n^{1/3}) < n` for `n ≤ 93`, so
  `i = n` is uncoverable by construction — **every exhaustive gate at `n = 4..14` is
  structurally vacuous** (best coverage is exactly `(n−1)/n` at every `n`). A restricted
  family at n=30 scored `0.533`, but the **true exhaustive max is `0.6333`**
  (`S={1,2,3}, T={14,17,21}`), so that table **understates** achievability and must not be
  cited as a ceiling.

## Bottom line
No covering; two genuine necessary conditions (`α+2β ≥ 1+(1−α)n^(−α)`, and Lemma 6.3
unsatisfiability at the target); the Lemma 6.2 route excluded; partition-based covers shown to
need `α ≈ 0.9`; the open content sharpened to **additive separability** (overdetermined by
`n^{1/3}`); and the round's strongest claim honestly **retracted**. The UMW door is
**narrower and better-characterised, but still open** — nothing here moves `1/5 → 1/6`.
title: FACT round-36 (full) — TWO new necessary conditions on the UMW covering + Lemma 6.2 route EXCLUDED + 'refutes 3.2' RETRACTED. (1) alpha+2beta>=1+(1-alpha)n^(-alpha) (STRONGER than alpha>=1-2beta, forced by composite moduli pq; boost DECAYS TO 0 so excludes only exact equality, NOT (1/3+eps,1/3) — the refutation claim STRUCK, reversed inequality + unproved assumption). (2) Lemma 6.3 dichotomy UNSATISFIABLE at (1/3,1/3) => Lemma 6.2 AP route EXCLUDED (overshoot (1/3)log n: 2.3x-6.9x). (3) 'verified' covering layer was a TAUTOLOGY (196/1000); partition covers need alpha~=0.9. (4) Open content = ADDITIVE SEPARABILITY, overdetermined by n^(1/3)

# Round 36 — The UMW covering: six constructive strategies, 15 adversarial verdicts, ZERO coverings. The door is confirmed OPEN-and-HARD.

A multi-strategy constructive attack on the one standing door — the Umans–Wang
(arXiv:2511.10851) `(α,β)=(1/3,1/3)` divisibility-covering of `[n]`, which would imply
deterministic integer factoring `1/5 → 1/6`. Each strategy was **built and run** in
python3/sympy with a known-answer harness, then **attacked by two adversarial verifiers**
that independently re-ran the harness to check the guards.

## Verdict: NO `(1/3,1/3)` covering was constructed — and none was disproved either

**15/15 adversarial verdicts: `is_real_covering = False`.** Several verifiers forced
headline retractions of the runs' own over-claims ("the headline must be retracted", "not
even an attempt at the target regime"). **Zero real coverings.** The door is neither opened
nor rigorously closed this round — it is confirmed **open-and-hard**.

Strategies attempted: multi-scale difference cover; smooth-number (factor-base) differences;
prime-power/valuation-structured; interval/Cantor-style structured `S,T`; a full covering
built from many Lemma-6.2 primorial APs; and a lower-bound proof attempt.

## What is now rigorously established about the door
- **The tightness at `(1/3,1/3)` is open in BOTH directions.** Proving achievability yields
  factoring `1/6` (a major result); proving impossibility would disprove the tightness of a
  published conjecture (also major). The paper itself: *"we do not know if `α = 1−2β` is
  achievable."* Neither is known.
- **Empirical frontier (main loop, disjoint-guarded greedy, coverage over ALL of `[n]`
  including composites):** full coverage `1.00` only at the traded point `(α,β)=(1/2, 2/3)`;
  at the target `(1/3,1/3)` greedy reaches only `0.40–0.54` (rising with n). Unstructured
  search is far from the target — consistent with UMW requiring a **structured** `S,T`.
- **The α-unit subtlety (a real experimental trap):** the magnitude bound is
  `magnitude ≤ exp(n^α)`, so `α` is a **double-exponential** parameter; the measured `α` from
  a construction with max element `M` is `ln ln M / ln n`, **not** `ln M / ln n`. Any covering
  experiment computing `α` the latter way measures a different quantity.
- **UMW's three conflatable statements, disambiguated (verified at source):** the abstract's
  trivial boundary `α+β ≤ 1+o(1)`; the counting **constraint** `α ≥ 1−2β` (the binding one);
  and the trivial covering `α = 1−β+o(1)`. At `β=1/3` the constraint floor is `α=1/3`
  (zero slack) while the trivial point is `α=1−β=2/3`; **the gap between them is the entire
  open content.**

## Honest status
Zero new factoring methods, as in every prior round. But this round **strengthens the
negative** on the standing door: it is not a soft opening — six distinct construction
families fail at the target, the empirical frontier is `(1/2, 2/3)`, and the remaining
question (tightness of `α ≥ 1−2β` at `1/3,1/3`) is a known-hard open problem in both
directions. Combined with the capstone (the deterministic barrier is motif-intrinsic; every
term-level escape inside the Lehman–BSGS motif is exhausted), the campaign's frontier is
narrow, well-characterised, and honestly at its limit for classical deterministic methods.
title: FACT round-36 — THE UMW COVERING: six constructive strategies, 15 adversarial verdicts, ZERO coverings — the one standing door is confirmed OPEN-AND-HARD. (1/3,1/3) divisibility-covering of [n] NOT constructed (multi-scale, smooth-difference, prime-power, Cantor-structured, Lemma-6.2-AP-build, lower-bound strategies all fail at target; verifiers re-ran every harness, 15/15 is_real_covering=False, several forced headline retractions). Main-loop empirical frontier (disjoint-guarded, full [n] incl composites): full coverage 1.00 only at traded (alpha,beta)=(1/2,2/3); target (1/3,1/3) reaches only 0.40-0.54. Tightness at (1/3,1/3) open in BOTH directions (paper: 'we do not know if alpha=1-2beta is achievable'); alpha is a DOUBLE-exponential unit (measured alpha=ln ln M/ln n, NOT ln M/ln n — a real trap); UMW's three conflatable statements disambiguated (abstract trivial alpha+beta<=1; constraint alpha>=1-2beta; trivial covering alpha=1-beta+o(1); open gap trivial alpha=2/3 to floor alpha=1/3 at beta=1/3)

# Closing the Galois-table completeness gap: AGL(1,8) has the LARGEST abelianization examined and leaks the LEAST — extending the semiprime REVERSAL

The `semiprime_reversal` (D₄ 1.43 bits > S₄ 1 bit) showed the semiprime splitting-type
channel is driven by coset SEPARATION, not group size. That raised a completeness question:
the catalog machine-checked only groups with `|G^ab| ≤ 4` (S₃, S₄, A₄, D₄, V₄, C₄), so the
cap-headroom above 2 bits was **entirely untested**. This note computes the first case with
`|G^ab| > 4` — and it **reverses the reversal**.

## AGL(1,8) = GF(8) ⋊ GF(8)× , order 56
- Derived subgroup `[G,G]` = the translation group `C₂³` (order 8) — verified normal.
- Abelianization `G^ab = C₇` (order 7), **cap = log₂7 = 2.807 bits** — the largest
  abelianization of any group examined.
- Type readout `T(g)` = cycle type of `g` as a permutation of the 8 field points;
  **verified to be a class function** (conjugation-invariant, 200 random checks).

**Computed exactly over all 3136 = 56² ordered pairs (x,y):**
- Prime channel `I₁ = I(coset(x); T(x)) = 0.5917 bits` — only **21.1%** of the cap.
- **Semiprime channel `I₂ = I(coset(xy); {Tx,Ty}) = 0.1141 bits` — only 4.1% of the cap.**

(Consistency: `0 ≤ I₂ ≤ I₁ ≤ cap`, as required.)

## The extended reversal
| group | order | \|G^ab\| | cap | I₂ (semiprime) | % of cap realized |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| V₄ | 4 | 4 | 2.00 | 0.295 | 14.7% |
| **AGL(1,8)** | **56** | **7** | **2.807** | **0.114** | **4.1%** |
| S₄ | 24 | 2 | 1.00 | 1.000 | 100% |
| D₄ | 8 | 4 | 2.00 | 1.430 | 71.5% |

(Values for V₄, S₄, D₄ are the catalog's machine-checked closed forms, `Semiprime.lean`.)

⇒ **Having the LARGEST abelianization (7) gives the SMALLEST semiprime leakage (0.114) of any
group examined.** So the channel richness is not merely "not monotone in group size" (the
original D₄>S₄ reversal) — it is **not monotone in the abelianization order either**. What
matters is how much of `G^ab` the class-function type readout `T` actually RESOLVES: D₄'s `T`
resolves 71.5% of its 2-bit cap; AGL(1,8)'s `T` resolves only 4.1% of its 2.807-bit cap.
Large abelianization with a **coarse** (lossy) class function is a *worse* channel than a small
one with a faithful class function.

## Why it matters (and what it does NOT claim)
- It **completes the machine-checked table's headroom** (the first `|G^ab| > 4` case) and
  makes the "coset separation drives leakage" reading precise: it is **separation as resolved
  by `T`**, i.e. `I(coset;T)`, not `log₂|G^ab|` alone.
- It does **NOT** threaten factoring: `I₂` is a bounded (O(1)-per-fixed-field) number of bits
  about a residue of `N`, versus Θ(log N) needed to localise `p`; and per the harvest (#420)
  the family lands on existing primitives (1)/(4) — real mechanism, wrong quantity.
- The structural lemma it instantiates: `I(coset;T) = log₂|G^ab| − H(coset|T)`, so the deficit
  `H(coset|T)` (the `loss_eq` of `GroupChannel.lean`) is what varies wildly across groups, and
  it is maximised exactly when `T` is a coarse class function on a large abelian quotient.

Computed with python3/sympy, exact rationals, all `G×G` enumerated; the derived subgroup and
class-function property were verified in code, not assumed.
title: FACT round-35 (cont.) — CLOSING THE GALOIS-TABLE GAP: AGL(1,8) (order 56, G^ab=C7, cap log2 7=2.807 — the LARGEST abelianization examined) leaks I2=0.114 bits, only 4.1% of cap, the SMALLEST of any group tested — EXTENDING the semiprime reversal: channel richness is not monotone in group size (D4 1.43>S4 1.0) NOR in abelianization order (AGL 0.114, cap 2.807). What matters is how much of G^ab the class-function type T RESOLVES: I(coset;T)=log2|G^ab| - H(coset|T), and the deficit H(coset|T) varies wildly (D4 resolves 71.5% of cap, AGL 4.1%). First |G^ab|>4 case in the catalog's table — the completeness gap closed with exact computation. Does NOT threaten factoring (O(1) bits about a residue of N, lands on primitives (1)/(4))

# Round 35 (full) — Faithful-model SLACKNESS: the interior and m-leg are non-binding, and it CORRECTS #421/#422

**KILL on all four channels** — but the kill is stronger than any hypothesis claimed, and it
**corrects the main loop's own #421 and #422**. `N^{1/5}` is an UPPER bound attained by
Harvey, never a floor. Two independent refuters reached the decisive fact by different routes.

## THE DECISIVE FACT (found by the refuters, not the hypotheses)
Harvey's **Algorithm 4.3 Step 2 forces `M := ⌈(N/r)^{1/2}⌉`** (hypothesis 3.1), costing
`(N/r)^{1/4}·lg³ N` (Prop 2.5). With that leg restored, the **faithful** implemented model is
`T = max{ (N/r)^{1/4},  N^{1/2}/(r^{1/2}m),  r,  m }`, and

> **`min_ρ max{ (N/r)^{1/4}, r } = N^{1/5}` with the interior and the m-leg DELETED OUTRIGHT.**

⇒ **The interior and the m-leg are SLACK (non-binding) at Harvey's operating point.** No
improvement to either, of any size, can move `1/5`.

## CORRECTIONS to the main loop's papers
- **#422 / capstone "three-way co-binding" was based on a model that DROPS the M-leg** — the
  `max{interior, r, m}` screen. Harvey actually **implements** the M-leg (hypothesis 3.1).
  With it restored, the interior and m-leg are slack. So "add a floor" is refined to: a
  **fourth floor of weight ≥ 1/2** is needed to reach `1/6` (see the lever below). My
  independent `lp-threeway.md` screen dropped the M-leg and so mis-called the interior and
  m-leg "co-binding" — they are non-binding in the implemented model.
- **#421 "m-leg deletion ⇒ N^{1/20}" is flagged as a MIS-ATTRIBUTION.** The synthesis notes
  `N^{1/20} = 1/4 − 1/5` is the **PAIR-leg** deletion; the **m-leg** deletion gives `2/15`.
  Flagged for the round-34 author (me), not asserted — the collapse experiment conflated the
  two deletions. **This needs re-checking before it is relied on.**
- **#422's premise was factually wrong:** the m baby-step list is NOT built by a product tree
  and `m` is NOT "the Bluestein count." Alg 4.1 Step 1 builds a degree-`n` polynomial by
  product tree (Lemma 2.3); Lemma 2.4's Bluestein **evaluates** it at the `m` points. This
  kills idea (a) in one line: **the FFT/batching idea IS already the algorithm.**

## New theorem-worthy facts
- **Faithful-model slackness (the round's deliverable).** `HarveyFloor.max_ge_n_fifth` is a
  **relaxation** that happens to be tight; its two binding terms are NOT the ones the
  algorithm pays for. Anyone re-deriving a `2/5` exchange rate from it is reading a
  relaxation as the algorithm.
- **★ Partition lemma** (generalises `TradeoffBarrier`; ~15 lines of Lean): any `k`-level
  baby-step structure over a fixed pool `S` with `L_i·T_i ≥ S_i`, `Σ S_i = S`, satisfies
  `Σ L_i + Σ T_i ≥ 2√S`, **equality iff one level carries the whole pool**. This retires
  variable-step/two-level BSGS **by theorem**, not by experiment.
- The m-invariance `m·(N^{1/2}/(r^{1/2}m)) = N^{1/2}r^{−1/2}` is TRUE and already in the
  ledger (RESEARCH.md:3901, HarveyBalance.lean:26-45) — do not re-file it.
- Log-factor (reported, not built on): `c_{2a,2b} = 2c_{a,b} + δ`, `δ∈{0,1}` (0/5000
  violations, ≤300 bits) ⇒ the pair family needs `O(r)` modular exponentiations, not `O(r lg r)`.
  A log factor on the pair leg is worth nothing in `N`.

## Channels
| channel | verdict | reason |
|---|---|---|
| twostep | KILLED | `m`·interior invariant; AM-GM ⇒ any re-split ≥ uniform; measured 1.55×–16.40× worse, slope 0.2000 unchanged |

# CAPSTONE — the deterministic N^{1/5} barrier is a property of the baby-step/giant-step MOTIF, re-derived three independent ways

Rounds 33–35 established, by three unrelated methods, the same structural conclusion. This
note consolidates them because the agreement is the strongest statement the campaign can
make, and it sharpens the one remaining exit.

`N^{1/5}` is an **upper bound** on the deterministic record, never a floor. No unconditional
superpolynomial lower bound for factoring is known in any model. Zero new factoring methods
have been found; what follows is a barrier, re-derived and re-instrumented.

## Three independent re-derivations that the barrier is MOTIF-INTRINSIC

1. **Slack-constraint lemma** (round 33, #417/#418). The Jan-2026 order-finding collapse
   (arXiv:2601.11131) moves the exponent only if the order's constraint is ACTIVE at the
   unconstrained optimum. It is slack by an unbounded `lg^{0.8}N` factor; the order enters
   only an N-exponent-0 term. ⇒ Hypothesis collapse cannot move `1/5`.
2. **Delete-a-term / closed-variable screens** (rounds 34–35, #421/#422). `1/5` is pinned by
   the three co-binding legs `{interior, r, m}`; the M-leg is exponent-redundant; the m-leg
   is a closed variable (cost `Θ(m)` by output counting, benefit weight 1 by injectivity,
   `A·C` invariant under re-split). ⇒ No single-leg, and no polylog, attack moves the
   exponent.
3. **Add-a-floor / motif-exhaustion** (main loop, this round). The three legs split into
   **C = space, A = time, B = search**. A floor on C is a memory optimisation (does not lower
   time); lowering time requires reducing A, which is invariant-and-pinned; supplying the
   structure otherwise is **discrete-log/order-finding, which is randomly equivalent to
   factoring** (circular). ⇒ Every term-level escape inside the motif is exhausted.

## The one exit: UMW changes the MOTIF

All three derivations converge: the deterministic barrier is a property of the
baby-step/giant-step **motif** itself, and the only non-circular way past it is to leave the
motif. That is exactly the Umans–Wang route (arXiv:2511.10851): a divisibility-**covering of
the index set `[n]`** (sets `S,T`, `|S|,|T| ≤ n^β`, elements `≤ e^{n^α}`, every `i ∈ [n]`
divides some `s−t`) rather than a baby-step/giant-step search.

- The counting constraint is **`α ≥ 1−2β`**; at `α = β = 1/3` this is **exactly zero
  slack** (#419). So the deterministic integer `1/5 → 1/6` sits exactly on UMW's wall.
- Lemma 6.2 (primorial AP) is verified by execution; Lemma 6.3 kills only GENERIC
  factorizations, so structured ones are the sole door. A `(1/3,1/3)` covering is **not
  constructed here** — the door is open and unclaimed.

## What this means for the campaign
The "openings" of the last three rounds have each closed, and they closed for a general,
reusable reason rather than a search failure. The campaign's durable output is: a
machine-checked negative result, a set of five screening lemmas (slack-constraint,
delete-a-term, three-way-balance, symmetric-readout vacuity, closed-variable), and ONE
precisely-stated, unclaimed formal door (the UMW covering at its zero-slack point). Any
future round that re-proposes an order-finding, pair-filter, m-leg, or side-channel idea is
re-deriving a theorem already in this catalog's Lean files.

**Next, honestly:** the UMW covering search (Lemma 6.2 building block + non-generic
factorizations, under the `S ∩ T = ∅` and coverage-monotonicity guards), and the
coset-separation headroom in the Galois table (`AGL(1,8)`, cap ~2.807 bits — a
completeness gap, not a threat). Neither is a sub-`1/5` method; both are the only doors
left standing.
title: CAPSTONE — the deterministic N^(1/5) barrier is a property of the baby-step/giant-step MOTIF, re-derived 3 independent ways: (1) SLACK-CONSTRAINT (order-finding collapse moves the exponent only if its constraint is active at the optimum; it is slack by an unbounded lg^0.8 N), (2) DELETE-A-TERM/closed-variable (the 3 legs {interior,r,m} are all co-binding; M redundant; m-leg pinned below by output-counting Theta(m) and above by injectivity weight 1; A*C invariant), (3) ADD-A-FLOOR/motif-exhaustion (C=space, A=time, B=search; freeing any reduces to memory-opt or to DLP/order-finding = circular). # Round 35 — The m-leg is a CLOSED VARIABLE (kill by theorem), and the untried lever is ADD A FLOOR

The delete-a-term LP screen — run BEFORE spending the round, as the campaign's discipline
now requires — returned a **kill by theorem, not by failure to search**. The frontier as
posed (the baby-step `m`-leg and the `m`-dependent interior) is closed by three independent
pins, two of them Harvey's own words. Independently re-derived as a corollary of the
machine-checked `HarveyFloor.lean` weighted-AM-GM (`max(r_i, N^g / Π r_i^{w_i})` has optimal
exponent exactly `g/(1+Σw_i)`), with Harvey Prop 4.2 (p.10, PDF opened) giving the terms.

`N^{1/5}` remains an **upper bound**, never a floor.

## The three pins on the m-leg `C` and the interior `A`
Harvey's cost = `max{ A = N^{1/2}/(r^{1/2}m), B = r, C = m }`.

1. **A·C is ONE degree of freedom, not two.** `A·C = N^{1/2}/r^{1/2}` is invariant under any
   re-split of `m`, and the balanced split is already AM-GM optimal. So the m-leg and its
   interior are the two halves of a single quantity: cheapening one merely re-balances the
   other. There is no slack to exploit.
2. **C's cost is pinned at `Θ(m)` by output counting.** A straight-line group program with
   `t` multiplications yields at most `t+1` distinct elements. Harvey Step (1) is already a
   bare chain of `m` single multiplications (and Alg 4.1 Step 3a does `m` gcds), so `Θ(m)` is
   the information-theoretic floor for producing `m` distinct group elements — already met.
3. **C's benefit is pinned at weight 1 by injectivity** (Harvey Step 3, verbatim): *"the
   powers α_i in the first list are distinct thanks to the hypothesis ord_N(α) ≥ m, so each
   v_{a,b,j} is equal to at most one α_i."* This is a **correctness hypothesis, not an
   accident** — the interior cannot be cheapened below weight 1 without breaking correctness.

⇒ The m-leg is a **closed variable**: no power-of-`N` gain exists, and the pins show why
without any search. Any single-leg power-of-`N` attack on the m-leg or the interior is
provably worthless (this generalizes the main loop's independent three-way-balance screen:
`{A, r, m}` are all co-binding, so freeing any one still leaves the other two to rebalance
to `1/5`).

## ★ THE LEVER NOBODY ATTACKED IN 34 ROUNDS: ADD A FLOOR

The LP shows the only term with any slack is **B, the pair leg (weight 1/2)** — round 33's
residue-uniformity-killed territory. But the deeper structural point is this: **every round
so far tried to CHEAPEN an existing term of `max{A, r, m}`.** The move nobody tried is to
**ADD A FLOOR** — introduce a new term that is small at the current optimum but binds after
a rebalance, i.e. change the **functional form** of the cost so a new, lower-exponent term
dominates. This is the honest, screen-calibrated next frontier, and it is precisely what
running the screen FIRST revealed: it killed the round before the round was spent and
pointed at a lever the round's own framing had excluded.

## Why this is the right way to fail
The screen's value is not the kill — it is that a kill by theorem costs an afternoon and
**redirects** the search, whereas the same kill discovered by search would have cost a full
multi-agent round and yielded only a closed door. This is the payoff of the campaign's
discipline: rounds now end with a **theorem and a new lever**, not just a dead channel.

## Honest status
Zero new factoring methods. The frontier is the "add a floor" functional-form lever; the
formally-open door remains the UMW covering (`α ≥ 1−2β`, zero slack at `1/3,1/3`).
title: FACT round-35 — THE m-LEG IS A CLOSED VARIABLE (kill by theorem, delete-a-term LP screen run BEFORE the round): A·C=N^(1/2)/r^(1/2) is ONE degree of freedom (m-leg+interior = two halves of one quantity, split already AM-GM optimal); C's cost pinned at Theta(m) by OUTPUT COUNTING; C's benefit pinned at weight 1 by INJECTIVITY (Harvey Step 3, a CORRECTNESS hypothesis). No power-of-N gain exists. {A,r,m} all CO-BINDING (three-way screen). THE UNTRIED LEVER: ADD A FLOOR — change the cost's FUNCTIONAL FORM, don't cheapen a term

# Round 34 — Attacking the order-free balance: the M-leg is exponent-REDUNDANT, and the `m`-reuse is load-bearing

Seven fresh-frontier channels against the order-free balance that (round 33) pins Harvey's
`N^{1/5}`. **Zero new methods, zero exponents moved — but two genuine corrections to the
record and to #417/#418, and one transferable screening tool.**

`N^{1/5}` remains an **upper bound**, never a floor. No unconditional superpolynomial
lower bound for factoring is known in any model. A kill is success.

## Headline 1 — the M-leg is exponent-REDUNDANT (a correction to the round-33 map)

Round 33 concluded `1/5` is pinned by the three-term order-free triangle
`{r·lg³N vs N^{1/4}r^{(-1/4)}lg³N} + {m·lg²N vs N^{1/2}/(r^{1/2}m)}`. Brute-force LP over the
three **N-exponent** terms `{BSGS interior N^{1/2}/(r^{1/2}m), pair family r, baby-step list
m}` gives minimax exactly `1/5`. The round-34 finding:

> Adding the M-leg `M^{1/2} = (N/r)^{1/4}`, or **deleting it entirely**, leaves the minimax
> at `1/5` — and it stays at `1/5` even when the M-leg is made **completely free**
> (constant-factor `M⁰`). The M-leg carries ~25% of the polylog-weighted budget at
> `N = 2^100` and is **arithmetically inert**.

So the smoothness-sieve term is a large-looking, zero-leverage term. This is the campaign's
diagnosed failure mode with the sign flipped: a term that *looks* load-bearing because it is
big is worth exactly nothing. **Correction to #418's "three co-leaders"** — the M-leg is a
co-leader only in polylog weight, not in exponent; the exponent is carried by the interior,
`r`, and `m` alone.

## Headline 2 — the m-reuse is load-bearing, not slack (experiment refuted the survivor)

The one channel to survive both refuters was `nonlegendre`: a "collapse coupling" that
removes the baby-step split to reinterpret the `(a,b)` grid via a product tree with
separable exponents (essentially Strassen's `N^{1/4}`, Harvey Prop 2.5 / Remark 2.6). A
ground-truth-verified pipeline (real NTT product trees, remainder-tree multievaluation) was
built and run:

> The mechanism is a **correct** factoring algorithm, but its dominant input-size exponent
> is **0.2500**, not `≤ 0.20`. The fitted penalty slope is `0.046–0.052` against the exact
> closed form `1/20 = 0.0500`, confirming an `N^{1/20}` penalty.

Interpretation: **dropping the baby-step split deletes the `m` term, degrading a 3-term
balance to a 2-term one.** The `m`-reuse (the zero-sum trade in `m`) is **load-bearing, not
slack** — a direct, experiment-backed statement about the record's core reuse mechanism. The
hunt's fabricated constant ("256") table is refuted by the fit.

## Headline 3 — the transferable tool: the "delete-a-term" LP screen

> **Screening rule.** In a minimax cost `max{term_1, …, term_k}`, a term is worth optimising
> **iff deleting it (or making it free) moves the minimax value.** A term that does not move
> the value is worthless regardless of its weight. Run this LP before spending a round on any
> term.

This is the round's most transferable artefact and costs an afternoon. It is in the same
family as the round-33 **slack-constraint lemma** and the **symmetric-readout vacuity lemma**
— a small set of general screening tools the campaign now carries.

## Other theorem-worthy facts

- **Any extreme of the gcd-reveal family is algebraically solvable.** `q = k(p−1) − 1` gives
  `kp² − (k+1)p − N = 0`, discriminant `≡ (2kp − (k+1))²` — one integer square root. More
  generally, in the gcd-reveal family the density-1 extreme is always the algebraically
  solvable case. (The `eulergap2` cross attempt died here: its surviving extreme is a
  closed-form quadratic with an exactly-square discriminant.)
- **General-exponent reveal identity.** `R(E) = d_p(q−1) + d_q(p−1) − 2 d_p d_q`, with
  `d_p = gcd(E, p−1)`, valid for **all** exponents `E`; it recovers `card_revealing` at
  `E = N−1`. Verified numerically. This generalises round 33's Euler-gap count from the single
  exponent `N−1` to arbitrary `E`.

## The next concrete target (untouched)

Round 33 attacked `r` (pair filter; killed on residue-uniformity). Round 34 showed `M` is
redundant and `m`-reuse is load-bearing. That leaves **the baby-step `m`-leg and the
`m`-dependent BSGS interior — the only two terms never attacked with a power-of-`N`
mechanism.** `m` is untouched. (Flagged per Rule 6: the proposed `T = N^{(1/2−δ)/5}` target
is unverified arithmetic — run the delete-a-term LP before committing a round.)

**Do NOT** spend a round on LLL/flatness over the UMW CRT lattice: the prefactoring kill
supersedes it — within that framework the `c=1` branch cannot reach `1/6` at any window size.

## Honest summary
Zero new factoring methods across 32 → 34 rounds — but the failures are now sharp,
non-repeating, and each round yields reusable general lemmas (slack-constraint, delete-a-term
LP, symmetric-readout vacuity) plus machine-checked corrections. The frontier is the
baby-step `m`-leg; the formally-open door remains the UMW covering.

# The Galois/Frobenius side-channel family is a FIFTH primitive — and it is closed three ways (an audit finding: entirely absent from the factoring record)

**Origin:** the round-33 audit measured that **145 of 185 factoring-relevant catalog
modules were never read** in 32 prior rounds. This note harvests the largest coherent
unread block — the **Galois/Frobenius residue-type side-channel family** — and reports
what it contains. The family is a genuine **candidate fifth primitive** alongside the
record's four (congruence-of-squares, order, smoothness/index-calculus, algebraic/CM), and
it is machine-checked **closed three independent ways**. It is a rigorous *negative*
result about a whole route family — and it was sitting unopened on disk the entire time.

`N^{1/5}` remains an **upper bound** (never a floor). A kill is success. All theorem names
below were read from the actual Lean files (Rule 5); the record (`RESEARCH.md`, 9,771
lines) contains **zero** occurrences of the family — verified by grep.

## The family (the unread modules)

- `Cryptography/NonabelianTypeChannel/{GroupChannel, SplitType, Semiprime, Completeness,
  Entropy, Fields}.lean` — the **type channel**: the splitting type (factorisation shape)
  of `p` in a number field, read as the cycle type of Frobenius.
- `Combinatorics/D12SemiprimeWhichFactorWall.lean`,
  `Bridges/CyclicCubicWhichFactor.lean` — the **which-factor wall**.
- `Algebra/{ECMParityFrobenius, ECMParitySymmetric}.lean`,
  `Novelty/CmEcmOrder*.lean`, `Shared/ECMStage1OrderCompletion.lean` — **CM-ECM order
  shadows** and ECM stage-1 order completion.
- `Speculative/AutoResearch/ResidueChannelNonabelianTorsor.lean`,
  `Bridges/ResidueLeakageTorsorTriviality.lean` — the **Artin-symbol / torsor** channel;
  conjecture C5′ settled.

## Closure 1 — the abelianization cap (`typeChannel_le_logb_index`)

For a finite Galois group `S`, derived subgroup `N = [S,S]`, coset readout `c`, and **any**
splitting-type readout `T`:

> `mutualInfo S c T ≤ log₂ [S : N] = log₂|G^ab|`.

The proof is two lines: `mutualInfo ≤ H(c)` (info can't exceed the coarser variable) and
`H(coset) = log₂[S:N]` (Lagrange). It is airtight and general. Exact prime-level values
(`Fields.lean`): `S₃ = 1`, `S₄ = 1`, `A₄ = log₂3`, `D₄ = 2`, `V₄ = 2`, `C₄ = 2` bits. So a
five-type `S₄` field still cannot push more than **one bit** through a residue channel.
Perfect groups leak exactly zero (`typeChannel_eq_zero_of_perfect`).

## Closure 2 — the which-factor wall is an EXACT zero (`whichFactor_wall`)

For the semiprime `N = pq` with factors in an asymmetric box, knowing *which* factor
carried which splitting type adds **exactly zero bits** to *every* swap-invariant readout:

> `uEnt (asym n) (whichFactor n) = 1 ∧ mutInfo (asym n) (whichFactor n) k = 0`
> for every `k` with `k p.swap = k p`.

The zero is **exact, not a bound** (`mutInfo_eq_zero_of_flip`: a flip-invariance argument,
not an estimate). It is non-vacuous: the *ordered* readout does carry information
(`whichFactor_ordered_full`). So a Frobenius reader cannot learn which factor is which.

## Closure 3 — the Artin/torsor channel prunes nothing (`nonabelian_no_pruning`)

Conjecture C5′ asked whether the non-abelian Artin-symbol channel gives a *proper* fibre
(the first residue-type channel with nonzero pruning). It does not, and the reason is
sharper than a counting bound:

> In **any** group, for any target `σ` and any candidate `p`, the element
> `q = p⁻¹σ` compensates. So the fibre projects onto **every** conjugacy class.

Hence the Artin channel prunes **exactly zero** candidates, abelianian or not. The
pruning half of C5′ is false.

## What is NOT closed (the honest seams)

1. **The cap bounds the RESIDUE content, not the full type.** `I(coset;T) ≤ log₂[G:G']`;
   a readout not factoring through the abelianization coset is bounded only by `H(T)`. A
   higher-rank non-abelian `G` with large `log₂[G:G']` **and** a positive ordered-vs-
   unordered `I₂` gap is not excluded in principle.
2. **The wall's hypothesis is symmetry.** Every wall theorem assumes the readout is a
   function of `N` (or swap-invariant). A readout of an **asymmetric side-input** is
   untouched by the wall — though nothing yet supplies such a side-input computable from
   `N`.
3. **Distributional assumptions** (Rule 6): some semiprime figures rest on Chebotarev-type
   models that are conjectural, not measured.

Any new method from this family must, as a **conjunction**: supply a readout of `p` that
(i) does not factor through `G^ab`, (ii) breaks the swap symmetry, and (iii) yields more
than `O(1)` bits about which factor is which — all from `N` alone. No such readout is known.

## Significance

- The record's four-primitive census **needs amendment**: a fifth primitive exists (the
  Galois/Frobenius side channel) and is now **rigorously closed**, with an abelianization
  cap, an exact which-factor wall, and a no-pruning torsor law. This is a *stronger and
  more general* barrier than anything the record holds on this family — because the
  record does not hold anything on it at all.
- It is also a template for the **145-module audit**: the campaign's largest single failure
  was not a wrong idea but an **unread theorem**. The lesson generalises — before
  proposing a route, check whether it is already machine-checked on disk.
title: FACT round-34 (harvest) — THE GALOIS/FROBENESS SIDE-CHANNEL FAMILY IS A FIFTH PRIMITIVE, AND IT IS CLOSED THREE WAYS — the abelianization cap typeChannel_le_logb_index (I(coset;T) <= log2[G:G'], airtight: mutualInfo<=H(c)+H(coset)=log2[S:N] by Lagrange; S4 field capped at ONE bit); the which-factor wall whichFactor_wall (uEnt=1 AND mutInfo=0 EXACTLY, not a bound, for every swap-invariant readout); and the Artin/torsor no-pruning law nonabelian_no_pruning (in ANY group q=p^-1 sigma compensates, so the fibre projects onto EVERY class, C5' settled FALSE). Verified at the Lean source; the whole family is ENTIRELY ABSENT from the 9771-line record (grep: abelianiz/typeChannel/torsor/WhichFactor/ECMParity/CmEcm = 0 hits each) — a template for the 145-module unread audit

# UMW correction: the constraint is `α ≥ 1−2β`, not `α+β ≤ 1` — plus a verified Lemma 6.2 construction

**Corrects #417 §6 and #418 §6.** Source opened in full (arXiv:2511.10851, ar5iv HTML);
all statements quoted verbatim. The round-33 synthesis and the main loop independently
reached the same "zero slack" conclusion, from the corrected boundary.

## The correction

**Conjecture 3.2 ((α,β)-Divisor Conjecture), verbatim:** "For infinitely many `n` there
exist subsets `S, T ⊆ ℤ⁺` such that the set of pairwise differences `A = {s−t ∣ s∈S, t∈T}`
satisfies the n-divisor property, and 1. all elements of `S,T` have magnitude at most
`exp(n^α)` 2. `|S|,|T| ≤ n^β`."

**The counting constraint, verbatim from the paper: `α ≥ 1 − 2β`.** The paper continues:
"we do not know if `α = 1−2β` is achievable. In fact, we do not even know if `α < 1−β` is
achievable (whereas `α = 1−β+o(1)` is trivial)."

⇒ The record (and #417) framed the trivial boundary as `α+β ≤ 1+o(1)`. That is the
**wrong** boundary. The trivial case is `α = 1−β+o(1)`; the counting obstruction is
**`α ≥ 1−2β`**. At the `α=β=1/3` target, `1−2β = 1/3 = α` **exactly** — zero slack.
This independently confirms (and now explains) the round-33 synthesis's "UMW's `1/6` is
its floor with zero slack": the deterministic-integer `1/5→1/6` consequence sits exactly
on the conjecture's counting wall.

## Lemma 6.2 (verified by execution)

"Let `U` be the product of primes in `[n]`. Given a factorization `U = U_1⋯U_ℓ`, define
`T_i` to be the multiplicative inverse of `U/U_i` (mod `U_i`), and `V_i = (U/U_i)T_i`.
There is an arithmetic progression `A = {b+ic : 1≤i≤ℓ}` containing multiples of each prime
in `[n]`, iff … `c·(Σ i·V_i) + b ≡ 0 (mod U)`."

Executed (`umw_lemma62.py`): enumerating 2-part factorizations of the primorial, a **2-term**
AP hits a multiple of every prime in `[n]` for several splits (verified for n = 10,15,20,25,30).
So the Lemma 6.2 construction is real and cheap. **But it is not the conjecture**: a 2-term
AP touches the *primes*, whereas Conjecture 3.2 needs the *difference set* of `S,T`
(each of size ≤ `n^β`) to divide-cover every `i ∈ [n]`. Assembling a full `(1/3,1/3)`
covering from the AP block is the open part — **not** obtained by this search.

## Lemma 6.3 (the generic obstruction, verbatim)

"Suppose for all positive integers `A_1,…,A_ℓ` with `A_i ≤ M` there exist `A'_1,…,A'_ℓ′`
in arithmetic progression, `A'_j ≤ M'`, such that for all `i` there exists `j` with
`A_i | A'_j`. Then either `ℓ′ ≥ M^{Ω(1)}` or `M' ≥ M^{log log M}`."
This rules out building the covering from an **arbitrary** partition of `[n]`. Only
**non-generic / structured** factorizations of the smooth integer escape it.

## Honest negative data point

A greedy/random set-cover search over disjoint `S,T ⊂ [1, e^{n^{1/3}}]`, `|S|=|T|=n^{1/3}`
(`umw_cover2.py`) gets coverage ≈ 0 at n = 64,128,256,512: a **random** `(1/3,1/3)`
construction does not cover. This is expected — the conjecture requires a **structured**
`S,T` — and is **not** evidence against UMW. It only shows any successful search must be
structural, not random.

## Status
UMW remains the one formally-open door (it acts on the index set `[n]`, the quantity the
whole campaign's `3/2`-barrier framing turns on). The exact open sub-problem, now stated
precisely: **for infinitely many n, construct structured `S,T` with `|S|,|T| ≤ n^{1/3}`,
elements ≤ `e^{n^{1/3}}`, whose difference set divides-covers `[n]`.** Lemma 6.2 supplies a
verified AP building block; Lemma 6.3 says only special factorizations of the smooth
integer can work. No such covering is constructed here.
title: FACT round-33 (cont. 2) — UMW CORRECTION: the counting constraint is alpha >= 1-2beta, NOT alpha+beta<=1 (the record and #417/#418 had the wrong boundary; the trivial case is alpha=1-beta+o(1)); at alpha=beta=1/3 this is EXACTLY zero slack, which is why 1/6 is UMW's floor. Lemma 6.2 primorial-AP construction VERIFIED BY EXECUTION (a 2-part split gives a 2-term AP hitting every prime in [n]) but that is NOT the covering; Lemma 6.3 obstruction quoted verbatim (only structured factorizations escape). Random (1/3,1/3) greedy search = coverage 0 (expected; conjecture needs structure). Corrects #417 and #418

body:
# Round 33 (cont.) — Correcting the record: the slack-constraint lemma, the `s = N^{1/6}` sieve target, a free sound pair filter, and a 145-module unread audit

**Supersedes/corrects** #417 (`FACT round-33 — THE ORDER-FREE OPENING IS CLOSED…`). The
adversarial gate caught errors in that paper and in the campaign record itself; this note
issues the corrections and the new rigorous facts. A kill is success; a caught error is
better than a retraction. Everything below was source-checked per Rule (5) — full texts
opened via `pdftotext`/HTML, Lean files read, numbers reproduced.

`N^{1/5}` remains an **upper bound** on the deterministic record (never a floor). No
unconditional superpolynomial lower bound for factoring is known in any model.

---

## 1. ★ The slack-constraint lemma (a general screening test — headline)

> **Lemma (slack constraint).** A "hypothesis `X` fell, therefore the exponent moves"
> argument is valid only if `X`'s constraint is **active at the unconstrained optimum**.
> If at the optimum the constraint's ceiling strictly exceeds what the algorithm needs,
> the constraint is slack and the exponent cannot move, no matter that `X` fell.

**Application (this is the round's cleanest general result).** The record argued that
because the order-finding hypothesis (arXiv:2601.11131) fell, the `N^{1/5}` exponent might
drop. Re-derivation shows the constraint on `m` (Harvey's baby-step ceiling) had ceiling
`N^{2/5}` while the optimum needs only `N^{1/5}` — **slack by a factor `lg^{0.8}N`, growing
without bound**. A slack constraint cannot transmit a hypothesis-collapse to the exponent.
Harvey's own Prop 4.3 calls the order-finding step "negligible." The "opening" is closed
for a *general* reason, not an ad-hoc one.

This lemma is the reusable screening tool the campaign lacked: **before claiming a
structural change moves an exponent, check whether the relevant constraint is tight at the
optimum.** It retires a whole family of "something fell ⟹ something improves" arguments.

## 2. ★ The sieve target is 3× harder than the file (and than #417) says

> **Correction.** Including Prop 2.5's smoothness-sieve carrier, the pair-filter rate is
> `e = 1/5 − σ/5`, **not** `1/5 − 3σ/5`. Reaching `1/6` needs **`s = N^{1/6}`**, not
> `s = N^{1/18}`.

Both the campaign record and paper #417 stated the `N^{1/18}` target. That is wrong by 3×
in the exponent, because the dominant `lg^{16/5}` carrier is Prop 2.5's sieve, which a
pair filter does **not** divide. The single most concrete derived target in the record is
therefore three times harder than advertised. (The *pair-sweep* term does fall with `s` —
that part stands — but it is not the carrier.)

## 3. A free, sound, quantity-matched pair filter exists

> **Correction to a negative.** "No quantity-matched filter on Harvey's `(a,b)` family is
> known" is **false**: **keep iff `a ≤ b`** is sound and free (`s = 2` exactly), because
> Harvey's Lemma 3.3 (via Hardy–Wright) guarantees the good pair has `a ≤ b`. It buys
> `0.93×` — not an exponent — but it falsifies a stated negative and shows the filter
> space is not empty.

## 4. The two summands of Harvey's `s` are exactly equal (2× accounting correction)

Measured ratio `1.000000` across seven bit sizes: `s = 2·N^{1/5}lg^{1/5}N`, the two summands
exactly balanced. The record's "the `r`-term dominates" is wrong by 2×, and its "the
`s`-term is 100% of the leading term" is also wrong — the `m` (baby-step) term is
**co-dominant**. Combined with fact 1's "three co-leaders, two order-free," this settles
an accounting question the record twice admitted it could not.

## 5. Euler-gap density is governed by cofactors, not the gap

> **Correction.** Substituting `p−1 = ga`, `q−1 = gb`, the reveal density is
> `ρ = (a+b−2)/(ab)` — **the gap `g` cancels entirely**. So `Sup ρ = 1`, not `1/2`.

The "large-Euler-gap" framing over-credited `g`. The variable that matters is the
*cofactors* `a, b` (how `p−1, q−1` decompose), not the shared factor. The `O(1)`-base
`p−1`-style reveal remains real on its promise class, but the governing quantity is
misnamed in the record.

## 6. UMW's `1/6` is its floor with **zero slack** — and the one open door

- UMW's budget for a covering is `n^{2β+α} = n` against `θ(n) ~ n`; the ratio `→ 1`.
  There is **no slack** at `α = β = 1/3`: `1/6` is the **floor of UMW's framework**, not a
  reachable-but-unreached point. (The `3/2 → 4/3` *polynomial*-factorization consequence
  keeps its own slack; it is the integer-`1/6` consequence that is tight.)
- **The only formally-open door in the campaign**, per UMW Lemmas 6.2–6.3: all design
  freedom is in *"the choice of the factorization of `U`"*; the generic case is killed by
  counting. Concrete task: enumerate factorizations `U = U_1···U_ℓ` of the relevant smooth
  integer meeting Lemma 6.3's bounds, build the associated AP/GAP pair, and test whether
  `S − T` covers `[n]` by divisibility at `n = 10^4–10^6`, with **`S ∩ T = ∅` enforced**.
  Two guards (both earned by retractions this round): reject any candidate with
  `S ∩ T ≠ ∅` (the zero difference satisfies the `n`-divisor property free, giving spurious
  100% coverage), and treat coverage that *decreases* with `n` under a raised cap as a
  lower bound on achievability, not a measurement.

## 7. The 145-module unread audit (the campaign's real diagnosis)

> **145 of 185 factoring-relevant catalog modules were never read** by the 32 prior
> rounds. Two of the campaign's most decisive kills — the **non-abelian/braid** route and
> the **CM order-shadow** route — sat unread the entire time.

Three of round 33's twelve channels were re-derivations of theorems already sitting
unopened on disk. The campaign's failures are **failures of attention, not insight**. This
is the single most important measurement of the round and it sets the frontier: the next
rounds must read the unread surface before proposing anything.

## 8. Further theorem-worthy facts (barriers/corrections)

- **Attribution:** the `N^{1/3}` large-order-target conjecture is **Hittmeir's** (GFHP
  Remark 3.6 → [Hit18]), not Harvey's. (#417 got this right; restated for the record.)
- **GFHP Lemma 3.5 caveat:** `δ = N^{1/3}` **violates** the lemma's own precondition
  (`δ ≥ N^{1/4}log^8N`) for every `N ≥ 2^96`. So the "large-order element already
  published" claim holds only below a size threshold; for cryptographic `N` it does not
  apply as stated. (Corrects an overclaim in #417 §2.)
- **CM order-shadow:** the claimed linear class-number "0.75h penalty" is an **instrument
  artifact** — the harness took `Re(j)` of complex `j`, producing non-real-rooted
  polynomials with Galois group `S_h` instead of `Cl(D)`. With true polynomials the class
  number **cancels exactly**, *confirming* `Capstone.lean` (not correcting it).
- **Short-window ergodicity is false:** 126 of 429 primes refute full-period
  `log₂`-uniformity, because the orbit starts at the rational point `1/N`, a periodic
  orbit in the exceptional null set of an a.e. theorem. The short-window value-level
  result is therefore a **null with empty tail**, not a proof.
- **Effective-sample-size rule:** only **163 of 38,635** primes in `[2^19, 2^20)` have
  13-smooth `p−1`. Report distinct-prime counts, never draw counts, for any
  smoothness-labelled permutation test (a p-value here treated replicated primes as
  independent draws — a Rule (6) violation).
- **Berggren A-spine identity** `a_k − b_k = (−1)^{k+1}` collapses five proposed gcds to
  ~one event.

---

### Net effect on the campaign
- The flagship "order-free opening" is **closed** for a general reason (slack-constraint
  lemma, §1) — not merely "not yet achieved."
- The single concrete derived target, the `(a,b)` pair filter, is now correctly specified
  at **`s = N^{1/6}`** (§2) and is **not known to be impossible** (§3) but is worth `0.93×`
  as it stands.
- The one formally-open door is a **constructive UMW covering via primorial
  factorizations** (§6), and the largest unexplored surface is the **145 unread catalog
  modules** (§7).

**Next:** read the 145-module surface (especially the unread non-abelian/braid and CM
order-shadow kills), and run the UMW primorial-factorization covering search under the two
guards. Both are the honest frontier; everything else measured is a dead channel or a
correction now issued.
title: FACT round-33 (cont.) — CORRECTIONS + 8 THEOREM-WORTHY FACTS: the SLACK-CONSTRAINT LEMMA (a hypothesis falling moves the exponent only if its constraint is ACTIVE at the optimum — here slack by an unbounded lg^0.8 N, so the order-free opening is closed for a general reason); the (a,b) sieve target is 3x HARDER than the record and #417 said (s=N^(1/6) not N^(1/18)); a FREE SOUND pair filter EXISTS (a<=b, s=2, 0.93x — falsifies a stated negative); s summands exactly EQUAL; Euler-gap density = (a+b-2)/(ab), gap g CANCELS; UMW 1/6 is its FLOOR with ZERO slack (n^(2beta+alpha)=n vs theta(n)~n); and the campaign's real diagnosis — 145 of 185 factoring catalog modules NEVER READ in 32 rounds (the non-abelian/braid and CM order-shadow kills sat unread the whole time). Supersedes/corrects #417

body:
# Round 33 — Closing the Order-Free Opening, and a Sharper Frontier for Deterministic Factoring

**Status:** research note / kill record with one confirmed negative and four new
source-grounded findings. **No new factoring method was found** — 12 hypotheses, 12
killed at an adversarial gate; the single surviving thread is a *negative* result that
closes an open channel. That negative is the round's contribution.

**Discipline.** This round is the first to enforce, in the workflow's *structure* rather
than as prose advice, the seven rules the prior 32 rounds violated: every hypothesis had
to (1) open its primary source, (2) name the exact quantity its mechanism acts on, and
(3) survive two independent refuters (a source-grounding lens and a quantity/cost lens)
before reaching a sympy experiment. A kill at the gate is success — it prevents a
retraction. Result: **12/12 killed, 0 retractions, 0 phantom citations that survived
verification.** All quotes below were read from opened sources (arXiv full text via
`pdftotext`/HTML, or local Lean files), per Rule (5).

Throughout, `N^{1/5}` is an **upper bound** on the deterministic record — not a proven
floor. No unconditional superpolynomial lower bound for factoring is known in any model.

---

## 1. Headline (the order-free opening is closed)

The campaign record's sharpest live question, opened by the January 2026 result
**arXiv:2601.11131** (Harvey & Hittmeir, *Deterministic methods for finding elements of
large multiplicative order*), was: *with hypothesis-free order-finding, is Harvey's cost
shape still right — can a large-order element rebalance the trade to beat `N^{1/5}`?*

**Answer (re-derived and experimentally reproduced): no. `1/5` is pinned by an entirely
ORDER-FREE triangle, so the 2026 result is structurally incapable of moving it.**

The re-derivation (from Harvey, arXiv:2010.05450, Prop 4.2/4.3) locates every place
`ord_N(alpha)` enters Harvey's algorithm: **exactly one** — the number of spurious
hash-table hits in Step (4), `n ≈ s·m/D`, the input length of the Alg 4.1 product tree.
That quantity has **N-exponent 0** (it is log-carrying). It does **not** enter:

- `r` — the Lehman candidate-pair budget (`{(a,b) : ab ≤ r}`, size `Θ(r lg r)`);
- `m` — the Bluestein baby-step budget (`Θ(m)` per giant step);
- `M = ⌈(N/r)^{1/2}⌉` — the smoothness-sieve range in Step (2).

Prop 4.3 pins the exponent at `1/5` via the balance `{ r·lg³N vs N^{1/4}r^{-1/4}lg³N }`
(the pair budget against the Step-(2) smoothness sieve) together with
`{ m·lg²N vs N^{1/2}/(r^{1/2}m) }` (the baby-step list against the BSGS interior).
**Both legs are order-free.** The order appears only in the product-tree term, which
*drops* (from `N^{1/5}lg^{16/5}N` to `lg^{22/5}N`) when order-finding is free — but two
other terms already sit at `N^{1/5}lg^{16/5}N`, so the `max` is unchanged. Even a
hypothetical maximal-order `alpha` with the order-finding step **literally free** leaves
the total at `N^{1/5}lg^{16/5}N`.

- **Rule (7) verdict: MISMATCH.** Mechanism quantity = N-exponent 0 (polylog hit count);
  target quantity = N-exponent `1/5`. The gap is `1/5`, so free order-finding cannot
  reach the exponent at all.
- **Reproduced:** an analytic script (`partA.py`) regenerates `F(N) = N^{1/5}lg^{16/5}N`
  exactly from Prop 4.3, and a numerical probe (`partB2.py`, 44-bit semiprime) confirms
  the hit-rate law. Both run in seconds.

This **closes** the record's "OPENING" (§7-undecuples-XXXIV/XXXV had hoped the opposite)
and replaces it with a settled negative. The record's own §7-undecuples-XXXIV/XXXV built
a "r-trade-off floor" argument that implicitly treated the order as load-bearing; it is
not. **This is a correction to the campaign's own prior reasoning, found by adversarial
gate rather than by a retraction.**

## 2. Large-order element production is already published, and is dominated

GFHP (**arXiv:2512.19076**, Gao–Feng–Hu–Pan, 22 Dec 2025) **Lemma 3.5** already gives a
deterministic algorithm: given `(N, δ)` with `N^{1/4}log^8N ≤ δ ≤ N`, return `alpha ∈ Z_N*`
with `ord_N(alpha) > δ` (or a factor, or a primality proof) in time
`O(δ^{1/2}log²N / (log log δ)^{1/2})`. Substituting `δ = N^{1/3}` the enabling sub-problem
"*deterministically produce an element of order ≳ N^{1/3}*" is **already solved** — at cost
`Õ(N^{1/6})`, which is *below* Harvey's `N^{1/5}` and therefore buys nothing.

- **Rule (7) MISMATCH, stated as a kill:** the order of `alpha` sets `m` (baby-step table
  size); the N-exponent is set by `r` (candidate-pair count). They are anti-correlated via
  the balance `m* = N^{1/4}r^{-1/4}`, so improving the order quantity cannot move `r`.
- **Attribution correction:** `Hit18` is **Hittmeir**, not Harvey.
- The order term (from GFHP Lemma 3.5, cost `~m^{1/2}`) is **dominated by the baby-step
  term `O(m)` everywhere** — a new, clean statement of the dominance the record asserted
  but never quantified against the whole curve.

## 3. The `(a,b)` pair-filter: right quantity, closed on cost

Harvey's Algorithm 4.2 Step 2 enumerates the pair family `P = {(a,b) : 1 ≤ ab ≤ r}`, size
`Θ(r lg r)` — the `T2 = r lg³N` term of Prop 4.2, the one term **not** divided by `m`. A
correct-quantity filter on this family is the single most concrete derived target in the
record: uniform compression `s` gives `N^{1/5}s^{-3/5}`, and `1/6` needs `s = N^{1/18}`.

**This round confirms, for the first time, that the filter acts on the RIGHT quantity** —
on Harvey's own `(a,b)` family, not on a value-range. It is therefore *not* a repeat of
the retracted XLI/XLII category error (which filtered a value-range, not the pairs). It is
killed on cost/domination instead, and a new negative falls out: **the good pair is
residue-uniform mod small primes**, so congruence sieves (QR-of-`a`, QR-of-`ab`, etc.)
act on it at the random rate. Two independent, distinct closures — "right quantity" and
"still closed" — are now cleanly separated.

## 4. A paper the 634KB record never saw: Rational Base Descent

**arXiv:2605.08846**, *Rational Base Descent: A Deterministic Algorithm for Factoring
Structured Semiprimes* (Sam Blake, 9 May 2026) is **absent from the entire record** (all
Lean files and the 634KB RESEARCH.md). Opened in full; Theorem 1 quoted verbatim: for
`N = pq`, writing `Δ = p − ⌊c(a/b)^n⌋`, a split occurs iff `(a/b)^n > q` and
`|Δ| < (a/b)^n/q`; per-run cost `O(log³N)`.

- **Rule (7) MISMATCH for balanced RSA:** the method acts on the *rational-power structure*
  of `p` (a Diophantine-approximation condition, essentially never true for a random
  prime), not on the cardinality of a search index. It is a genuine `O(log³N)` method on
  its promised *structured* class and the paper itself "poses no threat to balanced RSA."
  It does not yield a new N-exponent. The correct substitute quantity — a covering law
  `C(a,b) = t_max·(2J+1)` crossing `q` at a critical base `b* ~ N^{1/4}/√(2 ln N)` — was
  derived and measured as a characterization of the promise class, not a new method.

## 5. Value-level short-window features (Open Channel #16)

The file proves blindness for *collision structure* and for *full-period* value sets, and
marks *short-window* value-level features as explicitly out of scope. This round tested
them. The `gcd`-based route is a **`p − 1` restatement**; the non-`gcd` value-level
features are a **Rule (7) MISMATCH** (the one pre-registered test that fired refuted one
of the four banked sub-claims). Net: no factoring information in a short window's values at
`m ≪ ord`, consistent with the file's collision-structure theorems.

## 6. What this leaves open

- **UMW (arXiv:2511.10851)** survives the quantity lens: its conjecture (sets `S,T`,
  `|S|=|T|=n^β`, magnitudes `≤ e^{n^α}`, every `i ∈ [n]` divides some `s−t`; `α=β=1/3`
  best-possible) acts on the **index set** `[n]` — the right quantity — and its
  *secondary* consequence is exactly the deterministic `1/5 → 1/6`. (Its *flagship*
  consequence is `3/2 → 4/3` for **polynomial** factorization; integer factoring is the
  second consequence — a distinction the record's framing blurs.) UMW remains the one
  formalised conditional route past the `3/2` baby-step/giant-step barrier.
- **The large-Euler-gap promise class** (`gcd(a^{N−1}−1, N)` reveals a factor in `O(1)`
  bases when `gcd(p−1,q−1)` is large) is proved and tight but is a structured-promise
  method; no general route.
- The precise frontier for a sub-`1/5` deterministic method is now: **break the
  order-free pair-budget balance `{ r·lg³N vs N^{1/4}r^{-1/4}lg³N }` itself** — a
  `(a,b)`-family filter with `s = N^{1/18}` (§3) — or a mechanism outside the
  baby-step/giant-step motif (UMW). Order-finding is *not* a lever.

---

### Method note (a contribution in its own right)
The gated pipeline (hunt → refute×2 distinct lenses → sympy experiment) killed 12/12 and
recorded **no** retractions and **no** unverifiable citations. The two lenses caught
*different* failure modes — UMW died on source-grounding but passed quantity;
orderfree/pairfilter/shortwindow passed source but died on quantity — which is the
diversity that makes the gate informative. One **calibration bug** was caught in
post-hoc review: the quantity refuter for `orderfree` reasoned "refutation failed — the
negative is confirmed" but emitted `killed=true`, over-killing a *confirmed negative*.
The gate is not yet self-calibrating; future rounds should assert consistency between a
refuter's `killed` flag and its stated reasoning before counting the gate.
title: FACT round-33 — THE ORDER-FREE OPENING IS CLOSED: Harvey's 1/5 is pinned by an entirely ORDER-FREE triangle, so the Jan-2026 arXiv:2601.11131 large-order result is structurally incapable of moving it; plus a NEW paper the 634KB record never saw (arXiv:2605.08846 Rational Base Descent), the (a,b) pair-filter CONFIRMED on the right quantity (not a category error) but cost-killed, and an attribution correction — 12/12 hypotheses gated, 0 retractions, 0 phantom citations

**Paper 254** (`ResearchOutput/NewMathematics/254_ProfileGenerality.md`) · artifacts `ResearchOutput/scripts/2026-08-24-round74/exp605_*` · notebook Part 296 · assessment v360 → v361 · count 590 → 591.

## Question
Is the j²−N positional smoothness profile (papers 228/229: power-law decline + left-edge spike) universal across polynomial families?

## Pre-registration (script header, before analysis)
H1 (universal): same normalized profile shape for ALL of {j²−N, j³−N, j⁴−N} at matched sample sizes — all pairwise profile r > 0.8 after normalization.
H0 (family-specific): profiles diverge materially; report which family differs and how.
Bars fixed: (a) all pairwise r > 0.8; (b) every family left-decile > overall with boot P > 0.95; (c) every family Spearman ρ < 0 at p < 0.01. Overrides: <150 hits/arm ⇒ INCONCLUSIVE-LOWPOWER; control non-flatness (χ² p ≤ 0.01) ⇒ INVALID-CONTROL.

## Method
128-member npz-lineage population (exp581_regen_positions.npz); windows [r_k, 3r_k−4] anchored at the integer k-th root (k=2 reproduces [jlo, 3jlo−3] exactly); matched CRN grids L=3000/N/arm with tilt IDENTICAL across arms (paired); exact 1e6-cut gcd-chain B-smooth tester (unit-tested); controls C=1000/N/arm; 50-bin pooled profiles, WLS ln-rate fit on bins ≥3 hits, cluster bootstrap B=800 over the 128 Ns; sq2d dither probe (seeded dither ∈ [1, 2·jlo], isqrt preserved). Seeds 20260901 / 20260902. Wall 181 s.

## Result — VERDICT: H0-SIDE (family-specific)
| Bar | Observed | Pass |
|---|---|---|
| pair r > 0.8 | max 0.781 | **FAIL** |
| edge concentration | 4/4 arms P(ld>ov)=1.0 | PASS |
| monotone decline | cu3 Spearman +0.019, p=.92 | **FAIL** |

Per family (384k draws each):
- **sq2** (j²−N_rec): 8639 hits, rate .0225 — b̂ **+0.157 ± 0.008**, ld/ov 1.24×, Spearman −0.802 (p=2.5e−12)
- **qu4** (j⁴−N_rec): 7603 hits, .0198 — b̂ **+0.188 ± 0.013**, ld/ov 1.29×, Spearman −0.856 (2.4e−15)
- **cu3** (j³−N_rec): 287 hits, .00075 — b̂ +0.065 ± 0.037 [CI covers 0], Spearman +0.019 (p=.92) **FLAT**
- **sq2d** (dither probe): 248 hits, .00065 — b̂ +0.168 ± 0.038, ld/ov 1.47×, shallow shape-consistent

Pairwise normalized-profile r: **sq2|qu4 = 0.781 [0.565, 0.767]** — close to but below the pre-registered 0.8 bar; sq2|cu3 0.385; cu3|qu4 0.477; sq2~sq2d 0.495. Controls flat 4/4 (χ² p .08–.65). No override fires.

## THE DIFFERENCE-OF-SQUARES GATE (mechanism named)
Rate hierarchy **sq2 ≈ qu4 (~2×10⁻²) ≫ sq2d ≈ cu3 (~7×10⁻⁴) — ≈30× lower (29–34× across pairings)** is EXACTLY tracked by difference-of-squares factorability: N_rec = jlo² makes v_k = (j^(k/2)−jlo)(j^(k/2)+jlo) split for **EVEN k only**. Even powers share the small-factor route (b̂ .16/.19, ρ −.80/−.86, r .78); odd degree admits no integer split → baseline rate + flat profile. The sq2d arm confirms from inside the quadratic family: knock N off the exact-square locus and the rate collapses ~35× (~97% of mass gone) onto the cu3/sq2d level with only a shallow tilt left. The gate variable is ARITHMETIC (algebraic factorability of f(j)−N given N's form), not polynomial degree per se.

## Consequence
- Papers 228/229's profile law (with 238/245/253's bulk+spike decomposition) is a **QUADRATIC-FAMILY law, not a universal sequence law**; barrier-map entries citing it inherit the scope restriction.
- **Extension prediction pre-stated**: even degrees j^{2m}−N share the structure via repeated difference-of-squares for square N (k=4 confirms). Falsifiable follow-up: j⁶−N / j⁸−N at matched grids should land in the ~0.16–0.19 b̂ band with pairwise r > 0.8 vs sq2/qu4.
- Practical asymmetry booked: the strong structure lives on the perfect-square-N slice where trial division from jlo is already optimal — no scanning advantage transfers to general-N populations.

## Ledger catches / honest limits
- **Lineage APPROXIMATE, disclosed**: npz stores positions+bounds only (no N) — reconstruction N_rec=jlo² pins anchors exactly (residual ΔN < 2·jlo shifts effective left edge <1 integer step, profiling-invariant). Applicable check via N-independent v₂=(j−jlo)(j+jlo): stored npz hits classify smooth at .0226 ≈ ctl .0198 ⇒ **original N NON-SQUARE**; sq2/qu4 RATE LEVELS do not transfer to the general-N population of 228/229 — flagged for follow-up.
- cu3/sq2d thin (287/248 hits, just above the registered 150 low-power floor): their null-ish shapes are UNDERPOWERED, disclosed (used only for bar (c)).
- Smoke caught t-mat broadcast bug + key-name bug; both fixed pre-full-run. No commits mid-run; only exp605_* touched.

## Barrier framing
Closes the generality question the closed positional thread (250–253) left implicit; answer REDUCES exposure — the structure is scan-order geometry of the square-N slice, consistent with the standing method law (scan-order structure reflects proposal geometry, not N-information). Open frontier unchanged: u ≥ 6–14 scale-smoothness deviations, factor-local beyond scan-order, MA-1 effectivity, residue cap 4/3, external-hint laws; quantum closed.

Runs paper 234 §4a's named open refinement ("harmonic bulk × steeper-edge kernel — this tension travels forward on the ledger until that refinement is run or refuted") and CLOSES it as CONFIRMED.

### Data & method
9594 pooled hits over 128 Ns from `exp581_regen_positions.npz`, canonical normalization x=(p−jlo)/(jhi−jlo); control arm 512k ctl_* same intervals; seed 588; wall 12.9 s; nboot 500 main (+300/200 posthoc).
