## Question

NET-35 flagged a P3 long-context margin erosion at ctx=512 (the k* pass cleared the 0.98 bar by only 0.003 ≈ 2 SE); NET-36 showed it seed-fluctuating at 512, not systematic. The open stress point that could break the law: does the knee EVENTUALLY fail as context keeps doubling? The retained-curve depression (~0.01/doubling) extrapolates to ~0.97–0.98 at ctx=1024 — right at the bar.

## Method

Byte-identical harness to NET-15/20/33/35 — CausalTF d=4, dm=64, 4 heads, 5 Gutenberg novels, vocab 4097, contiguous 90/10 split, 2000 AdamW steps — at **d=4, seed=1, ctx=1024** (5516s train; 585 windows, 10% held out; extends the same-seed context chain 128→256→512→1024). Full-acc eval → concentration (eff support) → top-k sweep ks={32,64,96,128,192,256,384,512,768} → random-k control (seed 12345). k* = smallest k with retained ≥ 0.98·full. **Prediction stated before the run: k* = 128 (d·ctx/32).** Script /tmp/exp_net_attncost_ctx1024.py; log /tmp/net37.log.

## Results

| ctx (d=4, s1) | k* | predicted | margin at k* |
|---|---|---|---|
| 128 | 16 | 16 | +0.007 |
| 256 | 32 | 32 | +0.010 |
| 512 | 64 | 64 | +0.003 |
| **1024** | **128** | **128** | **+0.006** |

- **k* = 128 — EXACT, P1 outcome.** k=32 0.945 ✗, k=64 0.968 ✗, k=96 0.977 ✗ (≈2 SE below bar), k=128 **0.986 ✓** (≈4 SE above; k=192 0.991, k=256 0.993, k=384 0.996, k=512 1.000 [re-norm MC saturation], k=768 0.999). The law k* = d·ctx/32 holds at a fixed seed across an **8× context range (128 → 1024)** — every doubling exact, no ceiling.
- **Margin-erosion caveat RESOLVED:** the pass margin chain +0.007/+0.010/+0.003/+0.006 is **NOT monotonic** — the 512 dip was a fluctuation and the margin recovered at 1024 (0.006 > 0.003). The knee is exact at every doubling; the retained curve is still somewhat lower at the longest contexts but the knee is unaffected.
- **Concentration diffuses superlinearly:** eff support **291.16** (46.4→80.6→152.1→291.2, ×1.74/×1.89/×1.91); per-position 37.56/255.76/542.05 — NO bounded working set at 1024.
- **Selection importance survives:** random-k gaps +5.9 (k=64) / +4.6 (k=128).
- Nine-model full-acc set 0.1571–0.1620 (0.1594 at 1024), k*-irrelevant.

## Barriers

(a) circularity — no, prediction stated before the run, k* from the model's own trained attention; (b) known-method — no, long-context margin verification of an established law (Catalog re-scan: no context-length/margin/knee/top-k prior work); (c) toy-scale — confronted, 8× the original testbed context, real causal word LM, 4097 vocab, held-out loss+acc; (d) leakage — none, held-out last-10%, data-free top-k; (e) variance — the margin question answered by the 4-point same-seed chain (512 dip shown to be a fluctuation); honest limit: ctx=1024 cell is single-seed, knee fluctuation band ±0.003 wider at long context; (f) measurement — clean, k=512 1.000 = re-norm MC saturation (k=768 converges to full loss), binom SE ≈0.15%, pass +4 SE / fail −2 SE fix the knee; (g) baselines — fair, full-attention reference + random-k control at same k, same bar; (h) relevance — strengthened, the speedup lever's context-invariance now tested to 8×, margin-erosion caveat downgraded from open risk to resolved fluctuation.

## Verdict

**CONTEXT-MARGIN CHECK PASSED** — the attention-cost law k* = d·ctx/32 holds exactly at ctx=1024 (8× the original testbed context); the P3 margin-erosion hypothesis is refuted (the 512 dip was a fluctuation; the margin recovered). The context-invariant lever 32/d (8× at d=4) holds over the 8× range — longer context still buys no extra relative saving.

Open: ctx=1024 second seed; ctx=512 at d=8/16; d=8 @ ctx=256 s0 corner. Paper 81. Round-net-37, assessment v37.

## Question

## Results

| cell | predicted | k sweep (retained) | k* | verdict |
|---|---|---|---|---|

The margin at 512 is **seed-fluctuating ±0.002**, not systematically eroding; the retained curve is still ~0.005–0.01 below 128/256 at both seeds (mild long-context depression, knee unaffected). Re-check at ctx=1024.
- **Concentration reproduces to three significant figures:** eff support 152.11 = 152.11 (s1 vs s2), top-32 0.533/0.532, per-position 20.41–20.45 / 133.23–133.37 / 281.20–281.46. Depth-drift continues at d=16 (eff 52.73; 46.6→50.2→52.7).

## Barriers

(a) circularity — no, both predictions stated before the run, k* from each model's own trained attention; (b) known-method — no, two-seed grid-completion of an established law (Catalog re-scan: no prior work); (c) toy-scale — confronted, the grid's extreme corners (deepest d=16, longest ctx=512), real causal word LM, 4097 vocab, held-out loss+acc; (d) leakage — none, held-out last-10%, data-free top-k; (e) variance — the round's content, both last single-seed cells closed, concentration reproduces to 0.001; remaining non-threatening: ctx=512 at d=8/16, d=8 @ ctx=256 s0 corner, ctx=1024; (f) measurement — clean, k=384 recovers full loss exactly, retained 1.000 = re-normalization MC saturation, seed-2 margins exceed binom SE; (g) baselines — fair, full-attention reference + random-k control at same k, same bar; (h) relevance — strengthened, the speedup lever is seed-independent at every measured corner.

## Verdict

**GRID-COMPLETION CONFIRMED** — every measured cell of the (d × ctx) grid is now two-seed. The attention-cost law k* = d·ctx/32 (speedup 32/d, context-invariant) is seed-independent at every measured corner; no per-instance re-measurement needed within the measured grid.

## Program
Network/LLM research lab — round-net-35 (speed-axis round 8). Context-extrapolation of the attention-cost law beyond [128,256].

## Question
The law k* = d·ctx/32 (→ speedup 32/d, context-invariant) was established at a second seed in every cell of the (d∈{4,8} × ctx∈{128,256}) grid (NET-15/16/20/33/34) — but the context leg rested on exactly ONE doubling (128→256) and the whole ctx=512 regime was unmeasured. Does the law extrapolate to 4× the longest measured context, or does k* break (superlinear k* would kill the context-invariant speedup — the economically important direction)?

## Method
Byte-identical harness to NET-15/20/33 — CausalTF **d=4**, dm=64, 4 heads, 5 Gutenberg novels, vocab 4097, contiguous 90/10 split, 2000 AdamW steps — at **seed=1**, at **ctx=512** (1171 windows, 10% held out; train 2854s). Full-acc eval → Part A concentration → Part B top-k sweep {16,32,64,128,256,384} → Part B2 random-k control (seed 12345). k* = smallest k with retained ≥ 0.98·full. Prediction stated before the run: **k* = 64** (d·ctx/32 = 4·512/32).

## Results (retained = acc/full vs 0.98 bar)

| ctx | full acc | k sweep (retained) | k* | predicted |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 128 (s0/s1) | 0.1571/0.1577 | 16→0.984/0.987 ✓ | **16** | 16 |
| 256 (s0/s1) | 0.1612/0.1599 | 32→0.989/0.990 ✓ | **32** | 32 |
| **512 (s1)** | 0.1616 | 16→0.940 ✗ 32→0.964 ✗ 64→**0.983** ✓ 128→0.992 256→0.999 384→1.000 | **64** | 64 |

1. **k* = 64 — EXACT.** The law holds across a 4× context range at a second seed; the lever speedup = 32/d = 8× at d=4 is context-invariant over the quadrupled range (NET-20's core claim — longer context buys no extra relative saving — now tested to 512). k=384 recovers full loss exactly (5.0827 = full).
2. **NEW P3 CAVEAT (long-context margin erosion):** the k* pass clears the bar by only 0.003 (≈2 SE) vs ~0.007–0.010 at 128/256, and retained is uniformly ~0.01 lower at every k. The knee is real (k=32 fails ~10 SE below bar; 0.964→0.983 is a 12 SE jump) — the law's KNEE stays exact but its margin erodes with context. Re-check at ctx=1024.
3. **Concentration diffusion continues:** eff support 152.11 (46.4 → 80.6 → 152.1 across doublings, ×1.74/×1.89); per-position 20.41/133.37/281.20 — NO bounded working set at 512.
4. **Selection importance survives the longest context:** random-k gaps +5.3 (k=32) / +4.6 (k=64) — same family as 6.0–8.7 at 128/256.
5. **Seven-model full-acc set 0.1571–0.1616**, k*-irrelevant.

## Verdict
**CONTEXT-EXTRAPOLATION CONFIRMED.** k* = d·ctx/32 holds exactly at ctx=512 (k* = 64 = 4·512/32) — the law's first point at 4× the longest measured context — with the context-invariant lever intact and no bounded working set. The economically important claim (longer context buys no extra relative saving; 8× absolute at d=4) survives a quadrupled context range, with a documented long-context margin erosion as the honest caveat.

## Barriers (all 8 checked)
(a) circularity: no — prediction stated before the run from the law; (b) known-method: no — context-extrapolation verification (Catalog re-scan: no context-scaling/top-k-pruning result at any context length); (c) toy-scale: confronted — longest context the testbed has used, real causal word LM, 4097 vocab; (d) leakage: none; (e) variance: the extrapolation cell is EXACT but single-seed — remaining single-seed: d=16 @ ctx=128, ctx=512 at d=8/16; (f) measurement: documented — k=384 recovers full loss exactly, retained 1.000 = re-normalization saturation as every prior context, the thin pass margin reported as the P3 caveat not hidden; (g) baselines: fair; (h) relevance: strengthened — context-invariance now holds across 4× context.

## Open
ctx=512 second seed; ctx=1024 (margin-erosion check); d=16 second seed @ ctx=128; ctx=512 at d=8/16; carry chain at scale (the frontier).

## Program
Network/LLM research lab — round-net-34 (speed-axis round 7). Closes the last single-seed limb of the attention-cost law named open by NET-33 (issue #140).

## Question
The depth leg k* = 4d (NET-16 d=8, NET-17 d=16, both ctx=128) rests on seed-0 alone. Is it a single-seed artifact? Does the full two-parameter law k* = d·ctx/32 hold where depth AND context act together (ctx=256, d=8 — a never-measured grid cell)?

## Method
Byte-identical harness to NET-16/33 — CausalTF **d=8**, dm=64, 4 heads, 5 Gutenberg novels, vocab 4097, contiguous 90/10 split, 2000 AdamW steps (lr 3e-4) — at **seed=1**, at BOTH **ctx=128 and ctx=256**. Per context: full-acc eval → Part A concentration (eff support, top-k mass, per-position buckets) → Part B top-k sweep → Part B2 random-k control (seed 12345). k* = smallest k with retained ≥ 0.98·full. Prediction stated before the run: **k* = 32 @ 128 (4d), k* = 64 @ 256 (d·ctx/32 = 8·256/32)**.

## Results (retained = acc/full vs 0.98 bar)

| ctx | full acc | k sweep (retained) | k* | predicted |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 128 | 0.1620 | 16→0.962 ✗ 32→**0.988** ✓ 64→0.999 | **32** | 32 |
| 256 | 0.1620 | 32→0.968 ✗ 64→**0.990** ✓ 128→0.999 192→1.000 | **64** | 64 |

1. **BOTH cells land EXACT** — k*(s1, d=8, ctx=128) = 32 (identical to s0, NET-16) and k*(s1, d=8, ctx=256) = 64 (never-measured cell, margin 0.010 = same as every prior pass). k=192 recovers full loss exactly (5.0868 vs 5.0865).
2. **The full two-parameter law k* = d·ctx/32 now holds at a second seed in EVERY measured cell of the (d ∈ {4,8} × ctx ∈ {128,256}) grid** — the last single-seed limb is closed.
3. **Concentration reproduces to ≤0.003** at ctx=128 (eff support 50.16 vs s0 50.13; top-k masses identical to 0.001); context-diffusion extends to depth (eff 50.16→91.49 as ctx doubles, 1.82× vs d=4's 1.78×); per-position no-bounded-working-set shape preserved.
4. **Selection importance survives depth AND seed** — random-k gaps 4.5–8.0 pts at d=8 (vs 6.0–8.7 at d=4).
5. **Six-model full-acc spread 0.1571–0.1620**, k*-irrelevant.

## Verdict
**DEPTH-LEG SEED-ROBUST CONFIRMED.** The attention-cost law k* = d·ctx/32 (speedup lever 32/d: 8× at d=4, 4× at d=8) holds at a second seed in every measured grid cell, with depth-invariant concentration and selection importance. The deployable claim can be shipped without per-instance re-measurement.

## Barriers (all 8 checked)
(a) circularity: no — prediction stated before the run from s0 data + the law; (b) known-method: no — reproducibility verification (Catalog scan: no depth-leg/two-parameter result for top-k pruning); (c) toy-scale: confronted — deepest model of the law's own testbed at the longest context; (d) leakage: none; (e) variance: CLEARED for the depth leg at d=8 — honest remaining single-seed: d=16 (NET-17) and ctx=512; (f) measurement: documented — k=192 recovers full loss exactly, retained 1.000 is the same re-normalization saturation as before, acc noise ≈0.15% ≪ the k*=64 margin; (g) baselines: fair — full-attention reference + random-k control, same bar; (h) relevance: strengthened — depth+context speedup claim survives both levers changing.

## Open
d=16 second-seed point (closes the very last single-seed cell); a ctx=512 point; carry chain at scale (the frontier); d=8 compression floor check.

**Method (ALL_DONE_NET33, /tmp/exp_net_attncost_s1.py):** byte-identical harness to NET-15/20 — CausalTF d=4, dm=64, 4 heads, 5 Gutenberg novels, vocab 4097, contiguous 90/10 split, 2000 AdamW steps (lr 3e-4) — at seed=1, ctx=128 and ctx=256. Per context: full-acc eval → concentration (eff support, top-k mass, per-position buckets) → top-k sweep → random-k control (seed 12345). k* = smallest k with retained ≥ 0.98·full. Prediction stated before the run: k*=16 @ 128, k*=32 @ 256.

**Results:**
- **k* EXACT at the second seed.** ctx=128: k=8 0.973 ✗, k=16 **0.987** ✓ → k*=16 (predicted 16 ✓). ctx=256: k=16 0.973 ✗, k=32 **0.990** ✓ → k*=32 (predicted 32 ✓). Identical to seed-0 → the ∝-ctx proportionality is NOT a single-seed artifact.
- Knee if anything MORE favorable at s1: retained@k* 0.987/0.990 vs 0.984/0.989; cleaner fail/pass margin at ctx=128 (0.973→0.987 vs 0.971→0.984).
- Concentration reproduces to ≤3% relative: eff support 46.41 vs 46.63 (128), 80.57 vs 82.94 (256); top-k masses within 0.009; per-position no-bounded-working-set shape preserved (256: 11.12/70.08/150.44 vs 11.27/72.25/155.35).
- Random-k selection gap seed-stable: within 0.5 pts at every comparable (k,ctx) (+6.1/+8.3/+6.3 vs s0 +6.2/+8.7/+6.0).
- Full-acc spread across the 4 (seed × ctx) models: 0.1571–0.1612 (±0.4% of mean), k*-irrelevant.

**Verdict:** SEED-ROBUST CONFIRMED — k* = d·ctx/32 (lever 32/d, 8× at d=4, context-invariant in [128,256]) holds exactly at a second seed at both contexts; the diffuse-but-prunable structure is a property of the task/data scale, not of one run. NET-20's declared barrier-(e) gap is CLOSED.

**Barriers:** (a) clean — prediction stated before the run from s0 data; nothing injected; (b) clean — a reproducibility verification, not a re-labeled method (Catalog scan: no seed-robustness/concentration-fidelity result for top-k pruning); (c) confronted — same real-scale testbed as the published law; (d) clean — held-out last-10% windows, data-free top-k from eval attention; (e) THE round's content — CLEARED at d=4 for the ∝-ctx leg; honest remaining limit: the DEPTH leg (k*=4d at d=8/16) is still single-seed, k* exact at the sweep's k-resolution; (f) clean — k=192 recovers full loss exactly (5.0842 vs 5.0841), retained@k=128=1.001 is the known re-normalization artifact; (g) fair — full-attention reference + random-k control, same bar; (h) strengthened — a speedup claim that survives seed change ships without per-instance re-measurement.

**Open:** d=8/16 seed-1 depth-leg points (would close the last single-seed limb); a ctx=512 point; carry chain at scale (the frontier); d=8 compression floor check.
title: NET-33: The attention-cost law k*=d·ctx/32 is seed-robust — a second seed reproduces the lossless top-k knee at both contexts

## NET-32 — THE-INTERNALIZATION-TRAIT-IS-A-TRAINING-SOLUTION-PROPERTY-NOT-SEED-INTRINSIC

**Program:** Network/LLM research lab, round-net-32 (mechanism axis). Constructive test of NET-31's "seed-fixed trait": is the eval-load-bearingness of the exclusive boundary block INTRINSIC to the seed, or a TRAINING ARTIFACT of the converged solution?

**Method (ALL_DONE_NET32, /tmp/exp_net_eos_ftune.py):** 6 arms at E=23 (k=3), byte-identical EOSWidthGRU — the complete known-dependent population {13,14,15,17} + controls {16,18}. Standard 12000-step training → stage-0 ctl+zeroN (exact same-seed replication of NET-31 labels) → fine-tune T∈{300,1000,3000} steps with the exclusive block ZEROED at the EOS step (the zeroN eval condition made a TRAINING condition), eval at each stage.

**Results (n=8 full):**
- Stage-0 replication EXACT: zeroN {0.7041, 0.9014, 0.7104, 0.9932, 0.7437, 0.9995} = NET-31 to 4 decimals.
- Conversion: zeroN T=300 {0.9980, 1.0000, 1.0000, 0.7163, 1.0000, 1.0000}; T=1000 {0.9746, 1.0000, 0.9390, 0.6763, 0.9980, 0.9150}; T=3000 all 1.0000.
- T=3000 final: ctl/zeroN/zero1@0/flip1@0/scale0.1 = 1.0000 in all 6 arms × 5 interventions.

**Laws:**
1. The trait is a property of the converged SOLUTION, not the seed — 4/4 dependent seeds convert to self-sufficient in ≤3000 steps (≤2.5% of the training budget). INTRINSIC-TRAIT refuted.
2. Exact same-seed replication = the control (conversion measured on the identical solutions NET-31 labeled).
3. Fast onset: ≥0.99 at T=300 in 5/6 arms.
4. NON-MONOTONE in 4/6 arms (transient n=8 reorganization dip: s=13 T=1000 0.975, s=15 T=1000 0.939, s=16 T=300/1000 0.716/0.676, s=18 T=1000 0.915), always recovering by T=3000 — deploy only at full convergence.
5. Cure preserved: ctl ends 1.0000 in 6/6.
6. Post-conversion the block is INERT: zero1@0/flip/scale (never training conditions) are exact no-ops — the trained block-gated solution path (which needed all coords, zero1=0% at k≥2) is GONE.
7. Mechanism = dynamic stop-routing (block present at ~full magnitude, weight-decay-bounded ~0.97×; EOSCOORD-AFTER |0.06| was a scale0.1 measurement artifact, honestly corrected).

**Design rule upgrade:** ≥3 exclusive dims ⇒ reliable success; then a ≤3000-step no-boundary final fine-tune makes the block OPTIONAL seed-independently — the ~60% internalization lottery and verify-per-instance caveat are gone.

**Barriers:** (a) clean — ctl at full magnitude preserved, untrained interventions inert, n=6-8 length-gen survives; (b) confronted — no-boundary fine-tuning is a known qualitative family, the exact T-law + dip + inertia + trait-not-intrinsic are the novel content (Catalog: closest pkg 693/35 certified adversarial robustness, orthogonal); (c) toy-scale confronted (REAL-SCALE = frontier); (d) clean; (e) complete known-dependent population tested; (f) clean after honest correction of the EOSCOORD-AFTER artifact; (g) same-arm T=0 control; (h) high — one-time protocol replaces per-instance verification.

**Paper 76.** Script /tmp/exp_net_eos_ftune.py; log /tmp/net32.log.
title: NET-32: The internalization trait is a training artifact, not seed-intrinsic — a no-boundary final fine-tune converts 4/4 known-dependent seeds {13,14,15,17} to self-sufficient (exact same-seed replication; cure preserved; block left inert)

**Program:** Network/LLM research lab — round-net-31 (mechanism axis; seed-trait-vs-width-trait test). Paper 75. ALL_DONE_NET31, 12 arms.

**Design:** SEED-FIXED, WIDTH-SWEPT freeze. Part A = E=23 (k=3) × seeds 14–19 (7 interventions/arm: ctl/zeroN/zero1@0,1,2/flip1@0/scale0.1); Part B = E=22 (k=2) × seeds 14–19 (6 interventions/arm). The published E=21 (k=1) arms for the same seeds (NET-28 outcomes + NET-29 k=1 zero1 reads) are the k=1 rung, so every seed 14–19 now has internalization reads at k=1/2/3 — seed-fixed, byte-identical EOSWidthGRU, same-seed training, inference-only interventions, fresh eval draws per arm × manipulation.

**Headline law — INTERNALIZATION-IS-A-SEED-FIXED-TRAIT-AMONG-CURES:** the boundary-dependence set is the SAME at k=2 and k=3 — {13, 14, 15, 17} (this round: k=3 zeroN 0.9014/0.7104/0.7437, k=2 0.9141/0.8037/0.9067 for s=14/15/17; s=13 from NET-29/30 = 0.7041/0.7544) — and the same seven seeds are self-sufficient at both widths ⇒ internalization is ~60/40 (7/11 cures) and WIDTH-INDEPENDENT. Width sets P(cure); the seed sets internalization.

**Honest correction:** NET-29's "5/6 self-sufficient at k=3" was a SEED-SET-SPECIFIC HIGH (seeds 8–13: 1/6 dependent; seeds 14–19: 3/6 dependent + 1/6 marginal). Pooled k=3 over seeds 8–19 = 7/12 self-sufficient/marginal.

**Seed-trait confirmed, width-trait refuted:** s=14/15 (the k=1-dependent cures) stay ensemble-dependent at EVERY width and dependence GROWS with k (s=14: −2.8%→−9%→−10%; s=15: −1…−5%→−20%→−29%; s=13: −25%→−30%; s=17: −9%→−26%). But the trait has NO k=1 predictor (s=13 k=1-fail-no-op and s=17 k=1-partial-no-op are dependent at k≥2; s=16/18 k=1-fail-no-ops are self-sufficient) — it only manifests at widths where the seed cures.

**New markers:** (1) k=2 sign-sensitivity = clean dependence marker — flip costs −7 to −25% in 4/4 dependent k=2 arms (sign-opposition required in the two coords) and is flip-free in self-sufficient arms; at k=3 flip = 0% in all 12 arms across both seed sets. (2) NET-29's magnitude→dependence hint REFUTED (self-sufficient s=18 has larger coords than dependent s=14/17). (3) P(cure)=100% at k=3 extends to a SECOND seed set (12/12 merged).

**Mechanism:** at k≥2 the boundary block is used COLLECTIVELY (zero1 = 0% in every arm); dependent seeds gate the answer path on the aggregate block norm (zeroN 9–29%, scale0.1 1–5%).

**Design rule (sharpened):** ≥3 exclusive dims in a final-step boundary token ⇒ reliable training SUCCESS (12/12 cures at k=3, both seed sets), but only ~60% self-sufficient internalization — ~40% of seeds' answer paths lean on the boundary ensemble at eval, so keep re-serving the boundary token or verify internalization per instance.

**Barriers:** (a) clean (new E=22/E=23 solutions with own ctl baselines; k=1 rung = published same-seed arms; inference-only), (b) clean (Catalog no prior), (c) confronted — ≥3 dims = reliable success but ~60% self-sufficient; real-scale remains the frontier, (d) clean, (e) THE round's content (seed-set-heterogeneous rate reported pooled 7/12; the same-4-seeds trait is a within-seed-across-width reproducibility statement), (f) clean (exact writes, SEs, no-op = |Δ|≤1.2 SE), (g) strong (SEED-FIXED design — width the only training variable), (h) design rule + per-instance verification caution.

**Open:** REAL-SCALE transfer (frontier); a trained-WEIGHT predictor of the seed trait; pad384-vs-NET-24-hybrid parity; why dependence grows with k.

Script /tmp/exp_net_eos_freezek13.py. Log /tmp/net31.log.
title: NET-31: Internalization is a seed-fixed trait among cures — same 4 seeds dependent at k=2 and k=3; NET-29's 5/6 was a seed-set-specific high; dependent seeds stay dependent at every width

body:
**Part of:** Research plan — *Compression Beyond the Pigeonhole Bound* (capstone).

## The grand view
Every compression scheme = **(shared decompressor) + (message bits)**. The pigeonhole bound governs the message bits over *all* strings; breakthroughs come from:

1. Making the shared decompressor dramatically more powerful while keeping its cost **amortized** (Phase A: [[A1]]–[[A5]]).
2. Changing the *setting* so some bits stop counting — common randomness, distributed, almost-lossless — or making the search for short messages cheap (Phase B: [[B1]]–[[B6]]).

## Deliverable
A **unified evaluation harness** covering text (enwik8/9), binary/code, structured numeric/simulation output, and PRNG-generated data — measuring *total effective bits* including any amortized model delta, under the 16 GB decode-memory standard (see [[A5]]).

## Gate
Every result that moves bits from *message* to *shared* — and survives the decode standard — counts. Anything else is a trick.
title: Compression Research C: Unified framework — shared decompressor + message bits

body:
**Part of:** Research plan — *Compression Beyond the Pigeonhole Bound* (Phase B, Question 2: can random number generators help?).

## Research question
Worst-case short-program-finding is **provably hard under standard assumptions**: roughly, if you could always find a short description for every `x` quickly, you could invert one-way functions. Compression ⇋ computational hardness.

## Approach
- State precisely **which compression tasks are equivalent to inverting OWFs** (distinguishable / polynomial-time Kolmogorov complexity literature).
- Derive what that implies for achievable worst-case bounds.

## Deliverable
A precise characterization mapping compression tasks to cryptographic assumptions.

## Purpose
Calibrates the whole plan: **randomness helps compression exactly up to the computational-hardness boundary, and no further.** Converts the intuition "randomness should help" into a quantified expectation.

**Milestone:** M8 (theory, 3–6 weeks).
title: Compression Research B6: Compression ↔ one-way functions (the cryptography link)

body:
**Part of:** Research plan — *Compression Beyond the Pigeonhole Bound* (Phase B, Question 2: can random number generators help?).

## Research question
A surprising amount of real-world data **is** PRNG output: game worlds, simulations, certain file formats, crypto keys. Detect it and recover the seed → compress to ~0 bits beyond the seed.

## Approach
- Robust **PRNG fingerprinting**: which generator family produced this stream?
- **Seed recovery**: Berlekamp–Massey for LFSRs; solver-based inversion for other families.
- A classifier that routes each file to *seed-compressible* vs. *model-compressible*.

## Deliverable
Detection + seed-recovery tooling and a benchmark of seed-compressible files found in real corpora.

## Falsifiability / gate
For a recovered seed: decompressed output must exactly reproduce the file. Measures what fraction of real data is seed-compressible.

**Milestone:** M2 (cheap, warm-up infrastructure). Related: [[B1]].
title: Compression Research B5: PRNG-generated real-world data — detection and seed recovery

body:
**Part of:** Research plan — *Compression Beyond the Pigeonhole Bound* (Phase B, Question 2: can random number generators help?).

## Research question
The expensive part of program-search compression ([[A3]]) is *finding* the short program. **Randomized search is the right tool** — randomness helps compression the way it helps every hard combinatorial problem: in the search, not in the code.

## Approach
- MCTS / stochastic beam search / simulated annealing over the program space; randomized restarts.
- Randomized hashing to test whether a generated prefix agrees with the target — far cheaper than full comparison.
- Integrate with the A3 substrate as its search engine.

## Deliverable
A randomized search loop with measured search-effort vs. compression-quality tradeoffs.

## Falsifiability / gate
Must demonstrate concrete wall-clock / compute savings over deterministic search on the same program space.

**Milestone:** part of M3.
title: Compression Research B4: Randomness as the search engine for program-space search

body:
**Part of:** Research plan — *Compression Beyond the Pigeonhole Bound* (Phase B, Question 2: can random number generators help?).

## Research question
Pigeonhole governs *exact* decoding for *all* strings. Relax to: **decoder fails with probability ≤ ε** (almost-lossless). Random codebooks (Shannon's random-coding argument) then reach near-optimal rates — the counting bound relaxes by an ε-dependent factor.

## Approach
- Constructive almost-lossless schemes with small failure probability.
- The real obstacle is **decoder search complexity** (naive random coding is exponential), not the rate — tackle that.
- Error detection (checksums) so failures are **never silent**.

## Deliverable
A scheme plus a proof that decode succeeds with probability ≥ 1−ε, and its exact decoding complexity.

## Falsifiability / gate
For each scheme: bound on P(failure) and an explicit decoder-complexity figure. No silent corruption allowed.

**Milestone:** M9.
title: Compression Research B3: Almost-lossless / Monte Carlo compression

body:
**Part of:** Research plan — *Compression Beyond the Pigeonhole Bound* (Phase B, Question 2: can random number generators help?).

## Research question
In **distributed** compression (Slepian–Wolf / Wyner–Ziv), the encoder and decoder each see correlated but different observations. Shared randomness between them does **not** count toward rate and provably achieves the joint-entropy bound the encoder alone couldn't reach. A PRNG is the practical vehicle for that shared randomness.

## Approach
- Practical codes exploiting common randomness (linear codes + random cosets).
- The **seeding protocol**: how the PRNG seed is established out-of-band without counting against rate.
- Identify the regime where the PRNG-backed common source shrinks rate vs. the encoder's own side information.

## Deliverable
Constructive schemes with rate proofs and a seeding protocol.

## Falsifiability / gate
For each scheme: achievable rate vs. joint-entropy bound, with the seed demonstrably not counted as transmitted bits.

**Milestone:** M6. **This is the honest home for "PRNG helps compression" — it's about the setting, not the message.**
title: Compression Research B2: Common randomness in distributed compression (Slepian-Wolf / Wyner-Ziv)

body:
**Part of:** Research plan — *Compression Beyond the Pigeonhole Bound* (Phase B, Question 2: can random number generators help?).

## Claim (negative result)
A deterministic PRNG **cannot** help compress arbitrary data.

## Proof sketch
A fixed function seed → stream is deterministic: `2^s` seeds produce at most `2^s` distinct streams, so representing an arbitrary n-bit string still needs `s ≥ n − c`. A PRNG creates **no entropy** — the "compress to the seed" trick only works when the data was *already* PRNG-generated (i.e., it always had low Kolmogorov complexity and the PRNG is just the right decompressor).

## Deliverable
A crisp, citable proof plus a working demo (e.g., a seeded generator whose outputs appear "compressible" while a true random file stays at n bits).

## Purpose
Kill this dead end with evidence **before** anyone spends a year hunting "the seed that contains my file." Calibrates the team on exactly what randomness can and cannot do.

**Milestone:** M1 (days).
title: Compression Research B1: Negative result — PRNGs cannot beat pigeonhole (proof + demo)

body:
**Part of:** Research plan — *Compression Beyond the Pigeonhole Bound* (Phase A, Question 1: separating the decompressor from the data).

## Why this exists
Every compression result in the plan must be judged against the field standard, or it is **cheating, not compression**. This is a mandatory process / infrastructure issue for all other items.

## The standard (Hutter Prize rules)
- Decoded output must **exactly** match the input (lossless).
- Decoding must run under a **16 GB memory limit**.
- No precomputed dictionaries or hidden side channels.
- The decompressor must be reconstructible from the transmitted message + the *public, fixed* substrate.

## Deliverable
A verification harness enforcing this standard across all plan items — including the check that any model delta is counted as transmitted bits.

**Gate for every other issue:** if a result can't pass this harness, it's not a compression breakthrough — it's a trick.
title: Compression Research A5: Verification discipline — 16GB decode standard

body:
**Part of:** Research plan — *Compression Beyond the Pigeonhole Bound* (Phase A, Question 1: separating the decompressor from the data).

## Research question
What if the transmitted program itself contains a decompressor? `U(p)` where `p = (U', p')` — a **recursive / hierarchical** scheme. Does the overhead grow sublinearly across levels? Likely 2 levels capture nearly all the gain.

## Approach
- Analyze overhead growth per level analytically.
- Implement a 2-level demo and measure on corpora.

## Deliverable
A definitive result (positive or negative) on whether hierarchical decompressors pay for themselves.

## Falsifiability / gate
Must show per-message overhead vanishes or is absorbed across levels, under exact-match decoding.

**Milestone:** M7 (cheap, ~1 week).
title: Compression Research A4: Meta-compression — recursive decompressors

body:
**Part of:** Research plan — *Compression Beyond the Pigeonhole Bound* (Phase A, Question 1: separating the decompressor from the data).

## Research question
Instead of a fixed model, **search a space of programs** for the shortest one that emits `x`. This is a direct attack on Kolmogorov complexity `K(x)`. The interpreter is the shared decompressor (free, constant); the program is the message; the search is where cleverness goes.

## Approach
- Build a **compression substrate**: a small Turing-complete interpreter with cheap built-in primitives for patterns real data has (rep-patterns, LZ matches, arithmetic loops, tables).
- Apply modern heuristic search over the program space: MCTS, genetic programming, gradient-guided program synthesis.
- Tame the exponential search with *data-structured* program spaces and strong priors; budgeted search with early gating.

## Deliverable
The substrate + search loop, with measured compression on text and structured corpora.

## Falsifiability / gate
Must beat SOTA lossless baselines exactly, under the 16 GB decode standard. **This is the single most promising structural direction for decompressor separation.**

**Milestone:** M3. Related: [[B4]] (randomized search as the engine for this).
title: Compression Research A3: Program search as compression — Kolmogorov-approximation substrate

body:
**Part of:** Research plan — *Compression Beyond the Pigeonhole Bound* (Phase A, Question 1: separating the decompressor from the data).

## Research question
A fixed pretrained model (e.g., an LLM) used as the shared decompressor + arithmetic-coded residual beats classical compressors on text by a wide margin. The open problem: **the transmitted model delta costs bits** — how do we amortize it?

## Approach
- Benchmark LLM-as-decompressor against gzip/bz2/context-mixing baselines (enwik8/9).
- Investigate sparse / low-rank parameter patches (LoRA-style) as the transmitted program — how many bits to shift a shared decoder to a specific domain?
- Design an amortized protocol: decompressor adapts across a *stream* of messages, paying the delta once.

## Deliverable
SOTA text-compression baseline under the 16 GB decode standard, plus an amortized model-delta protocol.

## Falsifiability / gate
Must beat classical baselines *losslessly* (decoded output exactly matches input) with the decoder fixed at deploy time. Any delta is part of the transmitted message.

**Milestone:** M4.
title: Compression Research A2: Learnable shared decompressors — model is free, model delta is not

body:
**Part of:** Research plan — *Compression Beyond the Pigeonhole Bound* (Phase A, Question 1: separating the decompressor from the data).

## Research question
One shared decompressor `U` must serve all inputs. A decompressor specialized to a *class* of data does better per class. What is the **price of universality** — the minimax redundancy a universal scheme must pay over a per-distribution scheme?

## Approach
- Derive closed-form / tight bounds on universal redundancy for natural source classes: stationary sources, finite-state, Markov.
- Express redundancy as a function of message length `n` and class complexity.

## Deliverable
Rigorous bounds on universal vs. per-distribution redundancy, and a conclusion on whether specialized decompressors are theoretically worth pursuing.

## Falsifiability / gate
Bounds must match or beat known minimax rates from the literature (Rissanen-style redundancy). If specialization doesn't move bits from *message* to *shared*, the direction is dead.

**Milestone:** M5 (theory, ~2 weeks).
title: Compression Research A1: Price of universality — minimax redundancy of universal decompressors

## NET-30 — The k=2 freeze test (round-net-30, 12 arms, ALL_DONE_NET30)

The middle of the eval-dependence gradient (NET-29 open 1). Twelve same-seed reproductions of NET-27 arms (byte-identical EOSWidthGRU; all ctl re-baselines reproduce the published NET-27 outcomes on fresh draws). Inference-only interventions on the trained exclusive coords; fresh eval draws per arm × manipulation.

### Part A — k=2 (E=22) × seeds 8–13, 6 interventions/arm (n=8 full)

| seed | ctl | **zeroN** (both excl) | zero1@0/1 | flip1@0 | scale0.1 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 8  | 1.0000 | 1.0000 | 1.0000 | 1.0000 (n5 .9995) | 1.0000 |
| 9  | 0.9888 | 0.9902 | 0.9863 / 0.9902 | 0.9902 | 0.9873 |
| 10 | 0.9399 | 0.9453 | 0.9502 / 0.9390 | 0.9487 | 0.9380 |
| 11 | 1.0000 | 1.0000 | 1.0000 | 1.0000 | 1.0000 |
| 12 | 1.0000 | 0.9995 (n6/n7) | 1.0000 | 0.9985 (n5/n6) | 1.0000 |
| 13 | 0.9980 | **0.7544** | 0.9961 / 0.9990 | **0.7505** | **0.9067** |

**k=2 is NOT intermediate — it matches k=3.** Whole-block zeroing costs ≤0.010 in 5/6 arms (the two largest changes are POSITIVE — removal *helps* the imperfect s=10 arm, never breaks it). The 6th is **s=13 — the SAME seed as the k=3 outlier** — again a redundant ensemble (2-of-2-redundant: zero1 no-ops) but now sign-SENSITIVE (flip −0.25) and magnitude-sensitive, again with the LARGEST coords of its width (0.701 vs ≤0.660). k=3's s=13 flip was a no-op ⇒ **sign-sensitivity is width-conditional; NET-29's "signs never matter" was a k=3 statement.** Within-width ∝-quality REFUTED (s=10, the worst arm at ctl 0.9399, is self-sufficient).

### Part B — k=1 (E=21) × seeds 8–13, ctl/zero1 (n=8 full)

| seed | NET-27 ctl | ctl | zero1 | verdict |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 8  | 1.0000 | 1.0000 | **1.0000** | self-sufficient cure |
| 9  | 0.7715 | 0.7622 | 0.7432 | −0.019 (~2 SE, marginal) |
| 10 | 0.1567 | 0.1606 | 0.1592 | no-op |
| 11 | 0.8926 | 0.8892 | 0.8901 | no-op |
| 12 | 1.0000 | 1.0000 | **1.0000** | self-sufficient cure |
| 13 | 0.2656 | 0.2734 | 0.2510 | −0.022 (~2 SE, marginal fail) |

**NET-29's "k=1 internalization ∝ cure quality" is REFUTED at a second seed set.** Both fresh full cures (s=8, s=12) are fully self-sufficient — zeroing the sole coord costs 0% at every length. Pooled over all 12 k=1 arms (NET-29 seeds 14–19 + NET-30 seeds 8–13): **fails are no-ops in EVERY arm of both rounds; successes split seed-heterogeneously** (2/2 dependent at NET-29 seeds, 0/2 at NET-30 seeds). Self-sufficiency rate rises with k: k=1 ~1/2 of successes, k=2 5/6, k=3 5/6.

### The law

**INTERNALIZATION-SATURATES-AT-K=2 + THE-K=1-INTERNALIZATION-IS-SEED-HETEROGENEOUS + S13-IS-A-SEED-WIDE-OUTLIER.** (1) Eval-sufficiency of the exclusive boundary channel collapses between k=1 and k=2; NET-28's P(cure) ramp is a TRAINING-TIME success-rate effect only — k=3's knee buys reliable *training* success, *eval* sufficiency is bought at k=2. (2) s=13 is a seed-wide (not width-specific) trait — the same seed keeps its recovery boundary-dependent at eval at every width where it succeeds, always with the largest exclusive coords (magnitude→dependence hint now holds at two widths for one seed). (3) NET-29's ∝-quality law is corrected: the robust invariant over 12 k=1 arms is that removal of the sole coord is a no-op exactly where the model already failed, and at successes it is seed-heterogeneous. Design rule sharpens to **≥2 exclusive dims** for a self-sufficient recovery (≥3 for reliable success).

### Barriers

(a) same-seed reproductions of NET-27 arms, ctl reproduces published outcomes, inference-only; (b) target (saturation width, seed-wide outlier, ∝-quality refutation) new — Catalog no prior; (c) toy-scale — transferable statement is the training-time design rule; real-scale remains the frontier; (d) clean; (e) THE round's content — the NET-29 refutation recorded as an honest correction, seed-heterogeneity as a distribution, ~2 SE excursions reported as marginals (1 of 12 comparisons); (f) exact parameter writes, ctl reproduces, SEs, no-op = |Δ|≤1.2 SE; (g) byte-identical cell, within-arm ctl, Part A vs B differ only in E + intervention set; (h) design rule ≥2 exclusive dims + CAUTION updated (k=1 cures NOT reliably self-sufficient).

### Next candidates

## NET-29 — Causal freeze of the exclusive boundary channel (round-net-29, 12 arms, ALL_DONE_NET29)

The causal test NET-28's open (1) demanded. Twelve arms, each a SAME-SEED reproduction of a NET-28 arm (byte-identical EOSWidthGRU; trained EOS exclusive coords reproduce NET-28 to 3 decimals — interventions attach to the exact published trained solutions). Inference-only manipulations of the trained exclusive coords; fresh eval draws per arm × intervention; ctl re-baselines reproduce NET-28 outcomes.

### Part A — E=23 (k=3) × seeds 8–13, 7 interventions/arm

| seed | ctl | zero3 (all 3 excl) | zero1 (any single) | flip1 | scale0.1 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 8–12 | 1.0000 | **0.9971–1.0000** (5/6) | 1.0000 ×6 | 1.0000 ×6 | 1.0000 ×5/6 |
| 13 | 1.0000 | **0.7041** | 1.0000 | 1.0000 | **0.9692** |

**Removing the entire exclusive block at eval leaves the k=3 cure intact in 5/6 arms** (≤0.3% scattered, never a collapse). The 6th (s=13) is a MAGNITUDE-ENSEMBLE dependence (zero1→1.0000, scale0.1→0.9692, flip→no-op) — and s=13 has the LARGEST coords (|0.65–0.66|), a magnitude→dependence hint, FLAGGED. Zeroing ANY single coord costs 0% in all 6; signs never matter.

### Part B — E=21 (k=1) × seeds 14–19, ctl / zero1 (sole exclusive coord)

| seed | outcome | ctl | zero1 | Δ |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 14 | cure | 1.0000 | **0.9717** | **−2.8% (~3 SE)** |
| 15 | near-cure | 0.9858 | n5 **0.9531** | **−1 to −5% short/mid** |
| 16/17/18/19 | fails/partials | 0.16–0.79 | unchanged | **no-op** (all \|Δ\| ≤ 1.2 SE) |

**Eval-load-bearingness of the sole exclusive coord is PROPORTIONAL TO CURE QUALITY**: it costs real accuracy where the recurrence internalized it, and is a no-op where it failed — causally confirming NET-28's downstream-fragility (removal is free exactly where the model already failed with the coord present).

### Law

**THE-EXCLUSIVE-BOUNDARY-CHANNEL-IS-TRAINING-TIME-LOAD-BEARING.** At k=3, BPTT-through-time uses the unambiguous-boundary teacher signal to shape a SELF-SUFFICIENT depth-recovery that (in the majority) no longer needs the exclusive input at eval; the k≥3 benefit is realized in the weights, not held at the input. Internalization is seed-heterogeneous (5/6 self-sufficient, 1/6 ensemble-dependent). The ≥3-exclusive-dims rule is a TRAINING-TIME rule — an internalized answer path need not re-serve the exclusive token at inference.

### Barriers

(a) inference-only on same-seed reproductions, ctl reproduces; (b) input ablation standard but the target + internalization∝cure finding new (Catalog no prior); (c) toy-scale — the transferable statement is the training-time design rule; real-scale remains the frontier; (d) clean; (e) the round's content — seed heterogeneity reported as a distribution, byte-identical same-seed reproductions; (f) exact parameter writes, ctl reproduces published outcomes, no-op = |Δ|≤1.2 SE; (g) within-arm ctl baseline, Part A vs B differ only in E + intervention set; (h) training-time design rule + CAUTION: single-seed "boundary doesn't matter at eval" is untrustworthy, and k=1 cures genuinely need their single coord at inference.

### Next candidates

k=2 freeze test (is E=22 internalization intermediate — links the eval-dependence gradient to the P(cure) ramp); magnitude→dependence trend (~24 more E=23 arms); **REAL-SCALE transfer of the training-time ≥3-exclusive-dims rule**; pad384-vs-NET-24-hybrid parity.

## Summary

Round-net-27 fills NET-26's flagged open gap: the shape of the EOS-width P(cure) shift inside (20,28]. Twenty-four arms on the byte-identical NET-26 EOSWidthGRU (GRUCell(384→192), learned E-d EOS zero-padded to 384, ONLY E varies): E ∈ {21,22,24,28} × 6 FRESH seeds (8–13) — every sample an independent draw, merged anchors stay independent.

## Results (n=8 full)

| E (exclusive dims k) | 6 fresh seeds | P(≥0.99) | min |
|---|---|---|---|
| 21 (k=1) | 1.0000, 0.7715, 0.1567, 0.8926, 1.0000, 0.2656 | 2/6 | 0.1567 |
| 22 (k=2) | 1.0000, 0.9912, 0.9482, 1.0000, 1.0000, 0.9990 | 5/6 | 0.9482 |
| 24 (k=4) | 1.0000 ×6 | 6/6 | 1.0000 |
| 28 (k=8) | 1.0000 ×6 (8/8 combined) | 6/6 | 1.0000 |

## The law

**EOS-WIDTH-SHIFT-IS-A-MONOTONE-RAMP** — merges with NET-26's anchors into a full reliability curve:

- Failure mass vs E: **75% (E=20) → 67% (E=21) → 17% (E=22, worst case a near-cure 0.948) → 0 (E=24) → 0 (E≥28)**.
- Worst case n=8 full: 0.005 → 0.157 → 0.948 → 1.0000 → 1.0000; medians 0.044 → 0.83 → 1.0 → 1.0 → 1.0.
- **NO sharp critical width in (20,28]**: E=21 produces both a full cure (1.0000) and a hard failure (0.1567) among fresh draws.
- **The first exclusive dim is NOT sufficient** (the naive "any exclusive dim suffices" reading of NET-26's distinctness law is REFUTED). The benefit is SUBLINEAR — a reliability/optimization-fragility curve, not a capacity cliff.
- Failure mechanism is width-independent: same progressive-unroll collapse (n=5 1.0 → n=7 ~0.82 → n=8 0.16–0.27) and same probe signature (‖h‖ drift + maxconf dips at beyond-training cols) as E=20.
- E≥28 merged is now **26/26 clean cures**.

## Design rule

A real-LM final-step boundary token should reserve **≥4 exclusive dims in its own parameter subspace** (k=2 near-robust, k=1 fragile). Single-seed "thresholds" in toy mechanism studies should be read as draws from such a curve.

## Honest limits

n=6 per width makes the E21→E22 P-jump alone not significant (Fisher ≈0.24); the law rests on the monotone ordering across four widths plus the much larger merged anchors (12 at E=20, 26 at E≥28). E=23/25 untested (knee inside (21,24)). Barriers a–h checked in the paper.

## Summary

Round-net-26 resolves NET-25's flagged EOS-width threshold (28–384) on the carry-wall cure. Thirty arms on the plain n=5 task (GRUCell(384→192), learned E-d EOS zero-padded to 384, ONLY E varies):

- **Sweep** (E ∈ {20,28,64,96,128,192,256,384} × 2 seeds): E=20 {0.9990, 0.0166} fragile; **E≥28 cures 14/14 at 1.0000**.
- **Construction-order verify** (E=20, s0): after-seed 0.9990 = before-seed 0.9990 → NET-25's pad384/pad384-zeroEOS drew DIFFERENT init streams ("identical-weights" control **INVALID**) but timing is immaterial (the 0/2 was 2 unlucky draws from P(cure|E20)≈¼).
- **Endpoint distribution** (E=20/384 × seeds 2–7): E20 {0.0107, 0.1240, 0.0576, 0.0054, 0.0063, 0.0308}; E384 1.0000 ×6.

## The law

**EOS-WIDTH-DISTRIBUTION-SHIFT** — EOS width gates P(cure) one-sided, not a sharp boundary:

- Merged E=20 (12 samples): {0.999×3, 0.744, 0.124, 0.058, 0.031, 0.026, 0.017, 0.011, 0.006, 0.005} → **P(clean cure) = 3/12 = 25%**, median 0.044.
- Merged E≥28 (20 samples): **all 1.0000, 0/20 failures**.
- **Control variable = representational distinctness, not width**: E=20's EOS occupies exactly the digit subspace (dims 0–19, no exclusive dims) → boundary ambiguous with a digit step → seed-fragile; E≥28 adds exclusive dims → robust. pos28 (full-input-width EOS, no exclusive dims) is consistent.
- **NET-25 corrections**: "28-d fails (pos28 0.0049)" was a GRUCell(28)-architecture artifact (E28 cures 2/2 on the 384-d cell); "20-d fails 0/2" was a small unlucky draw. NET-25's mechanism (dense boundary input keeps hidden state in-distribution at depth) **SURVIVES** on stronger ground (20/20 vs 3/12).

## Evidence

- Failure mode: smooth progressive-unroll collapse (n=5 1.0000 → n=6 0.9556 → n=7 0.1445 → n=8 0.0166), column-clustered errors.
- Probe discriminator: cure = flat hidden-norm (Δ<0.2) + maxconf 1.000; failure = norm drift (Δ+2.2) + maxconf dips 0.945–0.984.
- Determinism exact: after-seed s0 = 0.9990 reproduced byte-identical twice.

## Barriers

Variance (e) is the central barrier of the round, now closed: 12-sample E20 distribution + 20-sample E≥28 distribution; the invalid control is demonstrated invalid AND immaterial. All other barriers clean/confronted (see paper).

**Program:** Network/LLM research lab — round-net-25 (performance axis; mechanism dissection of the NET-24 stateful-carry-cell cure). **Paper:** ResearchOutput/NetworkMathematics/25_StatefulCarryCellMechanism.md. **Status:** Machine-verified (ALL_DONE_NET25, _PAD, _SWEEP, _EOS). **Assessment v25, experiment 25.**

## Hypothesis
NET-24 resolved the five-axis carry-chain length wall with the FIRST positive cure (GRU carry cell over the walled encoder's per-column features → n=5/6/7/8 full=1.0000, both seeds) and RAW-STATE-ALONE-HITS-A-STATE-HORIZON (pure GRU on raw one-hots masters n=5, degrades at n=8 0.08–0.70), concluding the cure needs state AND the encoder's content-rich features. This round dissects the cure — WHICH answer-side ingredient is load-bearing? Three mutually-exclusive horns:

- **H1 CAPACITY** — the state-horizon is a 125k-param artifact. Test: capacity-matched hidden=384 (~471k) raw GRU on the same one-hots.
- **H2 REPRESENTATION** — high-dim well-separated features cure it; the encoder's LEARNING is not load-bearing. Test: UNTRAINED fixed random 384-d projection of the same one-hots.
- **H3 POSITION** — the encoder's step-position signal is load-bearing. Test: one-hots + 8-d RoPE-schedule sinusoid.

## Setup
Plain n=5 LSB-first base-10 a+b=c, bs=256, 12000 AdamW steps, teacher-forced eval n=5/6/7/8 (2048 fresh draws). 20+ runs across 4 scripts: 6-arm dissection + pad control + 13-seed variance sweep + EOS-density control.

## Results (n=8 full; chance 1e-9)
| Arm | n=8 full | params | reading |
|---|---|---|---|
| cap384-raw s0/s1 | 0.0078 / 0.0063 | 471,582 | H1 REFUTED — 471k raw GRU fails like the 125k one |
| proj384 s0/s1 | 1.0000 / 1.0000 | 335,242 | H2-strong REFUTED/weak CONFIRMED — UNTRAINED projection cures |
| pos28 s0/s1 | 0.0049 / 0.0049 | 129,830 | H3 REFUTED — position adds nothing |
| pad384 s0..s3 | 1.0000 × 4 | 335,242 | raw one-hots + dense EOS cure (364 dead dims) |
| pad384-zeroEOS s0/s1 | 0.7441 / 0.0259 | 334,878 | same-seed identical weights, 20-d EOS → raw20 range |
| raw20-192 s0..s6 | 0.0806, 0.6997, 0.0103, 0.0063, 0.0093, 0.0020, 0.0132 | 125,214 | 0/7 at 1.0; distribution, not a hard wall |

**The decisive control (airtight):** pad384 and pad384-zeroEOS draw IDENTICAL GRUCell/head weights for the same seed (construction order matches; only the EOS parameter count differs). GRUCarry's EOS is a DENSE LEARNED vector of size in_dim fed at the final carry step — 384-d for pad384 (the "dead" input columns are ALIVE there), 20-d for raw20. The EOS input dimension ALONE flips n=8 full 0.026–0.744 → 1.0000.

## The law
**DENSE-FINAL-STEP-IS-THE-CURE** — the stateful-carry-cell cure is the DENSE learned final-carry (EOS) input RICHNESS, NOT the encoder's content/context/position:
1. The cure is the dense EOS input (identical-weights control) — NET-24's "content-rich column features" interpretation CORRECTED.
2. The digit-path can be RAW (pad384's 364 dead padding dims cure; proj384 dense cures 5/5) — the pure-GRU failure was its 20-d EOS, not its 20-d digit inputs.
3. The raw20 state-horizon is real but seed-variance-heavy — a distribution (0.002–0.70), not a hard wall; NET-24's 2-seed law undersampled it, conclusion holds at 0/7.
4. EOS richness needs dimension FAR above the digit count (28-d learned EOS still fails 0.0049; 384 works, 20/28 fail — threshold 28–384 untested).
5. The carry TRANSITION was always length-general (final-carry 0.86–0.99 even in failing arms); the digit READOUT was the fragile part, and the dense EOS keeps it in-distribution at deep unrolls (mechanism hypothesis — boundary-step backprop conditioning — flagged, not proven).

## Verdict
None of the three original hypotheses survives; the true lever is final-step input richness. A dense-EOS raw GRU cures with NO encoder at all. Design lesson: for length-general sequential computation in state-augmented answer paths, the final step's input pathway must be rich — boundary-condition richness, not feature content/capacity/position, keeps recurrent readouts in-distribution at depth.

## Barriers
(a) clean (same-weights control cannot be circular); (b) controlled decomposition is the contribution (Catalog scan: no prior controlled length-gen cure dissection); (c) same dm-scale as NET-19/21/22/23/24; (d) clean — no beyond-max trained; (e) the central improvement — 2-seed "cures" re-measured at 5/5 (proj384) and 4/4 (pad384), raw20 at 0/7 with full distribution, EOS control same-seed identical-weights; threshold untested flagged; (f) teacher-forced full/per/per-position, cascade vs thin-dip distinguished; (g) raw20-192 = byte-identical NET-24 baseline, arms differ by exactly one architectural variable; (h) mechanism-level correction directing real-LM recurrence work toward well-conditioned boundary inputs.

## Scripts / logs
- /tmp/exp_net_stateful_ctrl.py (ALL_DONE_NET25) — 6-arm dissection
- /tmp/exp_net_stateful_pad.py (ALL_DONE_NET25_PAD) — pad control
- /tmp/exp_net_stateful_sweep.py (ALL_DONE_NET25_SWEEP) — 13-seed variance
- /tmp/exp_net_stateful_eosctrl.py (ALL_DONE_NET25_EOS) — EOS-density control
- Logs: /tmp/net25.log, /tmp/net25_pad.log, /tmp/net25_sweep.log, /tmp/net25_eos.log
title: NET-25 (paper 69): DENSE-FINAL-STEP-IS-THE-CURE — the stateful-carry-cell cure was the dense EOS (final-carry) input, not the encoder's content

body:
**Program:** Network/LLM lab — round-net-24 (performance axis; recurrence / stateful-carry-cell test of the carry-chain length wall). Machine-verified (ALL_DONE_NET24). Paper: ResearchOutput/NetworkMathematics/24_StatefulCarryCell.md (paper 68). Script /tmp/exp_net_stateful.py, log /tmp/net24.log.

## Claim
The carry-chain length wall (transformer masters n-digit addition, computes n+1/n+2 at chance — immune to depth/scale/schedule/task-remodeling/position-scheme, NET-4/5/19/21/22/23) is a **fixed-depth, STATE-FREE, position-parameterized ANSWER-FUNCTION expressivity limit**. Adding a length-general stateful answer cell (GRU carrying the carry in hidden state) over the walled transformer's per-column features unlocks length-general composition.

## Result (plain n=5 training, eval n=5/6/7/8, 2048 fresh draws each, teacher-forced, dm=192, bs=256, 12000 steps)
| Arm | n=5 | n=6 | n=7 | n=8 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| pure GRU s=0 (raw one-hot columns) | 1.0000 | 0.9980 | 0.7021 | 0.0806 |
| pure GRU s=1 | 1.0000 | 1.0000 | 0.9854 | 0.6997 |
| **hybrid-RoPE s=0 (walled encoder → GRU readout)** | **1.0000** | **1.0000** | **1.0000** | **1.0000** |
| **hybrid-RoPE s=1** | **1.0000** | **1.0000** | **1.0000** | **1.0000** |
| hybrid-abs s=0 (learned pos encoder → GRU) | 1.0000 | 0.9834 | 0.9634 | 0.9624 |
| NET-23 reference: RoPE transformer (state-free readout) | 1.0000 | **0.0000** | **0.0000** | **0.0000** |

## Laws
1. **STATEFUL-CARRY-CELL-UNLOCKS-LENGTH-GEN — the FIRST positive cure in the program.** Same encoder, budget, causal mask; the readout's STATE is the only difference from NET-23 and it flips beyond-max 0.0000 → 1.0000 (both seeds, zero errors on 18.4k fresh n=8 digit predictions).
2. **THE-WALL-WAS-THE-ANSWER-FUNCTION, NOT THE ENCODER.** NET-22's GIVEN-CARRIES-STILL-FAIL is explained: carries as INPUT tokens are useless to a state-free readout; the same carries as recurrent STATE are exactly the cure.
3. **THE-CURE-IS-POSITION-SCHEME-INDEPENDENT** (abs-pos hybrid also length-gens, n=8 full=0.9624; uniform thin column-error tail = feature-quality noise from untrained table entries, not a structural wall; RoPE gives the clean 1.0000).
4. **NEW — RAW-STATE-ALONE-HITS-A-STATE-HORIZON.** The textbook pure GRU extends ~1–2 steps past its training unroll (carry TRANSITION length-general, digit READOUT misfires) — recurrence alone is not a clean cure; state + the encoder's content-rich column features are. Capacity caveat (125k vs 782k) flagged.

## Barriers
(a) clean (eval n=6/7/8 fresh, never trained; encoder causal at all lengths, mask verified); (b) RNNs are textbook but the controlled decomposition isolating the wall to the answer function is new; (c) same dm=192 scale as the established wall; (d) clean (teacher-forced on input only); (e) strong on the central claim — 2 seeds both 1.0000 (0→1); pure-GRU state-horizon seed-dependent (honest); (f) per/full/per-position + mask identity verified; (g) NET-23 config byte-identical as the 0.0000 reference + pure-GRU solvability control; (h) mechanism-level: length-general sequential composition in an attention architecture requires STATE in the answer path — the real-LM transfer question is now the frontier.

Assessment v24, 24 experiments. Round-net-24 (1/1 done).
title: NET-24: A Stateful Carry Cell Unlocks Length-General Carry — The Wall Was the Answer Function (first positive cure)

body:
## NET-23 — RoPE vs the carry-chain length wall (position-representation axis)

**Paper:** ResearchOutput/NetworkMathematics/23_RopeCarryChain.md (paper 67). **Verdict: NEGATIVE — the positive horn is refuted.**

### Hypothesis
NET-22's GIVEN-CARRIES-STILL-FAIL proved the wall is a position-specific answer-COMPUTATION failure — but every length-gen eval in the program (NET-4/5/19/21/22) used **learned ABSOLUTE pos embeddings**, so beyond-max positions 25..36 were UNTRAINED table entries. Test: replace the pos table with **RoPE** (rotary q/k, no table, smooth extrapolatable positions — the scheme of essentially all modern LLMs) and re-run the wall.

### Setup
Plain n=5 LSB-first a+b=c, d=1/dm=192/untied/bs=256/12000 steps, identical arch/budget across arms — the `rope` flag is the ONLY difference. Arms: **abs-pos control (s=0)** + **rope s=0, s=1**. Eval n=5/6/7/8 teacher-forced, 2048 fresh draws, with per-position breakdown.

### Results (full chance 1e-7/1e-8/1e-9 at n=6/7/8)
| arm | n=5 full/per | n=6 | n=7 | n=8 | MSB pos n=6/7/8 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| abs-pos (s=0) | 1.0000 / 1.0000 | 0.0000 | 0.0000 | 0.0000 | 0.198/0.307/0.109 |
| **rope s=0** | **1.0000 / 1.0000 by st=1000** | 0.0000 | 0.0000 | 0.0000 | **0.587/0.571/0.565** |
| rope s=1 | 0.1040 / 0.8507 (permanently dissociated) | 0.0000 | 0.0000 | 0.0000 | 0.521/0.552/0.208 |

### The law
1. **ROPE-DOES-NOT-UNLOCK-LENGTH-GEN** — beyond-max full=0.0000 in BOTH RoPE seeds despite clean in-range mastery (s=0 perfect by step 1000, faster than any prior arm).
2. **THE-POS-EMB-CAVEAT-IS-RETIRED** — the first length-gen eval with NO position table. The wall survives smooth, training-consistent, extrapolatable rotary positions ⇒ it is a GENUINE fixed-depth expressivity limit, NOT a pos-emb extrapolation artifact.
3. **NEW — MSB/FINAL-CARRY-MARGINAL-TRANSFERS**: RoPE's beyond-max MSB accuracy (0.565–0.587 ≈ the P(carry-out≈1)≈0.5 prior) vs the abs-pos control's 0.11–0.31 on untrained entries. The final-carry DISTRIBUTION transfers; the computation does not — the cleanest separation yet of statistical-prior vs algorithm transfer.
4. **NEW — ROPE-DISSOCIATION-IS-SEED-DEPENDENT** with a ONE-COLUMN per-position shape (s=1 n=5 [0.107,1,1,1,1,1]: interior + final-carry columns perfect, only the LSB digit wrong — distinct from NET-4/5's carry-cascade, single-seed).

### Why it matters
The carry wall is now characterized on FIVE axes — depth (NET-4/5/19), scale (NET-19), schedule (NET-21), task-remodeling (NET-22), position representation (this round) — all negative for length-general composition. Scratchpad AND position encoding are both closed. Surviving levers (down from 3 to 2) change the STATE, not the position scheme: **recurrence / a stateful carry cell** (the only length-general state device) or an explicit **length-parameterized readout**. RoPE speeds in-range learning and transfers the beyond-max marginal, but not the composition — a caution against the "RoPE improves length generalization" framing for sequential arithmetic.

All 8 network barriers checked (see paper). 23 experiments, assessment v23. Script /tmp/exp_net_rope.py (ALL_DONE_NET23), log /tmp/net23.log.

# NET-22 — Round 22: the task-remodeling test of the carry-chain length wall

**Hypothesis tested:** NET-4's credit-assignment account says the carry-chain length wall (transformers master training-length addition but generalize to n+1/n+2 at chance) is a credit shortfall. If we EXPOSE the carry state as explicit per-column targets (scratchpad/CoT), the chain gets per-step credit and should length-generalize — the first positive cure.

**Setup:** LSB-first a+b=c, dm=192, untied readout, bs=256, 12000 steps, VOCAB=14 (+SC/GO), CTX=40 (n=8 scratchpad seq 4n+5=37 fits). Scratchpad target `SC c_1..c_n GO s_1..s_n c_n` — carries AND answers teacher-forced at train. Eval FULLY AUTOREGRESSIVE (model generates its own carries then answers — no teacher forcing) + a **given-correct-carries diagnostic** (feeds true carries, isolates answer-COMPUTATION from carry-GENERATION). Arms: d=1 plain control + scratchpad s0/s1; d=2 plain control + scratchpad s0/s1.

## Results

| arm | n=5 (in-range) | n=6 | n=7 | n=8 | given-carries n=6/7/8 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| d=1 plain control (s0) | **1.0000** (stable) | 0.0000 | 0.0000 | 0.0000 | — |
| d=1 scratchpad s0 | tf 1.0000→**collapse to 0.25 plateau** | 0.0000 | 0.0000 | 0.0000 | **0.0000** |
| d=1 scratchpad s1 | tf 1.0000→**collapse to 0.74 plateau** | 0.0000 | 0.0000 | 0.0000 | **0.0000** |
| d=2 plain control (s0) | 0.10 (stuck dissociation) | 0.0000 | 0.0000 | 0.0000 | — |
| d=2 scratchpad s0 | dip 0.80@st2000 → **1.0000 held** | 0.0000 | 0.0000 | 0.0000 | **0.0000** |
| d=2 scratchpad s1 | crash 0.041@st3000 → **1.0000 held** | 0.0000 | 0.0000 | 0.0000 | **0.0000** |

## Findings

1. **SCRATCHPAD-DOES-NOT-UNLOCK-LENGTH-GEN.** Beyond-max n=6/7/8 at chance (0.0000) in ALL FOUR scratchpad arms (d=1×2, d=2×2 seeds). The task-remodeling lever — NET-21's top surviving candidate — is CLOSED at both depths.
2. **GIVEN-CARRIES-STILL-FAIL (strongest wall diagnostic yet).** Feeding TRUE carries for n=6/7/8 still yields 0.0000 answers at both depths. A model that knows every carry exactly cannot compute the n+1-digit answer ⇒ the wall is a **position-specific ANSWER-COMPUTATION property**, not carry propagation, not credit assignment.
3. **SCRATCHPAD-COLLAPSE-IS-DEPTH-CONDITIONED (new).** Scratchpad n=5 mastery is UNSTABLE at both depths, but the terminal state is depth-dependent: at **d=1 both seeds collapse PERMANENTLY** from 1.0000 into carry-dissociation plateaus (full≈0.25/0.74 — carries still known, answer chain failed: the NET-4/5/19/21 correlated-error signature); at **d=2 both seeds recover to stable 1.0000** (s0 dip to 0.80, s1 violent crash to 0.041, both re-master). Plain d=1 control mastery is rock-stable ⇒ instability is scratchpad-specific. The mirror-image of NET-19's stochastic ESCAPE.
4. Scratchpad rescues **IN-RANGE** mastery at d=2 (both seeds 1.0000 where the d=2 plain control stuck at full=0.10) while leaving the **BEYOND-range** answer function untouched — the cleanest in-range-credit vs beyond-range-answer split in the program.

## The law

**SCRATCHPAD-DOES-NOT-UNLOCK-LENGTH-GEN + GIVEN-CARRIES-STILL-FAIL + SCRATCHPAD-COLLAPSE-IS-DEPTH-CONDITIONED.** The carry-chain length wall is characterized on depth (NET-4/5/19), scale (NET-19), schedule (NET-21), AND task-remodeling (this round) — all negative for length-general composition. The mechanism is now positional/representational expressivity of the fixed-depth answer function, not credit.

## Barriers check (summary)

- (a) circularity — clean: fresh held-out 2048/batch; auto eval generates carries+answers; nothing injected
- (b) scratchpad/CoT is mature — NEW = the controlled negative + given-carries answer-wall isolation + depth-conditioned collapse; Catalog scan: no scratchpad-vs-length-wall controlled result
- (c) same dm=192 scale as NET-19 (4.5–18× params)
- (d) clean: test lengths 6/7/8 never trained; given-carries feeds TRUE carries from fresh data
- (e) PARTIAL: 2 seeds per depth (scratchpad arm), 1 per plain control; decisive readings stark (0.0000 vs 1.0000; plateaus stable 7000–8000 steps)
- (f) documented; shared caveat: pos-emb extrapolation (train sees positions 0..24, beyond-max evals use up to 36) — RoPE is a surviving lever
- (g) same-run plain controls at both depths, identical budget/arch/seed
- (h) honest negative: the universal LLM-arithmetic recipe (scratchpad/CoT) does NOT fix length-gen on a controlled carry task, even with perfect carry supervision

**Surviving levers change the REPRESENTATION:** recurrence / stateful carry cell (architecture — length-general state), RoPE / position encoding (input), length-parameterized readout (output).

Paper: ResearchOutput/NetworkMathematics/22_ScratchpadCarryChain.md. Script: /tmp/exp_net_scratchpad.py (ALL_DONE + ALL_DONE_D2). Log: /tmp/net22.log. Assessment v22, 22 experiments.
title: NET-22: Scratchpad does not unlock length-gen — explicit per-column carry targets change mastery dynamics but not the length wall (given-correct-carries still fails; collapse is depth-conditioned)

**Round-net-21. Performance axis (training-schedule test of the carry-chain length wall).**

NET-19 (issue #115) named the training SCHEDULE as the untested lever on the memorize-without-compose length wall. This round tests it directly: does a length curriculum — or length-mixing — force a length-GENERAL carry procedure?

**Setup.** Byte-identical to NET-19 (pre-LN transformer, dm=192, 4 heads, d_mlp=4·dm, UNTIED readout, per-digit cross-entropy, teacher-forced GO-shift, LSB-first base-10 a+b=c, bs=256, 12000 AdamW steps, seed 0). ONE documented deviation: pos-embedding CTX 22→32 so beyond-max n=8 eval (3n+3=27) fits; all 5 arms — including the two plain controls — share it, so comparisons stay fair. Arms: C control plain n=3 (d=1); E control plain n=5 (d=1); A curriculum GROW 2→3→4→5 (d=1); B mixed lengths {3,4,5} each batch (d=1); D curriculum GROW (d=2).

**Results (full / per-digit):**

| arm | schedule | n=4 | n=5 | n=6 | n=7 | n=8 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| C control | plain n=3 | 0.0000 / .224 | 0.0000 / .211 | 0.0000 / .153 | 0.0000 / .158 | 0.0000 / .163 |
| E control | plain n=5 | — | **1.0000** | 0.0000 / .110 | 0.0000 / .106 | 0.0000 / .105 |
| A | cur grow d=1 | 0.0000 / .107 | 0.1929 / .854 | 0.0000 / .099 | 0.0000 / .133 | 0.0000 / .110 |
| B | mixed {3,4,5} | 0.0068 / .572 | 0.0142 / .670 | 0.0000 / .099 | 0.0000 / .107 | 0.0000 / .114 |
| D | cur grow d=2 | **0.0000** / .105 | **1.0000** | 0.0000 / .129 | 0.0000 / .111 | 0.0000 / .116 |

**Findings.**
1. **Beyond-max n=6/7/8 is at CHANCE in every arm.** Curriculum (d=1, d=2), mixing, plain-n3, and plain-n5 all fail length-gen. The plain-n5 control (E) — "trained longer" in isolation — also fails (masters n=5=1.0000, n=6/7/8 chance). The wall is NOT a training-distribution artifact.
2. **NEW — MIXING PREVENTS MASTERY (arm B).** Mixed {3,4,5} never masters ANY length: per-digit stuck 0.54–0.67 / full 0.00–0.02 for ALL 12000 steps — the carry-dissociation correlated-error regime (per ≫ per^n) is permanent under length diversity. Diversity blocks length-specific mastery without delivering length-general mastery.
3. **NEW — CURRICULUM FORGETS INTERMEDIATE LENGTHS (arm D).** The d=2 curriculum mastered n=5 perfectly (per-position all 1.0000) but n=4 — trained for 3000 steps — collapsed to chance (0.0000). Final-length training OVERWRITES intermediate lengths: the optimizer converges to a single length-SPECIFIC attractor (the last length), never a length-parameterized general algorithm.

**LAW: LENGTH-WALL-IS-SCHEDULE-ROBUST + MIXING-PREVENTS-MASTERY + CURRICULUM-FORGETS-INTERMEDIATE-LENGTHS.**

**Verdict.** NET-19's open lever ("carry curriculum") is REFUTED as a cure. The wall is now characterized on depth (NET-4/5/19), scale (NET-19), AND schedule (this round) — all negative for length-general composition. Surviving levers CHANGE THE PROBLEM, not the schedule: scratchpad/CoT intermediates (task), recurrence / stateful carry cell (architecture), explicit length token (input).

**Barriers.** (a) clean held-out 2048/batch over the 10^n pair space; (b) curriculum learning is mature but the NEGATIVE (curriculum does not fix length-gen on controlled per-digit arithmetic) + the two new mechanism findings are new; (c) same dm=192 scale as NET-19; (d) clean — test lengths 6/7/8 never trained; (e) PARTIAL — 1 seed per arm (stark 1.0000-vs-0.0000 readings + in-run plain-n3 control that reproduces the known wall keep it robust; second-seed replication of the two new phenomena is the strengthening step); (f) per/full separated, per-position at max trained length (D: all 1.0000 at n=5 while n=4 chance — complete forgetting), training curves every 1000 steps, chance ceilings per length; (g) same-run plain-n3 and plain-n5 controls at identical budget/arch/seed/pos-table; E isolates "trained longer" from "curriculum"; (h) honest negative with a clear next move: do NOT invest in schedule-only fixes for length-general arithmetic.

Paper: ResearchOutput/NetworkMathematics/21_LengthCurriculumCarryChain.md. Assessment v21 (21 experiments). Notebook Part 21. Script: /tmp/exp_net_curriculum.py (ALL_DONE).
title: NET-21: The length wall is schedule-robust — curriculum and length-mixing do not unlock length-general composition

**Program:** Network/LLM research lab — round-net-19 (depth axis, round 9; the carry chain at scale). Paper 63, issue #115. Assessment v20.

## Question
NET-4/5 decomposed the decomposable-error regime on LSB-first base-10 addition: the copy-self basin is a tied-readout artifact (untie ⇒ escape, NET-5), but the **carry chain** is a width/depth/readout-immune credit-assignment wall. The last open question: **does scale unlock depth pay?** Scale up vs NET-5 — dm=192 (untied, 4.5–18× params), bs=256 (2×), 12000 steps (~3× distinct pairs). d∈{1,2,4}×3 seeds = 9 configs, n=6, untied head, per-digit CE, teacher-forced GO-shift, pre-LN, 4 heads, d_mlp=4·dm.

## Part A — 9/9 MASTER, depth pays NOTHING (flat-mastery horn)
| depth | full (mean±std) | per (mean±std) | escape | masters |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 0.9940 ± 0.0085 | 0.9991 ± 0.0013 | [1000,1000,1000] | 3/3 |
| 2 | 1.0000 ± 0.0000 | 1.0000 ± 0.0000 | [1000,1000,1000] | 3/3 |
| 4 | 0.9976 ± 0.0035 | 0.9997 ± 0.0005 | [1000,1000,1000] | 3/3 |

**Scale unlocked depth-1 mastery** (NET-5's d=1 failed 2/3; here all 3 d=1 seeds master). But the d=1 vs d=4 gap is 0.0036 — within seed noise. Deeper nets do NOT beat shallow ones at 4.5–18× params and 3× data; credit-assignment depth-immunity holds at scale. The copy-self-basin + stochastic-escape mechanism reproduces at dm=192 (d=2 s=2: per≈0.87/full≈0.10 plateau st=2000–3000, per⁷=0.38≫full, jump to full=1.0000 at st=4000). Per-position: errors spread thin across interior columns — the model computes the full n=6 sum algorithmically (fresh-draw 1.0000 on a 10¹² pair space rules out memorization).

## Part B — the length wall survives scale: 9/9 at CHANCE
Every mastered config re-trained at n=3, then tested n=4/5/6 (chance 1e-5/1e-6/1e-7):
- 8/9 n=3 trainers master perfectly (full=1.0000); **d=1 s=2 reproduces the NET-5 carry-chain dissociation at 18× params** (per=0.8010 but full=0.2041 — per-high/full-low correlated errors).
- **full=0.0000 at every depth and seed** on n=4/5/6; per-digit ≈0.09–0.22 ≈ the digit floor. Examples: d=1 s=0 n=4 per 0.219; d=4 s=1 n=5 per 0.087 (below the 0.1 floor — the n=3 algorithm misfires structurally); d=4 s=2 all lengths ≈0.10–0.12.
- Deterministic replication: the fast probe (task #89) matched the marathon's d=1 s=0 and d=4 s=0 numbers BYTE-IDENTICAL (same seed/settings ⇒ identical results), confirming the wall at the two depth extremes ~6h before the marathon finished.

## Law
**SCALE-UNLOCKS-LENGTH-SPECIFIC-MASTERY, NOT COMPOSITION + CREDIT-ASSIGNMENT-DEPTH-IMMUNITY-HOLDS-AT-SCALE.** Fixed-length carry computation is depth-flat AND scale-solved (solved at every depth, d=1 included); length-general carry composition is depth- AND scale-immune (chance at every depth, every seed, at the largest arithmetic scale in the program). The carry chain's hard part is NOT capacity — it is length-general composition (memorize-without-compose, NET-3 leg-2 / NET-4/5), a training-objective problem.

## Barriers
- (a) Clean: fresh held-out 2048/batch, 10¹² pair space, no injection. (b) Partial: scale-invariant shallow-transformer results known; NEW = scale-resolution of NET-5's under-powered d=1 + the scale-immune length wall + the d=1 s=2 dissociation at 18× params; Catalog (698 pkgs) no carry-chain-at-scale depth law. (c) CONFRONTED — dm=192/bs=256/12000 steps is the largest arithmetic setup in the program; the scale-up failed to break the law, that IS the finding. (d) Clean: fresh random held-out batches, no test pair ever trained. (e) 3 seeds × every config (9/9 + 9/9) + byte-identical probe replication. (f) Per-digit AND full-number separated, chance ceilings per length, per^7 correlated-error diagnostic, per-position across all 7 columns, two-step d=2 s=2 escape documented. (g) Within-program d=1/d=2/d=4 identical architecture, NOT budget-matched (generous to depth) and still flat. (h) Honest negative: **do not scale depth or width to fix length-general arithmetic** — attack the objective (carry curriculum, scratchpad/CoT intermediates, a stateful carry cell / recurrence).

## Next
The depth axis has had 9 iterations (all flat — the load-bearing boundary still needs NON-POSITIONAL stack content / s≫64 / unbounded nesting WITH causal masking). Standing alternatives: attention-cost law at a second seed (k* ∝ ctx proportionality is 1-seed-per-point), or a fresh axis. Scripts: /tmp/exp_net_carry_scale.py (ALL_DONE), /tmp/exp_net_carry_lenprobe.py (PROBE_DONE).
title: NET-19: Scale unlocks length-SPECIFIC mastery but NOT length-general composition — the carry chain is solved at every depth at dm=192, the length wall is depth- and scale-immune (credit-assignment depth-immunity holds at scale)
